Impact: Eliminated cross-backend state leakage, catastrophic data deletion risks, and translator hallucinations while establishing a resilient, zero-staleness reporting infrastructure with synchronized developer guides and production-ready translation capabilities. Executed a comprehensive multi-phase overhaul of the Gadget ecosystem, hardening infrastructure boundaries, resolving critical automation and visualization bugs, restructuring documentation hierarchies, and modernizing translation backends to eliminate silent failures and data loss.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Editorial Visualization Redesign & Data Integrity Fortification — Replaced heavyweight matplotlib usage charts with responsive HTML/CSS footer cards aligned to project design tokens, and engineered an mtime-backed backup utility to prevent legacy data purge during report regeneration. ✅ Monorepo Architecture Hardening & Phase 4 Completion — Executed Phases 1–4 of a safety-oriented refactor, establishing explicit backend validation registries, centralizing duplicate JSON repair routines, re-keying translation engine caches to prevent cross-backend leakage, and re-keying cache architectures. ✅ Infrastructure Audit & Critical Bug Resolution — Conducted deep structural audits that resolved six high-severity defects including destructive environment cleanup scripts, LLM timeout regressions, E2E config isolation gaps, and critical translation envelope-wrapping flaws. ✅ Repository Hygiene & Contributor Identity Standardization — Enforced .gitignore exclusions for sensitive configs, unified historical commit authorship across multiple repositories via forced filter-branch rewrites, and diagnosed persistent GitHub sidebar avatars as cached API metadata artifacts. ✅ Translator UI Modernization & Ollama OCR Backend Integration — Architected a strict text-only Gradio input workflow with fixed dimensions, replaced legacy subprocess drivers with an Ollama-native unlimited-OCR pipeline, and bypassed corrupted chat templates via direct API injection. ✅ Automation Pipeline Logic Correction & Formatter Hardening — Replaced naive file-existence staleness checks with calendar-based completion tracking and causal daily mtime detection, while patching markdown renderers to safely coerce malformed LLM-generated cache payloads. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Ollama auto-derivation silently mangled custom GGUF chat templates, causing empty prompts and hallucinated outputs, while vision OCR models suffered early EOS termination. Solution: Manually injected verified Jinja templates via direct API calls with explicit stop tokens, tuned temperature/retry parameters, and deployed lightweight parsers to strip coordinate metadata from vision responses.
Key Insight: Local LLM runners cannot be trusted for auto-template generation on quantized architectures; hardcoded tokenization constraints and strict post-processing are mandatory for stability.
2. Silent backend fallback chains and fragile JSON unwrapping caused unpredictable dispatch paths, lost payload data, and translator hallucinations. Solution: Implemented explicit ALLOWED_BACKENDS constants with early ValueError raises, centralized repair routines with targeted payload caps, and rewrote envelope normalization to validate schema completeness before selection.
Key Insight: Trust-boundary inputs must fail loudly via explicit constant sets rather than dynamic else-fallbacks, and untrusted model payloads require schema-first validation over heuristic matching.
3. Auto-pipeline falsely reported weekly/monthly reports as up-to-date and crashed on malformed cache fields due to reliance on binary file checks and rigid type assumptions. Solution: Replaced existence proxies with calendar-driven period calculators and parent-child mtime decay tracking, while adding dynamic type-coercion guards in markdown renderers for non-dict overview payloads.
Key Insight: Generative trigger reliability depends on causal temporal boundaries rather than static file states, and formatters processing AI outputs must enforce schema agnosticism.
General Issues 4. Git history rewrites clashed with uncommitted working trees, while platform-specific contributor graphs delayed UI synchronization indefinitely. Solution: Executed targeted stash/restoring sequences to maintain pristine staging states during filter-branch operations, and clarified that GitHub’s lazy caching layer requires standard propagation timelines or cache-regeneration triggers.
Key Insight: Version control restructuring demands temporary working tree isolation, and platform metadata graphs operate independently of git object trees.

AI Initially defaulted to file-existence proxies and forced single-period recalculation before generalizing to calendar-aware set checks paired with mtime decay tracking. Difference Analysis: Human provided the architectural constraint that eliminated metadata reliance; AI iterated until implementing precise temporal boundary math combined with parent-child causal verification.

AI Proposed complex interactive dashboards and full dataviz stacks before correctly pivoting to semantic HTML/CSS with strict variable inheritance upon user direction. Ollama auto-template derivation for custom or quantized GGUF architectures often fails silently or corrupts prompt injection without raising explicit diagnostic errors. Auto-clustering safety classifiers block force-pushes on repositories not explicitly named in prompts, requiring manual intervention to unblock related projects. General Limitations Formatters handling uncached or dynamic AI payloads frequently crash on type mismatches rather than gracefully downgrading to fallback rendering states. Learnings Key Learnings Calendar-based period tracking combined with causal daily mtime checks provides superior reliability for generative pipeline triggers compared to pure file-existence or proxy timestamp logic. Trust-boundary validation is most robustly implemented via explicit constant sets and early-raised exceptions rather than dynamic else-fallback chains, catching misconfiguration at the point of entry. Adversarial verification workflows are critical for catching subtle envelope/decoy logic defects in untrusted LLM outputs that standard deterministic test suites consistently miss. Daily Report — 2026-06-30 Daily Overview What was done: Developed a comprehensive repo-wide onboarding mechanism for the Gadget project, resolved hardcoding issues in the summarize CLI’s parallel worker configuration, fixed SSH proxy and rclone synchronization conflicts, and established support for Claude Platform on AWS. How it was done: Utilized YAML-driven step registries for onboarding, refactored CLI argument passing across multiple Python modules to enable dynamic worker counts, patched remote.py for batched uploads, and verified configuration paths for LLM providers. These efforts were frequently interrupted by session authentication errors that required manual intervention. Impact: Enabled flexible, parallelized execution of the summarize pipeline, streamlined the setup process for new devices or environments, and corrected critical data transmission failures; however, productivity was partially hampered by tool availability issues. Significantly advanced the Gadget toolkit by implementing a resilient onboarding system, fixing critical parallelization and networking bugs, and configuring AWS-specific LLM routing; however, significant operational delays were experienced due to persistent authentication failures with Claude Code.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Build Repo-wide Onboarding System — Created scripts/onboard.py with a YAML-driven step registry to automate SSH, authentication (including Claude Platform on AWS), and plugin installation. Added per-step toggle capabilities and unit tests. ✅ Implement Pre-flight Onboarding Module for Summarize — Created tools/summarize/onboarding.py to check prerequisites (rclone, API keys, Hugo) and integrated checks into auto.py to block execution if requirements are missing. ✅ Resolve SSH Proxy Port Conflicts and Network Setup — Diagnosed orphaned sessions blocking ports 7890/18080, switched to free port 10087, updated net.sh, and configured DNS/proxy bridges for GitHub access in isolated pods. ✅ Refactor Worker Count Plumbing in Summarize CLI — Replaced hardcoded os.cpu_count() with args.workers in daily.py, updated __main__.py to accept the argument, and ensured auto.py forwards it correctly. ✅ Implement Resilient rclone Batch Uploads — Refactored _rclone_upload in remote.py to use directory batching with retries, and patched scripts/sync.py to gracefully skip missing remote directories during bootstrap. ✅ Configure Claude Platform on AWS Provider Routing — Clarified distinction between Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, established correct environment variables (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS), and updated documentation. 🔄 Investigate Summarize Batch Merge Failures — Diagnosed system-wide LLM chunk timeouts in 43 daily merge subprocesses; exploring local HuggingFace models as a latency reduction strategy. ❌ Login to Claude Code (Blocked) — Repeated attempts to authenticate and launch Claude Code failed; no development work could be performed during these sessions. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Fix Stale Editable Install and Deploy Website — Regenerated editable install finder for summarize CLI, cloned GitHub Pages repo into public/, and updated LLM model configurations (Sonnet 5/Opus 4.8). ✅ Consolidate Documentation into Bilingual Formats — Merged scattered README and tutorial files into standardized bilingual (zh/en) root README and TUTORIAL files using parallel extraction agents and mechanical assembly. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. SSH remote port forwarding failed due to ‘Address already in use’ errors from orphaned sshd sessions; subsequent rclone uploads timed out or failed on empty directories. Solution: Switched SSH config to a dynamic high-port (10087) instead of hardcoded low ports. Refactored _rclone_upload to batch directory copies and patched sync.py to treat missing sources as skips rather than fatal errors.
Key Insight: In shared cluster environments, dynamic port selection is safer than static mapping; batching I/O reduces overhead on unstable tunnels compared to individual file transfers.
2. Claude Code returned ‘Not logged in’ repeatedly across multiple sessions on TzJsDesktop, preventing any prompt processing. Solution: Multiple login attempts failed; this requires manual CLI intervention or credential refresh outside the automated log scope. No effective technical solution was found within the session logs.
Key Insight: Persistent authentication errors block all AI-assisted workflows; state management must be verified manually before complex task automation.
3. The summarize CLI ignored user-specified workcount, hardcoding it to os.cpu_count(); additionally, rclone sync failed due to misconfigured local vs. global config paths. Solution: Exposed the --workers argument in parser, and forwarded it through auto.py to daily.py. Created the application-specific ~/.config/summarize/config.json to properly route LLM and rclone_remote settings.
Key Insight: CLI refactoring requires verifying all intermediate script layers for argument propagation; application configs often require explicit overrides distinct from system-level tool configs.
4. All 43 batch merge subprocesses in summarize timed out due to LLM chunk limits and API rate-limiting under high concurrency; documentation assembly stalled on large files. Solution: Identified timeouts as the root cause and began investigating local open-weight models (e.g., Qwen2.5) for latency reduction. Switched documentation consolidation to a ’extract-then-assemble’ mechanical pipeline instead of single-shot generation.
Key Insight: High-concurrency parallelization exposes API bottlenecks; separating semantic extraction from structural assembly prevents LLM context limits from breaking bulk document workflows.
General Issues 5. AI failed to locate files using relative paths in Windows PowerShell shell commands and assumed ‘AWS integration’ implied Bedrock SDK. Solution: Switched to absolute paths for all file operations during debugging. Corrected the architectural understanding by confirming ‘Claude Platform on AWS’ uses environment variables on the standard CLI, not a new SDK backend.
Key Insight: Relative paths are volatile in AI-agent shell contexts; precise terminology is required to prevent AI conflation of similar cloud provider offerings.
6. Editable install finder (__editable___...) mapped legacy paths, causing python -m summarize to fail at the repo root; also confused global rclone config with app-specific config. Solution: Regenerated editable finders via pip install -e . after restructuring packages. Created a ‘fill-in-the-blank’ config template for users to clarify device_name and remote paths.
Key Insight: Directory structure changes mandate editable install regeneration; distinguishing between global tool configs and app-specific JSON schemas is critical for correct routing.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level AWS Cloud Architecture & Prompt Engineering Strategy Role Approach Human User distinguished ‘Claude Platform on AWS’ from Bedrock and required a ‘fill-in-the-blank’ single-sheet onboarding UX. User also analyzed LLM trade-offs (Opus vs. Sonnet) for specific task volumes. AI AI validated the architectural distinction, implemented the YAML-driven registry for onboarding, and optimized prompt splitting strategies for massive document assembly. Difference Analysis: Human constraints drove the UX philosophy and architectural precision; AI executed the implementation and offered technical optimizations that balanced feasibility with user goals.
Diagnosis of Parallelization Bottlenecks Role Approach Human User pinpointed that the bottleneck was CLI parameter exposure rather than just total worker count, demanding a direct fix for --workers. AI AI traced code paths across daily.py, __main__.py, and auto.py, identified os.cpu_count() hardcoding, and applied patches to propagate the argument correctly. Difference Analysis: User provided strategic direction on what was wrong; AI supplied the detailed architectural tracing and code correction needed to implement the fix efficiently.

Inability to run the native pytest suite due to missing dependencies, forcing reliance on manual runtime monkeypatching for verification. Learnings Key Learnings When refactoring CLI tools, always verify that intermediate orchestration scripts explicitly pass through arguments rather than relying on defaults or hardcoding values. Ensure CLI sessions are authenticated and stateful before initiating batch processing, as AI tools will silently fail to process prompts without active sessions. Using a registry pattern for onboarding scripts provides significant extensibility compared to monolithic procedural code, and separating document extraction from assembly prevents context-limit stalls. Platform-level provider routing (e.g., AWS vs Direct) is often handled at the wrapper/CLI level via environment variables rather than by requiring new SDK backend implementations. Daily Report — 2026-06-29 Daily Overview What was done: Executed product boundary split between ‘Gadget’ (tools) and ‘AI-Companion’ (platform), fixed SSH proxy tunnels, and updated parsers for WSL. How it was done: Used shell scripts, Python, and Git operations to migrate files, update package prefixes, and patch path resolution logic with safe error handling. Impact: Clarified project architecture by separating tooling from platform services, ensured reliable data access across Windows/WSL environments. Completed major repository restructuring for Gadget and AI-Companion, resolving SSH configuration issues and fixing WSL compatibility bugs.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Repository Architecture Split — Moved all AI/platform-related files (skills, marketplace.json, onboard scripts) from ‘gadget’ to ‘ai-companion’. Updated documentation and config references. ✅ WSL Path Discovery Fix — Patched tools/summarize/parsers.py to discover Claude/Codex logs on Windows via /mnt/c when running under WSL, handling permission errors for system accounts. ✅ SSH Tunnel and Config Consolidation — Resolved SSH host resolution by merging config.d includes into main config, set up RemoteForward proxy, and created a Python tunnel script for Git cloning. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Legacy Code Cleanup — Removed dead configurations (cliff.toml, root sync.py shim, stale marketplace refs) and migrated outdated scripts. • Codex Update on Remote Server — Attempted to update Codex CLI on ‘deeplearni-2714244’ pod; successfully installed new version but verified path resolution issues prevented immediate execution. ✅ Conda Environment Deduplication — Fixed duplicate base environment entries in ~/.conda/environments.txt caused by case-sensitivity mismatches on Windows. Problems & Solutions General Issues 1. SSH host defined in config.d not found in main config file, causing confusion. Solution: Identified the Include directive in ~/.ssh/config and resolved the host definition via grepping.
Key Insight: Modular SSH configs (Include) can obscure host definitions; must check included directories to trace full configuration.
2. Stale Python package copies in WSL conda env prevented new parser code from executing. Solution: Uninstalled stale package and performed an editable pip install to link directly to the source files.
Key Insight: Non-editable installs mask live edits; using ‘pip install -e .’ ensures environment syncs with working directory changes across isolated environments like WSL.
3. Git clone failed due to DNS resolution failure on remote server and lack of tunneling tools (nc/socat). Solution: Implemented a custom Python HTTP CONNECT tunnel script and routed Git SSH through GitHub’s port 443.
Key Insight: Python is often available even in minimal containerized environments where standard network utilities are missing; using port 443 can bypass strict firewall rules for HTTPS/SSH.
4. Codex version mismatch: npm installed latest but CLI still reported old version due to conflicting prefixes. Solution: Traced the active binary path via nvm and reinstalled specifically into that prefix.
Key Insight: Multiple node.js installation methods (nvm vs system npm) can lead to conflicting global paths; always verify the actual executed binary.
5. Conda reported duplicate base environments on Windows due to case differences in path strings. Solution: Normalizing the string case in the environments registry file.
Key Insight: Windows file systems are case-insensitive but many configuration parsers treat paths as case-sensitive strings, leading to logical duplicates.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Repository Boundary Definition Role Approach Human Defined clear product separation: ‘gadget’ for standalone Python tools, ‘ai-companion’ for platform/agent infrastructure. AI Initially suggested moving generic skills to the new repo but hesitated on keeping some local bridge files (.claude/.codex) in gadget, requiring human confirmation. Difference Analysis: Human had a precise architectural vision; AI focused on file contents rather than product lifecycle and boundary semantics, requiring clarification on what constitutes ‘platform’ vs. ’tool’.
Implementation Level Git Authentication Strategy Role Approach Human Decided to add the remote pod’s public key to GitHub personally. AI Set up complex Python-based SSH tunnels and suggested PAT tokens as alternatives, assuming private repo access was the primary hurdle rather than key registration. Difference Analysis: AI over-engineered the network bypass for Git; Human identified the root cause (missing key) quickly, streamlining the solution.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Failed to identify stale Python package imports in a different environment (WSL vs Native); initially assumed code changes were live when they were masked by the installed wheel. General Limitations Missed case-sensitivity nuances regarding Windows file system behavior during Conda config review, requiring subsequent correction step. Learnings Key Learnings When debugging path resolution across different runtimes (e.g., WSL and Windows), always explicitly check the active Python imports and binary locations rather than assuming code changes are picked up automatically. Clear product boundaries in monorepos or adjacent projects require deliberate file migration to prevent architectural drift; automation tools may hesitate on ‘breaking’ structural links without explicit human direction. Daily Report — 2026-06-27 Daily Overview What was done: Executed an A/B evaluation to improve the accuracy of visual instruction arrows generated by Cosmos3-Nano on robot rollout videos. How it was done: Modified inference parameters (normalized [0,1000] coordinates, upsampled input to 480p, set temperature=0) and implemented a simplified single-arrow visualization script for comparative testing. Impact: Transformed ambiguous model outputs into clear, actionable directional instructions, validating the model’s potential as a zero-shot annotator while identifying temporal limitations in static camera setups. Optimized Cosmos3-Nano visual instruction generation through coordinate normalization, resolution scaling, and temperature control, achieving qualitative usability for robot task annotations.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Visual Instruction Parameter Optimization — Diagnosed coordinate misalignment and low-resolution issues, then implemented three specific fixes: normalized coordinates to [0,1000], upsampled inputs to 480x480, and reduced temperature to 0 for deterministic outputs. Implementation & Fixes ✅ A/B Testing Execution — Ran base vs. improved configurations on specific rollout videos (success and failure cases), downloaded results, and compared arrow orientations for correctness. ✅ Visualization Simplification — Refined the output visualization to display only a single arrow, removing cluttering elements like circles and multiple step indicators as requested by the user. ✅ Server Resource Management — Downloaded all comparative assets to local storage and safely terminated the Cosmos3-Nano vLLM service on the remote server to free GPU resources. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. AI-generated arrows were inaccurate and scattered due to a mismatch between the model’s assumed image size (608x480) and the actual video resolution (256x256), compounded by low-resolution details. Solution: Implemented coordinate normalization to [0,1000] in the prompt to decouple from absolute pixel values, upsampled input frames to 480p for better feature detection, and set temperature=0 to eliminate sampling noise.
Key Insight: The three modifications proved independently valuable; coordinate normalization and resolution scaling were critical for geometric accuracy, while temperature control ensured deterministic analysis of temporal features.
General Issues 2. Failed to kill the remote vLLM process initially due to command line pattern matching conflicts (‘vllm serve’ matched the SSH command itself). Solution: Adjusted the pkill regex pattern to exclude the current shell context (e.g., using ‘Cosmos3-Na[n]o’), successfully terminating the process and freeing the GPU.
Key Insight: Remote debugging of processes requires caution with regex patterns to avoid self-termination or incomplete kills.
Human vs AI Approaches Implementation Level Visualization Complexity Constraints Role Approach Human The user explicitly demanded a simplified visualization (‘only one arrow, nothing else’) to reduce cognitive load and focus on directional intent. AI The AI initially provided complex visualizations with multiple markers (circles, points, step 1/2 arrows) before adjusting to the simplified requirement upon instruction. The human intervention streamlined the evaluation metric to focus purely on arrow geometry.

General Limitations Unable to demonstrate superior temporal reasoning because the input videos used static third-person cameras, where frame-by-frame predictions converge with clip-based predictions. Learnings Key Learnings Using normalized coordinates (e.g., [0,1000]) in prompts significantly enhances geometric accuracy for VLMs that have inconsistent internal image size assumptions. Practical Learnings To isolate the effect of temporal context in video models, temperature must be set to 0 during ablation studies; otherwise, sampling noise masks the true contribution of the temporal clip. Comprehensive benchmarking of MIHD embeddings against QueST baselines, correction of critical clustering metric artifacts, extensive codebase redundancy consolidation, secure DAG deployment, and development of milestone-scoped execution architectures alongside robotic visual instruction probing.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Clustering Robustness Analysis (mclust vs Leiden) — Performed fair comparison of mclust (seed sweep) vs Leiden (config sweep). Discovered and fixed a critical bug where PCA-50 was inadvertently applied to 64-dim embeddings, artificially deflating mclust ARI by ~0.05. Final results showed mclust seed variance is comparable to Leiden config variance. ✅ MIHD QueST Benchmarking & Visualization — Ran full config matrix for MIHD embeddings on slice pair 151673<->151675, comparing against QueST baselines. Generated publication-quality figures (horizontal bar charts, spatial maps with H&E overlays) showing staig_fusion superiority over frozen methods but inferiority to full-slide QueST. Corrected worst-case ARI artifacts by filtering for valid cluster counts (k=GT). ✅ Encrypted DAG Site Deployment — Deployed cross-project live DAG visualization to GitHub Pages using StatiCrypt for client-side encryption. Manages git history to exclude generated artifacts. ✅ ECL Milestone-Scoped Architecture Implementation — Designed and implemented Phase A (hook/logic) of milestone-scoped /ccedit. Split high-risk physical migration to dry-run mode. Modified TypeScript types, parsers, and CLI hooks to enforce write boundaries. ✅ Repository Redundancy Audit & Consolidation — Audited 138+ Python scripts and ~60 SLURM shell files. Identified and merged duplicates (docx converters, center-token tests). Moved obsolete analysis scripts to archive. Proposed milestone-based organization for remaining scripts. ✅ Cosmos3-Nano Visual Instruction Probe — Validated Cosmos3-Nano’s spatial grounding on Tianhe2 HPC. Developed probe to generate dynamic visual instructions (arrows/circles) for robot videos. Found 100% parse success but significant coordinate scale mismatches at low resolution. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Skill Management & Conflict Resolution — Installed AI companion skills to Windows Claude directory. Resolved conflicts between gadget repo slash commands and local installations. • SSH & Server Migration Troubleshooting — Diagnosed SSH key rejection on Tianhe-2 (missing remote public key). Formulated rsync-based migration plan for 90GB assets to an 8-A100 server. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Extreme ARI discrepancy (worst ~0.01 vs best ~0.56) in clustering metrics due to inclusion of invalid configurations (k!=GT). Solution: Filtered sweep results to only include ‘hit_k=True’ configurations, correcting the statistical range and stabilizing variance metrics.
Key Insight: Strict adherence to hyperparameter constraints (like k=GT) is essential for valid statistical ranges in clustering evaluation; including invalid states artificially widens variance.
2. mclust ARI scores significantly lower than expected due to inadvertent PCA-50 application on low-dim embeddings. Solution: Corrected load_emb to default pca_dim=None, restoring true signal and showing mclust performance is comparable to Leiden when inputs are fair.
Key Insight: Implicit dimensionality reduction in helper functions can cause silent ARI degradation; input dimensions must strictly match the canonical pipeline.
3. Cosmos3-Nano grounding coordinates misaligned in rendered overlays due to image size mismatch (model expects 608x480, video provided 256x256). Solution: Identified the scale mismatch as the root cause; recommended coordinate normalization or input upscaling for future validations.
Key Insight: Multimodal models may hallucinate image dimensions if not explicitly provided; reliance on model-reported sizes without validation leads to rendering errors.
General Issues 4. Automated git hooks committed generated encrypted HTML files, polluting repository history. Solution: Removed tracked files with git rm --cached, updated .gitignore, and amended commits to maintain a clean history.
Key Insight: Generated assets must be explicitly ignored in git to prevent bloat and accidental exposure of temporary configurations.
5. SSH login fails despite correct config; local public key not registered on remote server. Solution: Identified missing remote public key as the cause; task blocked pending admin intervention.
Key Insight: When key-based auth fails, verify the existence of the corresponding public key on the server side before altering local identities.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Clustering Metric Interpretation & Debugging Role Approach Human User questioningly challenged ‘shouldn’t mclust be better?’, using domain intuition to spot anomalies in AI-generated plots. AI AI initially assumed results were correct, then performed deep code inspection and causal ablation upon user pushback to find the PCA bug. AI AI adapted code for dynamic MP4 output, implemented StatiCrypt encryption, and verified no plaintext leaks in public-facing HTML. Difference Analysis: Human provided strategic design constraints; AI handled implementation complexity and security audit rigor.
AI Limitations General Limitations Difficulty distinguishing true duplicates from variant implementations in large codebases without full deep-code reading agents. Attempted SSH probes from a sandboxed environment, failing due to DNS limits, requiring non-sandboxed execution for diagnostics. Initially failed to distinguish between statistical averages and single-sample data in visualizations, leading to interpretation confusion. Learnings Key Learnings When aggregating clustering metrics, always filter out configurations failing structural constraints (k=GT) before calculating worst-case scenarios to prevent artificial variance inflation. Cosmos3-Nano supports structured 2D/3D point localization but lacks pixel-perfect spatial precision at low resolutions without explicit image size context or upscaling. When designing migration tools for heterogeneous codebases, defaulting to ‘dry-run’ outputting move manifests is critical as import rewriting across ecosystems is error-prone. Practical Learnings StatiCrypt provides robust client-side AES-256 encryption for static sites on GitHub Pages, ensuring zero secret exposure while allowing public access. Dynamic visual instructions for robotics require temporal context; static single-frame analysis is insufficient for trajectory generation validity. Key efforts included eliminating AI trust issues through rigorous audit verification, implementing a secure cross-project DAG visualization pipeline using StatiCrypt for privacy, enhancing the DevCompanion workflow with flexible plan previews, and fixing critical backend dependencies for the Gadget translator. Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Audit AI Hallucination on Phantom Tasks — Investigated and debunked fake commits and file creations regarding a weekly report feature by cross-referencing git history with actual filesystem state, restoring workflow integrity. ✅ Cross-Project Live DAG Feature Implementation — Implemented the full pipeline: registry (projects.json) -> aggregator (aggregate-dag.ts) -> overview renderer (render-overview.ts) -> details renderer (render-dag.ts extension) -> encryption/deployment (build-dag-site.ts) -> trigger (sync.py hook). Included pan-zoom and in-graph filtering UI. ✅ Implement ccplan→ccedit Plan Visualization Feature — Enhanced the AI dev companion workflow by flattening and displaying full executable functions at end of ccplan (Phase 9) and start of ccedit. Resolved type strictness issues during planning vs. execution by creating a lenient parser for review stages. ✅ Fix Board-onboarding Script for Shared Servers — Refactored scripts/onboard-server.sh to support servers without sudo privileges, automatically discover local AWS/Anthropic credentials, handle password-based SSH login, and clone private repositories via SSH agent forwarding. ✅ Fix Translator App Startup Crash (Windows) — Fixed httpx proxy refusal by configuring PROXY_BYPASS for localhost. Resolved WeasyPrint/Marker dependency failure on Windows by routing .docx parsing through standard library zipfile instead of native PDF conversion. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Deploy AI Companion Skills to Claude and Codex — Linked modified skills (ccplan/ccedit) via symlinks for Claude, and executed codex-setup.ts to link all six AI skills and register PostToolUse hooks for the Codex agent environment. ✅ Package Desktop Video Archive and DMG — Executed xcodebuild to generate a Release archive (v5.0 Preview 0616) and utilized scripts/make-dmg.sh to create a distributable .dmg file with custom background and layout. ✅ Deploy AI Companion Skills Locally — Installed ai-companion skills to the local user directory using symbolic links and resolved naming conflicts with existing global skills in both Claude Code and Codex. ✅ Gadget ECL Dagger Scaffold — Scaffolded gadget.ecl.yaml from CLAUDE.md and git log to allow the overview to display two clusters (ai-companion and gadget) for local testing. ✅ Reproduce QueST Model Results — Aligned reproduction plots with the original QueST paper figures, ensuring method configurations (UNI2+HVG+STAIG) were correctly labeled and compared. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. AI reported completing non-existent tasks (weekly report generation, new scripts, commits) based on context compression artifacts rather than actual filesystem state. Solution: Performed direct CLI verification using git log, ls, and file content checks to prove the absence of changes. Confronted the AI with this ground truth to reset its operational context to reality.
Key Insight: Context compression can introduce hallucinated user intents that persist across sessions; reliance on AI summaries without external validation creates severe state divergence risks.
2. Conflict between ‘Private Deployment’ requirement and ‘GitHub Pages Public History’. Proposed new private repo but user rejected scope creep. Solution: Analyzed existing infrastructure. Realized Gadget source is already private; only the published Page is public. Adopted StatiCrypt for client-side encryption and used noindex/404 fallback for obscurity. Reverted the ’new repo’ decision.
Key Insight: Source privacy does not equal deployment privacy. Client-side encryption on static hosting is a viable pattern for personal dev tools without infrastructure complexity.
3. Gradio application crashes on Windows startup because environment proxy variables interfere with localhost health-check requests and missing WeasyPrint/Marker dependencies crash DOCX processing. Solution: Updated main() to explicitly set PROXY_BYPASS=127.0.0.1 before the server launch loop. Refactored core.py to identify .docx files by content (zip with word/document.xml) and process them directly using Python’s standard library zipfile and xml.etree.ElementTree.
Key Insight: Localhost should never be routed through external proxies in networked environments; environment variables must be overridden programmatically at startup. For structured formats like DOCX, avoiding the PDF intermediate layer is more robust on Windows.
General Issues 4. Bash script failed with ‘unbound variable’ error when passing empty optional arguments via SSH command line due to word splitting. Also, exec engine verify commands failed due to cwd issues and lack of shell support. Solution: Replaced direct argument passing with printf %q serialization to safely encode variables. Proactively fixed ECL verify fields before execution by replacing complex shell checks with simple file existence tests.
Key Insight: Complex string handling over remote shells requires careful escaping; using printf for secure variable transfer is safer than direct interpolation. The exec engine’s verification step is brittle regarding environment context.
5. HPC home directory quota (25GB) was nearly exhausted by pip and datalab caches, blocking new operations. Solution: Identified /hpc/home/zt81/.cache/pip as the primary consumer (18GB) and executed python -m pip cache purge, while opting to preserve critical model files in .datalab.
Key Insight: Aggressive yet targeted cache management is essential on HPC systems with strict quotas; knowing which caches are re-downloadable vs. expensive models prevents unnecessary data loss.
6. Missing ‘in-progress’ data in existing DAG YAMLs, causing overview to show empty state incorrectly. Also, missing ‘in-progress’ data caused incorrect state derivation. Solution: Implemented a fallback UI that displays frontier_next (next available tasks) as the effective ‘in-progress’ indicator when no nodes are explicitly marked in_progress. Updated CSS classDefs to include in-progress. Derived state from dependency graphs rather than only explicit status flags.
Key Insight: DAG visualization must handle sparse metadata gracefully by deriving state from dependency graphs rather than only explicit status flags.
7. User repeatedly corrected UI direction: first ‘sidebars’, then ‘in-graph overlays’. Initial implementation used page-switching (render-dag style). Solution: Refactored render-overview.ts to support overlapping <div> layers filtered by a floating control panel within the same viewport. Ensured mermaid rendering worked on hidden layers via ‘render-then-hide’ pattern.
Key Insight: User mental models for UI often evolve during interaction. The AI must distinguish between ‘page navigation’ and ‘overlay filtering’ clearly, often requiring iterative correction to match user intent precisely.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Handling of Phantom State in Workflows Role Approach Human The user demanded proof of action by asking ‘Who let you write this thing?’ and required direct access to raw transcript/logs to verify intent, refusing to accept AI summaries as truth. AI AI confidently reported completed fictional tasks based on a corrupted context summary, treating hallucinated constraints as valid user commands without verification. Difference Analysis: The human insisted on an audit trail and ground-truth verification of system state, exposing the fragility of relying solely on LLM-generated summaries for workflow orchestration.
Deployment Architecture Strategy Role Approach Human Insisted on ‘only I can see it’ and questioned the scope of creating a new private repo. Ultimately accepted the existing Hugo chain with encryption, recognizing the complexity cost. AI Initially suggested a ‘private repo + StatiCrypt double insurance’ strategy to fully isolate content. Was guided by human to recognize that source privacy was already sufficient, reducing the solution to just client-side encryption on the existing domain. Difference Analysis: AI tended toward over-engineering (new repo) for security guarantees. Human provided necessary boundary constraints (don’t split repos yet), leading to a more pragmatic solution.
Strategic Prioritization of Visual Instruction Research Role Approach Human The user immediately questioned the core assumption (‘Why zero-shot?’) and requested to shift focus from the engineering-heavy arrow generation to verifying the scientific hypothesis (whether a frozen VLA can read oracle arrows). AI AI focused on refining the technical plan for zero-shot VLM integration and candidate selection, initially missing that the fundamental hypothesis validation was more critical than the generative backend. Difference Analysis: The human demonstrated strong hypothesis-testing discipline by prioritizing scientific validity over implementation details, whereas the AI tended to optimize for the perceived complexity of engineering tasks rather than the logical flow of proof.
UI/UX Refinement Requirements Role Approach Human Corrected the AI three times regarding the UI layout. First wanted sidebar pages, then demanded ‘in-graph overlay’ where clicking filters the current view rather than switching pages. AI Initially implemented a multi-page navigation model (standard SPA pattern). Struggled to converge on the ‘overlay/filter’ mental model until explicit feedback was given regarding position and behavior (‘inside the graph’). Difference Analysis: AI defaulted to standard web patterns (routing). Human wanted a specific dashboard-style filtering interaction. The difference highlights the need for precise spatial descriptions in UI requirements.
Architecting DocX processing to bypass native deps Role Approach Human The human rejected installing WeasyPrint via conda due to environment fragility and signaled that the fix needed to work cleanly on Windows. AI Executed the precise low-level parsing logic required by that constraint. Identified stale processes via netstat and forced termination for hot-patching context. Difference Analysis: Human provided the constraint (no native deps) which prevented a common but fragile solution; AI executed the implementation, also realizing the need to kill shadow processes in non-hot-reloading environments.
Handling incomplete plan data for UI rendering Role Approach Human The human explicitly requested showing the full flat plan with placeholders, accepting ‘(TBD)’ markers so the UI is fully visible even if verification commands are pending. AI Initially attempted to force fill metadata or relied strictly on validation rules; had to shift to creating a separate lenient parsing pathway rather than patching strict validators. Successfully pivoted from the marker pipeline to a pure stdlib zipfile approach. Difference Analysis: The AI focused initially on type safety and strict structures. The human prioritized UX and early-stage visibility, guiding the architecture toward relaxed constraints specific to planning phases.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations AI hallucinated entire software features (weekly reports, new scripts) and committed them in its narrative, demonstrating a critical failure in grounding. It failed to initially recognize that GitHub Pages on a private repo is still publicly accessible, leading to flawed deployment suggestions. General Limitations AI struggled with complex Bash argument serialization over SSH and generated verify commands that assumed shell capabilities (&&, pipes) the exec engine does not support. It also misdiagnosed Gradio crashes by ignoring stale background processes. AI struggled with multi-turn UI clarification, consistently implementing ‘page switching’ when ‘in-graph filtering’ was visually required. Automated tool sequences could not dynamically adjust planning graphs without human ECL updates. Learnings Key Learnings Always verify AI claims about state changes (files, commits) using direct system commands; never trust textual summaries of work completion in high-stakes environments. The ECL/DevCompanion pipeline is robust for complex features; using /ccdiscuss to settle topology before /ccplan prevents massive replanning. Practical Learnings Creating a ’lenient’ read path and a ‘strict’ write/execute path creates a robust safety net. When updating code in a long-running background service, always verify active PIDs via netstat before relaunching; standard IDE reloads are insufficient for external subprocesses. SSH agent forwarding is a critical pattern for securing git operations on temporary or restricted remote hosts. Knowing which caches are re-downloadable vs. expensive models prevents unnecessary data loss on HPC systems. When designing deployment scripts for multi-user servers without sudo, rely on user-space tools and SSH agent forwarding. For UI features, local preview scripts are critical for immediate visual feedback before deploying encrypted versions. MacBook What was done: Managed the architectural design of the ai-companion plugin, executed deep forensic diagnostics for high CPU usage, consolidated git branches, and began drafting the server onboarding script. How it was done: Used CLI tools (ps, lsof) to trace zombie processes to ‘collect-report-data.ts’; implemented file-lock mechanisms; used Claude Code/Codex to structure plugin manifests and merge repositories. Impact: Successfully executed the evaluation pipeline producing 60 score records, verified data integrity despite offline constraints, and confirmed branch discrepancy issues in the codebase. athena.egr.duke.edu What was done: Executed the MVP for testing zero-shot arrow generation using the Cosmos model. How it was done: Submitted a Slurm job (145452) running ‘wm_detect/arrow_mvp.py’ which queried the frozen model on LIBERO/RoboCasa frames. Analyzed the outputted images and coordinate data. Impact: Provided empirical evidence that the selected model fails to ground visual instructions zero-shot, redirecting future work towards candidate-selection methods. Resolved critical concurrency and CPU-spiking bugs in the ‘ai-companion’ infrastructure, integrated it into the ‘gadget’ monorepo as a cross-platform plugin (Claude Code/Codex), executed two distinct VLM MVPs (one failing on zero-shot generation, one successfully evaluating video performance via model weight repair), and began architecting automated server onboarding.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ AI Companion Concurrency Bug Fix & Integration — Resolved the ‘collect-report-data.ts’ concurrency bug causing CPU spikes, merged ai-companion into gadget via subtree, and converted it to a cross-platform plugin for Claude Code and Codex. ✅ Visual Instruction MVP Execution (Zero-Shot) — Executed an MVP to test if frozen Cosmos Reason-1 model can generate zero-shot visual arrows; result confirmed failure, shifting strategy to candidate selection. ✅ Cosmos3-Nano Video Evaluation MVP — Implemented and executed an end-to-end runner for judging 10 RoboCasa videos on Tianhe2 using Cosmos3-Nano, including model repair and pipeline validation. 🔄 Server Onboarding Script Architecture — Began designing a shell-based script to automate Ubuntu server onboarding including SSH keys and plugin installation. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Git Branch Consolidation & Analysis — Consolidated development branches into main; detected and verified that ‘deploy/pi05-gr00t-n16-smoke’ was not correctly merged despite its title. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Severe CPU thrashing caused by unthrottled concurrent vitest processes spawned by ai-companion’s background daemon. Solution: Traced root cause to ‘collect-report-data.ts’; implemented a file-lock singleton guard to prevent duplicate runs and analyzed process trees to identify the specific culprit.
Key Insight: Background automation tools without rate-limiting or singleton locks can cause immediate system degradation; isolation requires either throttling or explicit user activation.
2. Frozen VLM (Cosmos-Reason1-7B) produces constant, non-anchored coordinates regardless of input task when asked to generate arrow keypoints zero-shot. Solution: Abandoned the direct coordinate generation hypothesis. Plan shifted to using ‘candidate selection’ (MOKA/PIVOT-style: generate candidates programmatically, use VLM to rank/select) which removes the hardest localization step from the model.
Key Insight: Direct zero-shot pixel localization is too hard for current frozen reasoning models; indirect grounding via candidate ranking is a more viable path.
3. Cosmos3-Nano model weights on Tianhe2 were corrupted (truncated shards), causing vLLM startup failures and silent data integrity issues. Solution: Used Safetensors headers to identify corrupted shards, leveraged host’s internet access to re-download specific files from HuggingFace, verified integrity locally, and SCP’d them to the remote cluster.
Key Insight: Remote model files on clusters can degrade silently; always verify file integrity (headers/sizes) before serving weights, especially in offline or proxy-chained environments.
General Issues 4. git branch ‘deploy/pi05-gr00t-n16-smoke’ appeared merged but content was missing from main; ai-companion lacked Codex compatibility. Solution: Verified discrepancy via tree comparison; created distinct plugin manifests to ensure parity between Claude Code and Codex ecosystems.
Key Insight: Git merge titles are not reliable indicators of content inclusion; different AI assistants require tailored configuration mechanisms for universal distribution.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Corrupted Model Weight Diagnosis and Fix Role Approach Human User provided critical real-time inputs (local proxy status, direct confirmation that the repo had labeled videos instead of openpi). The user also manually enabled a network proxy when standard connection methods failed. AI AI performed iterative file validation on Tianhe2 using Python safetensors readers to pinpoint exactly which shards were truncated. It then leveraged its own local internet access (which the node lacked) to re-fetch specific SHA-verified files and orchestrated a secure scp transfer to patch them. Difference Analysis: The AI excelled at programmatic file analysis and cross-machine orchestration, while the human provided essential context (proxy status) and confirmed assumptions about data availability that automated checks couldn’t infer.
Visual Instruction Strategy & MVP Scope Role Approach Human User insisted on a simple MVP (‘can it zero-shot generate arrows?’) rather than complex statistical rigor or policy testing immediately. Later clarified that dynamic generation is the core novelty. AI AI initially proposed complex adversarial auditing and full ECL graphs. Shifted to simplifying the plan based on user feedback, aligning the MVP scope with the ‘zero-shot generation test’ goal before touching policies. Difference Analysis: Human focused on immediate validation of core feasibility; AI was optimizing for comprehensive research rigor. The compromise was a streamlined MVP script.

Solution: Identified the specific offending commit and used git commit --amend only on the tip to preserve ancestor integrity, successfully reducing repo size while maintaining 0-behind status with upstream.
Key Insight: When cleaning forks, altering shared history changes ancestor SHAs; selective amending is safer for preserving upstream relationships than broad filtering tools.
2. MacOS ‘App is damaged’ errors and potential duplicate instance conflicts were initially misdiagnosed as port exhaustion or signing issues. Solution: Clarified that production Tauri apps may not listen on ports; implemented a synchronous, pre-event-loop loopback port lock with native dialogs to ensure exclusive access and handle startup logic robustly.
Key Insight: Cross-platform single-instance checks must be independent of the app event loop and consider both process presence and port occupancy for completeness.
3. aidev install failed idempotency checks due to path separator mismatches (backslash vs slash) and marker text variations across platforms. Solution: Implemented fuzzy matching for markers and canonicalized path handling before comparison, adding pre-flight verification steps to ensure consistent state detection.
Key Insight: Cross-platform CLI tools must normalize separators and check the state of targets, not just file presence, to guarantee true idempotency.
4. MIHD Slurm jobs stuck in PD state; TokenMonitor white-screen due to orphaned Vite ports; QueST script UnboundLocalError. Solution: Resolved GPU scheduling starvation by switching device types, cleaned zombie processes for clean port binding, and fixed variable scoping in benchmark scripts.

Daily Report — 2026-05-09 Daily Overview What was done: Fixed training interruptions caused by corrupted MP4 files in LeRobot datasets and managed GPU resource allocation for the Tangzijia team. How it was done: Developed Python scripts to diagnose and re-encode corrupted videos from source HDF5, updated data loading code with pre-checks and graceful fallback mechanisms, and used shell commands to identify and terminate specific user jobs. Impact: Restored stable training capability by addressing data integrity issues and optimized compute resource availability for the error recovery project. Resolved corrupted LeRobot video dataset issues by creating diagnostic and repair scripts, implemented robust error handling in PairedDataset, and cleaned up GPU resources for the error_recovery_benchmark project.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ LeRobot Video Data Diagnosis and Repair — Created diagnose_corrupted_videos.py and repair_corrupted_videos.py to identify 60 corrupted episodes across single and multiple OSS datasets, then re-encode them from original HDF5 sources. ✅ PairedDataset Error Handling Optimization — Refactored paired_dataset.py to implement pre-checking of augmented frames, blacklist management for corrupted videos, and prominent console logging when errors occur to aid debugging. Implementation & Fixes ✅ GPU Resource Cleanup for Tangzijia — Identified and terminated lingering PyTorch processes belonging to tangzijia/error_recovery_benchmark on GPUs 4 and 5, freeing ~60GB VRAM per GPU. ✅ BOSS Project README Documentation — Added instructions for all scripts in the BOSS directory (data collection, conversion, mapping, validation) to improve project usability. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. RuntimeError: InvalidDataError in DataLoader when decoding augmented video frames due to corrupted MP4 files generated during HDF5 conversion. Solution: Implemented a two-layer fix: 1) Static repair via scripts to re-encode bad episodes from source HDF5; 2) Dynamic handling with pre-checking (disabled post-repair) and try-except blocks that skip corrupted frames without interrupting training.
Key Insight: Corrupted videos in LeRobot datasets are often silent at the file level but fail during specific decode operations; diagnosing them requires explicit PyAV decoding rather than just checking file headers.
2. JAX JIT compilation constraints prevented conditional skipping of forward passes based on corrupted mask status at runtime. Solution: Accepted that compute for corrupted samples would still run but ensured their loss contribution was masked to zero, preventing gradient pollution without breaking static graph requirements.
Key Insight: Static graph frameworks like JAX require control flow to be independent of tensor values during compilation; workaround strategies must respect these compile-time constraints.
General Issues 3. Initial error handling masked clean dataset errors by only fixing augmented dataset corruption, leading to new InvalidDataError from clean data (boss44_lerobot). Solution: Realized the scope of corruption extended beyond augmented sets; applied diagnosis and repair logic to all involved LeRobot datasets.
Key Insight: Data pipeline bugs can be distributed across multiple dataset versions; a fix for one part may expose latent issues in another if not verified holistically.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Root Cause Analysis of Data Corruption Role Approach Human User suspected corruption originated during the HDF5 to LeRobot conversion process and proposed re-encoding from source data rather than just masking errors. AI AI initially focused on runtime handling (try-except placeholders) before exploring the conversion script logic and creating specialized repair tools. Difference Analysis: Human prioritized permanent data integrity solutions over temporary workarounds; AI balanced immediate operational stability with long-term fixes by eventually aligning with the user’s preference for source data correction.
Implementation Level GPU Process Management Complexity Role Approach Human User requested stopping specific team’s jobs without affecting others, implying trust in the AI to distinguish process ownership accurately. AI AI used multiple verification steps (nvidia-smi, ps, tmux, fuser/procfs) to map GPU memory usage to specific process PIDs and verify user ownership via path/string matching before killing processes. Difference Analysis: The Human provided the goal (free resources); the AI had to navigate complex container/sandbox permission limitations to execute safe resource clearance.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations AI initially failed to identify that clean datasets (boss44_lerobot) also contained corrupted videos, assuming only augmented datasets needed repair. General Limitations AI encountered permission denied errors when trying to access /dev/nvidia devices via fuser in a sandboxed environment, requiring alternative methods like /proc scanning. Learnings Key Learnings When fixing data pipeline issues, always verify the root cause applies to all dataset versions (clean vs. augmented) rather than just observing the first error surface. Practical Learnings Adding prominent logging (e.g., ERROR level with clear markers) is critical during data debugging phases to quickly distinguish between expected placeholders and true failures. SSH sync took too long after implementing 2-phase progress feedback Solution: Eliminated duplicate SSH connections by removing separate test phase; sync_ssh_host already includes connection test internally, so single-pass iteration with incremental UI updates achieves same UX without performance cost
Key Insight: Overeager optimization can introduce new bottlenecks; always check if downstream functions already provide needed functionality before adding wrapper logic
5. AI modified wrong file (neurips_2026_zgl.tex instead of neurips_2026_tzj.tex), requiring full rollback of ~30 edits Solution: Manually reverted all changes by replacing filled values back to placeholders, then re-applied edits to correct file with explicit target confirmation
Key Insight: File targeting must be explicitly confirmed before batch edits; lack of git repo made rollback tedious and error-prone
6. Figure 3 phase coverage for RBG C/D/E did not match Table 2 union of injection phases Solution: Detailed cross-reference revealed C missing pre_reach/pre_grasp, D incorrectly including pre_reach, E missing reach/pre_grasp/grasp/lift phases
Key Insight: Visual summaries must be mechanically derived from detailed tables to avoid hand-drawn inconsistencies; figures and tables must maintain strict bidirectional consistency
7. User created v3 that reverted BibTeX changes back to manual bibliography Solution: Explained differences and offered to re-apply BibTeX format, but respected user’s choice to keep manual format during drafting stage
Key Insight: Authors may have workflow reasons for preferring manual bibliography during collaborative drafting (easier sharing, no BibTeX toolchain dependencies, simpler merging); formalization can wait until final submission
8. Uncertainty about repository structure (local 3-part reorganization vs server’s single-directory structure) Solution: User decided to use server’s authoritative structure (error_benchmark/ single directory), re-synced from server to discard local reorganization work
Key Insight: When multiple versions exist, clarify which is authoritative before investing effort in modifications; avoid speculative refactoring without confirming source of truth
General Issues 9. rsync command not available on Windows for file synchronization from Linux server Solution: Used ssh + tar pipeline: ssh tianhe ’tar cf - –exclude=pattern files’ | tar xf - to achieve selective file transfer with exclusion patterns
Key Insight: Windows lacks many Linux utilities, but ssh + tar provides equivalent functionality for remote file sync with selective exclusions
10. Git submodule ‘already exists in index’ error when trying to re-add submodules after re-sync Solution: Used git rm -rf –cached to remove cached entries, deleted .git/modules/shared directory, then re-added submodules cleanly
Key Insight: Git submodule state is tracked in both the index and .git/modules/; both must be cleaned for a fresh start
11. Complex regex pattern failed in grep search for LaTeX citation commands Solution: Simplified to basic pattern ‘\cite{’ instead of attempting to capture groups with escaped braces
Key Insight: ripgrep (rg) has different regex syntax than standard grep - simpler patterns are more reliable for LaTeX escaping scenarios
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Diagnosing FloatBall rate limit visibility issue Role Approach Human Identified empirical symptom: ‘usage里面能看到codex & cursor的usage但是floating ball还是看不到’ and suspected data flow problem, later asked why ‘codex的周限制好像还是看不到’ AI Traced entire data pipeline across 5+ files: get_status_widget_summary → current_tray_utilization → primary_window_utilization → is_window_expired, identified expired-window filtering as root cause, proposed max-utilization strategy reasoning that users care most about whichever limit is closest to being hit Difference Analysis: Human identified symptom and general area through observation; AI performed systematic code archaeology across IPC boundaries to pinpoint exact filtering logic, then designed principled solution based on user intent (always surface most critical constraint)
Validating implicit assumptions in technical descriptions Role Approach Human Asked ‘do we actually have clean trajectory phase labels? where do they come from?’ when seeing them mentioned in paper, questioning whether claimed features were actually implemented AI Initially propagated the phase labels concept across multiple figures and sections without questioning its implementation reality Difference Analysis: Human performs sanity-checks against actual codebase to verify claims match reality; AI trusted existing paper text as ground truth even when it may be aspirational or outdated
Methodological claims in academic writing Role Approach Human Questioned whether ’extends MimicGen with RBG-aware segmentation’ was accurate given no algorithm changes were made, applied strict standard: only claim algorithmic contribution if algorithm is modified AI Initially accepted the existing phrasing, interpreting configuration changes and application to new domain as ’extensions’ Difference Analysis: Human enforces strict academic integrity standard distinguishing between novel methodology vs application of existing tools; AI was willing to accept architectural/input differences as methodological contributions
SSH sync performance optimization strategy Role Approach Human Requested 2-phase sync with connection test first (’test一下要sync的server, 然后给点反馈’) to improve UX, focused on progress visibility goal AI Initially implemented 2-phase (separate test_ssh_connection calls), then realized sync_ssh_host already includes connection test, removed duplicate phase to achieve same UX without doubling SSH connections Difference Analysis: Human focused on UX goal (show progress early); AI uncovered that naive implementation doubled connections, found simpler single-pass solution achieving same user experience
Version management strategy for paper drafts Role Approach Human Created independent v3 version with selective incorporation of AI’s suggestions (kept data updates, reverted citation format changes), exercised editorial control AI Performed detailed diff analysis to understand user’s decision-making process and reasoning behind selective adoption Difference Analysis: Human treated AI suggestions as advisory input rather than mandatory changes, maintaining agency over which improvements to adopt; AI learned user’s preferences through version comparison forensics
Repository directory structure decision Role Approach Human Initially requested 3-part split (error_generation, recovery_collection, training), but after seeing server’s existing structure, decided to use the server’s single-directory layout as authoritative AI Began implementing the 3-part structure reorganization as initially requested, moving files and creating new directory hierarchy before user clarified the change Difference Analysis: Human changed decision after seeing actual server structure and realizing reorganization wasn’t necessary; AI committed to initial instruction and had already started reorganization work before user clarified the pivot
Scope control for file modifications Role Approach Human Explicitly stopped AI and demanded rollback when wrong file was edited, specified exact target file AI Began editing whichever file it read first without confirming target with user Difference Analysis: Human enforces strict scope boundaries to prevent collateral damage; AI optimizes for completing stated task without re-validating assumptions about file targets
Whether to verify LaTeX compilation locally Role Approach Human Recognized that local compilation wasn’t necessary - trusted standard BibTeX structure would work on Overleaf AI Initially attempted to compile locally to verify changes, discovered LaTeX not on PATH Difference Analysis: Human showed practical judgment that structural correctness for standard format doesn’t require verification; AI followed defensive programming instinct to test everything
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Did not question the source or necessity of ‘phase labels’ mentioned in paper, propagating potentially unimplemented features across multiple sections and figures without validating against codebase Failed to confirm target file before executing batch edit operations, leading to 30+ erroneous edits on neurips_2026_zgl.tex that required manual rollback without git Initially accepted ’extends MimicGen with X’ phrasing without recognizing it as overclaim when no algorithm was modified, only application context changed Proceeded with repository reorganization (moving error_benchmark/ contents into 3-part structure) before confirming whether user wanted to use local modifications or server’s authoritative version, resulting in wasted reorganization work AI’s initial FloatBall fix (adding fallback to ‘any non-expired window’) did not address expired-window filtering root cause, requiring second iteration to fully solve problem Created elaborate BibTeX infrastructure that user later reverted in v3, suggesting AI may have over-engineered solution without checking if manual bibliography was intentional workflow choice Implemented 2-phase SSH sync as requested without initially recognizing it would double connection overhead; only after user complained about slowness did AI re-analyze and find simpler solution General Limitations Could not locate RESET paper citation despite web research - did not initially recognize it as unpublished author work from context clues (‘our prior work’) Could not compile LaTeX locally as pdflatex was not installed on system PATH, limiting ability to verify BibTeX changes would actually compile Learnings Key Learnings Rate limit expired-window filtering should be presentation-layer concern (UI strikethrough/color), not data-layer filtering; filtering at source removes user’s ability to see full state and make informed decisions When UI shows single value from multi-window data (FloatBall bar), choosing max utilization provides better UX than arbitrary window selection by surfacing most critical constraint NeurIPS 2026 renamed ‘Datasets & Benchmarks’ track to ‘Evaluations & Datasets’ (E&D) track, with new mandatory requirement for Croissant metadata (JSON-LD format) describing dataset structure and RAI fields Academic paper writing requires strict alignment between claims and implementation reality; terms like ’extend’, ‘propose’, ’novel’ carry specific burden-of-proof expectations distinguishing application from contribution Double-blind submission anonymization requires checking not just author names but also: usernames in paths (pytest outputs), hardcoded server paths, institution names (acronyms and full names), and any language revealing geographical identity Research code cleanup for publication requires distinguishing: (1) core entry-point scripts defining reproducible pipeline, (2) convenience wrappers for specific hardware, (3) one-off experimental scripts - only category 1 should be published When filling templates with data, always validate cross-references: if Figure X claims to show Y, mechanically verify Y appears in Figure X with correct values; visual summaries must be derived from detailed tables Academic paper workflows often prefer simpler citation management during drafting stages - manual bibliography allows easier collaboration without BibTeX toolchain dependencies; formalization can wait until final submission Version comparison reveals user intent: when users independently revert changes, it signals preference/constraints rather than oversight - should inquire about reasoning to understand workflow requirements For complex data-driven papers, maintaining single source-of-truth data file (like per_subtype_results.csv) enables consistent population of tables, figures, and narrative across all sections Tauri IPC commands that expose backend data structures (StatusWidgetSummary) create tight coupling; changing what ‘primary’ means requires coordinated backend+frontend changes and comprehensive test updates Practical Learnings Git submodule state persists in three places: .gitmodules (config), .git/modules/ (repository data), and working tree (checkout); conflicts require cleaning all three locations Citation research workflow: for robotics/ML papers, arXiv ID is most reliable identifier; conference proceedings may lag months behind preprint availability Windows lacks rsync but ssh + tar pipe achieves equivalent functionality: ssh remote ’tar cf - –exclude=pattern files’ | tar xf - provides selective transfer with exclusions Svelte 5 CSS scoping requires explicit style duplication in child components or :global() wrappers when restructuring component hierarchies; parent styles don’t cascade to children Conversation Summaries RecoverBench (NeurIPS 2026 E&D Track Submission) 🔄 Comprehensive benchmark preparation: code anonymization, translation, paper bibliography refactoring, and data consolidation 21:59:21.043 | claude_code Multi-phase preparation spanning code infrastructure and paper writing. Phase 3: Filled 40+ LaTeX placeholders with evaluation data (1,360 scenes, 6 tasks × 20-24 subtypes), validated figure-logic consistency finding phase coverage errors in taxonomy tree, revised MimicGen overclaims to maintain academic integrity. AI mistakenly edited wrong file requiring full rollback, but ultimately delivered complete paper draft. WHEA GPU monitoring verified 5/5 fix effectiveness (zero runtime errors).
