(4B parameters, 4-bit quantization up to ~3.1GB, 13 language auto-detection, Apple Silicon MLX acceleration). Modification of live-subtitle.py, start.sh, health-check.sh, verification of API correctness through source code inspection. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Claude Code Permission Configuration Batch Setup — Creating unified.claude/settings.json for the algorithms directory (root+7 first-level projects+5 gadget subprojects): automatically allowing Read/Edit/Write/Glob/Grep/Bash/Agent/WebFetch/Skill; only asking about destructive operations (rm, git clean, git reset –hard, git push –force). 🔄 MIHD Project Progress Review — Reviewing MIHD plans.md to extract remaining work: identification of P0 blocking tasks (HD GPU jobs, published baseline data collection, DE analysis pipeline), P1 core tasks (in-sample query verification, multi-method query comparison, cross-section expansion, bootstrap CI), P2 enhancement tasks (HD tissue boundary biology, cross-section alignment evaluation, supplementary charts). Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. All MimicGen augmentation verifications failed (0/10 scenes), cubeA not lifted (height 0.82 desktop). Solution: Multiple rounds of diagnosis revealed the root cause: subtask fragmentation (6 subtasks = 5 independent warp boundaries, cumulative error) + lack of post-grasp buffer + gripper detection bug (search for first continuous closure) + retract subtask not warped + path parsing bug. Fixed one by one: simplified to 2-subtasks, added 15-frame buffer, improved gripper detection, merged retract into re_acquire, fixed path parsing.
Key Insight: Original MimicGen design principle: minimize the number of subtasks (2) + post-grasp buffer + start from home position. Each subtask boundary is a source of error, so it should be reduced as much as possible.
2. success_demos.hdf5 cannot serve as MimicGen source — missing env_interface_name and env_interface_type attributes. Solution: Added ensure_env_interface_attrs() helper, automatically completing the attributes in filter_valid_source, augment_success_demos, and generate_success_from_error; patch fixed HDF5 files for 7 existing tasks.
Key Insight: MimicGen DataGenerator relies on specific datagen_info attributes to identify environment interfaces; absence of these causes getenv_interface_info_from_dataset failure;Ensure integrity at each output point in the generation chain.
3. No response from the BetterSSH front-end button — WebSocket messages are silently discardedSolution: Traced to the null return value in the onMessage() placeholder in index.ts. Instantiated SessionManager, loaded SSH/BetterSSH configurations, connected to the full message routing (get_sessions, create_session, destroy_session, send_input, resize) Key Insight: The backend has a complete implementation of SessionManager (500+ LOC) but was never instantiated—a skeleton code trap; the interface exists but was never connected
4. Token usage data disappears when deleting JSONL logs Solution: Implemented a hourly append-only aggregation archive under {app_data_dir}/usage-archive, using time-based partitioning (archive covers [0..frontier], live source covers (frontier..now)) to prevent duplicate counting
Key Insight: Time-based partitioning eliminates overlap between archives and real-time data, ensuring zero duplicate statistics with minimal storage overhead (about 1KB/day/provider)
5. Claude Code frequently requires permission confirmation in exploratory projects, affecting development efficiency Solution: Simplified the permission for 80+ Bash commands listed one by one into a tool-level wildcard “Bash” that covers all Bash commands
Key Insight: Claude Code supports a tool-level wildcard (“Bash” matches all Bash commands), enabling relaxed permissions with minimal configuration, while retaining confirmation mechanisms for dangerous operations via the ask array
6. Anti-corruption review found WebSocket PTY writes without authentication (ATK-007) Solution: Added REQ-009: 127.0.0.1 binding + 256-bit session token (randomly generated and printed at startup), all WS upgrade verification require query string token
Key Insight: Security issues have the lowest cost to fix during requirement phase; red-blue confrontation should be enforced in Phase 8 (after architecture is determined, before coding begins)
7. OpenReview API returns 403 Forbidden, preventing access to NeurIPS paper review data Solution: Diagnosed double-layer blocking: (1) OpenReview API now forces all requests to require a authentication token (anonymous access disabled); (2) Frequent probes trigger nginx rate limiting. Used user OpenReview credentials (tongtongtot@163.com) via openreview-py SDK, successfully retrieved 61 reviews (7 Oral papers: 29 reviews + 7 AC decisions; 8 Spotlight papers: 32 reviews). Added delay between requests to avoid rate limiting
Key Insight: OpenReview’s authentication strategy has changed—even access to public content API requires a login token. The /login endpoint remains accessible (returns 400 validation error) while all data endpoints return 403, indicating application-level authentication is enforced. Web frontend work relies on Next.js RSC server-rendered usage of internal credentials
8. Poor terminal rendering quality—blurred fonts, slow scrolling, invalid middle-click paste Solution: Identified xterm.js as the industry standard (used by VS Code/Replit); the issue is the lack of plugins. Added WebGL renderer (GPU acceleration), Unicode11 (CJK), improved theme (Catppuccin Mocha), better font stack (Cascadia Code fallback chain)
Key Insight: xterm.js alone is insufficient—production terminals require a complete plugin ecosystem. WebGL provides 10x rendering improvement and clear fonts. Unicode11 prevents CJK width calculation errors
9. GLM5.1 and DeepSeek-Reasoner display $0.00 pricing, despite the OpenRouter integration being added Solution: Added a version field to the PricingCache structure (CACHE_VERSION=2), causing outdated caches (containing only LiteLLM data) to automatically expire when new pricing sources are introduced
Key Insight: The caching system needs explicit version control to handle mode evolution—relying solely on TTL allows outdated data to persist after code changes
10. Terminal session switching discards all terminal content—no rollback history Solution: Changed terminal lifecycle: create xterm instances once in useEffect([], []) and reuse across sessions. During switch: term.clear() → subscribe to new session → backend sends RingBuffer refill → term.write()
Key Insight: Terminal instances are expensive and store rollback state—should not be destroyed during session switching. The backend RingBuffer (2MB) provides a replay buffer
General Issues 11. tianhe cluster git pull fails, reporting ‘GnuTLS recv error (-110): The TLS connection was non-properly terminated’ Solution: Diagnosed proxy configuration mismatch: git global config points to 172.16.31.200:3138, while environment variable (from proxy_on) uses 127.0.0.1:10087. Used git -c http.proxy=http://127.0.0.1:10087 -c https.proxy=http://127.0.0.1:10087 pull to override proxy settings per command, successfully pulling data
Key Insight: Git has two independent proxy configuration layers (global vs environment variables) that may diverge. Using the -c flag per command provides an immediate solution without modifying persistent settings
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level MimicGen expansion strategy—repeated error injection vs fixed error scene + reset randomization Role Approach Human Humans identify the fundamental issue with current logic: re-error injection for each target scene to obtain diversity, which does not conform to the original MimicGen design; a fixed error scene should be used as a base scenario, and variants should be generated through randomization via env.reset() AI AI initially only saw the code implementation details (_replay_with_mimicgen_targets) and did not question the design at the ’expansion strategy’ level; after humans explicitly pointed out the problem, AI understood that the original MimicGen reset logic should be applied to the error scene Difference Analysis: Humans think from a system design perspective about ‘what is a reasonable expansion method’, while AI tends to accept the existing implementation and optimize within its framework; this is a strategic vs tactical difference
Whether to research existing solutions is needed Role Approach Human Humans actively ask after the design is presented: ‘I need you to search online to find any existing usable or comparable code, so I can avoid reinventing the wheel’ AI AI initially prepared to go directly to implementation (write design doc → invoke writing-plans), and did not propose research actively Difference Analysis: Humans show engineering pragmatism (reuse is better than rewrite), while AI tends to fall into the inertia of ‘implementing from scratch’ when not prompted. This is one of AI’s blind spots
Clarification of NeurIPS Writing Skill scope Role Approach Human User clarifies after initial exploration: ‘I want to extract a writing methodology—how they complete writing and present highlights. I hope the nuwa-skill format helps me write papers for the NeurIPS 2026 dataset track.’ Specifically requests focus only on Oral/Highlight papers (not all 544 papers) AI AI initially interpreted the request as extracting paper themes/themes. After clarification, it turned to analyzing writing structure (section organization), narrative strategy (narrative tension), reviewer psychology, and contribution presentation patterns (highlight presentation) Difference Analysis: Users have a clear metacognitive goal (learning the writing process itself), while AI initially focused on domain knowledge. nuwa-skill guides the right abstraction level—extracting cognitive frameworks rather than factual summaries. This highlights the importance of example-driven norms for complex creative tasks
Local session support (not considered initially) Role Approach Human Humans suddenly realize during design that ‘besides remote ssh, I will also use Claude and codex cli locally. I want this included too’ AI AI initially designed to cover only remote SSH sessions, and expanded to type: local Difference Analysis: Humans discover an implicit requirement (local session) during design, while AI fails to infer it from ‘I really don’t want to switch windows’—AI needs stronger requirement discovery ability
Simplify strategy for permission configuration Role Approach Human User identifies frequent confirmation as the main friction point in exploratory projects and requests to keep only deletion confirmation required AI AI provides a technical solution: using a tool-level wildcard “Bash” instead of listing each command, changing deletion commands from deny to ask Difference Analysis: User defines requirements and boundaries (exploratory project vs production project, deletion operations require confirmation), while AI provides technical implementation and optimization suggestions (use of tool-level wildcard)
Decision on archive scope Role Approach Human Choose ’local + SSH remote devices’, although SSH already has a persistent remote-cache, prioritizing additional security through a unified archive layer AI Recommendation: ‘only local’ to avoid duplication, since SSH already has a remote-cache mechanism Difference Analysis: Humans value redundancy and consistency (all data in a single archive system) more than technical efficiency (avoiding duplication)
Judgment on Terminal UX quality Role Approach Human Intuitive feel evaluation: ‘It doesn’t look like a terminal at all, something is wrong’—using real terminal’s immediate pattern recognition AI Technical checklist: identifying lack of WebGL renderer, Unicode11, appropriate theme, resize synchronization—system diagnoses the root cause Difference Analysis: Humans are good at overall UX evaluation, while AI is good at breaking down technical gaps. Humans detect issues immediately, while AI provides diagnosis and prescription
AI Limitations Critical Limitations- No proactive technical research proposal: The AI is prepared to implement directly after design completion, and no suggestion is given to ‘first investigate existing solutions’; human reminder is needed. Engineers lack the awareness that ‘reuse is better than rewriting’. Inadequate implicit requirement discovery: When users say ‘unwilling to switch windows’, the AI only focuses on remote SSH scenarios and fails to infer that local CLI also requires unified management. Stronger scenario completeness reasoning is required. 6 rounds of diagnosis are needed to identify all MimicGen bugs: subtask fragmentation → retract not warping → gripper detection error → insufficient interpolation steps → parallelization path bug → cache cleanup. The AI cannot predict all issues at once. Failed initial access to OpenReview API; no awareness of recent authentication policy changes. All 30+ attempts (API v1/v2, different endpoints, visitor login, various headers) return 403 until credentials are provided. The system lacks the latest knowledge on OpenReview authentication requirements for 2026. failed to detect that SessionManager was never instantiated during initial architecture scan — a lot of time was spent debugging port conflicts and WebSocket issues before the root cause of an empty onMessage handler was found. The AI initially analyzed but did not actively question the rationality of ‘repeated error injection’ design; human guidance is needed to explicitly state ’error scene should be fixed + randomization reset’ before refactoring begins. Wrong path assumption: The Agent initially assumed files were edited under recovery_collection_portable, but the user has moved out of that layer. All edits are lost and need to be applied under a new path. Failed to initially identify that an outdated pricing cache would prevent OpenRouter data loading — explicit code tracking through Litellm.rs cache logic is required to detect version control gaps. General Limitations Triggering OpenReview nginx rate limiting: Approximately 30 consecutive requests during the diagnosis phase led to a temporary IP ban (152.3.43.42). Exponential backoff or diagnostic authentication requirements should be implemented earlier. Subagent execution process is opaque: When 5 background agents run parallelly, users cannot see intermediate progress (only ‘waiting for completion notification’), lacking real-time visibility.感知 of large task progress is a UX pain point. Learnings Key Learnings Power of Superpowers skill chain: Brainstorming (requirement analysis) → ccplan (ECL-driven implementation) → optimize (quality improvement) form a complete software lifecycle. ECL documents serve as persistent ‘design contracts’ across sessions, enabling context consistency across multiple conversations, agents, and even different models. Value of adversarial review: Among the 9 issues identified by the Critic agent, 2 are CRITICAL (no authentication PPTY writing, SSH parameter injection) and 4 are HIGH (token brute-force attack, prototype contamination) — exposing them in a production environment would cause a security disaster. Repair costs at the requirement stage « at the code stage « at the production stage. Nature of object-centric warping: T_eef_new = T_obj_target × T_obj_src⁻¹ × T_eef_source is an invariant relative to object motion patterns. Two-step understanding: (1) eliminate the absolute position of the source object; (2) remap using the new object position. Wisdom in the original MimicGen design: (1) minimize the number of subtasks (only 2 in Stack); (2) post-grasp buffer of 10–20 frames ensures stable gripping; (3) env.reset() to home position reduces pose gap; (4) quasi-closed-loop execution (target_pose_to_action calculates delta per step). Core design of MimicGen is source demo + env.reset() randomization: Error scenes should be treated as fixed ‘initial states’, and variants should be generated using placement_initializer, rather than injecting errors for each target. Priority of NeurIPS DB Track review (based on 61 reviews): The most valued qualities are ‘comprehensive’ (17 mentions), ‘community’ (17), ’novel’ (15), ‘clear’ (28), ‘well-designed’ (13). Common criticism: ’lack of comparison’ (insufficient baseline), ‘insufficient detail’ (unclear methodology), ’limited scope’ (narrow application). The best paper (Artificial Hivemind) has the lowest average score in oral presentation (4.75) — AC decisions outweigh review scores. Oral average (5.00) < Spotlight average (5.16), confirming that scoring is not the only acceptance factor. Parallel agent scheduling mode: Independent modules (Config/Parser/LocalPTY) are assigned to different subagents for parallel execution, then aggregated for verification, increasing development efficiency by 3–5 times. The key is identifying leaf nodes in the dependency DAG with no dependencies to maximize parallelism. Claude Code –output-format stream-json: Through research, it was found that Claude natively supports structured output (newline-separated JSON), eliminating the need for regular expression parsing of PPTY. This improves Parser reliability from ‘heuristic’ to ‘deterministic’. Always research before reinventing. Return on investment of TypeScript strict mode: 195 tests + 0 type errors = production-ready code. The type system provides significant protection during refactoring (after extracting parsed-state-utils, all call points undergo automatic type checking). Spend 20% more time on types in the early stage, and save 80% of debugging time later. xterm.js is the industry-standard browser terminal (used by VS Code, Replit, Vercel, ttyd). Quality depends on a complete plugin stack: WebGL for GPU rendering, Unicode11 for CJK, Fit for resize, SearchAddon, WebLinksAddon. Only the basic xterm.js is insufficient for production. MimicGen-ready datasets require specific metadata structure: Each demo_*/datagen_info must contain env_interface_name and env_interface_type; otherwise DataGenerator cannot initialize the environment correctly. Human demonstration data quality verification should be前置 to collection stage: Simply teleop success is insufficient; replay stability and augmentability must be verified simultaneously, otherwise a large amount of unusable data will be collected. Time boundary partitioning (archive covers completed hours, live source covers current hours) elegantly solves duplication without explicit level tracking — zero overlap means zero duplicate counts. Claude Code permission system supports tool-level wildcards (e.g., “Bash” matches all Bash commands), allowing simple configuration instead of dozens of individual rules. Cost of subtask fragmentation: Each subtask boundary involves independent ‘check object pose → re-warp → 5-step interpolation’, leading to cumulative errors. 6 subtasks = 5 error sources, far more than the original 1. OpenReview API authentication architecture (2026): All data endpoints require login token; only the /login endpoint allows anonymous access (returns validation error). Web frontend uses server credentials via Next.js RSC. Rate limiting is handled at the nginx layer (based on IP), triggered by about 30 requests in a short time. Academic paper review API is increasingly locked down — institutional or personal credentials are required. Terminal resize synchronization requires full-chain coordination: ResizeObserver (frontend) → term.onResize → WebSocket message → SessionManager → PPTY.resize(). Mismatch causes line breaks in the wrong column. Debounce prevents flooding during resize dragging. Terminal instances should not be destroyed during session switching — they preserve a rollback buffer (10,000 lines). Correct pattern: create once, refill with clear() + backend RingBuffer (2MB) across sessions for reuse. The cache system must include explicit version fields when data sources can evolve — only TTL expiration is insufficient to handle mode/source changes. The allow/deny/ask three-tier permission mechanism can balance security and efficiency: allow enables automation, ask retains confirmation for dangerous operations, deny allows absolute prohibition. Claude Code configuration does not inherit automatically (independent configuration per project) — a standardized initialization process can be implemented via automated scripts (e.g., init-claude.sh). Complex robot system documentation should distinguish between developer and operator audiences: Structured questions clarify target readers, structure, language, and content retention to prevent ambiguity. React closure trap ref pattern: Registers in useEffect capturing expired props from third-party libraries (xterm.js onData) is a common bug. General solution: props → ref, sync ref.current in useEffect, read ref.current in callback. This is the best practice in the React ecosystem. Three pillars of WebSocket robustness: Reconnect (exponential backoff), backpressure (bufferedAmount check), heartbeat (not implemented but should be considered). The network layer of distributed systems must assume ‘connections may break at any time’ rather than ‘connections should be stable’. Importance of continuous closure detection: Robot gripping may have multiple attempts; the first gripper_closed > threshold may fail. Continuous closure (≥10 frames) must be detected to confirm successful grasping. Complexity of multi-process debugging: (1) Each worker requires independent env+augmenter instances; (2) path parsing is more error-prone (relative paths may miss levels); (3) absolute paths like demos_dir must be explicitly passed; (4) robosuite WARNINGs need to be suppressed separately in worker functions. Quota counting logic should reflect real availability: augmentable_only is stricter but more reasonable than replay_only, as non-incrementable demos cannot expand the training set even if replay is possible. Frontier ASR model landscape (2026): True streaming models are rare. Moonshine v2 (73–107ms latency, 34–245M parameters) and Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime (480ms, 4B parameters) represent the state-of-the-art. Moonshine uses a callback-based API suitable for real-time transcription; Voxtral requires manual chunking but offers higher accuracy. Both support Apple Silicon native acceleration (Moonshine via CoreML, Voxtral via MLX). Different permission requirements for exploratory and production projects: Exploratory projects prioritize efficiency (loose permissions), while production projects prioritize safety (strict confirmation). Step-by-step accumulation configurations easily cause inconsistency (e.g., 80+ long rules, diverse project styles); regular use of templates can improve maintainability. Practical Learnings Git proxy configuration operates in two independent layers: global configuration (git config –global http.proxy) and environment variables (http_proxy, HTTP_PROXY). Mismatch leads to cryptic TLS errors; using the git -c flag for each command provides an immediate solution while preserving existing configurations. LeRobot 0.4.0 save_episode error: ‘only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars’ on observation.dones field (shape=(1,) np.array) Solution: Root cause: LeRobot’s get_hf_features_from_features() maps shape=(1,) to scalar Value, but validate_frame() requires ndarray. Inserted loop before save_episode() to convert all dones arrays to Python int via .item()
Key Insight: When framework validation and encoding logic conflict, optimal insertion point is the buffer between them (episode_buffer), not modifying feature definitions or bypassing validation
2. Screenpipe 0.2.13 (Homebrew) startup failed with ‘Protobuf parsing failed’ error when loading wespeaker_en_voxceleb_CAM++.onnx model Solution: Identified Homebrew version as deprecated (does not build). Uninstalled via brew, deleted corrupted model cache (~/Library/Caches/screenpipe/models/), switched to npx screenpipe@latest or official desktop app, updated all documentation
Key Insight: Homebrew formula deprecated status is critical signal. When encountering low-level dependency issues, check upstream maintenance status first rather than debugging abandoned versions
3. Battery training loss immediately became NaN from first iteration despite data appearing normal Solution: Systematically traced pipeline: found cycle column had 4 NaN values from corrupt row (battery 31, cycle 833). StandardScaler computed NaN mean/std, causing (data - NaN) / NaN = NaN for all scaled values. Removed single corrupt row
Key Insight: NaN propagation through normalization: Single NaN in training data corrupts StandardScaler statistics (mean/std), causing all subsequent scaled values to become NaN. Always validate data cleanliness before normalization operations
4. TokenMonitor costs don’t match Claude Code /cost output Solution: Discovered TokenMonitor used 2.0x multiplier for 1h cache tokens while Claude Code uses unified 1.25x rate. Changed cache_write_1h pricing in pricing.rs to match Claude Code exactly
Key Insight: Claude Code’s /cost deliberately simplifies pricing (unified rate) despite API providing granular breakdown. UI simplicity can justify data aggregation — not every field needs exposure
5. CircuitBreaker HALF_OPEN race condition: state check outside lock allowed multiple probes to enter simultaneously Solution: Moved state check inside ‘async with self._lock’ block to ensure atomic state check + transition
Key Insight: Concurrent state machines must perform state check and transition atomically within same lock. Any lock-external check introduces race window
6. MIHD paper positioning unclear — initially framed as ‘fusion strategy benchmark’ with vague core contribution Solution: Repositioned as ‘frozen FM + self-supervised fusion paradigm evaluation’ answering ‘can this replace fine-tuned methods’. Changed narrative from method proposal to systematic boundary exploration
Key Insight: Benchmark papers evaluate paradigms, not methods. Core value is systematic boundary exploration, not SOTA claims. Precise problem definition drives correct narrative framing
7. LiteLLM pricing database missing major Chinese AI models (GLM, Qwen, DeepSeek) — systematic gap in Chinese AI ecosystem Solution: Integrated OpenRouter API (92 Chinese model entries) with concurrent fetch using LiteLLM-priority merge: OpenRouter provides base coverage, LiteLLM overwrites where available. Added 7-day TTL auto-refresh
Key Insight: Global AI pricing requires multi-source strategies with geographic diversity. Western databases systematically lack Chinese models; Chinese sources lack Western models. Redundancy is essential not optional
8. Initial uniform sampling used fixed 0-20 second range, producing invalid IR values (16, 15, 14…) instead of expected 0-0.024 range Solution: Changed strategy: interpolate within each cycle’s actual chargetime range (typically 10-13 seconds) rather than forcing into global fixed range. Avoided extrapolation beyond observed data points
Key Insight: Interpolation vs extrapolation: Forcing data into global range beyond observed bounds causes extrapolation with invalid values. Use per-sample adaptive ranges to stay within interpolation regime
9. ‘Zero-shot’ terminology easily misunderstood — STAIG fusion trains 550 epochs, reviewers would challenge if truly ‘zero-shot’ Solution: Switched to ’label-free / annotation-free’ emphasizing no manual annotation needed. Clarified ‘zero-shot’ refers to encoder level (frozen FM), while fusion is self-supervised using spatial coordinates as free signal
Key Insight: Precise terminology prevents reviewer confusion. Layered definition (frozen encoder + self-supervised fusion) avoids ambiguity and highlights practical value (no annotation cost)

User provided ‘source /app/bin/proxy.sh’ command. Updated git config http/https.proxy to new proxy (99.72.0.200:3138), npx openskills install succeeded

Deleted node_modules and package-lock.json, reinstalled to trigger correct platform dependency resolution Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. npx ccusage and all Node.js CLI tools couldn’t fetch external data despite working http_proxy/https_proxy environment variables and local proxy running on 127.0.0.1:10087 Solution: Discovered Node 24’s –use-env-proxy feature only reads uppercase HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY, not lowercase variants. Modified .bashrc and .bashrcy to export both uppercase and lowercase variables in proxy_on/net_on functions, and set NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 to enable Node’s native fetch() proxy support
Key Insight: Node.js 24+ has built-in environment variable proxy support via –use-env-proxy flag/NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY env var, but it strictly requires uppercase variable names. This is a cleaner solution than injecting undici ProxyAgent or wrapping individual CLI tools. Universal fix for all Node CLI tools, not tool-specific workarounds
2. After converting LLM prompts and Markdown rendering to English, validation revealed 6 categories of residual Chinese text that would break the English-first pipeline: LLM context strings, matplotlib chart labels, DEEP_EVAL annotations, project templates, JSON repair instructions, config defaults Solution: Used 3 parallel validation agents (one per module) to systematically grep for Chinese patterns and verify full pipeline consistency. Fixed all 6 issue types across summarize, research, and website modules
Key Insight: LLM prompt translation requires checking not just main PROMPT constants but also: (1) context strings injected during execution, (2) non-text output (charts), (3) code comments appearing in prompts, (4) generated templates, (5) error recovery prompts. Parallel agent validation (split by subsystem) is more thorough than single-pass grep for discovering runtime-injected strings
3. Remote SSH servers in different timezones caused incorrect date filtering - a record timestamped 2024-01-01T23:00:00+00:00 (UTC) was treated as Jan 1 instead of Jan 2 when local timezone is UTC+8 Solution: Added parse_remote_ts_to_local_date() helper that converts FixedOffset timestamps to Local timezone before extracting date. Modified 4 call sites to use local-timezone-aware conversion. Fixed Codex since_iso_filter to include UTC offset for correct cross-timezone string comparison
Key Insight: DateTime::date_naive() extracts the date in the server’s timezone, not local. Must convert to Local timezone first with .with_timezone(&chrono::Local) before calling date_naive(). Critical for any distributed system with cross-timezone data
4. meeting-helper needs Chinese-English mixed language transcription, but Whisper’s language detection is per-chunk (~30s) not per-sentence, causing poor quality for intra-sentence code-switching like “我们需要implement这个feature” Solution: Multi-layer mitigation: (1) added custom vocabulary in screenpipe-settings.json for common bilingual terms, (2) added retranscription workflow in CLAUDE.md guiding users to POST /audio/retranscribe API with bilingual prompt when quality is poor, (3) added Step 4 in pipe to check transcription quality and trigger retranscription for mixed segments, (4) documented limitation explicitly to manage user expectations
Key Insight: Whisper’s architectural limitation (per-chunk language detection) cannot be fully solved by model parameters. More effective strategy: custom vocabulary + secondary transcription + user feedback loop for incremental quality improvement, while honestly disclosing limitations in documentation rather than over-promising
5. LifeCopilot’s BackgroundCoordinator manages 18+ background services but has no health check mechanism. Service crashes only log errors without auto-restart, causing partial system failure without user awareness Solution: Ported health monitoring pattern from OpenClaw: created health_manager.py implementing ServiceHealthManager (4-state FSM: HEALTHY→DEGRADED→FAILED→STOPPED, restart budget 10/hour, exponential backoff 1→2→4→8→60s). Modified BackgroundCoordinator to integrate health management: 5min health checks, auto-restart on failure, mark as degraded when budget exhausted, EventBus notifications. Added GET /api/health endpoint exposing all service status
Key Insight: Porting mature patterns from production-validated open source projects (like OpenClaw’s health monitoring) is more reliable than designing from scratch. Key is understanding original design rationale (why 4-state FSM? why limit restart count? why exponential backoff?) and adapting to target project context
6. Float ball collapse animation on Windows showed visual flicker, but only when direction=‘left’ (ball on right side). Direction=‘right’ (ball on left) did not flicker Solution: Root cause: SetWindowPos simultaneously moves and resizes the window, but WebView2 rendering is async. When ball position jumps (x=96→x=0) during resize, the 1-2 frame gap shows old content clipped incorrectly. Fix: Wrap SetWindowPos with ShowWindow(SW_HIDE) before and ShowWindow(SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE) after, so WebView2 doesn’t render intermediate frames. Applied only to collapse (!expanded) to minimize side effects
Key Insight: Native window geometry changes (SetWindowPos) are synchronous, but WebView2 content rendering is asynchronous. When the window’s left edge moves (direction=‘left’ collapse), the WebView content coordinate system shifts, causing visible flicker during the 1-2 frame rendering lag. Direction=‘right’ doesn’t flicker because the left edge stays at x=0 - only the right edge shrinks
7. Reporting script bug caused pick_place and coffee to read stale full_run_200attempts.log, both showing incorrect 398/260 numbers instead of actual 168/85 Solution: Bypassed log parsing and directly inspected HDF5 files with h5py to get ground truth demo counts
Key Insight: Log-based reporting can drift from actual data artifacts; HDF5 files are the authoritative source for data validation
8. Float ball collapse animation caused ball to move left then right instead of staying in place Solution: Root cause: Setting expanded=false immediately removes .shell.expanded class, causing CSS justify-content to jump from flex-end/flex-start to center. During the 250ms capsule width transition, the ball drifts toward center. Fix: Remove .expanded condition from direction-based justify-content rules so they apply throughout the transition
Key Insight: CSS transitions interact with native window resize timing. Frontend CSS transition (250ms) completes before backend window resize (t=260ms). If CSS rules change immediately based on expanded state, the ball floats during transition. Direction-based positioning must persist throughout transition to anchor the ball
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Search-First strategy (research before implementation) Role Approach Human User emphasized “先搜索现有开源方案再实现” for meeting-helper and interrupted AI when it started requirements analysis: “你能用websearch先研究现有方案吗” AI AI initially wanted to proceed directly to ccplan Phase 0 requirements analysis, preparing to design architecture from scratch. AI knows this principle (mentioned in ccplan skill) but in execution tends toward “I can solve this” mindset and skips research phase. Node.js CLI proxy fix strategy Role Approach Human User framed problem as ’npx ccusage@latest doesn’t go through proxy’ and asked for ‘one-time-fix solution’, likely thinking about wrapping npx command, modifying ccusage source, or creating custom launch script AI AI investigated full dependency chain: checked ccusage source → confirmed it uses native fetch() without custom dispatcher → checked Node version (24.12.0) → found –use-env-proxy support → discovered uppercase-only variable requirement → verified user only had lowercase variables → proposed shell-level solution by unifying variable case in proxy helper functions Difference Analysis: Human focused on tool-specific workaround; AI found root cause at Node runtime level, enabling universal fix for all Node CLI tools. AI’s solution was simpler (3-line shell function change) vs wrapping/patching individual tools. Key: checking tool dependencies first before proposing solutions
Scope of English conversion for content generation pipeline Role Approach Human User initially requested: ‘modify JSON report → generate_markdown() to only output English version, then translate to Chinese at website level’. This suggested modifying only Markdown rendering layer AI AI recognized this required changing entire LLM prompt chain (not just rendering), proactively checked research module for similar patterns. During validation phase, AI used 3 parallel agents to discover residual Chinese in 6 additional categories (context strings, chart labels, templates, etc.) not obvious from initial requirement Difference Analysis: Human specified desired behavior but didn’t articulate all necessary changes; AI inferred full technical scope (prompts → rendering → charts → templates → error messages). AI’s multi-phase approach (convert → validate → fix residuals → optimize) was more thorough than user’s initial single-step request. Demonstrates AI’s strength in dependency analysis and completeness checking
Realistic limitations of Chinese-English mixed transcription Role Approach Human User asked “你能解决一下关键风险吗?” after meeting-helper v1 completion - explicitly pointing to ECL-documented CRITICAL risk (poor quality for intra-sentence code-switching) AI AI was overly optimistic in Phase 0-9 about Whisper large-v3-turbo’s multilingual capability (DEC-003 confidence=0.75), suggesting it could be “solved”. Only after user explicitly demanded “solve critical risk” did AI adopt more pragmatic mitigation strategy (retranscription API + custom vocabulary + documentation) Difference Analysis: AI tends toward technical optimism (“better model will solve it”), while human knows from practice that some technical limits are architectural (Whisper’s per-chunk language detection can’t be changed by tuning). Human intervention forced AI from “solve problem” mindset to “mitigate risk + manage expectations” mindset, which is more mature for handling inherent technical constraints
Testing hide/show workaround necessity Role Approach Human User asked to test direct SetWindowPos first before adding hide/show complexity, saying ‘ok，可以试试’ - pragmatic approach of validating whether workaround is actually needed AI AI initially proposed hide/show as definitive solution based on theoretical WebView2 async rendering behavior without testing if flicker actually occurs with direct resize Difference Analysis: Human favored empirical testing (’try it first’) over theoretical analysis. This revealed that direction matters - only left direction flickers, making the solution more targeted. AI jumped to fix without establishing baseline. Empirical testing beats theoretical analysis for edge cases
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Initial English conversion (Phase 1-2) missed 6 categories of residual Chinese text: LLM context strings in merge prompts, matplotlib chart labels, prompt annotations, templates, error recovery prompts, and config defaults. Only discovered after user asked ‘check the complete pipeline’. AI’s first-pass conversion focused on obvious locations (PROMPT constants, Markdown labels) but missed execution-time injected strings and non-text outputs AI didn’t anticipate Phase 11 user requests in meeting-helper (retranscription workflow, Q&A logging, speaker management). Though Phase 5 adversarial review found Chinese-English mixed transcription limitation, didn’t propose retranscription as mitigation; though researched Screenpipe’s speaker system, didn’t proactively include in Feature list; designed Q&A interaction but didn’t consider logging requirement. AI’s forward planning still has blind spots - can identify problems but may not propose best solutions, can research features but may not proactively recommend AI understanding of Whisper language detection mechanism was insufficient. In meeting-helper Phase 2-4, marked “Chinese-English mixed language” as confidence=0.75, suggesting Whisper large-v3-turbo + bilingual config could handle well. Actually Whisper’s detection is per-chunk (~30s) not per-sentence, poor for intra-sentence code-switching. AI tends to rely on “model is powerful” intuition when assessing technical feasibility, overlooking architectural-level inherent constraints Misread stale log file (full_run_200attempts.log) when pick_place and coffee lacked run_200att_*.log files, causing incorrect 398/260 reporting; failed to verify against actual HDF5 output artifacts before summarizing. For data validation tasks, AI should always verify against authoritative source (HDF5 files) rather than relying on potentially stale intermediate logs AI proposed CSS pre-positioning workaround (moving ball left then resizing window) for float ball flicker without fully analyzing IPC timing constraints. Only after user questioned it did AI realize CSS changes and Win32 SetWindowPos cannot synchronize across Tauri IPC boundary - they will always be 1+ frames apart, making approach fundamentally unworkable AI didn’t anticipate second animation bug (left-then-right movement during collapse) that emerged from first fix. Only user testing revealed CSS justify-content issue caused by immediate .expanded class removal during transition General Limitations AI couldn’t complete interactive shell verification on tianhe server: when testing Node fetch() through proxy, got ‘TypeError: fetch failed’ with EPERM. AI correctly identified this as sandbox proxy connection issue rather than code problem, but couldn’t complete real-world validation. Had to rely on theoretical correctness (bash -n syntax check + environment variable verification) instead of end-to-end test Over-reliance on file content caching led to multiple ‘File has been modified since read’ errors. AI should adopt paranoid strategy: always re-read immediately before Edit even if file was just accessed, especially in workflows with linters/formatters or multi-agent concurrency Learnings Key Learnings ccplan’s adversarial review (Phase 5 Adversarial Filtering) is extremely valuable. In meeting-helper, code-reviewer subagent as adversarial critic found 6 critical problems main planner missed, including CRITICAL-level Chinese-English mixed transcription limit (Whisper per-chunk detection causes poor intra-sentence code-switching quality), long meeting context overflow, speaker identification limits, installation complexity, privacy compliance. These weren’t sufficiently identified in Phase 0-4 single-perspective planning. Key insight: complex project planning must introduce independent critical perspective (adversarial review) focusing on “what planner would miss” not “whether plan is correct” MimicGen success rates from error scenes are low (57.4% overall for success demos, 9.57% for stack human demo augmentation); human teleoperation fallback is necessary for comprehensive coverage when automated generation hits success rate plateau Node.js 24+ has built-in environment variable proxy support (–use-env-proxy flag / NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1), but it ONLY reads uppercase HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY, not lowercase variants. Common pitfall when shell proxy setup scripts only export lowercase. Solution: always sync both cases in proxy helper functions. Universal fix for all Node CLI tools When refactoring LLM-driven pipelines from one language to another, validation must cover: (1) static prompt templates, (2) runtime context injection, (3) non-text outputs (charts/images), (4) code comments appearing in prompts, (5) generated templates/scaffolds, (6) error recovery logic. Parallel agent validation pattern (one per subsystem) is more thorough than single-pass grep Porting validated architecture patterns from mature open source projects is more efficient and reliable than designing from scratch. LifeCopilot’s OpenClaw integration demonstrated: health monitoring (4-state FSM + restart budget + exponential backoff), circuit breaker (closed→open→half-open), config hot reload (watchfiles + EventBus), speaker diarization (voice embeddings + calendar assist) all from production-grade implementations. Key: understand original design rationale (why 4 states not 3? why limit restart count? why exponential backoff?) then adapt to target context. “Understand → port → adapt” workflow significantly reduces design risk since source project already discovered pitfalls MCP (Model Context Protocol) as standard interface between AI assistants and external tools greatly simplifies integration complexity. meeting-helper demonstrated MCP’s power: Screenpipe exposes all capabilities through 27 MCP tools (list-meetings, get-meeting, search-content, list-speakers, update-speaker, etc.), Claude Code CLI achieves complete meeting Q&A functionality (real-time query, history search, speaker management) without any custom code. Proves value of standard protocols in AI tool ecosystem - tool providers implement MCP server once, all MCP-supporting AI assistants (Claude, Codex, etc.) can use directly. Compared to REST API or custom integration, each AI assistant would need separate adaptation DateTime timezone handling nuance: date_naive() on DateTime extracts date in source timezone, not local. For remote timestamp filtering, must explicitly convert to Local timezone first with with_timezone(&chrono::Local) before extracting date. Critical for any distributed system with cross-timezone data Multi-dataset contrastive learning requires mapping-level source tagging and Dataset-level list-based architecture; enables flexible sampling from heterogeneous augmentation sources (single vs multiple OSS perturbations) JSONL (append-only log) + in-memory cache hybrid architecture is highly effective for scenarios requiring both persistence and performance. LifeCopilot’s multiple subsystems use this pattern: session history (deque(maxlen=100) + data/sessions/{user_id}.jsonl), audit log, thoughts, mismatches. Key design points: (1) write with atomic operation (write tmp → os.replace) to prevent corruption on crash, (2) lazy load on read (first access reads recent N records) to avoid slow startup, (3) use bounded buffer in memory (like deque(maxlen)) to prevent memory leak, (4) unified timestamp with ISO 8601 UTC for timezone safety, (5) periodic archival (data_lifecycle.py cleans by retention_days) to prevent infinite growth. This architecture is best practice validated at scale in logging systems, event sourcing, audit trails WebView2 rendering is asynchronous relative to native window geometry changes. SetWindowPos modifies window size/position synchronously, but Chromium needs 1-2 frames to render new content. For transparent windows with complex layouts, this async gap causes visible flicker. ShowWindow(SW_HIDE) before geometry change and SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE after prevents intermediate frames from being composited by DWM SetWindowPos anchor point behavior: top-left corner is fixed, so resizing smaller means right/bottom edges move inward. When content needs visual anchor to right (like direction=‘left’ float ball), must simultaneously adjust x position by width delta. Fundamental Win32 API constraint affecting all window resize logic CSS transitions interact with React/Svelte state changes non-obviously. Removing class (like .expanded) immediately changes computed styles, but transitions may still be in progress. For multi-step animations involving both CSS and native operations, CSS rules must persist throughout transition period regardless of logical state, or use separate ’transitioning’ state Practical Learnings Character-ratio language detection (5% CJK threshold) is sufficient for technical content classification. English technical docs with occasional Chinese terms typically have <1% CJK ratio, providing wide margin. No need for complex NLP-based language detection for content pipeline classification tasks Code optimization pattern: extract reusable helper for complex parsing, then compose higher-level functions from it. parse_remote_ts → parse_remote_ts_to_local_date pattern eliminates duplication and is easier to maintain than copy-pasting RFC3339 format strings. Performance optimization should reduce redundant work without sacrificing clarity Configuring lenient permissions (auto-allow most operations) for exploratory projects significantly improves development experience while balancing security and efficiency. meeting-helper’s .claude/settings.local.json demonstrated this strategy: add 60+ common commands (Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/WebFetch/git status/npm/python, etc.) to allow list for auto-pass; keep ask confirmation only for destructive operations (rm delete files, git push, git reset –hard); directly deny extremely dangerous operations (rm -rf recursive force delete, git push –force, git clean -f). This three-tier permission strategy (allow/ask/deny) avoids frequent interruptions (exploratory work needs lots of file reads/writes, command runs) while preventing irreversible errors (deletion, remote push need manual confirmation) - best config for exploratory dev environments Conversation Summaries error-recovery-benchmark ✅ MimicGen result analysis and human collection workflow 05:38:51.216 | claude_code Analyzed MimicGen success demo generation (739/1365 scenes succeeded, 626 failed). BasicContrastive.py contrastive loss bottleneck: per-node Python loop over 3000-4000 spots with tensor cloning each iteration Solution: Vectorized loss computation using batch logsumexp operations eliminating the loop; masked self-similarity with fill_diagonal_(-inf); used boolean masks for positive neighbor filtering
Key Insight: Even mature deep learning code often contains un-vectorized loops from prototyping phase; profiling + vectorization can yield 10-50x speedups with no algorithmic changes
2. Crossformer LIPM version (MSE=9, MAE=1.3) performs 18x worse than master version (MSE≈0.5) despite patch mechanism designed for irregular battery data Solution: Diagnosed fundamental architecture mismatch: Crossformer’s DSW_embedding assumes continuous seg_len time steps with positional encoding, but LIPM patch method creates irregular gaps filled with zeros that break temporal continuity, waste model capacity, and lose time interval information. Recommended: interpolation to uniform grid, time window aggregation, or irregular time-series models (GRU-D, BRITS, NAOMI)
Key Insight: Zero-padding is NOT neutral for sequence models with positional encodings - it actively misleads model to learn ‘zero patterns’ instead of temporal dependencies. Architecture assumptions must match data preprocessing; forcing irregular data into patch+zero format breaks semantic meaning

content:
Daily Report — 2026-04-07 Daily Overview What was done: Conducted a comprehensive review of the website and update.sh script, fixed 4 script bugs, and set up a complete Hugo site deployment environment, restoring the website update process from continuous failures with exit code 1/127/128 to all 7 steps passing successfully. How it was done: A layered verification strategy: first read the code, then check dependencies, and finally run the script. This helped identify environmental deficiencies (Hugo, theme, deployment repository) and logical bugs (PID duplication, missing file replacement, directory protection issues). After manual installation of missing components by the user, multiple rounds of verification were performed. Impact: The website CI pipeline is now available, Hugo build and GitHub Pages deployment paths are functional, and subsequent content publishing requires no manual intervention. Additionally, silent errors in the video compression rollback branch were identified and fixed, preventing future content loss. Fixed 4 script bugs in website/update.sh and established a complete Hugo deployment environment. The website update process has recovered from total failure to all 7 steps passing, and the full daily/report/weekly MCP synchronization process has been initiated.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Verified the availability of website/update.sh script — The system checked all dependencies and directory structures of update.sh, identifying fatal and minor issues such as missing Hugo, missing themes/PaperMod/, missing public/ deployment repository, and missing pngquant/HandBrakeCLI. ✅ Fixed update.sh script bugs — Resolved 4 bugs: inconsistent step numbering (1/6→1/7), duplicate PIDs added to the pids array for video compression, HandBrakeCLI rollback branch did not replace original files after compression, and find triggered set -e termination when static/images and static/videos directories were missing. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Set up a complete Hugo deployment environment — Completed by the user: installed Hugo extended v0.154.5, cloned the PaperMod theme to themes/PaperMod/, cloned tzj2006.github.io to public/, and configured GitHub authentication. 🔄 Initiated full daily/report/weekly/monthly MCP synchronization and merging — Checked via the MCP gadget tool: found 6 dates (Apr 1-5, Apr 7) had sessions but no reports, and no weekly report. Data export for Apr 7 has been started; all dates need to be merged batchwise before a weekly report can be generated. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Hugo was not installed, causing the script to terminate at Step 5 with ‘hugo: command not found’ (exit 127) Solution: The user installed Hugo extended v0.154.5 using the system package manager.
Key Insight: set -e directly converts any command failure into script termination. The absence of Hugo prevented the 7-step process from reaching critical build stages.
2. Themes/PaperMod/ and public/ directories were missing, preventing Hugo build and deployment. Solution: The user cloned the PaperMod theme and tzj2006.github.io deployment repository.
Key Insight: Hugo site deployment depends on three independent components (hugo binary, theme repository, deployment git repository). Any missing component causes silent or termination-style failures, and these prerequisites should be clearly stated in the documentation.
General Issues 3. The static/videos directory was missing, causing a find error and set -e termination at Step 4. Solution: Added a directory existence check ([ -d “$DIR” ]) before the find command; the step is skipped if the directory does not exist.
Key Insight: Find operations on optional/empty directories must be protected in set -e scripts, otherwise normal “empty directory” scenarios can trigger unexpected script termination.
4. PIDs from HandBrakeCLI rollback branch were duplicated into pids and original files were not replaced after compression (output: .hb.mp4). Solution: Moved pids+=($!) and the echo statement into their respective if/else branches; added && mv after the HandBrakeCLI command.
Key Insight: The PID tracking logic for parallel background tasks must align precisely with the if/else control flow. Placing common code outside branches can lead to duplicate execution and silent data loss bugs.
5. git push failed due to missing GitHub authentication (could not read Username for ‘https://github.com’）’) Solution: The user configured SSH key or gh auth and re-run the script; the script passed completely.
Key Insight: HTTPS remote requires pre-configured credentials in a non-interactive shell. The deployment repository should use SSH remote to avoid environment differences.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Script Verification Strategy Role Approach Human Proposes verification tasks without specifying methods, expecting to know if the script works. AI Prefers static analysis: first reads the script and CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture, then checks external dependencies, directory structures, and logical correctness, before running the script. Difference Analysis: The AI’s layered verification identified all fatal issues before execution, avoiding multiple blind runs. However, the AI cannot resolve environment issues at the sudo level and ultimately relies on manual user action.
Implementation Level Hugo Installation Method Selection Role Approach Human Uses the system package manager (ubuntu apt) to install, obtaining v0.154.5. AI Suggests using snap or downloading pre-compiled binary from GitHub releases (v0.147.4), but cannot execute due to missing sudo permissions. Difference Analysis: The user’s system package method is simpler and the version is more up-to-date than the AI’s suggestion. The AI’s recommendation focuses on version control and cross-distribution compatibility, which may be too extensive for a local development environment.
AI Limitations General Limitations Cannot execute commands requiring sudo (Hugo installation, pngquant, etc.); can only generate scripts for manual execution by users, unable to set up the environment end-to-end. Cannot configure GitHub authentication (SSH key or gh auth), preventing initial full deployment and requiring manual intervention by the user. Parallel tool calls failed multiple times due to race conditions in this session and had to be changed to serial calls, significantly affecting verification efficiency. Learnings Key Learnings Hugo site deployment requires three independent dependencies to be present simultaneously (hugo binary, theme repository, deployment git repository). Any missing one leads to failure at different stages; these prerequisites should be clearly listed in the project documentation. Practical Learnings In bash set -e scripts, find operations on optional directories must include a directory existence check; otherwise, normal “directory not created” scenarios can trigger unexpected script termination. The code for parallel background task PID tracking must align precisely with the if/else control flow. Placing common code outside branches can introduce duplicate PID tracking and silent file replacement bugs. Conversation Summaries Gadget Website ✅ Verified and fixed fatal environment issues and script logic bugs in website/update.sh, fully enabling Hugo deployment 04:12:15.435 | claude_code The user requested verification of whether the website update script worked. The AI identified three fatal issues through layered analysis: missing Hugo, missing themes/PaperMod/, and missing public/ deployment repository, as well as 4 script logic bugs: inconsistent step numbering, duplicate video PID tracking, HandBrakeCLI rollback without file replacement, and set -e termination due to missing optional directories. After the user installed environment dependencies and configured GitHub authentication, all 7 steps passed, and Hugo build and GitHub Pages deployment were successful.
Gadget Summarize 🔄 Initiated full daily/report/weekly/monthly MCP synchronization and merging process via MCP gadget tool 04:25:03.485 | claude_code The user requested parallel execution of daily/report/weekly/monthly synchronization and merging. The AI first checked the status through MCP and found that 6 dates (Apr 1-5, Apr 7) had session data but no reports, and no weekly report existed. Considering the dependency order of day→week→month, the AI decided to export data for Apr 7 first and then merge all dates batchwise. The session ended during data export, and the subsequent process was not completed.

content:
Daily Report — 2026-04-06 Daily Overview What was done: Three editorial comments for the MIHD paper draft were planned and executed. This included adding query motivations to the Abstract, rewriting the Introduction P1 structure, expanding R5 cross-slice analysis (from 4 paragraphs to 6 paragraphs), and writing the R6 P3 case study on the immune microenvironment. How it was done: First, multiple sub-Agents deeply explored the code repository and existing experimental results to design a detailed execution plan. Then, three new RM-IDEAL cross-slice benchmark experiments were run in parallel (CPU background) while performing text editing, using actual data results to refine the original expected narratives. Impact: The paper draft has shifted from placeholders to data-driven storytelling. A new core argument—clustering versus retrieval trade-off—was identified (STAIG is good at clustering but suffers from excessive homogeneity; Attention fusion is more suitable for immune microenvironment retrieval)—and the issue of invisible query points in the HD Niche Query visualization was fixed. The planning and execution of three editorial comments for the MIHD paper draft were completed, including rewriting Intro P1, expanding Abstract and R5/R6, and running three new cross-slice query experiments while fixing the HD Niche Query visualization
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Three new RM-IDEAL cross-slice experiments — Three benchmark runs were performed: 151673↔151674 (same donor D3), 151508↔151509 (same donor D1), and 151673↔151669 (cross-donor D3↔D2). Each group requires approximately 40 minutes of CPU computation, and the complete results are backed up. ✅ Planning for three editorial comments — Three handwritten comments in draft_en.md were analyzed (missing query motivations in Abstract, need to start from the main figure for Intro P1, and R5 needs expansion to 6 references to QueST+TLS). The code repository and experimental results were explored, and a detailed execution plan with steps was generated and approved. ✅ R5 expanded to 6 paragraphs + reference to QueST — P1 of R5 added references to QueST and a description of the unique value of cross-section retrieval. P2 updated the method description. P3 of R6 changed from placeholders to a clustering–retrieval trade-off argument based on actual HD immune analysis data, with both Chinese and English updates. ✅ Rewritten Introduction P1 — The original general background paragraphs were rewritten into a 6-sentence roadmap structure, directly corresponding to the Results titles of R1–R6. The first sentence provided key numbers from ARI 0.26→0.55, with both Chinese and English updates. ✅ Patch-level query motivations added to Abstract — A description of the mechanism that frozen FM embedding naturally supports cross-slice retrieval was added at the end of the Abstract, along with the discovery of the clustering–retrieval trade-off (later updated from “immune boundary discovery” to a more accurate “trade-off” narrative based on experimental results). Both Chinese and English updates. ✅ Analysis of HD immune microenvironment Niche Query — A new file analyze_hd_immune_niche.py was created to calculate T cell/B cell marker scores, filter 23 epithelial-connective tissue boundary T cell enriched spots, and compare retrieval results of three methods: PCA/Attention/STAIG. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Fixing HD Niche Query visualization — The issue of invisible query points in visualize_hd_niche_query.py was resolved: the star markers were expanded from 20 to 26 with a white outer ring of 32, all 4 panels were labeled, and arrows were added for the H&E panel. Three figures were regenerated. ✅ W14 weekly report writing — WEEKLY_REPORT_2026_W14.md was generated, including 8 sections such as Leiden experiments, HD experiments, paper writing, and code updates, with complete numerical data tables. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. HD immune analysis revealed extremely sparse T cell marker expression (1278/17502 spots, mean 0.014), and TLS markers are even sparser (242 spots). The original argument that “multimodal outperforms single-modal capture of immune infiltration” does not hold. Solution: The narrative in R6 P3 was changed from “multimodal identification of immune infiltration boundaries” to “clustering–retrieval trade-off”: 96% of STAIG retrieval results are concentrated in the epithelium (excessive homogeneity), PCA gene expression is 3.8x more effective at capturing T cells than STAIG, and Attention fusion performs most evenly at the boundary (60/40 Epi/CT).
Key Insight: The optimal clustering strategy using frozen FM embedding (spatial contrast learning) differs from the optimal retrieval strategy (attention fusion), making this a more meaningful discovery than expected.
General Issues 2. benchmark_rm_ideal.py writes results to the same summary.csv by default, so the results of each new pair overwrite those of the previous pair. Solution: A backup is created immediately with cp after each pair experiment (summary_151673_151674.csv, etc.). The result for 151673↔151669 was manually reconstructed using heredoc (overwritten by 151674 results).
Key Insight: Long-running batch experiments require per-pair output directories to be designed at the script level or aggregated after the pipeline completes.
3. conda activate produces no output in the background command, and the output files of three experiment processes (bgqoqyepm, etc.) are always 0 bytes. Solution: conda run -n General python ... was used instead of conda activate General && python ... to ensure proper background output writing.
Key Insight: The background bash environment for Claude Code does not inherit the shell’s activate state, and conda run must be used to ensure environment isolation.
4. The same experiment was started twice with two different processes (conda activate version + conda run version), wasting resources with 6 benchmark processes running simultaneously. Solution: The PID of the conda run process was found using ps aux, and the duplicate 3 processes were killed to keep the original conda activate version.
Key Insight: When background processes output nothing, it is necessary to confirm whether the process is actually running (ps aux) before re-submitting.
5. The query points (red stars) in the HD Niche Query visualization are hard to see visually and cannot be used for paper presentation. Solution: The script was fixed: the star markers were increased from markersize=20 to 26, a white outer ring of size=32 was added, all 4 panels were marked, and an arrow plus text label was added for the first panel.
Key Insight: Query spots in paper figures require multiple visual cues (color, size, outer ring, label), and a single red star is completely hidden against the heatmap background.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Correction of TLS/T cell arguments Role Approach Human The human comment wrote “TLS T cell”, expecting to find regions enriched with TLS/T cells in HD colon cancer data as cases of multimodal advantage. AI The AI ran actual analysis and found extremely sparse T cell markers (7.3% of spots), and PCA gene expression shows that multimodal detection of T cell enrichment is better than STAIG, thus proposing a more accurate “clustering–retrieval trade-off” argument. Difference Analysis: Human intuition relies on the prior knowledge that TLS is a common immune structure in colon cancer, but AI found that immune infiltration in this region is insufficient to support the original argument; AI identified a more theoretically valuable trade-off discovery.
Identification and priority of paper comment content Role Approach Human Humans already know what the three comments are (query motivations, Intro structure, R5 expansion) and know they need to reference QueST and include TLS/T cell biology cases. AI AI needs to first read the file, compare differences, then explain each comment, and finally use multiple sub-Agents to explore the code repository to understand experimental results and feasibility. Difference Analysis: Humans provide direction and scientific requirements, while AI is responsible for feasibility verification and execution details; AI is more comprehensive in exploring the codebase but relies on code exploration for judgment about which experiments have results or need new ones.
Implementation Level Quality judgment of visualization Role Approach Human Humans directly look at the figure and notice “no query points visible”, providing clear user experience feedback. AI AI also confirmed the issue after reading the image file, but needed human guidance to notice it; AI identified and fixed the specific cause at the code level (too small markersize, lack of comparison). Difference Analysis: Human visual perception and paper usability judgment are better than AI’s code review; AI is more efficient in implementing fixes.
AI Limitations General Limitations No active reading of images to verify quality after generating visualization figures (e.g., query point visibility), requiring user feedback to detect issues; lacks active QA for image usability. Did not notice that benchmark_rm_ideal.py would overwrite summary.csv, resulting in the overwrite of 151673↔151669 results, which had to be manually reconstructed with heredoc based on memory. Initially misused conda activate as a prefix for background commands, causing all three experiment processes to output 0 bytes and wasting time troubleshooting; conda run should be used first. Because the status of the first batch of processes was uncertain, the same three experiments were submitted twice, causing 6 processes to run simultaneously, which had to be manually killed. Learnings Key Learnings A fork exists between the optimal fusion strategies for clustering and retrieval: STAIG spatial contrast learning is most suitable for global domain clustering (Avg ARI 0.546), but its strong spatial homogeneity leads to excessive focus on the same domain during retrieval at the boundary (96% Epithelium), while Attention fusion (60/40 distribution) is more balanced for boundary microenvironment retrieval—this is a new core argument in R6. Results of three new RM-IDEAL experiments: Layer 3 of the same donor cross-slice (151673↔151674) has a high Spearman ρ of 0.86, and same-label@50 reaches 100% for the same donor (151508↔151509); Layer 3 of cross-donor (151673↔151669) shows a negative correlation (ρ=-0.73), indicating systematic differences in the morphological structure of Layer 3 between different donors. In HD colon cancer data, T cell markers (CD3D/CD3E, etc.) are extremely sparse (7.3% expressed), and the ability of PCA gene expression to detect T cell enrichment (3.8x) is higher than visual + gene fusion (STAIG 2.2x), indicating that T cell signaling is mainly driven by gene expression rather than tissue morphology. Strategy at the beginning of Introduction: Directly presenting key numerical findings (ARI from 0.26 to 0.55) is more persuasive than general background introduction; corresponding Results section titles for each paragraph enhance structural consistency. Conversation Summaries**✅ Paper editing completed: Rewrite of Intro P1, update of Abstract, expansion of R5/R6 (synchronized in Chinese and English)** 21:30:00.000 | claude_code The AI synchronously reworked the 6-sentence roadmap structure of Introduction P1 (bilingual), added query motivations at the end of the Abstract, and incorporated QueST references into R5 P1/P2. For R6 P3, the placeholder was replaced with substantive content. Meanwhile, three new cross-slice RM-IDEAL experiments and HD immune niche analyses were run in the background. The HD analysis revealed extremely sparse T cell markers, and the unexpected result of excessive homogenization boundaries in STAIG prompted the AI to revise the arguments in R6 P3 and the Abstract from ‘immune infiltration recognition’ to ‘clustering-retrieval trade-off’. This was the most important narrative adjustment in this edit.
✅ Three cross-slice RM-IDEAL experiments completed: comparison of same-donor vs cross-donor conservation 22:00:00.000 | claude_code All three experiments, which took approximately 2 hours (CPU computation), were completed. The same-donor group (151673↔151674, 151508↔151509) showed high Spearman ρ for Layer 3-5 (up to 0.86) and high same-label@50 (up to 100%), while the cross-donor group (151673↔151669) exhibited a strong negative correlation in Layer 3 (ρ=-0.73). The results revealed the high conservation of tissue microarchitecture between slices of the same donor and systematic differences between cross-donors, providing key quantitative evidence for Paper R5.
✅ Draft comment analysis: identification of three editing suggestions and formulation of execution plans 21:02:12.402 | claude_code The user provided two versions of the paper draft, and the AI identified three handwritten comments through file comparison. Using multiple sub-Agents, the AI thoroughly explored the code library, existing experimental results, and RM-IDEAL implementation, completed a comprehensive evaluation of the comments’ feasibility, and generated a detailed execution plan including computational experiments and text editing. The plan was approved by the user. The core strategy is to run new experiments in parallel while performing text editing that does not depend on results, thereby improving parallel efficiency.
✅ HD Niche Query visualization correction: issue where query points are invisible 23:00:00.000 | claude_code The user reported that the query points in the HD niche query diagram were not visible. After confirming the problem by reading the image, the AI modified the annotation code in visualize_hd_niche_query.py: the star markers were increased from markersize=20 to 26, a white underlying marker (size=32) was added to enhance contrast, the annotations were expanded from only panel c/d to all 4 panels, and arrows and text labels were added on the H&E panel. After generating 3 new figures, the query points became clearly visible.
✅ W14 weekly report generation: summary of this week’s work (including complete experimental numbers) 22:28:27.357 | claude_code The user requested a summary of this week’s work. The AI reconstructed the complete W14 work content from git logs, file modification times, and experimental logs, and generated a detailed weekly report markdown file containing 11 sections, covering the full data tables for the Leiden experiments, the ranking of 12 methods in the HD experiments, the list of visualization scripts, and next week’s plans.

Weekly Report — 2026-W14 (2026-03-30 ~ 2026-04-05) This week, three main tasks were carried out simultaneously: preparation of the MIHD multimodal spatial transcriptome paper (5 days, DCC), completion of the TEDDY full embedding benchmark, Leiden comparison experiments, HD fusion evaluation, and bilingual paper outline writing to establish a differentiated research focus on “zero-sample FM embedding fusion”; systematic fix of TokenMonitor Linux FloatBall (5 days) evolved from symptom fixes to a fixed window + GDK Input Shape architecture reform through multiple iterations, and all 21 code review issues in PR #4 were completed; complete rearchitecture of Life-Copilot Discord Bot (2 days), net removal of 2823 lines, introduction of a multi-CLI Agent architecture, and implementation of multiple new features such as screen time tracking, Xoxo input channel, and MCP tool integration. In addition, research on 63 papers in the D&B Track of NeurIPS 2025 and setup of a new Linux workstation environment were completed.
Weekly Overview Metric Value Date Range 2026-03-30 ~ 2026-04-05 Active Days 7 / 7 Total Conversations 29 Projects Involved 12 Tasks Completed 44 Ongoing Tasks 9 Total Tokens 328,660,991 Total Cost $218.53 Claude Code Tokens 273,046,863 Claude Code Cost $189.80 Codex Tokens 55,614,128 Codex Cost $28.73 Average Daily Cost $31.22 Project Progress MIHD Multimodal Spatial Transcriptome Paper (5 active days) — 🔄 active Completed:
Completed extraction and multi-strategy evaluation of TEDDY-G 400M full 11-slice embeddings, confirming high robustness of the STAIG framework for gene encoders (Teddy ARI=0.495 vs PCA ARI=0.497). Integrated Leiden clustering (binary search matching n_clusters) and STHD pathological GT, completed full Leiden comparisons in DLPFC (9/9 groups).
