Per-section PCA/STAIG produce non-comparable embedding spaces, 10 out of 14 combinations in cross-slice retrieval have SL@50=0, normalize cannot fix [MIHD spatial transcriptome] (2026-03-16) Solution: Use pre-trained Foundation Model (scGPT): all slices share the same model weights, output is naturally in the same coordinate system; SL@50 increased from 0.013 to 0.416, hit rate 100%. Root cause is inconsistent coordinate systems (mathematically impossible to normalize), not insufficient gene feature information
2. CompositeBodyObject breaks during env.reset() (lid floating, base offset), but normal during HDF5 playback (set_sim_state_flat covering body position hides the problem) [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-16) Solution: Add locations_relative_to_corner instance attribute in generated_objects.py__init__, restore coordinate transformation logic from corner to center (aligned in commit 398af01b); all 139 unit tests pass
3. Semantic Scholar incorrectly merges papers by multiple researchers with the same name, famous professors like Pieter Abbeel are matched to the same person with h=4, h-index statistics severely distorted [Research Profiler] (2026-03-16)Solution: Refactor the disambiguation weight (quantitative metrics override string similarity) + add a three-level parsing chain (exact ID → paper reverse lookup → name search) + –author-id CLI parameter; when limiting speed, find the correct authorId via WebSearch and specify it directly 4. After the vla_infer.py task completes but current_prompt is not cleared, if chunk_count in the next loop is still ≥5 and the model score remains high, the done message is triggered again immediately, leading to an infinite loop reporting completion [robobrain_pi] (2026-03-17) Solution: Add current_prompt=’’ and publise_state(‘idle’) at the end of the task completion block; the state machine must reset both the trigger condition and the broadcast state change simultaneously upon completion
5. π₀.₅ Pi0WithCompletionHead uses a combination approach that adds pi0/ prefix to all parent module parameter paths, causing pytree merge to throw ‘2 children vs 1 child’ ValueError, and checkpoints cannot be loaded at all [π₀.₅] (2026-03-18) Solution: Change to inheritance (class Pi0WithCompletionHead(Pi0)), and align Pi0 parameters directly with the checkpoint path at the top level; inheritance in Flax NNX is the only way to keep checkpoint path compatibility
6. RobotwinOutputs.call only returns the {actions} field, silently discarding manip_progress; even if the model correctly predicts the progress field, external parties can never obtain it, and the eval txt file remains empty always [π₀.₅] (2026-03-18) Solution: Modify the return dict of the output transform to include the manip_progress field, and re-establish the data flow; to troubleshoot such bugs, track upward from the end of the data flow
7. When CalendarPro batch reports task status, the system returns ‘I’m not sure’ instead of processing the request [CalendarPro] (2026-03-18) Solution: Analyze the complete root cause chain: low embedding similarity → LLM classifier lacks this intent → GENERAL handler discards the AI response; add BATCH_UPDATE support across the routing/classification/processing three layers, and keyword counting rules can compensate for embedding blind spots
8. In MIHD all_aligned mode, the –alignment parameter is not injected during the evaluate phase, so EvaluationJob.alignment remains None, Harmony alignment results are completely ignored, and the alignment function actually fails [MIHD spatial transcriptomics] (2026-03-18) Solution: Add 3 lines of code before the run_pipeline.py evaluate phase: when phase==‘all_aligned’ and args.alignment has a value, inject alignment into extra_config for each experiment
9. drop_in_transit_D0 generates very few valid scenarios, with min_hold_height=0.85 being too low; objects on the desktop (z≈0.88) are misclassified as in the air, resulting in 80% false positives [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-20) Solution: Raise the threshold to 0.93 (desktop height 0.80 + Milk object height 0.08 + margin 0.05), eliminating false positives, and increasing D0 success rate from 10% to 50%
10. python summarize/daily_summary.py gets stuck permanently at @ccusage/codex step, with no output or error [gadget] (2026-03-21) Solution: Use subprocess.run(capture_output=True) to redirect stdin to DEVNULL, and the npx installation prompt for the first time forces infinite waiting; add –yes parameter to skip interactive confirmation in all 3 npx calls
11. In multi-object tasks like threading/pick_place, phase detection fails systematically, and all frames in threading are marked as pre_reach, causing 12/13 skills to fail to find an opportunity [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-21) Solution: Add InteractionSegmenter to segment trajectories by object interactions (EEF proximity + gripper state + co-motion detection), clearly define target_object and phase for each segment; completely bypass single-object phase detection instead of fixing the defect—increase threading subtypes from 3 to 25
12. The Panda robotic arm gripper action polarity is opposite to the code assumption: Panda requires action=+1 to close, but hardcoding -1 actually opens the gripper, leading to all injections for coffee/stack failing [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-22) Solution: Detect polarity via robot arm type in EnvWrapper.init, set PandaGripper to close_action=+1.0, and RethinkGripper to -1.0; add a helper and replace all hardcoded actions [-1]
13. drop_with_interaction generates 0 scenes for all tasks: the original implementation only applies a 1–3 cm offset before releasing, and objects spaced 10–20 cm never touch neighbors [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-22) Solution: Rewrite the inject logic: actively move the object directly above the non-target (+0.15m), then release the gripper to allow free fall, and track object-object contact throughout the settle process
Learning Insights Architecture Pipeline contract alignment must track the complete data flow: not only modify processing logic but also ensure data is persisted at the storage layer (e.g., segment_interactions() results written to NPZ); output transform is an implicit filter in the inference chain, and any field not in the return dict is silently discarded; CLI parameters in multi-stage pipelines must be explicitly passed to each downstream stage, not relying on implicit sharing. “Passing unit tests ≠ E2E correctness” In multi-object robot manipulation tasks, target_object must pass through all three stages (detector/injector/validator) as a primary citizen; objects[0] is the first object in dictionary insertion order, and using it in multi-object scenarios causes complete semantic errors without errors, leading to systematic misjudgments based on object state. graspable objects and fixtures must be distinguished by the grasp_geoms field, and target selection cannot rely solely on distance/position Independent processing per section (PCA/training) produces non-comparable embedding spaces, which is a fundamental architectural limitation and cannot be fixed through normalization or post-processing. The only correct zero-shot solution is pre-trained Foundation Model (shared weights). Gene FM (scGPT 100%) outperforms Vision FM (UNI2 71%) because gene expression has stronger cross-sample consistency due to the batch effect in H&E images Flax NNX extended models: inheritance (class Child(Parent)) is the only way to keep checkpoint path compatibility; combination (self.pi0 = Pi0(…)) adds a prefix before all parent module parameter paths, causing pytree merge to fail completely. The freezing mechanism (freeze_filter+nnx.DiffState) in existing frameworks usually considers scalability—prioritize reuse over creation Facing architectural design flaws, “bypassing” is more fundamental than “fixing”: the single-object phase detection assumption cannot be fixed through parameter tuning; directly bypassing it with InteractionSegmenter is a more elegant solution. Do not fix but bypass the flawed abstraction level Debugging State machine design principle: completing an event must do two things simultaneously—reset trigger conditions (clear current_prompt) and broadcast state change (_publish_state(‘idle’)). Doing only one of them leaves hidden bugs like infinite loops or upstream perception failure. None checks must precede any property access (defensive programming) When diagnosing behavior of unknown third-party libraries, writing a minimal test script is more reliable and efficient than static code analysis (robosuite gripper polarity case); log counter statistics are more effective for locating systematic bugs than reading each entry (1698 occurrences of ‘gripper not closed’ directly point to target_object ambiguity); troubleshoot implicit filtering bugs by tracking upward from the data flow Experiment naming conventions must strictly match actual implementation; inconsistent naming like “pca_uni2_staig_fusion” leads to long-term misunderstandings, and actual configuration must be confirmed by reading logs rather than just experiment names. Benchmark data quality issues (uneven distribution, all phase annotations as pre_reach) should include monitoring mechanisms during pipeline design Tools subprocess.run(capture_output=True) redirects stdin to DEVNULL, and CLI tools with interactive prompts (npx, etc.) must use –yes/-y, otherwise they hang indefinitely instead of timing out. capture_output=True is the high-level cause of hanging Slurm HPC cluster’s pam_slurm_adopt policy kills all related processes at job end, and SSH nohup cannot bypass this; long training tasks must submit formal jobs with sbatch. MuJoCo physics simulation (enable_camera=False) is a pure CPU task, and MUJOCO_GL=disabled can completely bypass OpenGL, with worker count exactly matching –cpus-per-task JAX has_aux mechanism: nnx.value_and_grad supports has_aux=True, compute_loss returns (loss_array, aux_dict) after which gradients are calculated only for loss_array, and aux_dict transparently carries monitoring metrics; stop_gradient strictly limits aux loss to MLP parameters, and the numerical ratio of action/aux loss does not indicate training imbalance Hugo best practices: .Title is the most stable field for identifying specific sections (.Section and.RelPermalink case sensitivity varies across platforms); static directory names matching content page base names cause path conflicts; auto-generated frontmatter should not use current system time as date; project-level layouts/partials can cover themes partially without forking the theme Spatial data nearest-neighbor query: Large point clouds (>10K points) should prioritize KD tree (O(N log N) preprocessing) instead of cdist (O(N²) memory); in HD spatial transcriptomics (17K+ cells), differences can reach OOM vs normal operation. Single truth source principle: constants referenced across multiple files must be imported from the only defined place Domain Knowledge- Recovery Behavior Group (RBG) grouping strategy: 29 error subtypes are clustered into 5 groups based on motor primitives, and demos within the same group can be cross‑augmented. MimicGen generates over 1,000 demos from 10 source demos; 1,740 simple requirements are compressed to 329 (saving 81%). This is a paradigm applicable widely to robot recovery data engineering. π₀.₅ computational graph characteristics: Reasoning follows a natural two‑step process (VLM prefix forward → action expert denoising). During training, Exp1–4 can be combined into one joint forward using teacher forcing. The from_hidden mode introduces circular dependencies due to the dependence on model output for conditioning, requiring an additional prefix‑only forward. Mean pooling of prefix_output is more suitable for classification tasks than suffix_output of action expert (for encoding global state understanding). The depth of LLM understanding in academic trajectory analysis exceeds expectations: It can automatically identify advanced features such as ‘infrastructure‑thinking researchers’ and ‘technical prerequisites for paradigm shifts’. The why_not_before field (attributing each breakthrough to data, compute, and insight across three dimensions) is the most valuable feature in researcher profiling. The recognition of conference awards has very low ROI with current LLM capabilities; it should be replaced by an external data source solution (exact title matching JSON library). AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:
✓ Parallel multi‑agent code review (independent analysis of reuse, quality, and efficiency across three dimensions for the same diff): Issues that do not overlap are found in all three dimensions, and parallel execution saves time. ✓ Systematic code tracking to locate root causes: Tracing upward from the data flow end point reveals silent bug elimination in output transform and S2 speed limit recursive loops. ✓ Proactive quality checks beyond task boundaries: Automatically identifying混淆 with the same name (abnormal ratio of h‑index to paper count, impossible domain span, etc.) during researcher profiling, without explicit requirement in the prompt. ✓ Academic trajectory analysis reaches the level of academic review: Automatically identifying advanced features such as ‘infrastructure‑thinking researchers’, and the why_not_before field exceeds expected value. ✓ Log aggregation and statistics to locate systematic bugs: Counter statistics of 1,698 “gripper not closed” events directly point to the ambiguity root cause of target_object, which is more efficient than individual analysis. Limitations:
✗ Tendency to locate isolated bugs when dealing with complex system problems; lacks the ability to analyze contract inconsistencies from the full data flow perspective, requiring human guidance at the architecture level. ✗ Lack of proactive global data flow verification after local fixes are implemented; passing unit tests gives a false sense of completion, and multiple omissions (e05/e06/e09, target_pos transmission, collect script not integrated) require systematic human review. ✗ Environment configuration not pre‑verified leads to full batch failure over multiple rounds (Agent sub‑agent lacks Bash permissions, conda activation fails, PYTHONPATH missing, API key type issues); individual tasks should be validated before batch expansion. ✗ Failure to actively identify efficiency bottlenecks: Only setting waiting periods when generating in serial mode, without proposing parallelization; no consideration of resource isolation due to Slurm job expiration when starting SSH with nohup. ✗ Insufficient anticipation of framework‑specific behaviors: No prediction of the impact of Flax NNX inheritance vs. combination on checkpoint paths; no realization that JAX/NNX TrainConfig mechanisms can be directly reused. ✗ Lack of knowledge about latest tool features (effortLevel: max only known after discovery), resulting in knowledge lag compared to rapidly evolving AI tool ecosystems. Next Week’s Priorities Core priorities next week:
(1) Complete Error Recovery Benchmark — fix three_piece_assembly (change get_target_object and InteractionSegmenter to _get_graspable_objects() with fallback to all objects), aiming to increase the number of subtypes from 4 to over 20; complete the collect script call to segment_interactions() to persist segmented data in NPZ.
(2) Restart π₀.₅ training — submit six sbatch tasks for Pi0.5‑base LoRA combined fine‑tuning, and generate 2,000 D0 data points; monitor the comparison of action_loss/task_loss curves for Exp1–4 and Exp5–9.
(3) Advance MIHD research — start writing a paper on cross‑slice analysis based on the zero‑sample advantage established this week with scGPT, integrating Harmony alignment results (batch_entropy 0.52) as a baseline.
(4) Release Research Profiler version 3 — implement support for paper title search (planned but not implemented this week), replace conference award recognition with an external Best Paper JSON database.
(5) Stabilize infrastructure — promote the completed unified staging architecture to all tools in research, summarize, and benchmark, and verify that sync.py synchronization works uniformly across all categories.

summary: This week, efforts were made across three devices—DCC, tianhe, and TzJsDesktop—to comprehensively advance two major research directions: robot operation and spatial transcriptomics. The Error Recovery Benchmark achieved progress from design of collection schemes (RBG group with 329 demo budgets) to architectural-level trajectory segmentation reconstruction (InteractionSegmenter), with a total of 1627 training scenes (covering 148 subtypes, +35%); MIHD spatial transcriptomics completed the full pipeline for cross-slide Embedding and established the zero-sample advantage of scGPT (100% accuracy vs UNI2’s 71%); π₀.₅ completed the full training process with loss ≈0.253, and five conditioning strategies (Exp5-9) were designed; the gadget toolchain completed the architectural reconstruction of Research Profiler disambiguation, the construction of a unified deploy staging architecture for the website, and the full upgrade of ECC to opus+max thinking. The key breakthroughs this week focused on “identifying and resolving architectural root causes”: the non-comparable per-section PCA coordinate system, ambiguity in multi-object target_object, and Flax NNX inheritance vs combination—these three systematic issues were fundamentally resolved this week.
title: Weekly Summary 2026-W12

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-22 Daily Overview What was done: Established complete weekly report archive (W05-W12), resolved blocking website deployment issues, and restructured the entire Hugo deployment pipeline by centralizing all auto-generated content (summaries, research, benchmarks) under a unified staging directory with hierarchical navigation How it was done: Batch-generated 8 weeks of structured reports via LLM; updated PaperMod theme and hardened update.sh against edge cases (no-change commits, find race conditions); built common.site_staging infrastructure with link-or-copy sync, migrated all tool deploy logic to staging, created website/sync_staging.py with bootstrap migration, and implemented custom Hugo header partial with hover dropdown CSS Impact: Created comprehensive project history documentation; eliminated three deployment blockers making the system production-ready; established single source of truth for auto-generated content preventing dual-write inconsistencies, enabled atomic updates with automatic cross-platform fallback, and provided clearer content organization with structured multi-level navigation Completed batch generation of W05-W12 historical weekly reports, fixed critical website deployment bugs (PaperMod theme update, update.sh robustness), and refactored gadget’s Hugo deployment architecture with unified outputs/site staging area, bugJournal dropdown navigation, and integrated benchmark report publishing
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Design and implement unified staging architecture — Created common/site_staging.py with resolve_site_staging_root, write_site_content, copy_site_static helpers; defined outputs/site/{content,static} as canonical staging root; added paths.SITE_OUTPUTS_DIR to common/paths.py ✅ Build website/sync_staging.py synchronization script — Created Python script implementing link-or-copy with os.link fallback to shutil.copytree; includes bootstrap_source for first-run migration of existing content from website/ to outputs/site; manages bugJournal/{daily,weekly,monthly}, research, benchmark.md, and static/{images,benchmark-report} ✅ Fix website deployment blockers and deploy to GitHub Pages — Updated PaperMod theme to latest version resolving missing partial issue, resolved merge conflicts preserving MathJax and checkbox customizations, hardened update.sh script handling no-change scenarios and find race conditions, successfully completed full deployment ✅ Migrate summarize deployment to staging — Refactored daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, monthly_summary.py to write to outputs/site instead of website/content; updated deploy detection logic to check staging paths; preserved existing CLI interface ✅ Migrate research deployment to staging — Updated research/output.py deploy_to_hugo and research_scout.py generate_hugo_post to use common.site_staging helpers; consolidated researcher profiles and daily reports under single research section ✅ Add benchmark Hugo publishing layer — Created test/benchmark/publish.py with stage_benchmark_report function; added –deploy flag to benchmark CLI; generates /benchmark/ wrapper page with iframe embedding /benchmark-report/report.html using fixed past date to avoid Hugo future content skip; added benchmark menu item ✅ Add bugJournal hierarchical dropdown navigation — Implemented parent-child menu structure in Hugo config.yml, created custom layouts/partials/header.html with submenu rendering and hover dropdown CSS, updated section _index.md files with descriptive text, normalized all URLs to lowercase /bugjournal/ for case-sensitive hosting Implementation & Fixes ✅ Update website build scripts (update.sh and update.ps1) — Modified both scripts to run python sync_staging.py before Hugo build step; preserved existing incremental image/video compression and git push workflow; updated sync.py rclone configuration to sync outputs/site/* instead of website/content/* ✅ Batch generate historical weekly reports (W05-W12) — Generated structured weekly reports for 2026 weeks 5-12 covering MIHD, Error Recovery Benchmark, CalendarPro, RoboBrain, Life Copilot, and other parallel projects across multiple devices ✅ Verify end-to-end staging sync and Hugo build — Validated py_compile on all modified files, executed sync_staging.py confirming bootstrap and link-or-copy logic, ran hugo –destination .verify-public3 confirming /benchmark/index.html, /benchmark-report/report.html, and all bugjournal sections render correctly; did not execute final push to GitHub Pages Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. First-time staging sync would overwrite existing website/content history accumulated over months Solution: Implemented bootstrap_source in sync_staging.py: if staging path doesn’t exist but website path does, move website content to staging first, then proceed with normal sync; one-time migration preserves all history
Key Insight: Switching source-of-truth requires migration path preserving existing data; bootstrap-on-first-run pattern enables safe cutover without manual pre-migration or data loss risk
2. PaperMod theme outdated causing Hugo v0.157.0 build failure due to missing get-page-images partial Solution: Cleaned macOS resource fork files (._pack-*) causing git corruption, stashed local changes and pulled latest theme, manually resolved head.html merge conflict preserving upstream theme-toggle plus local MathJax and checkbox scripts
Key Insight: macOS resource fork files (._ prefix) corrupt git repositories on cross-platform projects; theme updates require careful preservation of local customizations through manual conflict resolution
3. update.sh script aborted when git commit returned non-zero exit code on no-change scenarios Solution: Added git diff –cached –quiet check before commit; skip commit and push with friendly message when no changes detected
Key Insight: Shell scripts using set -e must explicitly handle all normal failure cases; relying on command exit codes without state checks creates fragile automation
4. /benchmark/ wrapper page not rendering: Hugo recognized content/benchmark.md but didn’t generate /benchmark/index.html Solution: Changed wrapper date from datetime.now() (future content) to fixed 2025-01-01 past date; moved from content/benchmark/_index.md (section) to content/benchmark.md (page) to avoid conflict with static/benchmark directory
Key Insight: Hugo silently skips future-dated content by default; sections with same name as static directories create ambiguous output paths—single pages are safer for wrapper content
General Issues 5. find command in update.sh failed when accessing subdirectories after parent directory deletion during recursive cleanup Solution: Added 2>/dev/null || true after find … -exec rm -rf {} + to gracefully ignore expected race condition errors
Key Insight: Recursive deletion operations create race conditions where find traverses paths that get deleted mid-execution; explicit error suppression required for this expected behavior
6. Hugo URL case normalization: config.yml used /bugJournal/ but Hugo generated /bugjournal/, risking 404s on case-sensitive GitHub Pages Solution: Normalized all bugJournal references in config.yml and content frontmatter to lowercase /bugjournal/ matching Hugo’s canonicalization behavior
Key Insight: Hugo’s canonifyURLs and slug generation lowercase section names automatically; mixed-case URLs in config create inconsistencies breaking on case-sensitive static hosts
7. Windows PowerShell execution policy blocking py_compile and verification scripts Solution: Used python -m py_compile directly or embedded Python code in PowerShell strings with python - to bypass script file execution restrictions
Key Insight: Environment execution policies can block even non-destructive verification commands; inline Python via stdin bypasses file-based restrictions without privilege escalation
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Deployment architecture: unified staging directory as single source of truth Role Approach Human User identified dual-write problem (tools writing to both outputs/ and website/) and proposed clean architectural cut: centralize all tool outputs in outputs/site matching website structure, then automatically link or copy to final locations before Hugo build AI AI initially inspected existing per-tool deploy paths scattered across website/content/* and looked for incremental refactoring opportunities within existing structure without questioning fundamental architecture Difference Analysis: Human saw systemic design flaw and prescribed architectural solution upfront; AI was anchored to existing code patterns and would likely have continued piecemeal refactoring without explicit architectural directive
Website deployment system repair iteration process Role Approach Human User executed scripts after each AI fix to verify outcomes, surfaced new issues through real testing, and maintained oversight of complete system integrity throughout multi-stage repair AI AI adopted incremental fix strategy addressing only currently visible issues, requiring multiple user-feedback iterations to achieve full robustness across all edge cases Difference Analysis: User’s empirical testing drove completeness of repair; AI’s initial solutions addressed surface problems without anticipating deeper edge cases until user feedback revealed them through actual execution
Implementation Level Benchmark publishing strategy: wrapper page with embedded iframe Role Approach Human User didn’t specify implementation details; accepted AI’s iframe-based proposal after AI encountered Hugo path conflicts during exploration AI AI initially attempted section-based publishing (content/benchmark/_index.md with static/benchmark/report.html), hit Hugo rendering conflicts, then pivoted to page + separate static directory pattern with iframe embedding Difference Analysis: AI explored multiple Hugo content model options (section, page, static file) through trial-and-error; user trusted AI to discover correct Hugo pattern and didn’t prescribe technical solution upfront
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Failed to anticipate all shell script edge cases during update.sh repair, requiring multiple user test-feedback cycles to address no-change commit handling and find race conditions sequentially rather than comprehensively General Limitations Required 3 iterations to diagnose Hugo /benchmark/ rendering failure: initially suspected staging path issue, then section vs page confusion, finally identified date: datetime.now() future content problem Did not proactively verify Hugo’s URL case normalization behavior or warn about case-sensitive hosting implications; user had to discover /bugJournal/ vs /bugjournal/ mismatch independently During git merge conflict resolution, correctly preserved both sides’ critical code (theme-toggle + local customizations), but this judgment relied on code function understanding—complex scenarios may require human review Learnings Key Learnings Bootstrap migration strategy for source-of-truth cutover: when transitioning from scattered deploy targets to centralized staging, first-run detection with automatic content relocation (move existing website/ → outputs/site before sync) prevents data loss and eliminates manual pre-migration burden Hugo theme updates require three-layer approach: ①git repository integrity (clean corrupted resource fork files), ②dependency alignment (theme version compatible with Hugo version), ③local customization preservation (manual conflict resolution for head.html, config overrides) Hugo content model edge cases: sections (_index.md) conflict with same-name static directories creating ambiguous paths; single pages (foo.md) safer for wrapper content; future-dated content silently skipped unless –buildFuture flag used; canonifyURLs lowercases all section names requiring case normalization in config Shell script robustness principles: ①check git state before operations rather than relying on exit codes, ②add error handling for filesystem operations (2>/dev/null || true for expected failures), ③explicitly exempt normal failure scenarios when using set -e Link-or-copy synchronization pattern: os.link provides zero-copy atomic updates when filesystem supports hard links; automatic fallback to shutil.copytree ensures cross-platform compatibility (Windows FAT32, networked drives) without manual intervention or user configuration Conversation Summaries gadget/summarize ✅ Batch generation of W05-W12 historical weekly reports 19:30:00.000 | claude_code Generated structured weekly reports for 2026 weeks 5-12 using daily_summary.py tool. Reports covered MIHD spatial transcriptomics (STAIG alignment fix, scGPT fusion, Harmony experiments), Error Recovery Benchmark (error injection framework, three-pool architecture), CalendarPro (intent classification upgrade), RoboBrain (task completion detection), Life Copilot (multi-intent refactoring), and Pi0.5 LoRA training across DCC, tianhe, MacBook, TzJsDesktop devices. Emphasized multiple high-density parallel project weeks with stage breakthroughs.
gadget/website ✅ Fix blocking deployment issues and deploy to GitHub Pages 20:55:34.064 | claude_code Diagnosed Hugo build failure caused by outdated PaperMod theme missing get-page-images partial. Updated theme to latest version, resolved head.html merge conflict preserving local MathJax and checkbox customizations. Fixed two update.sh robustness issues: no-change commit handling (added git diff –cached –quiet check) and find race condition (added 2>/dev/null || true). Successfully completed full deployment pipeline to GitHub Pages.
gadget ✅ Hugo navigation restructure and unified deployment architecture refactor 01:21:42.819 | codex Implemented hierarchical bugJournal dropdown navigation with daily/weekly/monthly submenus using custom header partial and hover CSS. User proposed centralizing all tool outputs under outputs/site staging directory to eliminate dual-write inconsistencies. AI refactored deploy logic across summarize, research, and test tools to use common.site_staging helpers; created website/sync_staging.py with link-or-copy and bootstrap migration; added benchmark Hugo publishing layer with iframe wrapper; updated build scripts to sync staging before Hugo build. Verified end-to-end with Hugo build showing /benchmark/, /bugjournal/{daily,weekly,monthly}/, /research/ all rendering correctly. Daily Report — 2026-03-21 Daily Overview What was done: Synchronized repository state via git and rclone, fixed subprocess bugs in summarization tools, integrated Codex usage tracking into monthly reports, upgraded ECC plugin to use Opus 4.6 across all agents, and created comprehensive documentation How it was done: Used git conflict resolution with remote preference, implemented Windows path fixes with Path.as_posix(), added –yes flags to npx subprocess calls, modified monthly_summary.py to aggregate codex_token_usage separately, batch-edited 28 agent YAML files with sed, created tutorial and contributor documentation Impact: Established reliable data sync workflow between devices and cloud storage, eliminated hanging subprocess calls that blocked daily summarization, enabled full Codex usage tracking in monthly reports, maximized AI reasoning quality with Opus 4.6 and effortLevel max, and provided clear onboarding materials for the ECC plugin system Configured development environment, fixed critical bugs in summarization pipeline, integrated Codex support, and upgraded all AI agents to Opus 4.6
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ ECC plugin exploration and configuration — Explored Everything Claude Code plugin (28 agents, 47+ skills), upgraded all agents from sonnet/haiku to opus, changed effortLevel from ‘high’ to ‘max’, created detailed ECC_TUTORIAL.md ✅ Fix npx subprocess hanging bug — Identified that npx without –yes flag caused interactive prompts in subprocess.run(capture_output=True), blocking token usage collection. Post-fusion Harmony alignment improved batch mixing metrics but degraded cross-sample niche retrieval quality Solution: Analyzed results and concluded Harmony’s linear correction cannot handle non-linear dimension meaning misalignment from per-section independent training. Recommended Joint STAIG multi-section training for next iteration.
Key Insight: Batch correction methods like Harmony assume linear offset but fail when independent training produces embeddings with misaligned dimension semantics—batch mixing and semantic alignment are distinct properties. Linear correction on embeddings trained separately cannot preserve semantic correspondence across samples.
2. CalendarPro could only handle single intent per message, losing subsequent actions like ‘schedule 3PM meeting and move dinner to 7PM’ Solution: Replaced single-intent dual-verify flow with Claude CLI MultiIntentAnalyzer returning list of intents. Updated _process_message_queue to loop through intents and combine responses. Removed 7-layer keyword override system.
Key Insight: Single-intent classification is fundamental architectural limitation, not parsing problem. Keyword hacks (always-general, context-dependent, 7-layer override) were symptoms of broken abstraction. Moving to LLM-native multi-intent removes need for all heuristics.
3. MimicGen augmentation failing: pos_delta computed but never applied to action warping, causing <5% success rate Solution: Fixed _replay_with_warping to apply pos_delta to warped_actions[:, :3] before adding noise, enabling proper object-centric trajectory transformation. Expected success rate: 50%+ for D0 translation errors.
Key Insight: MimicGen augmentation requires actual coordinate transformation, not just noise injection. The 10→1000 path depends on: 10 seeds × 200 targets × 50% success = 1000 demos. Without pos_delta fix, success rate collapses catastrophically.

Initial deep-wide analysis of Yuke Zhu with single 5MB prompt (100 papers full-text) far exceeded LLM processing capacity causing failure Solution: Implemented three-layer solution: ①added _MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=150K threshold to auto-trigger segmentation; ②_chunk_papers_by_year greedy algorithm grouping by year + per-paper splitting when single year too large; ③TRAJECTORY_MERGE_PROMPT using LLM to merge 47 chunk analyses into complete report
Key Insight: Ultra-large-scale text analysis key lies in ‘divide-and-conquer + semantic merge’: technically control single LLM load through dynamic segmentation, cognitively guide LLM to extract cross-segment consistency rather than simple concatenation through merge prompt. 150K chars corresponds to approximately 15-20 medium-length papers, empirically optimal point
5. Task completion model training plateaued at loss~0.035 despite grad_norm=0.7-1.0 with 4% positive vs 96% negative samples Solution: Applied positive sample weighting (pos_weight=10) in BCE loss to balance gradient contributions, effectively raising positive sample ratio from 4% to ~30%.
Key Insight: Low loss doesn’t guarantee good positive sample recall in imbalanced datasets. Gradient magnitude alone is misleading when dominated by well-learned negative samples. Class imbalance requires explicit gradient balancing.

Key Insight: INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS and BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT serve different code paths—main LLM classification uses BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT. Keyword fallback is reliable LLM safety net. Past events must remain visible to prevent re-creation.

Verified with 373 passing tests.
Key Insight: Archive > delete for complete implementations. Preserving orphaned but working code in archive/ with context enables future reintegration while cleaning active tree. Audit revealed config drift and broken imports.

Changed schedule_essentials to get_today_events(include_past=True) so already-started meals remain visible.
Key Insight: Field parsing order matters critically—always prioritize ISO-format fields over display strings to avoid silent parse failures. Past events must remain visible to scheduler to prevent re-creation.

Gadget summarize finalize mechanism deadlock: historical log files with _finalized=False permanently exist, preventing report._finalized from ever becoming True, causing sync-all to repeatedly invoke LLM merge wasting API costs Solution: Root cause diagnosed: two-tier finalize (log + report) requires all source logs finalized before marking report finalized. Export sets _finalized=True only when (target_date != today() AND conversation_count unchanged). Historical logs stuck at False because: (a) only exported once when target_date == today(), leaving False; (b) conversation count changed after first export, writing False. _finalized flag embedded in JSON content, synced via rclone. Solution: re-run export on affected devices for these dates—since dates now past and conversation counts stable, will auto-mark True. Alternative: manually edit JSON _finalized field to true and rclone upload.
Key Insight: Two-tier finalize mechanism requires all sources finalized before marking report done; _finalized flag in JSON content synced via rclone ensures cross-device consistency; but historical False entries create permanent deadlock. Core value: save LLM API costs (merge stage), not rclone download time. Fix via ‘data repair’ (re-export to auto-flag) respects existing architecture better than ’logic change’ (removing all_sources_finalized check would break consistency).

Final merge step succeeded with ~660s timeout
Key Insight: Timeout design should be linearly correlated with data scale rather than fixed value: large model processing speed relatively stable (~200-300 chars/s), estimating time based on prompt length + 50% buffer is reliable strategy
14. LLM-generated researcher profile JSON long-text fields exhibit systematic unescaped quote issues causing JSON parsing failures (12+ errors) Solution: Identified and manually escaped special symbols in trajectory_summary, breakthroughs[].description and other fields (e.g., “让机器人…"→"让机器人…", single quotes in technical terms); for truncated JSON objects, semantically completed missing right brackets and array closing symbols based on context
Key Insight: LLM escaping of embedded quotes unstable when generating long-text JSON fields, especially in academic text with frequent term citations (e.g., “看图理解” to “边看边动”) triggering format errors. Solution requires: (1) explicitly require escaping special characters in prompt; (2) set length limits for ultra-long text fields or adopt multi-round segmented generation; (3) add JSON schema validation step to auto-repair common format errors after generation
15. LLM-generated long JSON outputs systematically fail with format errors: truncation (especially in final fields), unclosed quotes, unescaped Chinese quotation marks (”"), missing closing brackets in nested structures, particularly when containing technical descriptions, Chinese text, and deep nesting (>3 levels) Solution: Implemented four-stage repair pipeline: (1) direct json.loads attempt; (2) extract ```json code blocks; (3) depth-based brace matching to complete unclosed structures; (4) LLM repair with model escalation (haiku→sonnet→opus) for complex errors. Dedicated JSON repair prompt instructs AI to extract and fix JSON, returning only pure JSON without explanations. All failures logged to outputs/logs/json_repair_failed/ for pattern analysis and future optimization.
Key Insight: LLM long JSON generation exhibits systematic failure modes varying across sessions even with identical prompts (string escaping issues vs. truncation vs. nesting errors). Single repair strategy insufficient; requires layered fault tolerance. Chinese quotation marks ("") semantically valid but must be escaped as ASCII double quotes in JSON string values. Production systems need post-generation JSON validation + automatic repair retry.
16. For high-productivity researchers (130+ papers), single-pass analysis with full corpus causes prompt length errors or shallow analysis lacking technical depth. 206-paper analysis for Yuke Zhu failed with ‘Prompt is too long’ error Solution: Adopted year-stratified iterative analysis strategy: segment papers by publication year, analyze 1-3 representative papers per round with deep dive into breakthroughs (description, why_not_before, impact, technical_insight). Maintains analysis depth while controlling single-call complexity. Paper selection: year-based grouping + citation count ranking + conference award identification (Best Paper/Highlight/Spotlight/Oral via LLM recognition), max 10 papers per year.
Key Insight: Year-stratified analysis strategy superior to either full-corpus single-pass (prompt too long/analysis shallow) or random sampling (misses temporal evolution). Balances temporal dimension completeness with paper quality. ‘Few but deep’ iterative mode more effective than ‘many but shallow’ one-shot mode for academic profiling.

Key Insight: Flow matching denoising dominates cost, but unnecessary VLM forwards add measurable overhead. Unified method eliminates redundancy with minimal refactoring.

Requires LLM understanding of task causal relationships (e.g., ‘Implement Feature’ → ‘Fix Bug’ → ‘Verify Fix’ recognized as stages of same work thread) and thematic similarity.
Key Insight: Direct concatenation causes information redundancy. Synthesis requires identifying causal relationships between tasks (sequential stages vs. truly parallel) and thematic similarity (repeated debugging of same module should be one task with phases), not just string matching.

Launched resource-intensive Explore agent on empty directory without checking if exploration was needed, wasting time until user interrupted Failed to audit _finalized default value logic across export vs merge stages when adding –force flag; required user to spot semantic inconsistency Over-delegated codebase audit to 3 parallel agents despite task requiring holistic architectural judgment. User correctly recognized this would fragment understanding and stopped delegation. Failed to recognize data contamination risk: initially suggested generating scenes without train/test splits until user explicitly requested separate directories AI experienced 5 retries in Yuke Zhu analysis process, each iteration adjusting parameters (chunk size, timeout formula), but failed to predict optimal parameters through single analysis or reasoning, significantly prolonging total time (~2-3 hours) Cannot process researcher profiles with full publication history (200+ papers) due to prompt length constraints. 206-paper Yuke Zhu analysis failed with ‘Prompt is too long’ error. Lacks built-in sampling or hierarchical analysis strategies for large corpora. Initial inability to autonomously detect homonymous researchers from paper metadata alone. Required explicit user flagging to distinguish different researchers with same name. After first correction, improved to proactively flag institutional/domain mismatches. In daily report merging task, initially inclined to enumerate all details rather than proactively synthesize. Required user repeated emphasis of ‘focus on synthesis and distillation, not copying entries verbatim’ to trigger consolidation logic, indicating lack of intrinsic ‘readability’ and ‘information density’ balance awareness. When analyzing same researcher multiple times, failed to identify temporal evolution relationships across different year papers. Each analysis isolated without temporal causal inference dimension. In analyzing academic papers, tends toward ‘what was done’ and ‘what impact’ descriptions, but ‘why not feasible before’ historical dimension excavation requires explicit user prompting to deepen. Defaults to technical summary without historical insight. Initial inability to detect name conflicts in researcher analysis without explicit prompting, generating unified trajectory for papers from different researchers until user flagged domain inconsistency Initial renaming plan only covered display names/code references, missing infrastructure layers (conda env, folder, repo, systemd). Required human correction to expand scope. Rationalized performance inefficiency: accepted duplicate VLM forward passes as ‘acceptable overhead’ without optimization until user questioned redundancy Added Query Intent Classification to INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS (only used by multi_intent.py) instead of BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (used by main classification flow), not understanding code path differences In processing ultra-long text fields (e.g., 86-paper complete trajectory_summary), truncation risk exists causing incomplete JSON objects (field_impact and other fields truncated midway). Lacks proactive output length monitoring and warning mechanism. AI chose 60K chunk size initially (too conservative leading to 102 chunks), failed to recognize ‘reasonable chunk count’ implicit constraint in one attempt, needed timeout failure feedback before adjusting to 150K. Lacks prior reasoning about ‘user expects reasonable chunk count (10-50)’. Initially missed relative imports (from ..browser) when searching for module usage with ‘from src.browser’ pattern, falsely concluding browser/ was dead code. Only caught error after checking executor.py directly. Cannot autonomously capture user implicit intent. User’s multi-round analysis of same researcher with different year subsets actually tests tool’s paper selection robustness, but AI unaware of this validation purpose. AI batch-processed gadget/summarize tool causing 4-5 dates to fail due to API 32000 token output limit, but AI did not proactively detect output length limit or propose batch processing solution, passively accepting failure results Cannot proactively identify self-generated JSON format errors, requires human external validation (e.g., JSON parser) to discover problems then provide feedback Lacks global progress tracking for batch tasks—cannot proactively tell user ‘N more days of historical data need processing’ or current completion percentage. User must manually track task progress. Initially designed daily report tool as single-layer end-to-end generation, missing need for hierarchical aggregation (conversation→device summary→daily report) until user corrected with recursive architecture General Limitations Misunderstood domain terminology: ‘by title’ and ‘by abstract’ assumed to potentially mean LLM-based selection logic, while user actual meaning was ‘only summarize title’ vs ‘summarize abstract’. Needs explicit clarification Cannot effectively track processed date lists and pending tasks when handling large volumes of historical daily report data. Requires user-provided explicit task checklist and one-by-one confirmation mechanism. Initially only added terminal ERROR logs for calendar API failures instead of user-visible Discord message output. Needed user clarification to understand product requirement for in-chat error feedback. Learnings Key Learnings Batch correction methods like Harmony provide global distribution mixing but cannot preserve semantic alignment when independent training produces embeddings with misaligned dimension meanings. This requires shared training (Joint STAIG) or foundation models. Batch mixing and semantic alignment are orthogonal properties. MimicGen-style augmentation is fundamentally about coordinate transformation, not noise injection. pos_delta (source→target object offset) must be applied to action trajectories. Without this, 10→1000 augmentation collapses due to <5% success rate. Ultra-large-scale text analysis engineering paradigm: ①automatic segmentation (150K chars ~15-20 papers optimal granularity) ②semantic merge (LLM-driven merge not concatenation) ③dynamic timeout (linearly scaled based on prompt length, 300s baseline+120s/50K chars) ④caching mechanism (avoid retry cost). All four essential for deep-wide mode usability Academic trajectory analysis multi-angle validation method: Through iterative analysis of same researcher’s different paper subsets (from 1 paper to 100 papers), can build stereoscopic cognition from micro (single representative work deep analysis) to macro (complete publication list trajectory characterization). Yuke Zhu case reveals: visual understanding (Visual Genome) → embodied intelligence (AI2-THOR) → robotics learning ecosystem building (robosuite/RoboTurk) → LLM-driven embodied intelligence (MineDojo/Voyager) → geometric intermediate representations + VLM alignment clear evolution trajectory, only fully presentable with complete paper list Yuke Zhu’s research trajectory exhibits clear ‘perception→manipulation→infrastructure→open world’ evolution: from early 2012 visual RL to 2026 DreamDojo world models, consistently centered on ’enabling robots to efficiently learn from data and generalize to real world’ core proposition. Represents ‘data infrastructure builder’ → ‘foundation model pioneer’ → ‘world model architect’ progression. Single-intent classification is architectural constraint that cannot be fixed with keyword hacks. CalendarPro’s 7-layer keyword override system was treating symptoms of broken abstraction. Multi-intent LLM analysis eliminates need for all heuristics. Class imbalance in binary classification requires explicit gradient balancing. Low overall loss can mask poor minority class learning when 96% of samples are one class. pos_weight effectively rebalances gradient contributions. Analysis mode design key dimensions: ①data scale (papers/year) ②analysis depth (abstract vs fulltext) ③computational cost (LLM invocation count). Five-mode system through two boolean dimensions + one numeric dimension combination, covers complete need spectrum from ‘quick overview→deep excavation’ Structured data generation prompt engineering essentials: For fixed schema JSON output, need to explicitly declare in prompt all required fields, their types (string/array/object), length limits, default values (placeholder text when no data), and special character escaping rules. gadget summarize tool’s daily_overview layered format evolution proves: relying only on example inference cannot guarantee output consistency, must use enumeration-style specification to clarify generation logic for each field Robotics learning field research infrastructure building pathway: Yuke Zhu’s academic trajectory reveals important pattern—field breakthroughs often accompanied by infrastructure-type work (AI2-THOR simulation environment, robosuite standard benchmark, RoboTurk crowdsourcing platform, MineDojo internet-scale dataset), these works’ citation counts though not exceeding algorithm innovation papers, but actual impact on overall field advancement may be greater. For any emerging research direction, prioritizing establishment of reproducible evaluation benchmarks and data collection toolchains has more strategic value than publishing single algorithm papers Two-tier finalize mechanism (log + report) requires all source logs finalized before marking report done; _finalized flag in JSON content synced via rclone ensures cross-device consistency; but historical False entries create permanent deadlock. Core value: save LLM API costs (merge stage), not rclone download time. Fix path: re-execute idempotent operation (export) to auto-correct historical metadata, respecting architectural design. Batch iterative workflow (process daily reports date-by-date, academic analysis year-by-year) more reliable than one-shot bulk processing, effectively avoiding JSON truncation and analysis depth insufficiency. Critical for gadget tools to add auto-retry mechanism with JSON validation. Academic database homonym disambiguation problem high-frequency and high-impact data quality issue in automated researcher profiling. Must establish homonym detection module through multi-dimensional signals: co-author clustering, topic clustering, temporal continuity, institutional affiliation consistency. Train/eval data separation is non-negotiable in ML pipelines. Evaluation set must never leak into training. Different data purposes require different generation quotas and strategies. Archive > delete for complete, tested implementations even if orphaned. archive/ pattern with explanation README preserves optionality (future reintegration) while cleaning active tree. Default values in data processing pipelines must match stage semantics: export (missing=incomplete→False) vs merge (missing=stable→True). Subtle inconsistencies cause silent bugs. DateTime field parsing order matters critically—always prioritize ISO-format fields (start_iso) over display-format strings (start_time ‘08:00’) to avoid silent parse failures that break existence checks. Gadget project’s daily report generation tool demonstrates strong information extraction and structuring capability in complex multi-device, multi-project, cross-temporal scenarios. Can accurately distinguish cross-device parallel work, identify task causal relationships, synthesize conversation_summaries, validating production readiness. Research profiler consistently identified Yuke Zhu’s core research directions and methodological evolution from different year paper subsets, proving tool’s academic trajectory extraction capability. Voyager (2023) demonstrated LLM-as-autonomous-agent paradigm: 3.3x more unique items, 15.3x faster tech tree unlocking in Minecraft. Skills stored as executable JS code rather than neural weights, avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Open X-Embodiment (2023): 22 robots, 21 institutions, 160K tasks demonstrated positive transfer across embodiments, establishing ImageNet-moment for robotics data consolidation. Researcher profile information density tiers: Tier 1 = h-index/citation count (quantitative metrics), Tier 2 = representative works list (enumerable facts), Tier 3 = research trajectory narrative (needs LLM to extract implicit evolution logic). Three tiers correspond to fast/normal/deep mode output complexity respectively LLM long-text JSON output fault tolerance requires layered mechanism: direct parsing→code block extraction→brace matching→LLM repair (model escalation). Single strategy cannot cover all failure modes. All failures should be logged for manual review and subsequent optimization. Breakthrough paper characteristic analysis framework (why_not_before + impact + technical_insight) effectively reveals technological innovation’s historical inevitability, domain influence, and core insights, more valuable than simple abstract summaries. Researcher analysis paper selection strategy should balance temporal completeness and quality. Year-based grouping + citation count ranking + conference award identification (via LLM) three-layer mechanism can balance foundational early work and recent frontier breakthroughs at controllable computational cost. LLM-generated JSON systematic error pattern recognition: Through 12+ JSON repair tasks discovered, unescaped quote errors mainly concentrate in: (1) academic term citations (e.g., “看图理解”); (2) Chinese and Western quotation mark mixing; (3) special symbols in technical nouns (e.g., + in C++, mathematical symbols like σ_w²). Solution requires multi-layer protection: prompt explicitly requires escaping rules + output schema validation + regex auto-repair common patterns Year-stratified analysis strategy superior to either full-corpus single-pass (prompt too long/analysis shallow) or random sampling (misses temporal evolution). Balances temporal dimension completeness with paper quality. ‘Few but deep’ iterative mode more effective than ‘many but shallow’ one-shot mode for academic profiling. When implementing recurring event schedulers, must include already-started events in existence checks (include_past=True), otherwise past-time events become invisible and get re-created every cycle. In multi-component systems, understand where prompts are actually used. INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS and BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT serve different code paths—main LLM classification uses BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, multi_intent.py uses INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS. Historical daily report backfill workload substantial but value significant: 30+ days historical records covering multiple projects across 4 devices, involving dozens of technical decisions and hundreds of task entries. Establishing complete work record system foundational for subsequent monthly report generation and project retrospectives. Code refactoring backward compatibility strategy: default value from fast→normal, but from_dict still fallback to fast (protecting old profile data); choices list expansion doesn’t break old config files; re-export shim enables dependent parties to migrate without awareness. Embodies ‘progressive evolution’ superior to ‘destructive rewrite’ Long-running task development experience optimization: ①caching mechanism makes retry cost controllable (47 chunks fully cached, only need to re-run merge) ②progress observability (tqdm+PYTHONUNBUFFERED) ③timeout formula self-adaptive (avoid manual parameter tuning) ④parallel Agent handling independent subtasks (docs update) gadget/research toolkit consists of three independent tools (paper discovery, researcher profiling, citation graph analysis), unified under research_scout.py CLI. Researcher profiling uses citation count + award weighting for paper selection, not LLM scoring When refactoring mode system, preserve existing sorting logic and add new dimensions (quantity, processing depth) as independent parameters. This minimizes risk and keeps behavior predictable Systematic import analysis (grep for patterns + verify init.py exports) essential before declaring modules ‘dead’. Relative imports (..module) require separate search patterns from absolute imports (src.module). Keyword fallback mechanism is reliable LLM safety net—even if LLM fails to return structured data, detecting keywords in original input enables correct routing. Project renaming requires two-layer approach: (1) code/docs (automatable via search-replace), (2) infrastructure (manual: conda, git, hosting, services). Checklist both layers upfront to avoid partial migrations. Daily report synthesis ‘distillation’ requires LLM understanding task causal and containment relationships, recognizing ‘Implement Feature’→‘Fix Bug’→‘Verify Fix’ as stages of same work thread not three independent tasks. This semantic relationship understanding capability key to report readability. pip install -e . (editable mode) is correct way to make shared utility packages importable in multi-tool projects rather than PYTHONPATH manipulation. Hot reload in Python is nearly impossible for stateful systems (Discord bots with event loops, singleton caches, background schedulers). Process-level restart via watchfiles is only practical solution. Practical Learnings robosuite provides official utilities (input2action, input_utils) that handle device→action conversion correctly. Manual parsing of action_dict loses coordinate transforms and controller scaling. Test infrastructure hardening (pytest-timeout, @pytest.mark.external, skip logic) prevents one category of flaky tests from blocking entire suite. Pattern is reusable across projects. Using max_per_year=0 as ‘unlimited papers’ sentinel value clearer than boolean flag or None, because zero never valid use case for paper limit Git rebase workflow (stash → pull –rebase → stash pop) cleanly integrates diverged branches with independent changes, avoiding merge commit clutter. title: Bug Journal 2026-03-19

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-18 Daily Overview What was done: Extended CalendarPro’s intent classification system with a new BATCH_UPDATE intent to handle multi-task status reports from users How it was done: Implemented semantic routing with 21 utterances, keyword scoring with completion verb detection, LLM prompt fragments, and a calendar-integrated handler across 8 files Impact: Resolved a critical UX gap where users couldn’t efficiently report status on multiple tasks at once, eliminating ‘I don’t understand’ fallback responses for batch updates Added batch update intent to CalendarPro for handling multi-task status reports, with full test coverage and documentation updates
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Implement BATCH_UPDATE intent feature — Added new intent type across 8 files: enum definition, semantic routes (21 utterances), keyword scorer with 2+ completion verb boost, LLM prompt fragment with updates array schema, context assembler mapping, dual verify default reply, discord_bot handler with per-task calendar operations, and improved GENERAL fallback ✅ Diagnose batch update classification failure — Launched 3 parallel exploration agents to understand intent routing system (24 types), task completion handling, and general intent protection. Identified root cause: no BATCH_UPDATE intent exists, semantic router scores ~0.20 vs 0.50 threshold, LLM classifier defaults to GENERAL with clarification type that triggers hardcoded ‘I don’t understand’ template ✅ Create implementation plan for batch update feature — Designed comprehensive 8-step implementation plan covering IntentType enum, semantic routes, keyword patterns, LLM prompts, context assembly, dual verify defaults, discord_bot handler with calendar integration, GENERAL fallback improvements, route JSON regeneration, and test suite Implementation & Fixes ✅ Write comprehensive test suite for BATCH_UPDATE — Created 21 tests covering keyword scoring, enum, handler (complete/cancel/reschedule/note/multi/empty/permission), route registration, context map, prompt fragment, and dual verify default reply. All tests passed with no regressions in 72-test suite ✅ Update CLAUDE.md documentation — Rewrote CLAUDE.md to focus on non-obvious architecture: removed redundant file listings, added ‘Common Multi-File Changes’ section with step-by-step guides for adding AI providers/intents/services/events, documented singleton test isolation, consolidated architecture patterns Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Bot fails to classify multi-task status updates (e.g., ‘A完成了，B也解决了，C需要改时间’), falling back to ‘I don’t understand’ despite substantive user input Solution: Added BATCH_UPDATE intent with semantic route (21 utterances), keyword scorer boost for 2+ completion verbs, LLM prompt teaching updates array schema, and handler that searches calendar, deletes completed tasks, reschedules/notes others, logs completions, and emits EventBus events. Also fixed GENERAL fallback to use substantive LLM replies instead of discarding them
Key Insight: Intent classification failures often stem from three-layer gaps: (1) no enum member, (2) no semantic route examples, (3) no LLM prompt fragment. Fixing all three layers plus keyword scoring creates robust classification. GENERAL fallback should preserve useful LLM responses rather than blindly templating.
2. Semantic router scores batch updates at ~0.20 vs 0.50 threshold, causing LOW_CONFIDENCE classification Solution: Created BATCH_UPDATE_ROUTE with diverse Chinese/English utterances (‘A完成了，B也搞定了’, ’tasks A and B completed, C needs rescheduling’) and added keyword scorer rule: 2+ distinct completion keywords → +0.30 boost, capturing the defining characteristic of batch updates
Key Insight: Embedding-based semantic routing misses multi-entity status patterns. Explicit keyword counting (2+ completion verbs) is a simple but effective heuristic for batch detection that complements embedding similarity.
3. LLM classifier has no batch_update in allowed intent list, defaults to GENERAL with clarification type, which triggers hardcoded ‘I don’t understand’ template that discards useful AI-generated replies Solution: Added batch_update to INTENT_PROMPT_FRAGMENTS with updates array schema (task_name, action, note, new_time) and to allowed intent list in build_prompt(). Improved GENERAL handler to check if clarification-type replies have substantive LLM content (>20 chars, not template phrase) and use it instead of hardcoded template
Key Insight: Fallback templates should be last resort, not default. When LLM generates substantive replies, preserve them even if confidence is low. Template overrides waste the LLM’s reasoning and create worse UX.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Diagnostic strategy for batch update failure Role Approach Human User showed real Discord conversation failure (‘你好 → bot replies with task summary → user gives batch status → bot says I don’t understand’) and asked ‘how should we solve this?’, providing the concrete symptom without prescribing the diagnostic method AI Claude launched 3 parallel exploration agents to systematically understand: (1) all 24 intent types and routing, (2) task completion handling, (3) general intent protection feature. Then read critical files to verify details, used Plan agent to synthesize findings into implementation plan Difference Analysis: Human provided the ‘what’ (symptom) and ‘why we care’ (UX problem), but not the ‘how to investigate’. AI chose parallel agent-based exploration rather than sequential file reading, showing strategic use of subagents for broad discovery. Human likely would have done more linear ‘read this file, then that file’ approach.
Implementation approach for BATCH_UPDATE feature Role Approach Human User provided a fully structured 8-step implementation plan with exact file paths, line numbers, code snippets, data schemas, and test requirements before asking Claude to execute AI Claude followed the plan precisely, reading files in parallel, making edits sequentially where dependencies existed, regenerating derived data (route JSON), and writing comprehensive tests Difference Analysis: Human did upfront architectural design and specified exact changes; AI executed the plan as a reliable implementer. This shows human taking ‘architect’ role while AI takes ‘builder’ role, which is efficient for complex multi-file changes where the human has already done the systems thinking.
AI Limitations General Limitations In test_batch_update.py, Claude initially tried to import DiscordBot class which caused import errors, then pivoted to testing the handler function in isolation. Could have checked import structure first or used better mocking patterns When first attempting to run full test suite, Claude used pytest tests/ -v --timeout=30 -x which failed because pytest-timeout plugin wasn’t installed. Fell back to running subset of tests instead of installing the plugin or removing the flag initially Learnings Key Learnings Multi-layered intent classification requires coordinated updates across 8+ files: enum (models.py), semantic routes (intent_routes.py), keyword scorer (keyword_scorer.py), LLM prompts (prompts.py), context assembly (context_assembler.py), dual verify defaults (dual_verify.py), handler + routing (discord_bot.py), plus derived data (route JSON). Missing any layer causes classification failure Parallel agent exploration (3 agents for intent routing, task handling, general protection) is more efficient than sequential file reading for complex diagnostics. Each agent provides focused perspective that synthesizes into complete understanding Fallback templates in AI systems should preserve useful LLM-generated content rather than blindly overwriting it. Check if LLM reply is substantive (>20 chars, not template phrase) before replacing with hardcoded fallback Keyword scoring can capture patterns that embedding similarity misses: 2+ distinct completion verbs is a simple heuristic for batch updates that complements semantic routing. Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ QCVLA project documentation creation and improvement planning — Created initial CLAUDE.md via /init covering 7-step pipeline, SingleStepDiT architecture, and critical gotchas. Generated improvement_analysis.md with 11 proposals from FLARE + 9 papers. Documented perturbation & bridging data augmentation strategy. Identified some D0 samples insufficient (<10) requiring replenishment, threading task only injection collision_empty due to all phase_labels being pre_reach 🔄 Error benchmark D0 sample replenishment — Some error types at D0 degree have sample count < 10 (e.g., collision_self: 2, drop_at_wrong_place: 8), need to rerun pipeline to supplement; threading task needs analysis of why only collision_empty can be injected ✅ CALVIN dataset conversion script optimization — Corrected RLDS-to-LeRobot conversion script dataset name (calvin_abc vs calvin_abc_d), key mappings (rgb_static vs image), removed non-existent fields, added progress bars and overwrite confirmation logic ✅ LIBERO custom test suite integration — Added libero_object_com suite to LIBERO benchmark framework, modified task_map, registered Benchmark class, created BDDL files, updated client main.py Implementation & Fixes ✅ GPU monitoring tool duplicate process fix and interactive navigation — Fixed gpumon.py showing 35 duplicate processes (reduced to 8) by implementing ENV+FD verification and parent chain deduplication. Added nvitop-like interactive features: arrow key navigation, command scrolling, visual highlighting for selected row ✅ RoboCasa MimicGen dataset download failure diagnosis — Traced ‘No dataset for this task and dataset type exists!’ error through download_datasets.py → dataset_registry_utils.py → box_links_ds.json, confirmed 0 MimicGen entries exist (upstream data publishing issue) ✅ Remote server environment configuration (athena.egr.duke.edu) — Configured SSH key authentication (user manually ran ssh-copy-id after initial failure), automated installation of fnm + Node.js 22, installed Claude Code 2.1.77 and Codex CLI 0.115.0, transferred qcvla_bridge_pipeline project (51 files, 3.1MB) via rsync. Server ready for distributed development. ✅ Git proxy configuration fix — Diagnosed git fetch network error, tested multiple proxies to find localhost:9999 works, updated local git config to override unavailable global proxy ✅ wandb account configuration — Provided 4 solutions for directory-level wandb account configuration, recommended WANDB_API_KEY environment variable or direnv approach Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. QCVLA: DAgger Round 2 only improved by +1pp (60%→61% SR), indicating saturation. Bridge only sees its own naturally-produced error distribution, which is limited in diversity Solution: Proposed perturbation & bridging data augmentation: during DAgger rollout, randomly inject short action sequences followed by reverse recovery actions. Captures coherent large-magnitude deviations bridge would never naturally produce, expanding training distribution coverage. Trains both bridge (feature prediction on perturbed states) and action head (recovery action sequences).
Key Insight: Self-supervised training saturates when model only sees its own error modes. Injecting synthetic but realistic deviations (inspired by FLARE’s perturbation strategy) expands the distribution. Coherent action perturbations are more effective than per-frame Gaussian noise for robotic manipulation.
2. VLA inference: task completed but infinite loop sending done messages because current_prompt was not reset, causing chunk_count to remain non-zero and model to continuously output high scores Solution: Set current_prompt = "" after task completion and call _publish_state(“idle”) to prevent next round from triggering immediately; moved None check before task_completed.item() to avoid crashes on non-pi05 models
Key Insight: State machines require explicit reset of all related variables at each termination node, otherwise unpredictable loops occur; multi-device compatibility (pi05 vs non-pi05) needs early boundary condition handling
3. MIHD: NEEDS_COORDS_FUSIONS tuple was duplicated in pipeline/runner.py and pipeline/evaluation_planner.py, with adaln_attention missing from both (latent bug), making it hard to maintain consistency when adding new fusion strategies Solution: Centralized NEEDS_COORDS_FUSIONS as a constant in models/Fusion.py, imported by both files. Added missing adaln_attention to the tuple, fixing a bug where this fusion strategy would fail to receive spatial coordinates.
Key Insight: Duplicate constants across modules lead to inconsistency and missed updates. Single source of truth prevents latent bugs and simplifies maintenance.
4. MIHD: refine_labels_spatial_majority in utils/clustering.py used scipy.spatial.distance.cdist with O(N²) memory complexity, causing OOM on Visium HD data with 17K+ spots Solution: Replaced cdist with scipy.spatial.cKDTree.query which has O(N*k) complexity for k-nearest neighbor search. Changed from computing full distance matrix to on-demand radius neighbor queries.
Key Insight: Spatial queries on large point clouds require tree-based structures (KDTree, BallTree) to avoid quadratic memory explosion. For HD spatial data (10K+ points), algorithmic choice matters more than implementation details.
5. Training combined action_loss and task_loss into single value logged to wandb, unable to monitor each separately Solution: Modified compute_loss to return (combined_loss, {“action_loss”: …, “task_loss”: …}) tuple, training loop uses nnx.value_and_grad(…, has_aux=True) to unpack auxiliary metrics and add to info dict
Key Insight: JAX/Flax’s has_aux=True mechanism elegantly returns additional monitoring metrics from loss function without affecting gradient computation; requires synchronizing all compute_loss implementations (pi0 and pi0_fast) to maintain interface consistency
6. Error benchmark threading task can only inject collision_empty, other error types cannot be generated Solution: Analysis found all clean trajectory phase_labels for threading are ‘pre_reach’, lacking grasp/lift/transport phases, causing errors dependent on these phases (like drop_in_transit) to have no injection opportunities; need to check get_task_phase logic or threading task definition
Key Insight: Error injection depends on task phase segmentation; incomplete phase recognition causes some error types to be uncoverable; need to verify all tasks cover expected phases during opportunity map generation
7. gpumon.py counted bash/ffmpeg/claude processes with inherited CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES as GPU processes, and showed DDP worker processes separately instead of grouping with parent Solution: Modified _get_proc_gpus() to require both CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES env var AND open /dev/nvidia* file descriptors; added parent chain traversal in get_gpu_procs() to collapse child processes with identical GPU sets to their ancestor
Key Insight: Process GPU usage detection requires both environment variable inheritance check and actual device file descriptor verification to avoid false positives
8. All 317 RoboCasa tasks failed to download MimicGen data with error messages, unclear if code bug or data availability issue Solution: Systematic analysis revealed: 257 tasks have no mg_path registration (yellow warnings), 60 tasks have mg_path but box_links_ds.json contains 0 MimicGen download URLs (red errors). Confirmed this is upstream data publishing issue, not code defect.
Key Insight: When download failures are systematic across all items, investigate data availability before attempting code fixes. box_links_ds.json grep for ‘/mg/’ returned zero matches, conclusively proving missing download links
9. CALVIN RLDS dataset conversion failed with KeyError: ‘image’, actual field names are ‘rgb_static’ and ‘rgb_gripper’ Solution: Read features.json to confirm actual schema, modified frame extraction key names, removed non-existent environment_state and relative_action field definitions from dataset
Key Insight: Dataset format conversion must verify source data schema before assuming field names; RLDS features.json is authoritative source for determining actual field names
10. How to implement interactive keyboard navigation in a monitoring tool that needs to refresh periodically without blocking on input Solution: Used select.select() with 0 timeout for non-blocking keyboard input detection, termios/tty for raw mode terminal control, stored selected_idx and scroll_offset state across renders, applied reverse video (\033[7m) for highlighting
Key Insight: Non-blocking I/O with select() enables real-time interaction in monitoring tools while maintaining refresh intervals. Terminal raw mode requires careful state management to capture arrow keys without echo
General Issues 11. git fetch reported Could not resolve host: github.com, global configured proxy 172.16.31.200:3138 unavailable Solution: Used curl to test multiple proxy ports, found localhost:9999 returns 200; updated git local config http.proxy and https.proxy to available proxy, overriding global config
