Daily Report — 2026-03-15 Daily Overview What was done: Executed full-stack CalendarPro optimization (semantic routing, hybrid classification, system prompt splitting, provider retry, scheduling scoring, learning loop, caching), major gadget toolkit refactoring (common/ package extraction, output directory consolidation, research tools unification), and comprehensive academic landscape mapping for robotics/embodied AI field How it was done: Deployed 5 parallel agents for CalendarPro implementation, created pip-installable common/ package with modular architecture and re-export shims, implemented homepage-scraping-based student discovery with LLM extraction, built three-stage evaluation pipeline with citation impact analysis, and leveraged ArXiv/Semantic Scholar APIs for batch researcher profiling Impact: CalendarPro’s intent understanding accuracy and task execution reliability significantly improved; eliminated sys.path hacks and code duplication across four gadget tools; created production-ready unified research workflow enabling rapid domain understanding; successfully mapped advisor relationships and research trajectories for 13+ robotics leaders including Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn, Pieter Abbeel, Yuke Zhu, Yunzhu Li, Mingyu Ding, Ruoshi Liu, Xiaolong Wang, and Shuran Song Completed comprehensive CalendarPro optimization with 7-phase parallel implementation (230 tests passed), unified gadget research toolkit integrating paper discovery/profiler/citations into single CLI, extracted shared utilities into common/ package eliminating 400+ lines of duplication, consolidated all output directories into structured outputs/ hierarchy, and profiled 13+ leading robotics/AI researchers establishing systematic academic research tracking
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ CalendarPro full optimization implementation (7 phases) — Implemented semantic routing thresholds, hybrid keyword+embedding routing, system prompt splitting (530 lines → base + 11 fragments), provider retry logic with exponential backoff, scheduling scoring system, auto-learning loop from mismatches, and ThoughtStore caching. All 230 tests passed using 5 parallel agents. ✅ Unify Research Scout + Profiler + Citation Graph tools — Integrated three independent research tools into single CLI: research_scout.py now includes paper discovery, researcher profiling via ‘profile’ subcommand, citation graph analysis via ‘citations’ subcommand, three-stage evaluation pipeline with citation impact analysis, and multi-backend LLM support (claude_cli/anthropic/openai). Deleted duplicate ‘New feature/’ directory. ✅ Extract shared utilities into common/ package — Created pip-installable common/ package with 6 modules (io, cache, json_utils, llm, hugo, paths) eliminating 400+ lines of duplicated code, converted summarize/llm_backends.py and research/cache.py to re-export shims, eliminated sys.path hacks, updated pyproject.toml and all documentation ✅ Consolidate output directories into unified outputs/ structure — Migrated all tool-specific output paths into unified outputs/ hierarchy organized by type (reports/, logs/, cache/, data/, site/), created centralized path constants in common/paths.py, updated all imports and documentation ✅ Robotics research tracking and comprehensive researcher profiling — Created robotics-leaders project, profiled 13+ researchers (Sergey Levine h-index 166, Pieter Abbeel h-index 164, Chelsea Finn, Yuke Zhu, Yunzhu Li, Mingyu Ding, Ruoshi Liu, Xiaolong Wang, Shuran Song), identified PhD advisors, generated detailed trajectory reports with breakthrough papers and research themes, discovered Open X-Embodiment, MineDojo (NeurIPS 2022 Best Paper), Value Iteration Networks (NeurIPS 2016 Best Paper) ✅ Implement homepage-based student discovery — Added source/status fields to StudentCandidate model, created research/homepage_discovery.py with HTMLParser-based text extraction and LLM student name extraction, restructured discover_students() to use homepage-first + co-authorship supplement strategy with polite rate limiting (1 req/2s) ✅ Update comprehensive documentation (CLAUDE.md, TUTORIAL.md, README.md) — Rewrote root CLAUDE.md with MCP server docs and sub-project references, updated summarize/CLAUDE.md for new import structure, rewrote research/CLAUDE.md covering profiler architecture and unified CLI, completely rewrote Chinese TUTORIAL.md from 10 to 13 chapters adding multi-source search/profiler/citations sections and 4 new workflow examples, updated README.md with missing tools Implementation & Fixes ✅ Deploy researcher profiles to separate Hugo section — Created website/content/research/ section for researcher profiles (separate from bugJournal temporal reports), added deploy_to_hugo() function in research/output.py, updated config.yml with research menu item, added –deploy and –hugo-site CLI flags ✅ CLAUDE.md analysis and similar projects research — Analyzed CalendarPro CLAUDE.md (comprehensive, no changes needed), researched similar open-source projects (FluidCalendar, CoPaw, Khoj, OpenDAN, Cal.com, Leon, Rasa, Home Assistant), concluded CalendarPro’s energy-aware scheduling + three-tier architecture + dual verification combination is unique ✅ Fix mcp_server.py import error — Fixed function name mismatch: globally replaced _load_known_arxiv_ids with _load_known_paper_ids in 4 locations across import statements and call sites Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Co-authorship analysis returned 0 students for all tested professors (Sergey Levine, Pieter Abbeel, Chelsea Finn) despite correct implementation Solution: Human recognized faculty homepages explicitly list students; implemented homepage-first discovery with LLM extraction of student names from faculty pages, using co-authorship data only as supplementary enrichment with source tracking for transparency
Key Insight: Faculty homepages are the authoritative source for student lists and more reliable than inferring relationships from co-authorship patterns. When heuristic algorithms fail due to data sparsity, switch to direct information sources (professor webpages) rather than debugging scoring algorithms. Ground truth beats inference.
2. Semantic Scholar matched wrong researchers for 6+ names due to name ambiguity (Ming Yu→explosives chemist, Xiaolong Wang→veterinary scientist/geologist/NLP researcher, 5 out of 6 initial queries failed) Solution: Human provided full name clarification (Mingyu Ding); relied on ArXiv paper matching which was more accurate; AI correctly identified data quality issues by recognizing incompatible research domains, returned explicit warnings rather than generating false trajectories; recommended ORCID+institution verification for common Chinese names
Key Insight: Common Chinese names create severe disambiguation problems in academic databases requiring mandatory institution/ORCID matching. Same-name aggregation is a critical data quality issue - need field-based clustering or institution filtering before analysis. Multi-source data integration (homepage + ArXiv + S2) with explicit source tracking provides robustness against individual failures. Better to return ‘data unusable’ than propagate false profiles.
3. Output files scattered across tool-specific subdirectories (summarize/logs/, research/cache/, test/benchmark_results.csv) with hardcoded Path(file).parent patterns created tight coupling and difficult disk space management Solution: Designed unified outputs/ structure organized by type (reports/, logs/, cache/, data/) then by tool, introduced canonical path constants in common/paths.py, replaced all hardcoded paths atomically, updated environment variable fallbacks
Key Insight: Type-first organization (reports/, logs/, cache/) is more maintainable than tool-first when multiple tools share similar output patterns. Centralized path management enables atomic refactoring - changing one constant propagates everywhere without breaking code. Phased execution with verification checkpoints prevents cascading failures.
4. Two overlapping research tools in same directory (monolithic research_scout.py + modular profiler package) causing code duplication, unclear single entry point, and undocumented features. Initial /init attempt interrupted by user suggesting AI was heading toward documentation improvements rather than architectural changes. Solution: User provided explicit 9-step integration plan with precise function signatures, line counts, and architectural decisions. AI executed plan: kept research_scout.py as stable CLI entry point, refactored modular package as importable library, added profile/citations subcommands, implemented three-stage evaluation with citation analysis, added multi-backend LLM support
Key Insight: For complex architectural changes, detailed written plans prevent scope creep and ensure AI stays on track. Hybrid integration (preserving stable CLI while refactoring internals) reduces migration risk vs full rewrites. Human architectural vision + AI tactical execution works better than letting AI improvise. Gradual migration is safer than big-bang changes.
5. Major new modular tool (researcher profiler with ~15 Python modules) completely undocumented in CLAUDE.md causing confusion about codebase capabilities; AI initially missed ‘New feature’ directory entirely Solution: Used Agent exploration to thoroughly map package structure, then rewrote CLAUDE.md to document both tools with separate sections for architecture, usage, and configuration
Key Insight: Documentation rot happens rapidly when new features are added without updating guidance files; requires proactive documentation maintenance or automated detection of undocumented code paths. Update CLAUDE.md immediately after structural changes to prevent drift.
6. JSON parsing failed for Yuke Zhu trajectory analysis after three-tier LLM repair attempts (haiku → sonnet → opus), resulting in incomplete reports Solution: Accepted partial results (paper list without trajectory analysis) and documented the failure; analysis completed with degraded output quality
Key Insight: LLM repair escalation has limits; when all three model tiers fail, underlying issue may be prompt/context rather than model capability. Persistent failures indicate need to revisit input structure or question decomposition.
7. arXiv search returned 0 results for robotics leaders despite using correct author names due to sorting/recency issues in search API Solution: Switched from arXiv search API to Researcher Profiler which uses both arXiv and Semantic Scholar data sources for more robust multi-source fetching
Key Insight: API search behavior is not always intuitive; multi-source data fetching is more robust than single-API queries. Don’t debug API quirks when better data sources exist.
General Issues 8. Researcher profile reports initially deployed to bugJournal section mixing profiles with daily scout reports; lack of semantic content separation Solution: Human pointed out profiles should go to separate research/ folder; created new website/content/research/ section with dedicated menu item and _index.md; updated deploy_to_hugo() to target new section
Key Insight: Different content types benefit from separate Hugo sections for better organization and navigation; researcher profiles are reference material while bugJournal is temporal reporting. Semantic taxonomy matters for content discoverability.
9. Research profiler failed with ‘No module named research’ when running research_scout.py directly Solution: Changed execution method from ‘python research/research_scout.py profile’ to ‘python -m research analyze’ to properly respect package structure
Key Insight: Complex Python packages need correct entry points; using -m flag ensures proper module resolution for packages with internal imports
10. pip install -e . failed with Windows file lock on gadget-mcp.exe during package reinstallation Solution: Verified that common/ package imports work directly from sys.path since editable install already has package root available; skipped reinstall and proceeded
Key Insight: Editable installs add project root to sys.path, so new packages are immediately importable without reinstalling when executable is locked
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Student discovery methodology Role Approach Human Recognized that faculty homepages explicitly list students and proposed homepage scraping as primary method after co-authorship analysis failed, applying domain knowledge that professors maintain authoritative student rosters AI Initially implemented only co-authorship analysis based on Semantic Scholar data with 4-dimensional scoring (first-author 40%, time concentration 25%, collaboration frequency 20%, recency 15%); would have continued debugging scoring algorithm rather than switching approaches Difference Analysis: Human directly identified the most reliable information source based on real-world knowledge of academic practices, while AI relied on quantitative signals from publication metadata. Human knew where ground truth lives; AI defaulted to available data APIs and statistical inference. This highlights human advantage in knowing authoritative sources vs AI’s strength in processing structured data patterns.
CalendarPro root cause diagnosis Role Approach Human User described high-level symptoms (‘overall experience poor’, ‘intent understanding inaccurate’, ’task completion unreliable’) and specified using Claude Local CLI (strong model), wanting ‘comprehensive improvement’ AI Immediately performed structured root cause analysis decomposing system-level issues into 7 specific technical problems across intent classification layer (no confidence threshold, LLM timeout, no learning) and task execution layer (no provider retry, crude token estimation, incomplete agent implementation) Difference Analysis: User provided symptoms and context; AI systematically debugged complex system to identify actionable technical problems. AI demonstrated strength in systematic debugging where humans see overall dysfunction, recognizing the problem is not in the model but in pipeline design.
Architectural integration strategy Role Approach Human User specified ‘Keep research_scout.py as unified entry point. Import from modular package as library code.’ Preserves monolithic entry while leveraging modular code. Provided detailed 9-step plan with specific file paths and line counts. AI Initially attempted to improve existing CLAUDE.md documentation without proposing architectural changes. Only after receiving explicit integration plan did AI execute unification. Would have focused on incremental documentation improvements. Difference Analysis: Human saw strategic value of unified interface for better UX and provided prescriptive specification. AI focused on incremental improvements and needed architectural guidance for cross-cutting changes. Human provided ‘what’, AI provided ‘how’.
Citation scoring approach for paper evaluation Role Approach Human Specified citation count should be used for sorting/tiebreaking only, not influence composite relevance score; recognized popularity is orthogonal to project relevance AI Initially proposed making citation count part of composite evaluation score, conflating ‘important paper’ with ‘relevant to project’ Difference Analysis: Human recognized highly-cited papers may not match project focus; AI defaulted to treating citation count as quality signal rather than discovery hint. Reveals AI’s tendency to optimize for global importance rather than context-specific relevance.
Researcher trajectory analysis depth Role Approach Human Provided raw paper lists with basic metadata (title, year, citations) and requested high-level trajectory analysis AI Synthesized comprehensive multi-paragraph narratives covering phase transitions, breakthrough papers with ‘why not before’ reasoning explaining historical context, research themes, and methodology evolution Difference Analysis: Human requested analysis at high level; AI generated multi-dimensional synthesis including causal reasoning about why breakthroughs happened when they did. AI went beyond pattern recognition to historical contextualization.
Researcher name disambiguation Role Approach Human Immediately recognized ‘Ming Yu’ was too generic and provided full name ‘Mingyu Ding’ when reviewing erroneous results; knew common Chinese names would have disambiguation issues AI Accepted first Semantic Scholar match without questioning correctness; flagged data quality issue only after seeing obviously wrong papers (explosives chemistry, veterinary science) Difference Analysis: Human preemptively knew common names need disambiguation; AI detected problem only post-hoc from result inspection. Human applied prior knowledge of systemic issues; AI relied on empirical detection.
When to trigger citation analysis in report pipeline Role Approach Human Always run automatically for top-5 papers; prioritized convenience over explicit control based on actual usage patterns (would be wanted in most cases) AI Proposed making citation analysis opt-in via –citations flag; defaulted to explicit user choice for potentially expensive operations Difference Analysis: Human considered real-world workflow friction while AI focused on theoretical flexibility and cost optimization. Human prioritized reducing friction in common workflow over architectural purity.
Refactoring plan execution approach Role Approach Human Provided detailed multi-phase plan with specific file paths, line counts, expected changes, and explicit checkpoints - prescribed exact steps AI Started by reading files in parallel to understand current state before making changes, verified import chain worked after each phase, added verification steps and parallel I/O optimization not in original plan Difference Analysis: Human used prescriptive specification with clear checkpoints; AI added verification steps and parallelization. Both valued systematic phased execution over atomic big-bang changes. Human’s detailed plan eliminated ambiguity and ensured consistent implementation.
Hugo content organization Role Approach Human Specified researcher profiles should go in new research/ section, not bugJournal/, understanding semantic difference between reference material and temporal reporting AI Would have followed existing pattern of deploying to bugJournal/ since that’s where research_scout.py reports go, seeing both as ‘research content’ Difference Analysis: Human distinguished between temporal content (daily reports) and reference content (researcher profiles) requiring separate sections; AI saw both as same category and would have lumped them together. Human understood content taxonomy for navigation.
Implementation Level Handling missing conference award data Role Approach Human Expected AI might have award information in training data; asked AI to identify papers with conference awards AI Recognized knowledge limitation - could not confirm specific awards with high confidence, returned empty list with explanation rather than guessing, maintained conservative ‘unknown’ response Difference Analysis: Human assumed AI training data might include award info; AI understood uncertainty boundaries and chose not to propagate potentially false information. Shows AI understanding of when to say ‘I don’t know’.
Documentation language choice Role Approach Human Explicitly requested ‘Now please use Chinese to update tutorial.md’ after code implementation, recognizing target audience (Chinese researchers) needed native-language tutorial AI Had been using English for code/comments but immediately switched to comprehensive Chinese documentation when requested, defaulting to English for technical docs Difference Analysis: Human recognized end-user needs based on target audience; AI used neutral default. Reflects user’s understanding of user demographics vs AI’s language-agnostic approach.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Failed to proactively detect Semantic Scholar name disambiguation issues in initial researcher analyses - accepted obviously wrong matches (explosives chemistry, veterinary science, geology) and required human-observable symptoms or explicit clarification to trigger error detection. Did not question matches despite domain mismatches. Required explicit 9-step integration plan to execute complex architectural changes; initial /init attempt was interrupted by user suggesting AI was heading toward documentation improvements rather than structural refactoring. Needed architectural guidance for cross-cutting changes. Initially designed co-authorship-only student discovery without considering that faculty homepages are the authoritative and explicit source for student lists; required human suggestion to switch approaches Initially missed entire ‘New feature’ directory when first analyzing codebase; required explicit user prompt pointing it out before discovering undocumented profiler tool with ~15 Python modules Failed to parse Yuke Zhu’s trajectory analysis JSON even after three-tier LLM repair escalation (haiku → sonnet → opus), resulting in incomplete report with only paper list but no analytical insights Required explicit user correction to understand that researcher profiles belong in separate Hugo section from daily research scout reports, lacking semantic understanding of content taxonomy (reference vs temporal) Proposed citation count as part of composite relevance score without recognizing that popularity and project-specific relevance are orthogonal dimensions; conflated ‘important paper’ with ‘relevant to project’ General Limitations Cannot automatically test end-to-end functionality after large refactoring - verified imports work but did not run actual tool commands with new paths to confirm correctness Cannot reliably verify conference awards (Best Paper, Spotlight, Oral) from training data alone - requires real-time access to official conference websites or paper metadata APIs. Returned empty arrays with disclaimers rather than guessing. Did not propose cost optimization alternatives for citation analysis (e.g., citation_count threshold, opt-in flag); blindly implemented ‘always analyze top-5’ as specified without questioning API cost implications Defaulted to English documentation despite codebase being part of Chinese-language user project; required explicit instruction to switch to Chinese for TUTORIAL.md Cannot automatically aggregate final state across multiple parallel agents; human verification needed to confirm all 230 CalendarPro tests passed after 5 agents completed their work When pip install failed due to Windows file lock, did not suggest alternative approaches like stopping MCP server process or using –user flag until after first failure Defaulted to making citation analysis opt-in (–citations flag) rather than considering usage patterns that would favor automatic execution for convenience Learnings Key Learnings For large architectural refactoring, detailed written plans with function signatures, line counts, and architectural decisions dramatically improve AI execution accuracy and prevent scope creep. Human architectural vision + AI tactical execution works better than AI improvisation. Large-scale refactoring should be parallelized by phase/domain: CalendarPro’s 7 phases implemented by 5 concurrent agents each owning a subset of changes, then integrated with test verification. Phased execution with verification checkpoints prevents cascading failures that are hard to diagnose. Academic profiling systems must implement name disambiguation as first-class concern - common Chinese names create severe disambiguation problems requiring mandatory ORCID/institution matching. Same-name aggregation creates entirely false researcher profiles that appear plausible until domain expertise reveals incompatibility. Better to return ‘data unusable’ than propagate false information. Multi-source data integration (homepage scraping + co-authorship + ArXiv + Semantic Scholar) with explicit source tracking provides robustness against individual data source failures or inaccuracies. Faculty homepages are more authoritative than co-authorship analysis for student discovery as they explicitly list current and former students with status. Re-export shims with lazy imports enable large-scale code refactoring while maintaining backward compatibility and avoiding circular dependency issues. Centralized infrastructure modules (paths.py, cache.py, llm.py) enable atomic refactoring - changing one constant propagates everywhere without breaking downstream dependencies. Modular architecture enables clean integration: keeping research_scout.py as monolithic CLI entry point while treating profiler package as library code separates concerns beautifully. Hybrid integration approaches (preserving stable CLI while refactoring internals) reduce migration risk compared to full rewrites. Academic research analysis tools enable rapid domain landscape understanding: researcher profiler quickly reveals field leaders’ trajectories, current directions, and breakthrough works. Systematic framework for tracking cutting-edge research directions. Type-first organization (reports/, logs/, cache/) is more maintainable than tool-first organization when multiple tools share similar output patterns. Centralized path management enables atomic refactoring across entire codebase. Parameter threading through nested call chains requires backward-compatible defaults (backend=‘claude_cli’) and incremental syntax testing (py_compile) to prevent cascading errors. When adding parameters to deeply-nested call chains, default values preserve backward compatibility. Use parallel Agent exploration for thorough codebase understanding before making architectural decisions; sequential exploration misses connections between components. Documentation files like CLAUDE.md become stale rapidly as features are added; need active maintenance or automated detection of undocumented code paths. Documentation-driven development pays off: updating CLAUDE.md and TUTORIAL.md immediately after code changes prevents doc rot and ensures knowledge transfer to future sessions. Documentation synchronization critical for maintainability. Heuristic algorithms depend critically on data quality: student discovery with Semantic Scholar co-authorship failed when data was sparse; need multiple sources or ground truth (homepages). When heuristics fail, switch to direct information sources rather than debugging scoring algorithms. LLM repair escalation (haiku → sonnet → opus) has limits; persistent JSON parse failures may indicate prompt or context issues rather than model capability problems. When all three model tiers fail, revisit input structure or question decomposition. Always ask users about design tradeoffs (scoring weights, automatic vs opt-in features, performance vs convenience) rather than assuming defaults; user context reveals non-obvious priorities like preferring automatic citation analysis over cost optimization. When extracting shared utilities, best-of-breed merging (taking most robust implementation from each source) produces better results than arbitrary selection. API search behavior is not always intuitive; multi-source data fetching is more robust than single-API queries. Practical Learnings Hugo content organization benefits from semantic separation: reference material (researcher profiles) and temporal content (daily reports) should go in different sections for better navigation and user experience. Daily Report — 2026-03-13 Daily Overview What was done: Developed two independent systems: (1) Academic researcher analysis toolkit for robotics/VLA domain with ArXiv/Semantic Scholar integration, LLM trajectory analysis, and student discovery; (2) Per-frame variable collection system for RoboTwin manipulation task tracking progress and target poses How it was done: Research tool via modular Python package with multi-stage JSON parsing, SHA-256 disk caching, and year-based paper selection; RoboTwin via post-processing pipeline overriding move() to patch pickle files with new variables after trajectory completion Impact: Research tool enables systematic study of how robotics pioneers achieved breakthroughs with recursive student discovery; RoboTwin system provides richer training signal for VLA models to learn manipulation progress and predict target end-effector poses MacBook What was done: Implemented full gadget research tool (15 modules, 2000+ LOC), fixed critical bugs in JSON parsing and paper selection logic, analyzed trajectories of Levine/Abbeel with detailed breakthrough analysis How it was done: Created APIs layer (ArXiv HTML/PDF extraction, Semantic Scholar metrics), prompts layer (Chinese output templates), analysis orchestrator with BFS recursion, scoring algorithms, and CLI with analyze/show/list/config subcommands Impact: Tool now supports fast mode (abstract-only) and detailed mode (full-text download), year-stratified paper selection (≤10/year), LLM award recognition, and generates both JSON profiles and Markdown reports with bilingual support tianhe What was done: Designed and implemented new variable collection system for RoboTwin Place Dual Shoes task: removed critical_region, added 5 new per-frame variables (manip_progress_time, manip_progress_distance_left/right, target_endpose, target_joint) How it was done: Used Explore and Plan agents for codebase analysis, implemented post-processing pipeline by overriding _take_picture() and move() to track EE positions and patch pkl files, debugged base class behavior and added clipping for progress values Impact: Successfully extended data collection to capture manipulation progress metrics without modifying base task infrastructure or breaking existing pkl-to-hdf5 conversion pipeline, enabling VLA model to learn richer manipulation signals Built academic researcher profiling tool with LLM-powered trajectory analysis and award recognition while implementing per-frame manipulation progress tracking system for RoboTwin Place Dual Shoes task
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Build academic researcher analysis tool — Created complete Python package with ArXiv/Semantic Scholar integration, LLM trajectory analysis, award recognition, student discovery, and CLI interface ✅ Add target_endpose and target_joint prediction variables — Recorded final 7D endpose (xyz + quat) and joint angles at move() completion as per-frame labels for VLA target prediction ✅ Fix JSON parsing escalation bug — Refactored parse_json_response to use haiku→sonnet→opus escalation chain, save failed responses to disk, avoid infinite recursion with _try_parse_json helper ✅ Implement year-based paper selection with award prioritization — Replaced citation-only sorting with year stratification (≤10 papers/year), award weight-based ranking (best_paper=4, highlight=3, spotlight=2, oral=1), chronological ordering ✅ Analyze Sergey Levine and Pieter Abbeel trajectories — Generated detailed academic trajectory analyses for two robotics pioneers, identifying breakthrough works (TRPO, MAML, SAC, DDPM, Decision Transformer) and explaining why they succeeded when others did not ✅ Add manip_progress_distance_left/right tracking — Computed 1 - |current_pos - final_pos| / |start_pos - final_pos| for both arms with np.clip to [0,1] range to handle curved trajectories ✅ Add LLM-based award recognition — Implemented new analysis stage that uses LLM to identify best paper/spotlight/highlight/oral awards from paper titles, venues, and years ✅ Add manip_progress_time tracking — Implemented linear interpolation from 0 (move start) to 1 (move end) for each frame in a move() call Implementation & Fixes ✅ Create documentation (tutorial.md, CLAUDE.md) — Wrote comprehensive Chinese tutorial covering installation, usage, analysis modes, student discovery, scoring system, and CLAUDE.md for future AI context ✅ Fix detailed mode paper download scope — Changed from downloading only top 10 most-cited papers to downloading full text for ALL filtered papers (already capped at ≤10/year by selection logic) ✅ Fix critical_region still appearing in HDF5 output — Added pkl_data.pop(‘critical_region’, None) in post-processing after discovering base class unconditionally writes this key ✅ Fix Semantic Scholar logging ambiguity — Changed log message ‘[S2] 获取论文: 1736651’ to ‘[S2] 获取作者 1736651 的论文…’ to avoid misreading author ID as paper count ✅ Fix negative progress_distance values — Applied np.clip(progress_dist, 0.0, 1.0) after user reported negative values from real data runs ✅ Remove critical_region variable from Place Dual Shoes task — Deleted get_critical_region_label() override and added pkl post-processing to remove the key written by base class get_obs() Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. JSON parsing fails catastrophically when Haiku repair fails, losing original LLM response and making debugging impossible Solution: Implemented escalating repair chain (haiku→sonnet→opus) with _try_parse_json helper to avoid recursion, saving failed responses to output/logs/json_repair_failed/.txt for debugging
Key Insight: When LLM-based repair is involved, must avoid infinite recursion by separating pure parsing logic (_try_parse_json) from repair-invoking logic (parse_json_response), and always preserve original output on total failure
2. ArXiv only returns recent 100 papers, Semantic Scholar has 500 papers with citation data, but merge logic discarded S2 papers without ArXiv matches, losing most historical high-impact work Solution: Reversed data source priority: S2 becomes primary source (has year/citation/venue/abstract), ArXiv enriches with arxiv_id/pdf_url/categories, then add orphan ArXiv papers. Result: comprehensive timeline coverage
Key Insight: When merging datasets with different biases (ArXiv=recent, S2=comprehensive), use the more complete source as foundation and enrich from the specialized source, not vice versa
3. Sorting papers only by citation count lost temporal research trajectory, making it impossible to see how researcher’s focus evolved over career stages Solution: Implemented year-stratified selection: group by year, sort within year by award weight then citations, take ≤10/year, display chronologically. Preserves trajectory narrative while highlighting top work per period
Key Insight: For longitudinal analysis, temporal structure is often more valuable than global ranking; stratified sampling maintains both dimension
4. manip_progress_distance_left/right contained negative values and values >1 in collected data Solution: Added np.clip(progress_dist, 0.0, 1.0) to constrain both left and right progress distance to valid [0,1] range
Key Insight: Curved robot trajectories can cause current EE position to temporarily exceed start-to-target distance during interpolation, breaking the 1 - |current-final|/|start-final| formula assumptions. Explicit bounds enforcement is necessary for progress metrics.
5. ArXiv and Semantic Scholar APIs don’t provide award data (best paper, spotlight, etc.), but this is critical for identifying breakthrough work Solution: User suggested leveraging LLM training data: send paper titles+venues to LLM, ask it to recall known awards. Implemented as new analysis stage with separate caching
Key Insight: LLMs can serve as auxiliary knowledge bases for data not available via APIs, especially for prestigious but unstructured metadata like conference awards
6. critical_region still appeared in HDF5 files after deleting the override method Solution: Analyzed base class _base_task.py:510 and found get_obs() unconditionally writes pkl_dic[‘critical_region’]. Added post-processing step to pop this key from patched pickle files.
Key Insight: Deleting override methods only changes return value; base class code paths must be traced to ensure keys are truly removed from output. Post-processing pkl files before HDF5 conversion is effective for removing unwanted keys.
General Issues 7. Log message ‘[S2] 获取论文: 1736651’ ambiguous—looks like 1.7M papers fetched, actually author ID. User spotted this immediately Solution: Changed to ‘[S2] 获取作者 1736651 的论文…’ and ‘[S2] 作者 1736651: 获取到 500 篇论文’. Explicit subject-verb-object structure eliminates ambiguity
Key Insight: Log messages must be unambiguous even when read out of context. Numbers should always have explicit labels indicating their semantic type
8. Detailed mode only downloaded full text for top 10 most-cited papers, but after year-stratified selection already have ≤10 papers/year—should analyze ALL of them in detailed mode Solution: Removed ‘sorted(…, reverse=True)[:10]’ filter, changed to ‘papers_for_download = [p for p in papers if p.arxiv_id]’. Now downloads full text for all filtered papers
Key Insight: When selection logic already enforces quality threshold upstream, downstream shouldn’t re-filter with different criteria—causes inconsistency between modes
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Award data sourcing strategy Role Approach Human User proposed ‘download paper titles, then let Claude search if it’s spotlight paper’—directly leveraging LLM as knowledge base AI AI initially focused on API-based solutions, looking for structured award datasets or scraping conference websites Difference Analysis: Human recognized LLMs trained on academic data already ‘know’ famous awards, no need for real-time web search. AI defaulted to traditional data pipeline thinking. Shows human insight into LLM capabilities exceeding tool-builder’s initial assumptions
Data source priority for paper merging Role Approach Human User explicitly requested year-based timeline coverage ‘but only if there are publications that year’, implying exhaustive temporal coverage matters more than citation threshold AI AI initially used ArXiv (recent 100) as primary and S2 as enrichment, implicitly prioritizing recency over completeness Difference Analysis: Human requirement ‘cover all years with publications’ reveals goal is trajectory reconstruction, not just current impact survey. AI’s initial heuristic (use smaller dataset as base) was computationally sensible but semantically wrong for this use case
Base class behavior analysis for critical_region removal Role Approach Human User ran data collection, inspected HDF5 output, and reported that critical_region still exists despite code changes AI Claude deleted the override method and assumed base class default (return 0) would be sufficient; did not trace base class get_obs() execution path during initial implementation Difference Analysis: Human used empirical testing to validate removal; AI relied on static code analysis that missed unconditional writes in base class. User’s black-box testing approach caught the issue AI’s white-box analysis missed.
Escalation vs. fallback in error handling Role Approach Human User specified ‘haiku can’t fix → use sonnet, still fails → use opus, still fails → log to file’—explicit escalation chain with terminal failure handling AI AI initially implemented single-tier repair (only haiku) with early return on failure, treating repair as binary operation Difference Analysis: Human applied cost-graduated retry strategy (cheap → expensive → abort), common in production systems but not obvious in prototype code. Shows operational maturity thinking about failure modes
Handling progress_distance edge cases Role Approach Human User discovered negative values from actual data and requested explicit clamping to [0,1] range based on semantic meaning of ‘progress’ AI Claude initially implemented the mathematical formula 1 - Difference Analysis: Human reasoned from data semantics (progress must be bounded) and observed failures; AI focused on formula correctness without considering physical edge cases like non-linear trajectories. User’s domain knowledge about manipulation progress drove the fix.
Implementation Level Identifying log message ambiguity Role Approach Human User immediately recognized that ‘获取论文: 1736651’ could be misread as paper count rather than author ID, spotted the UX issue without testing AI AI wrote log message focusing on technical accuracy (ID is logged) but didn’t consider how number-like IDs appear ambiguous in isolation Difference Analysis: Human instinctively reads logs from naive reader perspective (what could this mean?), AI focuses on information completeness from writer perspective (does it contain the data?). UX requires reader-centric design
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Used smaller dataset (ArXiv 100 recent) as merge base rather than comprehensive dataset (S2 500 historical), prioritizing algorithmic simplicity over semantic completeness for trajectory analysis Static code analysis insufficient for tracing data flow: Claude deleted get_critical_region_label() override but failed to trace that base class get_obs() unconditionally writes pkl_dic[‘critical_region’], requiring user to discover this through runtime testing Initially defaulted to traditional data pipeline thinking (API scraping, structured datasets) for award information, missing the insight that LLMs already ‘know’ famous conference awards from training data Implemented single-stage LLM repair (haiku only) rather than multi-stage escalation, treating error recovery as binary rather than graduated cost-benefit problem Limited physical reasoning about edge cases: Did not anticipate that curved robot trajectories could cause progress_distance to exceed [0,1] bounds, implementing formula without considering trajectory geometry constraints Over-reliance on method inheritance logic: Assumed deleting override would remove variable from output, without verifying all code paths that write to data structures. Needed empirical testing to catch base class unconditional writes. General Limitations Failed to anticipate log message ambiguity: wrote ‘[S2] 获取论文: 1736651’ without considering how bare number appears ambiguous to readers. Required user correction to make subject-verb-object structure explicit Did not proactively verify that detailed mode’s paper selection logic aligned with year-stratified selection—allowed inconsistency where selection caps at ≤10/year but download recaps at global top 10 Learnings Key Learnings For researcher trajectory analysis, temporal structure preservation (year-stratified sampling) is more valuable than global citation ranking. Shows domain-specific sampling strategies matter more than generic ‘sort by metric’ approaches Post-processing approach for ‘future-dependent’ variables: When per-frame variables require knowledge of move() completion state (like target poses), recording frames normally then patching pickle files after move() finishes is cleaner than complex state machines during frame capture LLMs can serve as knowledge bases for unstructured metadata (conference awards, paper prestige) when APIs don’t provide it. This ‘LLM as auxiliary database’ pattern is underutilized—requires prompt design skill but no infrastructure When implementing LLM-based repair in recursive parsing logic, must extract non-LLM stages into separate helper to avoid infinite loops. Pattern: _try_parse (pure) vs parse_response (with repair) Multi-source data merging: when sources have different biases (recency vs comprehensiveness), use most complete as foundation and enrich from specialized. ArXiv=recent, S2=historical → S2 base + ArXiv enrichment Error recovery should implement cost-graduated escalation (cheap model → expensive model → human intervention via logs) rather than binary fail/succeed. Maximizes automated recovery while preserving debugging information Base class data flow requires deep tracing: In complex OOP hierarchies with per-frame data collection, deleting overrides may not remove keys from output. Must trace base class execution paths (e.g., get_obs() → _take_picture() → pkl files) to ensure variables are truly excluded. Physical quantities need semantic bounds enforcement: Progress metrics derived from geometric formulas should be explicitly clamped to their semantic range [0,1] even if the formula theoretically produces valid values, as real-world trajectories introduce edge cases Practical Learnings ArXiv HTML rendering now preferred over PDF for full-text extraction: faster, no OCR errors, preserves structure. PDF as fallback for pre-HTML papers. Shows infrastructure evolution requires periodic revisiting of ‘best practices’ Logging numbers without semantic labels creates ambiguity: ‘1736651’ could be count/ID/size. Always use explicit labels: ‘author 1736651’ or ‘1,736,651 papers’. Cost is two extra words, benefit is eliminating entire class of interpretation errors For academic analysis tools, Chinese output is preferred for narrative sections but English for technical terms. Bilingual approach: structure in English (breakthrough, why_not_before, impact), explanation in Chinese When selection logic exists upstream (year stratification → ≤10/year), downstream stages should not re-filter with different criteria. Causes mode inconsistency (fast mode sees different papers than detailed mode) Multi-agent exploration pattern: Using Explore agent for codebase understanding → Plan agent for design → sequential implementation with user validation creates clear separation of concerns and allows plan review before execution Conversation Summaries gadget research tool ✅ Research tool design and full implementation 20:08:05 | claude_code Designed and built complete academic researcher analysis tool for robotics domain. Initial discussion covered requirements (analyze why leaders became influential, breakthrough works, recursive student discovery, fast/detailed modes). historical records could not open old files How it was done: Enabled App Sandbox to make security-scoped bookmarks effective, repaired bookmark parsing fallback logic, and added an NSOpenPanel reauthorization mechanism Impact: User historical record functionality is restored, the app adheres to macOS best practices, and the path to App Store submission is cleared tianhe What was done: Handled PyTorch environment dependency conflicts in the RoboTwin project, resolved curobo compilation issues, and optimized the readability of the GPU monitoring tool How it was done: Matched torch/torchvision via pip version matrix, configured the CUDA toolchain path (CUDA_HOME and CPATH) in the conda environment, and rewritten the process aggregation logic to limit output width Impact: The robot policy evaluation environment has most of its functionality restored, GPU resource monitoring is more efficient, but the checkpoint path mapping issue remains unresolved Fixed the sandbox permission architecture for macOS wallpaper apps and resolved PyTorch dependency chain and CUDA compilation issues in the deep learning evaluation environment
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Fixed historical record inability to open old videos in macOS wallpaper apps — enabled App Sandbox, repaired bookmark parsing logic (added non-scoped fallback), added permission error retry mechanism (NSOpenPanel reauthorization), updated localization and ChangeLog ✅ Fixed torch/torchvision version conflict in RoboTwin evaluation environment — upgraded torchvision from 0.21.0 to 0.22.1+cu126 to match torch 2.7.1, resolved torchvision::nms operator registration failure ✅ Recompiled curobo to match current PyTorch ABI — removed old.so file, installed ninja, configured CUDA_HOME and CPATH, recompiled from source via pip install -e . ❌ Resolved checkpoint path absence issue in RoboTwin — the eval.sh parameter specifies checkpoint_id=5000, but only 15000/25000/29999 directories exist. Analysis of the parameter mapping logic interrupted sessions Implementation & Fixes 🔄 Optimized GPU monitoring tool output format — limited width to 80 columns, removed duplicate processes, filtered noise sub-processes. Users reported that understanding errors interrupted sessions Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. macOS non-sandbox applications cannot persist file access permissions, and old videos in historical records report Operation not permitted error Solution: Enable App Sandbox permissions (com.apple.security.app-sandbox and files.user-selected.read-write), fix ensureFileAccess to add non-scoped bookmark fallback parsing, add NSOpenPanel reauthorization mechanism to showVideo/showImage
Key Insight: The macOS TCC mechanism requires App Sandbox to create security-scoped bookmarks. Non-scoped bookmarks only parse URLs but do not grant access permissions, causing old files to fail to open. A combination of sandbox + downgrade path is required
2. torch 2.7.1 and torchvision 0.21.0 ABI incompatibility causes torchvision::nms operator registration failure Solution: Upgrade torchvision to 0.22.1+cu126 to match torch 2.7.1 version
Key Insight: Custom operators in torchvision are linked to torch’s C++ API during compilation, and version mismatch leads to operator registration interface failure. torchvision 0.21.0 corresponds to torch 2.6.x and cannot be used with torch 2.7.x
3. Pre-compiled .so file of curobo is incompatible with current PyTorch ABI, and JIT compilation cannot find CUDA_runtime.h Solution: Remove old.so file, install ninja compiler tool, set CUDA_HOME=/path/to/conda/env and CPATH=/path/to/targets/x86_64-linux/include, recompile via pip install -e .
Key Insight: C++ extensions require recompilation after PyTorch version upgrade. The nvidia package installed via conda in the environment places CUDA headers in non-standard paths (targets/x86_64-linux/include/), and environment variables need to be correctly configured for JIT compilation to find them
General Issues 4. GPU monitoring tool output width is too large and processes are displayed repeatedly, making it difficult to read Solution: Limit output to 80 columns, aggregate GPU lists by process, filter noise sub-processes such as multiprocessing workers
Key Insight: The original implementation grouped by GPU caused a multi-card process to appear repeatedly across multiple GPUs. Aggregation by process and display of all used card numbers in the GPU column are needed
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Deep explanation of macOS file permission issues Role Approach Human Intuitively asks ‘why is there insufficient permission?’ and requires AI to explain the underlying principles of TCC and sandbox mechanisms AI Provides technical solutions but does not actively explain background principles, requiring human follow-up to give a complete context Difference Analysis: Human problem-oriented thinking guides AI to provide a more complete background explanation rather than directly jumping to solutions. Humans focus more on ‘why’, while AI focuses on ‘how’
Strategy for choosing repair solutions Role Approach Human Clearly selects a defensive approach of ‘combination of sandbox + NSOpenPanel reauthorization’ AI Provides two independent options (sandbox or reauthorization) but does not suggest a combination actively Difference Analysis: Humans prefer defensive programming (multiple layers of protection), while AI tends to favor a single optimal solution. Human combined strategies solve the root cause and provide a downgrade path, making them more robust
Implementation Level Understanding of GPU monitoring tool requirements Role Approach Human Corrects ’each process appears once per GPU’ instead of ’each process appears once’ and emphasizes the many-to-many relationship AI Misunderstands the requirement, aggregates multi-GPU processes into a single line, and displays card numbers separated by commas in the GPU column Difference Analysis: Humans accurately understand the many-to-many relationship display requirement for process-GPU, while AI’s over-optimization causes information loss (resource usage of a process on GPU0 and GPU1 should be displayed in two lines)
AI Limitations General Limitations Failed to actively explain technical background (macOS TCC/sandbox mechanisms), requiring human follow-up to provide complete context. AI should actively explain ‘why’ when proposing solutions Misunderstood GPU monitoring requirements, simplified the many-to-many relationship to one-to-many aggregation, leading to information loss. Inaccurate understanding of visualization needs for complex data relationships When analyzing checkpoint path issues, started overly detailed code analysis (continuous Read operations) without first confirming the problem scope with the user. High-level parameter mapping logic should be understood first Learnings Key Learnings macOS TCC permission mechanism: Non-sandbox applications cannot create security-scoped bookmarks; only non-scoped bookmarks (only parsing URLs without access permission) can be created, causing historical file access to fail after app restart. App Sandbox must be enabled to persist file access permissions PyTorch C++ extension ABI compatibility: Custom operators in torchvision (such as torchvision::nms) are linked to torch’s C++ API during compilation, and versions must match exactly (torchvision 0.21→torch 2.6, torchvision 0.22→torch 2.7). Version mismatch causes operator registration failure Conda environment CUDA toolchain configuration: The nvidia package installed via pip places CUDA headers in targets/x86_64-linux/include/ instead of standard include/ paths. JIT compilation of C++ extensions requires setting CUDA_HOME to point to the conda env and CPATH to include the targets path Defensive programming principle: A combination of sandbox + reauthorization is more robust than a single solution. Sandbox addresses the root cause (persistent permissions), NSOpenPanel provides a downgrade path (temporary authorization), and the combination ensures users can always access files Conversation Summaries Desktop Video ✅ Fixed permission issue preventing opening old videos in historical records 07:52:05.359 | claude_code User reported that old videos cannot be opened in historical records (Operation not permitted Code=257). Log analysis revealed that the app did not enable sandbox, causing security-scoped bookmark creation failure. ensureFileAccess only tried.withSecurityScope parsing, resulting in non-scoped bookmarks failing forever, and finally being denied by macOS TCC. Three-layer fixes were implemented: enable App Sandbox permissions, fix bookmark parsing to add non-scoped fallback, and add NSOpenPanel reauthorization mechanism to showVideo/showImage. Code modifications, localization updates, and ChangeLog were completed, and build verification passed

AI rewrote the process table logic, aggregating each process into a single line, displaying card numbers separated by commas in the GPU column, and filtering out noise sub-processes such as multiprocessing workers. User corrected their understanding, pointing out that it should be ’each process appears once per GPU’ instead of aggregated display, causing session interruption
RoboTwin Policy Evaluation**🔄 Dependency conflicts causing the failed execution of eval.sh diagnosis** 02:23:18.758 | claude_code The user encountered an error when running bash eval.sh; the AI identified three levels of dependency issues: 1) torch 2.7.1 does not match torchvision 0.21.0, resulting in failure to register the torchvision::nms operator; 2) curobo pre-compiled.so is incompatible with torch ABI, and JIT compilation lacks ninja; 3) the checkpoint path does not exist (the parameter specifies 5000, but only has values of 15000/25000/29999). The AI provided a version upgrade solution, and the user chose to upgrade torchvision.
🔄 Fixed dependencies and resolved subsequent compilation issues 02:34:02.614 | claude_code Execution of repair plan: torchvision was successfully upgraded to 0.22.1+cu126 and its compatibility with torch 2.7.1 was verified; ninja compilation tool was installed; after removing the old.so file, curobo was recompiled by configuring CUDA_HOME and CPATH (pointing to conda env’s targets/x86_64-linux/include/); curobo’s import was verified to work properly. pi05 training unblocked; identified JAX version as 20-30% performance bottleneck; aligned pi05 dependencies to eliminate training time gap; expected ~25% speedup Multi-project productivity: MIHD file restructuring + benchmarking, K8s GPU monitoring tool, VLA training optimization (torch/torchvision fix + 33% speedup via JAX/dependency alignment)
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ MIHD file structure reorganization — Executed 8-step plan to migrate outputs/ directory: benchmark_results→DLPFC, hd_results→HD, rm_ideal split into cross_section/single_section. Updated 14 code files and multiple docs. Cleaned up old directories. ✅ GPU monitor tool development (gpumon.py) — Built nvitop-style GPU monitoring tool for K8s containers. Features: /proc/fd + CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES GPU detection, double-border tables, process grouping by GPU, colored progress bars, auto-filtering of monitoring processes. Supports live refresh and one-shot modes. ✅ Analyze and resolve openpi vs pi05 training speed gap — Investigated 15h vs 20h training ETA discrepancy (33% gap). Used parallel exploration agents to identify root causes: JAX version (0.5.0 vs 0.5.3 - primary), num_workers (8 vs 16), lerobot git revs, IMAGE_KEYS difference, conda base envs. Systematically aligned 6 dependencies in pi05 to match openpi, added override-dependencies to resolve lerobot torch constraint conflict, completed uv lock/sync. ✅ MIHD patch query bug fixes — Fixed 3 bugs causing ‘queried patches don’t match’: barcode ordering mismatch between cache and adata, data path inconsistency, coordinate system alignment. Updated 4 files with explicit barcode-to-index mapping. ✅ MIHD RM-IDEAL benchmark (151673-151508) — Ran RM-IDEAL cross-section benchmark on CPU using existing embeddings and cache. Results: avg Spearman r=0.1804, Layer_4/Layer_1 perform well, Layer_3/Layer_6 show negative correlation. Data saved to summary.csv. ✅ Pi05 torch/torchvision version fix — Resolved training startup error ‘operator torchvision::nms does not exist’. Diagnosed torch 2.7.1 + torchvision 0.21.0 mismatch. Added torchvision==0.22.1 to pyproject.toml, ran uv sync, verified upgrade. Training environment restored. Implementation & Fixes ❌ Error-recovery v5 scenes visualization — User requested 720p re-rendering of v5 error scenes (existing 480p videos). Plan mode repeatedly rejected, task abandoned. Likely environmental issue or user changed intent. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. MIHD patch query returned wrong physical spots: ‘queried patches don’t match current patch’ Solution: Root cause: barcode ordering mismatch between cache (sc.read_10x_h5 order) and visualization (sc.read_visium order). Fixed by explicit barcode-to-cache-index mapping: {str(b): i for i, b in enumerate(cache_barcodes)}. Also fixed data path and coordinate conventions.
Key Insight: Index-based lookups fail when data sources have different orderings. Always use explicit key-based alignment (barcodes in this case) when bridging cached data and runtime reloads.
2. K8s container PID namespace isolation prevents nvidia-smi from showing process info Solution: Built custom GPU monitor using /proc//fd/ to scan /dev/nvidia* device files and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES env var. Filter out monitoring tools (nvitop, gpustat, claude) that open all GPUs. Implemented nvitop-style TUI with rich library.
Key Insight: Containerized GPU monitoring requires proc filesystem inspection. /proc/fd symlinks reveal opened devices; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is the ground truth. Monitoring tools opening all GPUs are false positives - filter by checking CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES absence.
3. Training time for identical commands differed by 33% across two projects (openpi 15h vs pi05 20h), despite same hardware and configurations Solution: Identified JAX version difference (0.5.0 vs 0.5.3) as primary cause through parallel exploration agents. Systematically aligned 6 dependency versions: JAX 0.5.0→0.5.3, torch>=2.5.1→2.7.1, orbax-checkpoint 0.11.1→0.11.13, numpy, beartype, transformers. Added override-dependencies to resolve lerobot’s torch<2.7 constraint conflict.
Key Insight: Minor JAX version upgrades (0.5.0→0.5.3) can yield 20-30% performance gains due to XLA compiler optimizations; multi-project dependency drift is a stealth performance bug requiring periodic alignment audits. uv’s override-dependencies provides surgical conflict resolution without forking upstream code.
4. MIHD file structure was cluttered with inconsistent naming (benchmark_results, hd_results, rm_ideal split across dirs) Solution: Executed systematic 8-step migration plan: create new hierarchy (DLPFC, HD, rm_ideal/{cross_section,single_section}), migrate files, update 14 code files + docs, cleanup old dirs. Used bash mv + Edit tool for bulk path updates.
Key Insight: Large-scale refactoring requires upfront planning (create dirs first), then file migration, then code updates, then doc updates. Batch sed for archived docs acceptable since they’re historical.
5. Pi05 training failed at startup: ‘RuntimeError: operator torchvision::nms does not exist’ Solution: Diagnosed torch 2.7.1 + torchvision 0.21.0 version mismatch (0.21.0 compiled for torch 2.6.x). Added explicit torchvision==0.22.1 to pyproject.toml dependencies, ran uv sync to upgrade. Verified: torch 2.7.1+cu126, torchvision 0.22.1+cu126.
Key Insight: PyTorch and torchvision have strict version pairing (2.7.x needs 0.22.x). Indirect dependencies resolved by uv/pip may select incompatible versions - always pin critical binary-coupled dependencies explicitly.
General Issues 6. pi05 wandb logs showed num_workers=16 despite code default being 8 Solution: Traced to CLI parameter –num-workers 16 overriding the default; recommended not passing the parameter rather than modifying code
Key Insight: Configuration parameters can originate from multiple sources (code defaults, CLI args, config files); full provenance tracing is necessary before making code changes
7. Initial gpumon.py layout had line wrapping, column truncation, and cluttered process lists Solution: Iterative improvements: 1) Fixed column width calculations for GPU info, 2) Switched to table-based layout, 3) Adopted nvitop double-border style, 4) Filtered monitoring tool processes, 5) Grouped processes under respective GPUs.
Key Insight: Terminal UI design requires multiple iterations. Reference existing tools (nvitop) for user expectations. Auto-filtering noise (monitoring processes) improves signal-to-noise ratio.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level MIHD file reorganization execution approach Role Approach Human Human provided detailed 8-step plan: create dirs first, migrate files by category, update code refs, update docs, verify final structure. Clear separation of phases. AI AI would likely explore first, then propose changes incrementally. Less upfront planning, more discovery-driven. Difference Analysis: Human’s systematic planning prevented mid-execution issues (like updating code before files moved). AI tends toward exploratory, iterative execution. Human’s approach better for large-scale refactoring with many interdependencies.
Error recovery v5 visualization plan rejection loop Role Approach Human After multiple plan rejections, human said ‘just run it now’ (wanted immediate execution, not more planning). But continued rejecting exit plan mode attempts. AI AI interpreted ‘just run it now’ as ’exit plan mode and execute’. Kept trying ExitPlanMode tool. Didn’t recognize user might have environmental blocker or changed intent. Difference Analysis: Communication breakdown: user’s repeated rejections signaled an unspoken issue (GPU node unavailable? task no longer needed?). AI should have asked ‘what’s blocking this?’ after 2-3 rejections instead of retrying same approach.
Dependency alignment strategy Role Approach Human Direct instruction: ‘align all pi05 dependencies to openpi and set num_workers to 8’ AI Granular analysis: compared both pyproject.toml files, categorized dependencies into shared (6 to update), pi05-specific (RoboTwin packages to keep), openpi-specific (not needed in pi05), and pinned git revs (lerobot to preserve) Difference Analysis: AI decomposed the request into surgical edits (6 specific version changes + 1 new config section) rather than wholesale replacement, preserving project-specific dependencies and avoiding compatibility risks from changing lerobot git rev
GPU monitor UI design expectations Role Approach Human Human explicitly requested ‘refer to nvitop layout’, ‘group processes by GPU’, ‘don’t show processes not using GPU’. Clear reference point and priorities. AI AI’s initial design was generic TUI with process lists - didn’t reference domain-standard tool (nvitop). Only adapted after multiple user corrections. Difference Analysis: Human knew the established pattern (nvitop) and expected it. AI didn’t proactively check existing tools for UX patterns. Lesson: when building CLI tools, research category leaders first.
Implementation Level num_workers configuration fix Role Approach Human Requested explicit code change to set num_workers=8 AI Investigated actual execution context, found code default already 8, traced override to CLI parameter –num-workers 16, recommended non-invasive solution (omit the CLI flag) Difference Analysis: AI chose behavioral correction over code modification after discovering the real source of the discrepancy, avoiding unnecessary code churn
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Plan mode death spiral: In v5 visualization task, AI attempted ExitPlanMode 4+ times, all rejected. Didn’t fallback to asking user ‘what’s preventing us from proceeding?’ until very end. Should detect rejection loops earlier and switch to clarification mode. General Limitations Did not anticipate lerobot’s torch<2.7 constraint conflict when initially editing pyproject.toml; only discovered the issue after uv lock failed, then reactively added torch to override-dependencies. Could have pre-analyzed transitive dependency graphs. Used two parallel exploration agents for near-identical codebases (openpi and pi05 share the same OpenPI framework), which yielded redundant findings. A single agent with sequential exploration would have been more efficient. Initial GPU monitor design was generic, not domain-aware. Didn’t proactively check nvitop (category leader) for UX patterns. Required multiple user corrections to reach expected layout. Should research existing tools when building CLI utilities. Didn’t predict torch/torchvision version incompatibility until user provided error traceback. Could have proactively validated dependency compatibility when reading pyproject.toml (torch 2.7.1 without explicit torchvision pin was a red flag). In training speed analysis, launched two parallel Explore agents but didn’t initially compare uv.lock files (the ground truth for installed versions). First checked train.py, config.py, etc. Lock files should be priority #1 for dependency-related issues. Learnings Key Learnings K8s PID namespace isolation prevents nvidia-smi process detection. Solution: /proc//fd/ inspection for /dev/nvidia* device files + CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES env var. Monitoring tools opening all GPUs without CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES are false positives. JAX/XLA minor version upgrades (0.5.0→0.5.3) can deliver 20-30% training speedups through compiler optimizations; even patch-level framework updates merit performance audits in compute-intensive ML projects. Multi-project dependency drift is a stealth performance bug requiring periodic alignment. PyTorch/torchvision strict version pairing: torch 2.7.x requires torchvision 0.22.x, 2.6.x needs 0.21.x, etc. C++ operator registration breaks if versions mismatch. Always explicitly pin both in dependencies when using torchvision, as indirect resolution can fail. Barcode ordering pitfall in spatial transcriptomics: Cache created with sc.read_10x_h5() may have different barcode order than runtime sc.read_visium(). Index-based lookups silently map to wrong spots. Always use explicit barcode-to-index mapping: {str(b): i for i, b in enumerate(cache_barcodes)}. When plan mode repeatedly rejected, user may have unspoken blocker (environment unavailable, changed priority, technical constraint). After 2-3 rejections, switch from ’let me fix the plan’ to ‘what’s preventing us from proceeding?’. RM-IDEAL centroid computation: For a query niche, take embeddings of all spots in that niche, compute mean vector → centroid. Compare centroid to all ref section spots via cosine similarity. This compresses N-to-M comparison into 1-to-M, improving efficiency and robustness. uv’s override-dependencies is a precise tool for resolving transitive dependency conflicts without forking or patching upstream packages; particularly useful when pinning git revisions with incompatible constraints. Practical Learnings Configuration parameter provenance must be traced across all sources (code defaults, CLI args, config files, environment variables) before assuming a fix; the actual runtime value may differ from code inspection. Large-scale codebase refactoring requires phase separation: 1) Create new structure, 2) Migrate files, 3) Update code references, 4) Update docs (bulk sed acceptable for archived docs), 5) Verify final structure, 6) Cleanup old dirs. Doing code updates before file migration causes breakage. 3. Robobrain Pi training loss oscillates significantly - suspected dimension processing issue in action prediction Solution: Deep analysis revealed 14-dim real actions (right arm 6DOF+gripper + left arm 6DOF+gripper) padded to 32-dim for model architectural compatibility, but MSE loss computed over all 32 dimensions. This means 56% of loss (18/32) comes from zero-padded dimensions where model learns trivial noise→zero mapping, severely diluting gradient signals. Recommended: action_loss = mean(square(v_t[…, :14] - u_t[…, :14]))
Key Insight: Zero-padding for architectural compatibility severely dilutes gradient signals when included in loss computation - always mask loss to real dimensions only. In this case, 56% of gradient signal was wasted on learning a trivial mapping. This is a subtle but critical bug affecting training efficiency

9. Kubernetes container nvidia-smi shows [Not Found] for all GPU processes despite GPU being actively used Solution: Root cause: PID namespace isolation. nvidia-smi queries kernel driver returning host PID (e.g., 3076643), but container PID namespace has different numbering (e.g., 990465). Solution: developed gpumon.py tool combining psutil (reads container-internal /proc for process info: CPU/memory/cmdline/runtime) with nvidia-smi (GPU hardware state: VRAM/utilization/temperature), visualized via rich TUI
Key Insight: Container namespace isolation breaks cross-namespace process ID mapping. Tools must collect information within their respective namespaces then aggregate. This is why standard monitoring tools fail in containerized environments - they assume unified PID space
10. Openpi-moe serve_policy.py crashes with ‘MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID must be between 0 and 0, got 6’ Solution: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 restricts process to single GPU remapped as device 0 in CUDA context, but EGL renderer attempted to use original hardware index 6. Added os.environ.setdefault(‘MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID’, ‘0’) at script startup to align with CUDA remapping
Key Insight: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES remaps GPU indices to 0-N range for isolated process; dependent libraries (MuJoCo EGL, rendering contexts) must use remapped indices not original hardware IDs. This is subtle but critical interaction between CUDA device isolation and rendering frameworks. Always set rendering device IDs to 0 when using CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES with single GPU
11. CALVIN calvin_agent module not found despite install.sh completing successfully Solution: Discovered pip install executed in different conda environment than active univla environment. Editable installs create .egg-info directories but package availability is scoped to Python environment executing the install. Reinstalled with pip install -e . –no-deps in correct environment to avoid overwriting PyTorch
Key Insight: Editable pip installs are environment-scoped - artifacts may exist but imports fail if installation ran elsewhere. Always verify ‘which python’ matches intended environment before troubleshooting missing modules. –no-deps flag allows installing package structure without touching existing dependencies

Use –no-deps to install package structure without overwriting existing dependencies (critical for avoiding PyTorch version conflicts) MIHD clustering methods: KMeans (default, fast), mclust (R GMM via rpy2, used for STAIG, has zero-variance fallback → KMeans), Leiden (auto cluster estimation for HD data without ground truth). Spatial refinement via k-NN majority voting (refine_labels_spatial_majority) only for STAIG fusion. Selection logic based on fusion strategy and data characteristics Terminal encoding troubleshooting: Issues propagate through multiple layers (client terminal → SSH protocol → tmux → shell). When one user has problems but others don’t on same server, investigate client-side first. Comparative observation (‘works for others’) immediately narrows from shared components to user-specific config. For Windows: check code page (chcp 65001) or enable ‘Beta: Use Unicode UTF-8’ in Region Settings Conversation Summaries MIHD (Multi-modal Integration for High-Definition Spatial Omics) • Comprehensive documentation restructuring and cleanup 2026-03-10 | claude_code Five-session arc: (1) Archived 16 files, consolidated to 4 core docs (README/tutorial/plans/RESULTS). (2) Enhanced README with 145-line clustering & RM-IDEAL evaluation section (WWL message passing, Wasserstein transport, cross-section metrics). (3) Code-documentation consistency audit via 3 parallel agents - found 1 critical bug (STAIGTrainerE2E.py missing but referenced → ImportError) + 6 dimension discrepancies. (4) Project cleanup: archived 4 dead code files + 11 obsolete dirs + 34 summaries, cleaned pipeline_config.yaml, created 6 reference guides (48.9KB) - user immediately rejected as too detailed. (5) Began outputs/ reorganization (DLPFC/HD separation) but blocked by ExitPlanMode rejection loop. Also: removed staig_fusion_e2e feature from 14 files, fixed 3 critical patch query visualization bugs (barcode alignment, coordinate system mismatches). Overall: reduced documentation from 25+ files to 4, exposed critical ImportError risk, improved spatial visualization correctness, but revealed tension between AI’s comprehensive classification approach vs user’s minimal usage-oriented philosophy
RoboBrain Pi (Bimanual VLA Training) ✅ Training loss computation debugging and optimization 2026-03-10 | claude_code Three-part optimization: (1) Diagnosed loss oscillation - identified 56% MSE loss dilution from zero-padded action dimensions (14-dim real actions padded to 32-dim for model compatibility, but loss computed over all 32). Recommended masking to real dims. (2) Task completion classifier hyperparameter evaluation - found severe class imbalance (9:1 negative:positive ratio from last 20 frames of 200-frame episodes) with task_pos_weight=1.0 providing no balancing. Recommended task_loss_weight=0.1-0.15 (avoid overpowering 50-step action loss) + task_pos_weight=5.0 (address imbalance). (3) Environment troubleshooting: reinstalled uv package manager, set WandB offline mode, handled multi-user WandB account conflicts via WANDB_API_KEY env var, debugged Chinese terminal rendering (client-side UTF-8 encoding issue). Also verified task completion implementation mathematically correct (CLS token + MLP head, allow_partial=True for param mismatch). Impact: identified two critical training efficiency bugs (gradient dilution + class imbalance), provided concrete hyperparameter recommendations, resolved development environment usability issues
Error Recovery Benchmark 🔍 v5.0 architecture redesign and planning 2026-03-10 | claude_code Major architectural shift spanning multiple sessions: (1) Initial /init attempts to improve CLAUDE.md (multiple rejections before successfully adding 4 missing make targets). (2) User presented redesign vision: move from online physics-force injection to offline two-stage pipeline (collect clean trajectories → scan opportunities → quota injection → context replay). Defined 11 error types × 3 deformation dimensions (D0/D1/D2) = 26 subtypes. (3) Launched 3 parallel exploration agents to analyze v4 codebase - identified 60% reusable components (EnvWrapper, StateExtractor) vs complete rewrite needed (detectors/injectors/validators → Error Skill modules). (4) Provided detailed 24-type generation feasibility analysis: 7 high-feasibility via injection, 6 medium, 7 requiring natural capture. User indicated ’new ideas’ multiple times but rejected AI’s AskUserQuestion attempts to force decisions. Plan remains in exploratory phase - user needs flexibility while vision crystallizes. Key insight: VLA temporal context dependency requires errors to ‘grow from correct trajectories’ rather than being initial state perturbations. Offline scan+quota architecture more efficient and achieves better dataset balance
Infrastructure Tools ✅ GPU monitoring and Node.js tooling 2026-03-10 | claude_code Two infrastructure improvements: (1) Developed gpumon.py for Kubernetes containers - nvidia-smi shows [Not Found] for processes due to PID namespace isolation (host PID 3076643 ≠ container PID 990465). Solution combines psutil (container-internal process info: CPU/memory/runtime) + nvidia-smi (GPU hardware state: VRAM/utilization/temperature) with rich TUI visualization. User interrupted during layout optimization. (2) Fixed npx ccusage unable to fetch LiteLLM model pricing (fallback 46→2696 models). Root cause: Node.js v24’s fetch (undici) doesn’t respect HTTPS_PROXY by default, 1.4MB JSON takes 28s through campus proxy exceeding timeout. Solution: NODE_OPTIONS="–use-env-proxy". Impact: filled critical monitoring gap in containerized environments, restored token pricing tool functionality in restricted networks
Robot Learning Environments (CALVIN, Openpi-moe, RoboTwin) ✅ Multi-project environment setup and debugging 2026-03-10 | claude_code Systematic debugging across three projects: (1) CALVIN: fixed calvin_agent import failure - install.sh ran in wrong conda environment, reinstalled with pip install -e . –no-deps in univla environment. (2) Openpi-moe: diagnosed serve_policy.py crash - CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 remapped GPU to index 0, but MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID=6 exceeded remapped range. Fixed by setting EGL device to 0 at script startup. (3) RoboTwin: modified dataset conversion to randomly sample instructions (np.random.choice) instead of always using first instruction, matching reference implementation pattern for training diversity. Also: terminal UTF-8 encoding troubleshooting (Windows client-side code page issue), Claude Code API config file location query. Impact: unblocked three critical research pipelines, enabled robot learning experiments to proceed. All issues traced to subtle environment/configuration mismatches requiring careful layer-by-layer diagnosis
