Daily Report — 2026-03-09 Daily Overview What was done: 在三个设备上并行推进五个主要方向：(1)MIHD空间转录组项目核心算法开发（跨样本结构评估+跨模态增强架构），(2)VLA/机器人学习系统开发（文档、数据管道、理论分析），(3)gadget工具架构转型（CLI→MCP服务器），(4)跨项目集成（CalendarPro自动化工作流），(5)研究工具增强（多数据源+生产级日志） How it was done: 使用WWL图核建立空间结构评估基准、设计基于空间邻域的cross-attention机制（并解决CUDA硬件兼容性问题）、系统性文献调研foundation model性能、创建MCP协议包装层暴露工具、通过conda subprocess实现跨环境调用、扩展research_scout到三个学术数据源（arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed）、建立生产级日志系统 Impact: 建立可复用的跨样本空间评估工具链和跨模态增强方法、揭示scGPT foundation model不如传统方法的关键发现、使gadget工具可被所有AI agent发现和使用、实现CalendarPro自动化每日研究和总结工作流、将研究覆盖范围从arXiv单源扩展到三大学术来源并建立完整的错误追踪机制 DCC What was done: MIHD空间转录组项目全流程工作：跨样本RM-IDEAL实验与可视化（151673-151508/151676）、CrossModalEnhancer设计与实现（含多轮CUDA调试）、CLAUDE.md维护、scGPT文献调研 How it was done: 在HPC环境运行大规模实验（3639 spots），使用conda环境管理+多轮CUDA错误调试（最终采用mini-batch workaround和CPU训练fallback）、执行并行web search和WebFetch获取benchmark数据、生成空间热力图可视化 Impact: 产出完整的跨样本评估报告（7张空间热力图+中文技术文档）、交付可工作的CrossModalEnhancer模块（已集成到Fusion.py）、获得scGPT性能的关键洞察（zero-shot弱于传统方法）、识别PyTorch CUDA版本兼容性问题并建立CPU训练fallback流程 TzJsDesktop What was done: 全栈集成与工具增强工作：创建workspace文档（5个项目）、gadget MCP服务器实现（9个工具）、CalendarPro-gadget集成桥接（13个测试）、research_scout增强（日志系统+多数据源，500+行新增代码）、文档维护更新 How it was done: 使用并行agent编排进行代码库探索、系统性逐文件实现并在每阶段验证、通过subprocess隔离实现跨repo集成、实现全面测试（import检查、CLI验证、日志文件验证）、使用urllib.request实现零依赖API客户端 Impact: 建立统一开发环境与清晰文档、使gadget工具可被工作区所有AI agent访问、实现CalendarPro自动化每日研究工作流、将research_scout从arXiv单源转变为三源系统并具备生产级可观测性、保持所有工具文档与代码同步 tianhe What was done: 多VLA/机器人项目推进：UniVLA文档创建、CALVIN环境故障排查、RoboTwin→LeRobot数据转换、Pi0 flow matching理论分析 How it was done: 创建全面的CLAUDE.md（build/test命令、架构概览）、诊断DNS解析失败（Kubernetes环境）、实现convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py（14-DOF，50 episodes，11,459 frames）、详解条件flow matching（Beta(1.5,1)时间采样+Euler积分） Impact: 建立复杂VLA代码库的文档标准、支持demo_clean数据复用于pi0.5训练、阐明flow matching实现细节用于机器人动作生成 完成MIHD空间转录组核心功能（跨样本RM-IDEAL评估、CrossModalEnhancer跨模态增强、scGPT文献调研）、推进多个VLA/机器人项目（UniVLA文档、RoboTwin数据转换、flow matching分析）、实现gadget工具MCP服务器化与CalendarPro集成、增强research_scout多数据源支持
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Run 151673-151508 cross-sample RM-IDEAL benchmark — Execute benchmark comparing spatial niche structure similarity between two DLPFC sections using PCA+UNI2+STAIG_fusion embeddings. Generated detailed correlation metrics (Spearman ρ) for all 7 tissue layers in both directions. ✅ Implement CrossModalEnhancer module — Created models/CrossModalEnhancer.py (~350 lines) with CrossModalAttentionBlock and CrossModalEnhancer classes supporting 3 modes (gene→image, image→gene, bidirectional). Integrated into Fusion.py dispatcher. ✅ Debug CUDA/cuBLAS compatibility issues — Resolved PyTorch 2.9/CUDA 12.9 cuBLAS bug on RTX 2080 Ti causing crashes on large matrix operations. Final solution: mini-batch (512 samples) InfoNCE loss to avoid N×N full-matrix backward. ✅ Research scGPT clustering benchmark literature — Conducted systematic web search and literature extraction to evaluate scGPT and scGPT-spatial clustering performance. Found zero-shot scGPT underperforms traditional methods (PCA, scVI) and scGPT-spatial lacks independent SOTA comparisons. ✅ Create CLAUDE.md for UniVLA repository — Comprehensive documentation covering build commands (torchrun, accelerate), linting (black/ruff), training stages (LAM, VLA pretraining, finetuning), evaluation (LIBERO, CALVIN, R2R, SimplerEnv), and architecture overview (VLM→PrismaticVLM→OpenVLA, vision/LLM backbones, action tokenization, draccus config, RLDS pipeline) ✅ Refactor MCP tools to return content — Modified 5 MCP tools (summarize_export/merge, research_report, benchmark_run/report) to return full content (markdown/JSON) with optional save parameter, bypassing cmd_* wrappers to control file I/O ✅ Transform gadget tools into MCP server — Created mcp_server.py exposing 9 tools (summarize_export/merge/list_dates, research_search/report/list_projects, benchmark_run/report/system_info) with stdout capture and SystemExit handling ✅ Integrate gadget tools into CalendarPro — Built external tool integration layer (src/tools/) with async subprocess runner via conda run, implemented ResearchScoutTool and DailySummaryTool, created background services with cron scheduling, wrote 13 unit tests ✅ Add bioRxiv and PubMed support to research_scout — Implemented search_biorxiv() and search_pubmed() with urllib.request (zero new dependencies), added multi-source orchestration with unified caching, extended CLI with –source flag, generalized paper_id/arxiv_id handling with backward compatibility ✅ Generate RM-IDEAL spatial heatmap visualizations — Modified _viz_rm_ideal.py to generate 7 PNG files (one per niche label) showing ground truth, RM-IDEAL scores, and embedding similarity side-by-side for 151673↔151508. ✅ Write comprehensive cross-sample patch query documentation (Chinese) — Created docs/CROSS_SAMPLE_PATCH_QUERY_REPORT.md with complete methodology (WWL graph kernel, Wasserstein distance, two-path evaluation), code paths, data flow, results analysis, and reproduction guide. ❌ MIHD cross-sample patch visualization with STAIG fusion — Implement 151673→151676 patch query using UNI2+PCA+STAIG_fusion embeddings and visualization. Blocked by GPU CUDA compatibility issue (PyTorch 2.9.0+cu129 vs CUDA 13.1 driver incompatibility). CPU training started as workaround. ✅ Convert RoboTwin demo_clean to LeRobot format — Created convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py script to convert 50 episodes (11,459 frames) from demo_clean (14-DOF HDF5 format) to LeRobot dataset structure at RoboTwin/data/place_dual_shoes_lerobot ✅ Add logging system to research_scout — Implemented RotatingFileHandler (5MB, 3 backups), migrated ~77 print statements to logger, added empty-field and zero-score warnings, enhanced error handling in API calls and cache operations ✅ Design CrossModalEnhancer architecture — Architected cross-modal enhancement module using spatial k-NN neighbors as K/V sequence to avoid single-token attention degradation. Designed symmetric InfoNCE loss and residual connections. ✅ Analyze Pi0 flow matching implementation — Explained conditional flow matching in pi0.py: linear interpolation path x_t = t·noise + (1-t)·actions, Beta(1.5,1) time sampling, MSE loss ‖v_t - u_t‖², Euler method sampling with 10 steps from t=1→0 ✅ Analyze CALVIN training data pipeline — Detailed explanation of how finetune_calvin.py uses DiskCalvinDataset to load auto_lang_ann.npy, episode_*.npz files, extract rgb_static/rel_actions/robot_obs, pass through LAM encoder and VLA with ActionDecoder Implementation & Fixes ✅ Create CALVIN dataset extraction script — Created extract_eval_files.py to extract only eval-needed files (validation/.hydra/merged_config.yaml, metadata) from full dataset, reducing size from 1.3GB to 600KB ✅ Create workspace-level CLAUDE.md — Analyzed 5 independent projects (CalendarPro, OCR, gadget, get-shit-done, openclaw) and created unified CLAUDE.md with quick reference commands and architecture highlights ✅ Update CLAUDE.md documentation for research_scout.py — Identified and documented previously undocumented features: author search (–author flag, search_arxiv_author), init –from-overview (LLM-based project creation), updated line count from ~2500 to ~2650, added author search cache pattern ✅ Update CLAUDE.md with cross-modal and RM-IDEAL content — Added CrossModalEnhancer to core modules, RM-IDEAL benchmark commands to common commands, cross-sample documentation references, and enriched utils descriptions (rm_ideal.py, niche_utils.py). ✅ Streamline CLAUDE.md module listings — Condensed Architecture section from ~30 lines of per-module function lists to ~10 lines focusing on non-obvious module relationships. Preserved all critical architectural patterns. ❌ Troubleshoot CALVIN environment installation — Diagnosed DNS resolution failure (Errno -3) preventing pip from reaching pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn or pypi.org in Kubernetes environment. Identified proxy config (http_proxy=localhost:9997) but didn’t resolve issue. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. PyTorch 2.9/CUDA 12.9 cuBLAS bug on RTX 2080 Ti causes crashes during backward pass of large matrix operations (3639×3639 logits for contrastive loss). Multiple architecture rewrites attempted before identifying root cause. Solution: Redesigned contrastive loss to use mini-batch sampling (512 samples per batch) to avoid full N×N matrix computation. Added gradient clipping and LayerNorm for stability. For cross-sample visualization task, switched to CPU training as fallback when GPU incompatibility confirmed (PyTorch 2.9.0+cu129 vs CUDA 13.1 driver).
Key Insight: GPU hardware/driver compatibility issues cannot be solved through model architecture alone—algorithmic workarounds at the loss function level are necessary. Version mismatches between PyTorch CUDA build and driver version cause sporadic ‘illegal memory access’ errors that pass basic tests but fail in complex training loops. CPU fallback is valid strategy for medium-scale training (3460 spots).
2. MCP server stdout corruption: gadget tools use print() extensively, but MCP uses stdout as JSON-RPC transport Solution: Created capture_stdout() context manager to redirect print() output, wrapped all tool invocations with _safe_call() that captures stdout/stderr and converts SystemExit to RuntimeError, returned captured logs in JSON response’s _logs field
Key Insight: When integrating existing CLI tools into protocol-based systems, stdout isolation is critical. Context managers provide clean, reversible redirection without modifying original code
3. research_scout hardcoded arxiv_id throughout codebase, blocking multi-source expansion Solution: Introduced paper_id as canonical ID with source field, kept arxiv_id as backward-compatible alias, created _paper_id()/_paper_url() helpers, updated prompts to use paper_id, made merge logic check both fields when matching LLM responses
Key Insight: When generalizing from single-source to multi-source, introduce new abstraction while maintaining old field as alias. Helper functions centralize ID/URL logic, making future source additions trivial
4. RM-IDEAL correlation low for Layer_3 (ρ=-0.21/-0.36) in 151673-151508 cross-sample query, while Layer_1/4/5 show high positive correlation (ρ>0.4) Solution: Analysis revealed Layer_3 is the largest DLPFC layer with high internal heterogeneity, making embeddings unable to capture unified spatial structure. Smaller, unique layers with clear boundaries (Layer_1: ρ=0.62, Layer_4: ρ=0.66) perform best.
Key Insight: Tissue layer size and internal heterogeneity critically affect embedding quality for spatial structure capture. Distinct, boundary-clear layers yield better cross-sample matching than large heterogeneous regions.
5. Single-token cross-attention degenerates to linear projection when each spot has only one gene vector and one image vector Solution: Used spatial k-NN neighbors to construct K/V sequences, allowing cross-attention to operate on neighborhood context. Reused QFormerFusion’s batched neighbor construction infrastructure.
Key Insight: Spatial transcriptomics data provides natural sequential context through neighborhood structure. Leveraging spatial adjacency enables meaningful attention even without temporal or batch dimensions.
6. RoboTwin demo_clean data (14-DOF, directory-based) incompatible with existing LeRobot conversion script (16-DOF, zip-based) Solution: Created new script convert_robotwin_democlean_to_lerobot.py: read directly from data/instructions directories, change ACTION_DIM/STATE_DIM to 14, use LeRobotDataset.create() with root parameter instead of HF_LEROBOT_HOME env var hack
Key Insight: Robot data format variations (DOF count, storage format) require tailored conversion scripts. Directory structure and HDF5 key names are project-specific.
7. Empty motivation/innovation_point fields in research_scout screening stage due to silent LLM JSON parsing failures Solution: Added empty-field detection after _screen_papers() and _screen_papers_chunked(), logged warnings with count and DEBUG-level per-paper details, enhanced _try_repair_result() to log raw response preview when repair fails
Key Insight: Silent .get() fallbacks mask data quality issues. Explicit validation and logging at aggregation points (after batch processing) provides actionable debugging information without cluttering per-item logic
8. Initial CrossModalEnhancer design outputting original modality dimension (1536d for image) triggered cuBLAS GEMM failure on 128→1536 projection Solution: Revised architecture to output in hidden_dim space (128d) instead, avoiding problematic large-matrix projections. Used projection heads for contrastive loss while keeping core output compact.
Key Insight: Engineering constraints (GPU bugs) can force architectural decisions that differ from ideal semantic design. Practical systems must balance theoretical elegance with implementation robustness.
General Issues 9. FastMCP constructor rejected ‘version’ parameter on user’s conda environment Solution: Used inspect.signature() to check actual constructor, removed version parameter and passed only ’name’ and ‘instructions’, let mcp library handle versioning internally
Key Insight: SDK APIs evolve. When integration fails, inspect actual signatures rather than relying on documentation or assumptions. The mcp library’s FastMCP API changed between versions
10. CLAUDE.md documentation was outdated - missing author search feature, init –from-overview capability, and incorrect line count Solution: Systematically explored codebase using Grep to find undocumented functions (search_arxiv_author, create_project_from_overview), verified line count via wc -l, then made 6 targeted edits to update documentation sections (Usage, Code Organization, Key Implementation Details, File Layout)
Key Insight: Documentation drift is inevitable in actively developed tools; systematic code exploration (grep for patterns like –author, –from-overview) is more reliable than manual review
11. DNS resolution failure in Kubernetes pod preventing pip from accessing PyPI mirrors Solution: Diagnosed issue (nameserver 10.96.0.10, proxy localhost:9997), but didn’t resolve - likely cluster-level networking config issue
Key Insight: Kubernetes cluster DNS and egress proxy configurations can break standard pip workflows. May need cluster admin intervention or use of cached wheels.
12. conda run with –no-banner flag failed on user’s conda version with ‘unrecognized arguments’ error Solution: Removed –no-banner flag entirely. Conda run works without it, and banner output goes to stderr (doesn’t corrupt stdout). Tested with conda run -n calendarpro python -c ‘print(test)’ successfully
Key Insight: Optional flags that improve output cleanliness but aren’t functionally required should be omitted if they risk compatibility issues. Banner in stderr doesn’t affect stdout-based protocols
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level MCP tool design philosophy Role Approach Human Insight that summarize/research are ‘Claude Code enhancement skills’ - should return content, not just write files. Explicitly framed as architectural principle. AI Initially implemented tools as file-writing scripts with metadata returns, not recognizing the in-context usage pattern Difference Analysis: Human user understood the tool-assistant interaction model and desired workflow. AI implemented based on existing script patterns without considering integration context.
CalendarPro-gadget integration approach: MCP vs. subprocess vs. shared code Role Approach Human User explicitly chose subprocess + conda run despite AI’s MCP recommendation. User understood that gadget tools are monolithic CLI scripts (2800+ lines) and preferred zero gadget code modification with clear separation via subprocess boundaries AI AI initially recommended MCP server as primary approach, viewing it as ‘cleanest’ due to native tool discovery. Only after user clarification did AI fully commit to subprocess approach with detailed ToolRunner design Difference Analysis: Human prioritized maintainability and separation of concerns (zero cross-repo dependencies) over ‘cleanliness’ of protocol. AI initially favored protocol elegance. Human’s choice reflects pragmatic systems thinking about long-term evolution of independent codebases
GPU vs CPU training decision after CUDA errors Role Approach Human Immediately questioned ‘Why use CPU training? Can run on GPU!’ - prioritized using faster hardware and debugging GPU issues AI After encountering CUDA errors, conservatively switched to CPU training to avoid failures without deeply investigating GPU problem root cause Difference Analysis: Human strongly prefers optimal performance (GPU) and pushes to debug issues; AI tends toward error avoidance with safer fallback (CPU). Human intuition that GPU should work outweighs initial failure signals.
CrossModalEnhancer output dimension design Role Approach Human Original plan specified output dimension matching original modality (1536d for image) to preserve semantic space, prioritizing theoretical soundness AI After encountering cuBLAS bug on large matrix projection, pragmatically revised to output in hidden_dim space (128d) to avoid hardware constraints Difference Analysis: Human maintains ideal architectural design from theoretical perspective. AI adapts architecture based on discovered implementation constraints, prioritizing ‘working code’ over ’elegant design’ when they conflict.
Data file relocation strategy Role Approach Human Directly suggested ‘你直接把…剪切过来就好了’ (just move it over) - identified that correct data already exists, use filesystem move AI Planned to delete old data and regenerate from scratch - more conservative but wasteful when correct data already available Difference Analysis: Human quickly recognized existing data validity and chose direct filesystem operation; AI defaulted to regeneration for correctness guarantee. Human efficiency vs AI caution.
Implementation Level scGPT benchmark research methodology Role Approach Human Posed broad question: ‘search for existing papers’ views on scGPT and clustering benchmarking’, expecting comprehensive synthesis AI Decomposed into multiple targeted keyword searches (zero-shot, ARI/NMI metrics, specific comparisons), executed parallel WebSearch and WebFetch, then synthesized findings with structured summary Difference Analysis: Human frames questions at conceptual level (‘what do people think?’). AI translates to executable search strategies with specific metrics, datasets, and comparison baselines, then reconstructs the conceptual answer.
RM-IDEAL visualization requirement Role Approach Human Immediately asked ‘where is your visualization?’ when noticing benchmark script only produced numerical CSV outputs, expecting visual outputs as standard deliverable AI Initially ran benchmark and reported numerical results (Spearman ρ, Precision@K) without generating visualizations, prioritizing quantitative metrics over visual outputs Difference Analysis: Human emphasizes visual validation and presentation-ready outputs as integral to analysis completion. AI defaults to numerical correctness and assumes visualization is a separate optional step.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Insufficient CUDA debugging experience led to 4 architecture rewrites (gather neighbors→project, project→gather, output in hidden_dim, mini-batch loss) before identifying cuBLAS large-matrix bug as root cause. Failed to recognize known GPU driver compatibility issues upfront. Originally designed MCP tools as file-writing scripts returning metadata, not recognizing the pattern that tools should return content for Claude Code to consume directly When encountering CUDA errors, conservatively switched to CPU training without sufficient investigation of GPU compatibility issues. Multiple failed attempts before recognizing PyTorch CUDA build vs driver version mismatch. Initially didn’t recognize that torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) conflicts with PyG scatter operations on CUDA, attempting multiple workarounds before identifying the core issue Failed to anticipate stdout/stderr isolation requirement for MCP server until seeing the architecture context. Only recognized the issue when designing the wrapper layer, not when initially exploring gadget CLI tools General Limitations When user proposed large refactoring task (‘organize all docs, merge duplicate functions, archive unused code’), launched 3 parallel Explore agents but session was interrupted before agents returned, demonstrating poor handling of long-running multi-agent workflows across session boundaries. WebFetch encountered 403 errors on multiple key papers (bioRxiv scGPT-spatial preprint, ResearchGate links) without attempting fallback strategies like archive.org snapshots or requesting user to manually download PDFs, limiting depth of literature analysis. Did not proactively generate visualizations when running RM-IDEAL benchmark, requiring user to explicitly ask ‘where is the visualization?’. Failed to anticipate that spatial analysis naturally demands visual validation. When implementing bioRxiv/PubMed support, did not proactively question whether user wanted to modify 2600-line monolithic file vs. refactor into modular package. Directly implemented as requested without offering architectural alternatives DNS troubleshooting session ended without resolution - didn’t fully explore cluster networking configs or suggest alternative wheel distribution methods Learnings Key Learnings RM-IDEAL uses WWL (Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman) graph kernel to compute spatial niche matching: iterative neighbor label hashing → node feature distributions → optimal transport (Wasserstein distance) between subgraphs. Provides topology-based ground truth for evaluating embedding quality. Cross-attention on single tokens degenerates to linear projection. Spatial transcriptomics provides natural solution: k-NN neighbors form K/V sequences that encode neighborhood context. This pattern (spatial neighbors as attention context) is broadly applicable to spatial omics architectures. PyTorch 2.9 + CUDA 12.9 on RTX 2080 Ti has cuBLAS bug causing illegal memory access on large matrix operations (gemm failures at specific shapes like 128→1536, backward on N×N where N>3500). Workaround: mini-batch processing to keep matrices small. PyTorch CUDA build version (e.g., cu129) must match GPU driver CUDA version. scGPT foundation model underperforms traditional methods (PCA, scVI, Harmony) in zero-shot clustering benchmarks (Genome Biology 2025). AvgBIO scores on Pancreas/PBMC datasets show scGPT ~0.52-0.60 vs. HVG baseline ~0.60-0.77. scGPT-spatial requires fine-tuning and only compares to weak baselines (SpaGCN, stLearn), not SOTA (GraphST, STAGATE). Independent benchmarks more reliable than original paper claims. Conditional Flow Matching for robot action generation: learns vector field u_t from noise to actions using linear interpolation path x_t = t·noise + (1-t)·actions, Beta(1.5,1) time sampling for stability near noise endpoint, Euler integration with 10 steps for inference. Key insight: time conditioning via sinusoidal embeddings + MLP (or adaRMS for Pi0.5). MCP tool design principle: tools for Claude Code should return content by default (markdown reports, JSON data), with optional file persistence. Learning Insights Architecture- Three standard checks after large-scale implementation: (1) Whether the new service is connected to the startup chain; (2) Whether cross-layer updates (IntentType→route→handler→service) are consistent; (3) Whether silent exceptions (except: pass) hide runtime errors. Passing tests is a necessary condition rather than a sufficient one, and defects in the integration layer can only be detected through end-to-end verification. Before designing an Agentic system, actively study mature similar projects—OpenClaw’s EventBus/CronScheduler/Plugin registration pattern and GSD’s STATE.md persistent memory/multi-Agent context isolation are highly reusable architectural patterns; related fixes should be merged into a single change rather than implemented in stages to avoid code rework. apply_tree(strict=False) is an implicit risk in ML training pipelines: if new training features that need normalization are not updated simultaneously with the norm_stats calculation script, it will cause silent scale mismatch affecting training quality; the mismatch records of AI systems are free annotation data, and automatically returning them as utterance augmentations can achieve low-cost continuous self-improvement. Two-stage information processing (rough screening + fine evaluation) is better than single-stage full processing in terms of token efficiency and analysis depth: Stage 1 focuses on problem relevance/innovation/authority of source (30 seconds judgment), Stage 2 focuses on key insights driving effects rather than engineering details, and critically examines the baseline and metrics chosen by the author. Debugging Analysis of the root cause of low GPU utilization in VLA inference: action chunking makes inference calls sparse (about 8 calls per trial × 2.5 s/200 s total time = 10%); multi-client concurrency does not improve strict serial inference throughput. The correct optimization direction is BatchedVLAServer batch inference + independent deployment on multiple GPUs. Diagnostic path for BC-RNN SR=0%; first check whether the observation key name/dimensions match training, then use historical training logs to distinguish “evaluation bug” vs “training already failed” to avoid misdiagnosis as model capability issues; bare except is the most common debugging obstacle in rendering/simulation frameworks, and should be immediately changed to except Exception: traceback.print_exc(). Parameter settings should be driven by experiments rather than intuitive estimation: first collect a small amount of data to verify the actual distribution before setting thresholds; incorrect estimation of key parameters (such as distance threshold, driving version) will cause the entire batch of data to be invalid or installation failure. Tools 4-way parallel sub-Agents + the main thread handling non-parallelizable parts can control the large-scale migration of 65 symlink files within a single session; the key is dividing agent task boundaries based on non-overlapping file sets; BatchedVLAServer parallel evaluation (44 minutes/9 tasks) saves about 80% time compared to serial execution. Standard solution for fixing headless HPC nodes’ Vulkan/EGL rendering: extract a user-space GL library from the NVIDIA official .run package that strictly matches the kernel version (no need to install kernel modules), inject it via VK_ICD_FILENAMES/__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES/LD_LIBRARY_PATH, without root; EGL/Vulkan device configuration is independent of CUDA; normal CUDA performance does not mean Vulkan is available. The arXiv comment field is a de facto conference acceptance announcement area; by searching the full text with all:"CVPR 2025" and filtering after comment, a specialized search for conference papers can be achieved; au:"Author Name" AND (kw1 OR kw2) is an effective way to track specific researchers’ latest work in the system. Domain Knowledge Learning-based fusion (QFormer) is significantly better than simple concatenation: scGPT 512d representations themselves are valuable but require non-linear projection to be fully activated (+117% vs scGPT-only); STAIG’s gene encoder is decoupled from GNN training, and differences between documents and code can only be found through code tracking; zero-shot capabilities are the core competitive point against methods that rely on training. Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning reaches 95–100% on Stack-like tasks (overall 58.9%), while BC-RNN fails completely (0%); task complexity (multiple steps, fine operations) is the main factor determining the success rate gap between VLA and traditional sequence modeling; the Pi0.5 LoRA mode also requires at least 2 × 80GB GPUs (FSDP is a necessary prerequisite). AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:
✓ Multi-layer code tracking (3–4 call stacks) accurately identifies the facts of STAIG architecture, providing evidence at the line-level, which is more reliable than document analysis. ✓ 4-way parallel Agents divide tasks based on non-overlapping file sets, enabling the large-scale migration of 65 symlink files to be completed within a single session. ✓ Systematic analysis of sacct step timestamps correctly excludes misjudgments caused by AI operations leading to NODE_FAIL, establishing a causal evidence chain. ✓ Actively clarify ambiguous requirements by AskUserQuestion (whether author search needs LLM evaluation), precisely transforming product requirements into engineering solutions. ✓ Systematically verify the correctness of experimental configurations (source of base model) with three layers of evidence, outperforming intuitive judgment. Limitations:
✗ No verification that new features are connected to the system startup chain after implementation; only relying on unit tests omits integration layer checks (BackgroundCoordinator not started). ✗ No active study of mature industry implementations when designing Agentic systems; need user clarification before referring to OpenClaw/GSD architectural patterns. ✗ Parameter settings lack experimental validation (τ=0.10m purely estimated), resulting in all critical_region labeled data being 0. ✗ Research contributions describe technical details rather than competitive advantages; the differentiated positioning of zero-shot needs user clarification. ✗ Initial task scheduling is conservative and serial, without actively identifying opportunities for parallel execution of long-term GPU tasks + lightweight visualization tasks. ✗ Lack of necessary resume/fresh-start intent confirmation before resource-intensive operations (GPU training); misstarting fresh-start overwrites checkpoints. summary: This week, across three devices—DCC, Tianhe Supercomputing, and TzJsDesktop—four main projects were advanced in parallel: space transcriptome research, robot operation training/assessment, AI personal assistant, and paper management tools. The MIHD project completed the full set of fusion experiments for scGPT+UNI2 (QFormer avg ARI=0.370, +117% vs scGPT-only) and established a zero-shot cross-sample assessment framework; Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning achieved a total success rate of 58.9%, fully surpassing BC-RNN (0%), thereby quantitatively validating the advantages of the VLA model; CalendarPro achieved a structural leap from passive response to active decision-making (321 tests all passed), while exposing and fixing critical integration defects such as the BackgroundCoordinator never starting; gadget Research Scout was built from scratch to production-ready, completing a two-stage LLM paper evaluation pipeline in a single day and providing three research direction suggestions for the first time; error_recovery_benchmark completed the full cleanup of 65 symlinks and the infrastructure for visualizing error scenarios in MP4 format. The most important engineering experience this week is: test passing ≠ system availability (the integration layer must be verified independently), and before designing an agentic system, it is necessary to actively study the architectural patterns of mature similar projects.

Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Design critical region annotation methodology for VLA — Designed distance-based heuristics with gripper-state filtering to annotate critical regions for 10 RoboTwin manipulation tasks ✅ Implement critical region annotation system — Modified _base_task.py and 10 task files to inject critical_region labels and ee_target_distances into observation data ✅ Implement author search feature (–author flag) — Added search_arxiv_author() function, updated cache functions to support author parameter, modified cmd_search() and cmd_report() for author search mode, added CLI arguments to search and report subparsers 🔄 Plan symlink removal for error_recovery_benchmark — Mapped 65 symlinks and created comprehensive refactoring plan to eliminate backward-compatibility technical debt Implementation & Fixes ✅ Generate visualization videos for error benchmark — Created 9 MP4 videos from coffee and stack task error scenes, covering natural failures (grasp_miss, premature_release, overshoot) and injection errors (tip_over) ✅ Update research CLAUDE.md documentation — Corrected line count (~1870 → ~2000), documented –language flag, added dedup early-stop feature (known_ids + 5-consecutive-known), updated section numbering ✅ Fix RoboTwin rendering device error — Added Vulkan/EGL environment variables to collect_data.sh to enable headless GPU rendering ✅ Locate episode_num configuration — Identified episode_num field in task_config YAML files controlling data collection count ✅ Review CLAUDE.md documentation — Validated existing CLAUDE.md is production-quality with no changes needed Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. VLA models fail consistently at specific task phases (imprecise pressing in click tasks, failed grasping/placing in manipulation tasks) Solution: Designed distance-based heuristics with gripper-state filtering to annotate binary ‘critical region’ labels during data collection, enabling cls token classifier training
Key Insight: Systematic VLA failures at task-critical phases can be addressed by training a binary classifier to predict when the agent is in high-stakes regions requiring extra caution
2. All critical_region labels were 0 after data collection, indicating threshold (0.10m) was too conservative Solution: Added get_ee_target_distances() method to record raw EE-to-target distances for all tasks, enabling empirical threshold tuning
Key Insight: When designing ML data labeling heuristics, always log raw features first before committing to threshold values for labels
General Issues 3. SAPIEN renderer fails with ‘RuntimeError: failed to find a rendering device’ in headless environment Solution: Added three Vulkan/EGL environment variables to collect_data.sh (VK_ICD_FILENAMES, __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES, LD_LIBRARY_PATH) pointing to nvidia_libs directory
Key Insight: Headless GPU servers require explicit Vulkan ICD and EGL vendor configuration to locate NVIDIA rendering drivers, even when nvidia-smi works correctly
4. SSH commands failed with ‘No such file or directory’ when running visualization script from remote shell Solution: Changed from relative paths to absolute paths for both project root and Python script, ensuring working directory was correctly set before execution
Key Insight: SSH does not inherit working directory; must use ‘cd /absolute/path && command’ or provide absolute paths to all file arguments
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Critical region annotation threshold selection Role Approach Human User empirically discovered 0.10m threshold was too small after collecting data, requested distance logging to tune threshold based on actual data distribution AI AI chose 0.10m threshold based on code analysis of existing pre_grasp_dis patterns without empirical validation Difference Analysis: Human took iterative empirical approach informed by actual data; AI made theoretical choice based on code patterns. Human correctly identified need for observability (distance logging) before finalizing heuristic parameters
Implementation planning for author search feature Role Approach Human Provided complete implementation plan upfront with specific line numbers, function signatures, mutual exclusion checks, and verification commands AI Initially wanted to explore codebase first, ask clarifying questions via AskUserQuestion, then launch Plan agent to design the feature Difference Analysis: Human preferred directive top-down approach with detailed spec, AI preferred exploratory bottom-up approach with question-driven discovery
Symlink removal refactoring scope Role Approach Human User requested complete removal of all 65 symlinks to eliminate technical debt, focusing on end goal of clean structure AI AI comprehensively mapped symlink dependency graph and designed surgical refactoring plan with careful import rewrites to minimize breakage Difference Analysis: Human focused on strategic goal (eliminate technical debt); AI focused on tactical execution (safe migration path). Both necessary - human sets direction, AI ensures safe implementation
AI Limitations Critical Limitations AI initially chose critical region threshold (0.10m) based on code patterns without empirical validation, resulting in all labels being 0. Required iterative correction to add distance logging for proper threshold tuning based on actual data distribution General Limitations AI required multiple exploration rounds with subagents to fully map the symlink dependency graph (65 total symlinks across root, scripts/, and nested output directories with complex import patterns) Failed to correctly handle SSH working directory context, requiring multiple attempts to construct command with proper absolute paths Learnings Key Learnings For VLA training on manipulation tasks, binary classification of ‘critical regions’ using distance-based heuristics + gripper-state filtering can systematically address failure patterns at task-critical phases (pressing, grasping, placing) arXiv API supports author queries via ‘au:“Author Name”’ syntax, can be combined with keyword filters using AND/OR operators, and uses relevance-based sorting for author searches When designing ML data collection heuristics, always implement observability (log raw features) before committing to threshold-based labels. Empirical tuning requires actual data distribution visibility research_scout.py now supports three distinct search modes with different caching strategies: keyword/category (date-sorted, lookback-filtered), conference (relevance-sorted, comment-filtered), author (relevance-sorted, no post-filter) Symlink-based backward compatibility creates complex dependency graphs requiring comprehensive mapping before refactoring (65 symlinks × multiple import patterns = high breakage risk without careful planning) Practical Learnings MuJoCo visualization can be generated from pre-saved .npz scene data without re-running full policy rollouts, enabling efficient post-hoc video generation Headless GPU rendering in SAPIEN requires three Vulkan/EGL environment variables: VK_ICD_FILENAMES, __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing to NVIDIA driver library directory Conversation Summaries gadget/research ✅ Implement author search feature and update documentation 03:25:22.536 | claude_code User provided detailed implementation plan for adding –author flag to enable searching papers by specific researchers. Assistant implemented search_arxiv_author() function, updated cache layer to support author parameter with dedicated cache files, modified both search and report commands to handle author mode with mutual exclusion checks against –conference. UNIX uses bash for update.sh), replaced 3 hardcoded bash calls in daily_summary.py and 1 in monthly_summary.py ✅ Batch generation of February historical reports (20+ days) — Used gadget/summarize tool on TzJsDesktop to generate structured reports for 20+ historical dates from 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-06, covering multiple key sessions across MIHD, ErrorRecoveryBenchmark, CalendarPro, gadget, DesktopVideo projects, processing cross-device (DCC, MacBook, tianhe, TzJsDesktop) conversation data through export/merge two-stage process ✅ Add language configuration system to research_scout.py — Implemented full language support: _DEFAULT_LANGUAGE constant, _language_instruction() helper, {language_instruction} in 3 prompt templates, language parameter through entire pipeline, –language CLI flag, config.json integration ✅ Implement init –from-overview feature — Added LLM-driven reverse initialization: create_project_from_overview() function, OVERVIEW_EXTRACT_PROMPT for parsing, CLI args (–from-overview, –api, –timeout) ✅ Multi-task BC-RNN error scenario generation — Generated error scenarios using injection+natural_capture modes for 6 tasks’ BC-RNN models in training environment, added –task parameter to 1c_generate_from_policy.py for automatic checkpoint/dataset/task_config parsing, fixed 2_visualize_scene.py is_natural guard and load_demo_actions extension, completed 191 error scenarios total ✅ Robot Manipulation 3D-MVP paper deep evaluation — Deep analysis of arXiv 2406.18158v2 (3D-MVP: 3D Multiview Pretraining for Robotic Manipulation), extracted three key highlights: ①3D-aware pretraining significantly improves downstream generalization through Objaverse large-scale dataset, ②modular decoupling of visual encoder and action decoder enables modular pretraining, ③multi-view input provides robust 3D scene understanding through implicit triangulation. Output includes relevance=4/novelty=4/inspiration=4 scores and benchmark design suggestions ✅ Implement arxiv_id deduplication and early-stop in search — Added _load_known_arxiv_ids() to scan cache, modified search_arxiv() with consecutive-known counter (stops after 5 consecutive cached papers), threaded known_ids through cmd_search and cmd_report Implementation & Fixes ✅ Generate and improve CLAUDE.md for research/ directory — Analyzed 1871-line research_scout.py codebase, created comprehensive CLAUDE.md with code organization section (0-10 sections), parameters table, key implementation details, and pipeline function names ✅ Desktop Video transparency bug fix and volume sync — Removed webView.setValue(false, forKey: “drawsBackground”) to fix WKWebView scrollbar track transparency, added .background(Color(nsColor: .windowBackgroundColor)) to ScrollView in AppMainWindow.swift to fix control panel slider transparency, removed isWebContent guard in setVolume() to show volume/mute controls for all content types, fixed applyWebSettings to check isGlobalMuted for volume sync when switching content ✅ Windows environment Hugo installation and configuration — daily_summary.py merge step failed calling Hugo deployment with ‘hugo’ is not recognized error. Installed version 0.157.0 via winget install Hugo.Hugo.Extended, needed to restart PowerShell for PATH environment variable to take effect, finally successfully executed Hugo build and deploy ✅ Rename all ‘周报’ references to ‘日报’ — Systematic text replacement across 12+ locations: function names (generate_weekly_report → generate_daily_report), docstrings, UI messages, markdown headers Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. BC-RNN RP(0.003) abnormally lower than Random RP(0.020), evaluation results completely unreasonable Solution: Code review found 4 bugs jointly causing metric distortion: demo_len=0 broke SPL, trigger_step=0 further broke SPL, transport always False capped RP at 0.5, successful episode RP not 1.0 caused baseline deviation. Fixed collector.py:487 field name demo_length→demo_len, collector.py:488 changed to read from scene.dataset for trigger_step, env_wrapper.py added _get_target_pos() runtime dynamic target position retrieval, collector.py added if success: rp=1.0
Key Insight: Evaluation metric distortion is often not a single bug but cascading chain of multiple bugs. RP ceiling of 0.5 revealed transport stage judgment failure, demo_len=0/trigger_step=0 revealed field propagation errors
2. Browse mode WKWebView cannot receive mouse/keyboard events, even with ignoresMouseEvents=false ineffective; .desktopWindow layer causes window non-interactive Solution: Set window.level=.normal in enterBrowseMode (not on top but interactive), restore CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow) in exitBrowseMode
Key Insight: macOS .desktopWindow layer is below Finder desktop icons layer, windows at this layer don’t receive any input events at system level, ignoresMouseEvents=false ineffective for this layer. .normal(level=0) is lowest layer that’s both interactive and doesn’t cover other apps
3. LLaVA base model download blocked by proxy bandwidth bottleneck (~50KB/s, downloading 14GB model would take weeks); GPU node no DNS cannot direct connect; xet CDN through proxy timeout Solution: Discovered cluster had nyw’s HF format llava-1.5-7b-hf (safetensors), wrote _convert_hf_to_llava.py to convert to original LLaVA pytorch_model.bin format (including vocab truncation fix 32064→32000), entire process completed locally without network
Key Insight: Don’t assume must download—first search for existing model copies on cluster, even different formats can be converted. HF model format conversion isn’t just renaming keys, involves semantic differences (like vocab size)
4. Phoenix diffusion policy training GPU utilization only 5-6%: DataLoader num_workers=0 caused GPU to wait for CPU random reads from NFS HDF5 files Solution: Preload all HDF5 data to memory once in init (uint8 saves 4× storage), close file handles, then all getitem slices from numpy arrays; changed DataLoader to num_workers=8, pin_memory=True
Key Insight: h5py file handles cannot be shared across fork child processes (known PyTorch DataLoader limitation), only safe solution is complete loading in main process before fork. NFS random reads far slower than sequential reads, one-time loading 10× faster than on-demand
5. Phoenix MPM training after launch discovered severe training duration estimation error (actual 13.5 days vs expected hours), dataset scale estimation error (160K→1M) Solution: User halted training, requires replanning and optimization (possibly including reducing training steps, increasing GPU count, optimizing data loading, etc.)
Key Insight: Before launching large-scale training, must first verify actual dataset size, per-step time and total steps to avoid resource waste. Dataset scale estimation error can lead to weeks of wasted compute resources
6. CalendarPro intent classification ambiguity due to general_keywords pre-check interception: ‘你安排在几点了呀’ → ‘几点了’ matches general_keywords → forced GENERAL → error Solution: Split general_keywords into always_general (always force GENERAL, like ‘天气’) and context_dependent (force GENERAL only without active session, like ‘几点了’); added confirmation_words (‘ok’,‘好的’,‘是的’ etc.) with _is_confirmation_input() fast path; rewrote _process_input() as 6-step flow
Key Insight: Context-aware intent classification needs to combine session state (session_id, last_activity_at) and conversation history, pure keyword matching causes ambiguity; confirmation phrases (‘ok’) should route directly when active proposal exists
7. Current research scout paper evaluation processes all 50 papers at once, wasting tokens and lacking depth Solution: Designed two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 fast screening of all papers (only title+abstract first 1000 chars, classify high/low relevance), Stage 2 deep analysis of high-relevance papers (max 20 papers, extract 3 highlights + detailed scoring + direction suggestions)
Key Insight: Mimicking human researcher paper reading workflow (fast screening→deep reading high-value papers) can dramatically improve LLM evaluation efficiency and quality, while also generating literature reading records for low-relevance papers for future reference
8. Pipeline couldn’t read overview.md due to project.json ID (‘robot-manipulation’) not matching directory name (’error-recovery-benchmark’) Solution: Updated project.json id field to match directory name; pipeline uses project[‘id’] to construct overview.md path
Key Insight: Directory name and project.json id must be identical; _extract_current_methods() uses project[‘id’] to locate overview.md
9. Stage 2 evaluation received ‘(暂无记录)’ for current methods because overview.md section header ‘## 3. 当前技术路线’ didn’t match pipeline’s regex pattern ‘##\s*当前方法与进展’ Solution: Renamed overview.md section headers to match OVERVIEW_TEMPLATE format; removed numbered prefixes and section dividers
Key Insight: Pipeline uses strict regex matching for section extraction; template format must be exactly followed
10. FLARE norm stats calculation failed: norm stats script import openpi loaded zhaoganlong’s installed version, couldn’t find tangzijia’s new config name Solution: Set PYTHONPATH=/HOME/…/tangzijia/shared_deps/openpi/src:$PYTHONPATH in script to prioritize loading tangzijia’s openpi source copy, bypassing old version in conda env
Key Insight: When multiple users share same conda env, their source modifications create import priority conflicts. PYTHONPATH is minimal invasive solution, doesn’t affect other users
11. WKWebView scrollbar track transparent (CSS injection setting background-color ineffective) + sandbox app cannot load any network resources Solution: Removed webView.setValue(false, forKey: “drawsBackground”) to restore default opaque background making scrollbar track visible; added com.apple.security.network.client=true to .entitlements
Key Insight: drawsBackground=false makes entire WKWebView rendering layer transparent, CSS layering semi-transparent styles on transparent layer still transparent, fix must be at rendering layer not CSS layer. App Sandbox blocks all outbound network by default
12. LLM output contained too much English when user expected Chinese; no way to configure output language Solution: Implemented 3-tier language system: _DEFAULT_LANGUAGE constant, _language_instruction() generator, {language_instruction} in all prompts; config resolution chain CLI > project.json > config.json > default
Key Insight: Language instruction must be injected at prompt level, not post-processed; different sections need different language rules (JSON keys vs content)
13. No way to create project from existing overview.md without manually extracting keywords/categories Solution: Added create_project_from_overview() that uses LLM (OVERVIEW_EXTRACT_PROMPT) to parse overview.md and extract title, search_keywords, arxiv_categories, open_questions; writes project.json then copies original overview.md
Key Insight: LLM can reliably extract structured metadata from unstructured text; reuse existing _call_llm() and _parse_json_response() utilities
14. Batch generating reports repeatedly encountered incomplete or syntax-error JSON output from LLM, causing parsing failures Solution: User provided raw text, AI manually extracted and repaired JSON fragments (removed non-JSON prefixes/suffixes, fixed quote escaping, completed missing closing brackets, etc.)
Key Insight: LLM generating structured output, especially JSON with many nested objects and long text content, prone to format errors; need to add auto-repair and validation steps in pipeline
General Issues 15. Windows environment Hugo command not found, daily_summary.py merge step calling website/update.ps1 failed with ‘hugo’ is not recognized Solution: Installed Hugo 0.157.0 via winget install Hugo.Hugo.Extended, installer prompted need to restart shell, restarted PowerShell and hugo command worked
Key Insight: Windows environment winget-installed command-line tools require shell restart for PATH updates to take effect, cannot use immediately in same session
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level BC-RNN RP anomaly diagnosis strategy Role Approach Human User found BC-RNN SR near 0% in M14 inconsistent with training rollout, directly pointed to possible evaluation metric bugs, demanded systematic check of metric calculation logic AI AI initially inclined to explain ’error recovery is inherently difficult’, trying to justify low SR as expected result, rather than prioritizing suspicion of evaluation code bugs Difference Analysis: User inferred evaluation problems based on normal behavior observed during training, while AI tended to rationalize anomalous data. User’s intuition more accurate, ultimately discovered 4 cascading bugs causing metric distortion
Risk assessment before training launch Role Approach Human After Phoenix training launch, user immediately discovered severe training duration estimation error (13.5 days), decisively halted and demanded replanning to avoid resource waste AI AI didn’t fully verify actual dataset size (mistook 160K for actual 1M), per-step time (7.2s/step) and total steps (161K) before training launch, causing severe duration estimation error Difference Analysis: Humans better at risk control and timely loss cutting, AI executing tasks easily overlooks upfront validation of resource consumption
Paper reading workflow design Role Approach Human User proposed two-stage reading strategy—fast screening phase (30 seconds decide if worth deep reading) and deep understanding phase (find 3 core highlights: motivation/method insight/experimental design/limitations) AI AI initially designed single-stage full evaluation, sending all 50 papers’ complete abstracts to LLM for scoring at once Difference Analysis: Humans designed from actual researcher’s cognitive load, recognizing fast screening and deep analysis need different information granularity. AI inclined to one-time processing, overlooking token cost vs evaluation depth tradeoff
Debugging project configuration bug Role Approach Human User provided the overview.md path and asked AI to ‘fix the format’; didn’t diagnose the root cause AI AI traced through code to discover 3 interconnected bugs: ID mismatch, header format, missing marker Difference Analysis: AI’s systematic code analysis revealed cascading issues user couldn’t see; user correctly identified symptom (‘can’t read overview’) but not causes
Window layer solution iterative decision-making Role Approach Human User directly rejected .floating solution from user experience perspective (‘不要始终置顶’), after AI proposed .desktopWindow non-interactive, decisively pointed out should use .normal layer AI AI tried solutions by technical feasibility: first used .floating to ensure interaction, after rejection removed level change (kept .desktopWindow), discovered non-interactive then awaited user instruction Difference Analysis: Humans quickly eliminate unreasonable solutions from user experience and expected behavior, AI iteratively trial-and-error from technical implementation
Feature implementation details Role Approach Human User described what they wanted (‘从 overview.md 构建项目’, ‘改日报’, ‘去重’) but needed AI to propose implementation options AI AI asked clarifying questions with multiple options (init –from-overview vs replace, dedup by ID vs content hash) before implementing Difference Analysis: User had clear requirements but needed AI to explore implementation space; AI correctly recognized ambiguity and asked instead of guessing
Identifying missing language configuration feature Role Approach Human User immediately recognized the UX problem (‘总结的部分英文太多’) and asked if language could be configured AI AI didn’t proactively consider language configuration until user requested it; then implemented comprehensive solution Difference Analysis: User’s domain knowledge of bilingual academic workflows identified the gap; AI needed explicit request
Implementation Level FLARE training task quantity adjustment Role Approach Human After AI launched 9 tasks training, user requested ‘reduce to 4 D0 tasks’, clearly stating only need 4 D0 difficulty tasks AI AI initially planned full 9 tasks (3×D0+2×D1+1×D2) training, attempting to complete all tasks at once Difference Analysis: User based resource and time tradeoff, prioritized D0 task completion quality, while AI inclined toward completeness
AI Limitations Critical Limitations When diagnosing BC-RNN RP anomaly, AI initially inclined to rationalize anomalous data (’error recovery inherently difficult’) rather than prioritizing suspicion of evaluation code bugs. Only after user insisted evaluation had problems did AI systematically audit code and discover 4 cascading bugs AI didn’t fully verify actual dataset size (mistook 160K for actual 1M), per-step time and total steps before Phoenix training launch, causing severe training duration estimation error (13.5 days vs expected hours), lacking upfront validation awareness of resource consumption Insufficient understanding of OS window layer system: initially thought removing .floating layer setting would ‘maintain desktop layer’, didn’t realize .desktopWindow layer cannot receive any user input events, causing browse mode functionality completely unusable When designing paper evaluation workflow, AI didn’t spontaneously adopt human researcher’s two-stage reading strategy (fast screening→deep analysis), instead inclined toward one-time full processing engineering approach, overlooking cognitive load and cost-benefit tradeoff AI didn’t catch the project ID/directory name mismatch proactively; only discovered it after user provided the path and AI traced through _extract_current_methods() code When batch generating reports, AI repeatedly generated incomplete or syntax-error JSON (quote escaping errors, missing closing brackets, mixed non-JSON text, etc.), requiring manual intervention to repair, indicating AI’s insufficient reliability in generating ultra-long structured output AI did not proactively identify the language configuration gap until user explicitly complained about English output; should have noticed Chinese comments in codebase and suggested bilingual support earlier When processing historical records, AI cannot proactively identify which are ‘meta-tasks’ (about generating reports itself) vs ‘actual tasks’, easily confusing two levels, needs explicit human distinction When implementing configuration management, AI’s initial method used hardcoded constants, only realized need for layered configuration parsing mechanism after user explicitly stated ‘should be modifiable in config file’ General Limitations When planning the 3 new features, AI created a plan file but user immediately rejected and said ‘Implement the following plan’ instead; AI should have asked ‘Should I implement now or just create the plan?’ before writing plan file Learnings Key Learnings Zero-shot foundation model embedding fundamentally underperforms PCA in clustering tasks: FM optimizes for cross-tissue generalization capability (pretraining objective is language modeling/contrastive learning), not variance maximization; PCA does task-aligned dimensionality reduction, maximizing variance≈maximizing cluster separability. This conclusion validated by Microsoft and 3+ papers + MIHD own data (PCA ARI=0.261 vs scGPT=0.170, 54% gap) Evaluation metric distortion often not single bug but cascading chain of multiple bugs: BC-RNN’s demo_len=0, trigger_step=0, transport always False, successful episode RP not 1.0 four bugs jointly caused RP to drop from expected 0.5 to 0.003. Need end-to-end validation not isolated unit tests macOS window layer controls not only visual Z-order but event routing permissions: .desktopWindow layer (below desktop icons) fundamentally doesn’t receive user input events, must use .normal or higher layer to implement truly interactive ‘browse mode’; this is system-level constraint not API configuration issue In GPU cluster environment, prioritize searching existing model copies and performing format conversion (like HF format→original LLaVA format) rather than downloading through proxy, can save weeks; LLaVA base model conversion from HF format to original format (including vocab truncation fix 32064→32000) successful case proves this When designing automated paper management tool, should mimic human researcher’s actual cognitive flow: fast screening (relevance+novelty+source authority)→deep analysis (core insight+problem definition+experimental design+limitations), not one-time full evaluation h5py file handles cannot be shared across fork child processes (known PyTorch DataLoader limitation), only safe solution is main process preload to numpy then fork. NFS random reads far slower than sequential reads, one-time loading 10× faster than on-demand, can use uint8 to save 4× memory Must verify actual dataset size, per-step time and total steps before launching large-scale training to avoid resource waste; Phoenix MPM training case where dataset scale estimation error (160K→1M) caused 13.5-day training duration severe mistake, proving importance of upfront validation Context-aware intent classification needs to combine session state (session_id, last_activity_at) and conversation history, pure keyword matching causes ambiguity (like ‘几点了’ could be query time or ask scheduled time); CalendarPro resolved this through context_dependent keyword classification and confirmation fast path research_scout.py architecture: 1871-line single file organized into 0-10 numbered sections; two-stage LLM pipeline (screening → deep analysis); three backends (claude_cli, anthropic, openai); parameter resolution chain CLI > project.json > config.json > default; cache validation by keywords hash Command-line tool parameter configuration should use layered parsing strategy: CLI flag > project-specific config > user-level global config > hardcoded default, providing flexibility while maintaining reasonable defaults Batch document generation tool design needs two-stage architecture: export stage locally parses raw data on each device, merge stage aggregates cross-device; when single-day session count especially large, also need ‘intra-segment merge’ step to deduplicate and consolidate multiple outputs from same day Multi-user shared conda environment import priority conflict minimal invasive solution: set PYTHONPATH=/path/to/user/src:$PYTHONPATH at script execution, prioritize loading user’s own source copy, doesn’t affect other users and doesn’t require creating separate env Language configuration for LLM pipelines requires injection at prompt level, not post-processing; different parts of output need different rules (e.g. JSON keys stay English, content in target language) Reverse-engineering structured data from documentation works well with LLM; OVERVIEW_EXTRACT_PROMPT can reliably parse overview.md to extract title/keywords/categories/questions Pipeline regex patterns must match exactly; ‘## 3. 当前技术路线’ won’t match ‘##\s*当前方法与进展’; template-driven architectures require strict format adherence arXiv search returns results in reverse chronological order; consecutive-known-paper counter is effective heuristic for early-stop since it indicates reaching already-processed timeframe Practical Learnings Cross-platform script porting key adaptations: Windows use Get-Item .LastWriteTime instead of find -newer, Start-Job instead of & parallel, Push-Location/Pop-Location instead of cd, [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText ensure BOM-free UTF-8, -replace instead of sed/perl. PowerShell and bash differ significantly in flow control and error handling mechanisms Conversation Summaries MIHD ✅ Update CLAUDE.md and create overview.md research positioning document + scGPT performance systematic investigation 20:29:42.417 | claude_code Through parallel agents exploring 13+ key files in codebase, precisely updated CLAUDE.md (added pipeline configuration structure, cache directory details, code statistics updates), then created 676-line overview.md covering one-sentence positioning, 4 core questions, technical roadmap, 10 fusion strategy rankings, 8 open questions. Launched 4 parallel agents to retrieve scGPT-spatial paper, zero-shot limitation paper, BioLLM framework paper, MIHD internal results, aggregated to demonstrate zero-shot scGPT fundamentally underperforms PCA (PCA ARI=0.261 vs scGPT=0.170, 54% gap). Established patch query clinical vision-driven zero-shot vs STAIG differentiated narrative.

Tuned noise parameters for three error classifiers. Completed all 127 unit tests passing, GPU validation confirmed demo_len=605, trigger_step=55 non-zero and RP highest 0.800. Daily Report — 2026-03-06 Daily Overview What was done: Worked across six major projects covering spatial transcriptomics analysis, life management chatbot debugging and documentation, robotics manipulation benchmark codebase restructuring, training pipeline design, and containerized simulation rendering How it was done: Combined parallel multi-agent exploration for rapid codebase understanding, systematic code tracing for data pipelines and context management, symlink-based project restructuring, driver-library version matching for Docker rendering, and comprehensive training infrastructure design Impact: Resolved critical data format questions affecting research, diagnosed and designed fix for user-facing context loss bug, created 1674-line complete tutorial, restructured research projects with 99% disk savings (78GB to 37MB), unblocked Docker GPU rendering for robot simulation evaluation, optimized 67 lines of documentation, and built end-to-end training pipeline covering 9 tasks with resource optimization strategy DCC What was done: Analyzed normalization and preprocessing pipelines in ContraVAE and STHD spatial transcriptomics projects, clarifying data formats and processing steps How it was done: Inspected h5ad files, traced preprocessing scripts, verified data characteristics to track the full pipeline from raw counts to normalized expression matrices Impact: Clarified user confusion about data formats, confirmed the meaning and processing of X matrix, layers[‘counts’], HVG selection, and spatial coordinates across two different preprocessing approaches TzJsDesktop What was done: Fixed CalendarPro Discord bot context loss issue and wrote comprehensive 1674-line Chinese tutorial covering both end-users and developers How it was done: Used parallel agents to explore conversation history management, intent classification, and AI provider call chains, designed context-aware fix; systematically extracted all configs, commands, and architecture to generate structured tutorial Impact: Identified three-layer root cause of bot amnesia (keyword pre-check, timing, missing history parameter) with actionable fix plan; created complete documentation resource covering user guide (60%) and developer guide (40%) tianhe What was done: Optimized error_recovery_benchmark CLAUDE.md documentation, restructured Motion-based Self-Reflection Framework into separate Phoenix/FLARE projects with shared dependencies, designed complete training pipeline for 9 MimicGen tasks, created CALVIN documentation, resolved SAPIEN rendering errors in Docker, and documented RoboTwin simulation architecture How it was done: Streamlined documentation redundancy, executed directory separation with symlink management for 99% disk reduction, explored training framework architectures and created 7 scripts (data generation, conversion, training, evaluation, orchestration), performed driver-library version matching and environment configuration for Vulkan/OpenGL stack, traced multi-layer simulation code Impact: Reduced documentation from 225 to 167 lines with improved readability, established maintainable project structure (Phoenix 37MB, FLARE 368KB, shared_deps 9.3GB), built end-to-end training pipeline including missing config completion and checkpoint reuse strategy, resolved critical Docker rendering blocker preventing model evaluation, and documented complex codebases for onboarding Cross-project work spanning spatial transcriptomics data analysis, CalendarPro bug fix and comprehensive documentation, robot learning codebase restructuring, Docker rendering stack resolution, and Phoenix/FLARE training pipeline design
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Analyze spatial transcriptomics data preprocessing pipeline — Traced normalization steps for ContraVAE and STHD projects, clarified X matrix vs layers[‘counts’], HVG selection, and spatial coordinate systems ✅ Diagnose CalendarPro context loss bug — Identified three-layer issue causing bot to lose conversation context on follow-up messages, designed fix plan ✅ Design Phoenix/FLARE 9-task training plan — Designed complete training infrastructure for Phoenix diffusion policy and FLARE retry framework across all MimicGen tasks ✅ Resolve SAPIEN rendering error in Docker container — Diagnosed and fixed ‘Render Error’ blocking robot simulation evaluation. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Create Phoenix training scripts — Built SLURM job script for Phoenix multi-task diffusion policy training ✅ Create FLARE data generation and training scripts — Built warmup data generation, LeRobot conversion, training, and evaluation scripts for FLARE pipeline ✅ Document RoboTwin data collection and simulation architecture — Provided detailed explanation of two-phase data collection pipeline (seed finding + replay with deterministic seeds) and traced complete simulation execution flow using place_dual_shoes task as example. ✅ Optimize error_recovery_benchmark CLAUDE.md — Reduced documentation from 225 to 167 lines by trimming Commands section, adding PYTHONPATH details, and streamlining references ✅ Complete OpenPI training configs — Added missing finetune and inference configs for coffee_task_D1, stack_three_task_D1, and three_piece_assembly_task_D1 ✅ Fix frozen dataclass mutation errors in policy loading — Resolved FrozenInstanceError when loading pi05 policy. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. CalendarPro bot fails to understand follow-up messages like ‘你安排在几点了呀’ (What time did you schedule?) Solution: Identified three-layer issue: (1) general_keywords pre-check executes before AI sees conversation history, (2) pre-check uses overly broad keywords like ‘几点了’, (3) AI provider calls don’t receive history parameter. Designed fix to remove pre-check bypass and pass full conversation history to AI
Key Insight: Context loss is typically a multi-layer problem: data not collected → data not passed → data not used. Must trace the complete call chain from storage through provider interface to prompt construction
2. SAPIEN ‘Render Error’ in headless Docker container - RuntimeError: failed to find a rendering device Solution: Discovered missing NVIDIA Vulkan/OpenGL rendering libraries (libGLX_nvidia.so, etc). Container had CUDA compute libraries but not rendering stack. Downloaded matching NVIDIA driver version 535.104.12 to match kernel driver, extracted libraries to user directory, configured VK_ICD_FILENAMES and LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variables in eval.sh.
Key Insight: Docker containers with NVIDIA GPUs need both CUDA runtime AND Vulkan/OpenGL libraries for graphics-based simulation. Driver version must exactly match between kernel module and user-space libraries or Vulkan ICD fails to load.
3. Phoenix training checkpoints exist in zhaoganlong’s directory, unclear whether to reuse or retrain Solution: User pointed out should check existing checkpoints and symlink when available, only train missing ones on an53 free GPUs
Key Insight: Before designing training plan, inventory existing resources (checkpoints, datasets, configs) to avoid wasting compute. Establish checkpoint reuse strategy first
4. User assumed normalized data came from STHD pipeline, but data characteristics didn’t match pipeline code Solution: Traced code to discover STHD doesn’t perform normalization - it uses raw counts directly. The normalized data user saw was from external scanpy preprocessing (normalize_total + log1p)
Key Insight: Need to distinguish between pipeline-internal processing and external preprocessing. Code inspection is more reliable than assumptions based on data appearance
General Issues 5. OpenPI config missing warmup training configurations for 3 out of 9 MimicGen tasks Solution: Added finetune and inference configs for coffee_task_D1, stack_three_task_D1, and three_piece_assembly_task_D1 using add_finetune_config and add_inference_config helper functions
Key Insight: Use config generation functions to maintain consistency across task configurations rather than manual duplication
6. FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field ‘asset_id’ in policy_config.py Solution: DataConfig was defined with @dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True), making it immutable. Replaced direct assignment (data_config.asset_id = value) with dataclasses.replace(data_config, asset_id=value) which creates a new instance.
Key Insight: Frozen dataclasses enforce immutability at the language level - modifications require explicit use of dataclasses.replace() to create new instances rather than mutating in-place.
7. FileNotFoundError with duplicated path: assets/norm_stats.json/norm_stats.json Solution: When robotwin_repo_id is provided, asset_id was incorrectly set to ’norm_stats.json’ (filename instead of directory). Modified code to load directly from assets/ directory using normalize.load() without appending asset_id subdirectory.
Key Insight: Path construction bugs often arise from mixing directory identifiers with filenames. Explicit handling of special cases (local files vs remote repositories) prevents path duplication.
8. MulticoreTSNE build failure due to CMake version incompatibility (system 3.26.4 vs required <=3.18) Solution: Identified that MulticoreTSNE is only used for optional TSNE visualization, not core training/eval. Suggested commenting out dependency in requirements.txt to proceed with installation (user rejected this approach).
Key Insight: Distinguish between critical dependencies and optional visualization tools. In research code, it’s often acceptable to skip non-essential dependencies that cause build issues.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Detecting bot context loss from user experience Role Approach Human User noticed from end-user perspective that bot failed on obvious follow-up question ‘你安排在几点了呀’ AI AI diagnosed root cause by tracing code through three layers: keyword pre-check mechanism, history passing in provider calls, and dual-verify intent flow Difference Analysis: Human detects symptoms from usage experience; AI diagnoses root cause through systematic code analysis. However, AI didn’t proactively monitor system to prevent such issues - relied on user bug report
Checkpoint reuse before training Role Approach Human User pointed out should reuse existing checkpoints via symlinks and only train what’s missing, considering resource efficiency AI AI designed complete training-from-scratch plan without checking for existing checkpoints first Difference Analysis: User has cost awareness and practical constraints; AI tends toward clean-slate implementations. Should always inventory existing resources before planning new work
Implementation Level Installing NVIDIA libraries in restricted Docker environment Role Approach Human User immediately knew that apt-get must be accessed via custom path /app/ubuntu/bin/apt-get due to container security setup AI AI initially tried standard apt-get command, which would have failed or required sudo Difference Analysis: Human had domain knowledge about the specific container’s package manager configuration that wasn’t discoverable from the codebase. AI learned this through user correction.

Handling MulticoreTSNE dependency conflict Role Approach Human User rejected the file edit to comment out MulticoreTSNE, possibly preferring to handle installation differently or accepting the limitation AI AI immediately suggested editing requirements.txt to remove the problematic dependency as a quick workaround Difference Analysis: User may have wanted to preserve the original configuration or had alternative solution in mind. AI focused on unblocking progress but didn’t confirm approach preference first.
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Designed training plan without checking for existing checkpoints - needed user reminder to consider reuse strategy. Should always inventory resources before implementation Initially attempted to install NVIDIA graphics libraries (libnvidia-gl-535) without first checking kernel driver version compatibility, leading to version mismatch (535.288.01 vs 535.104.12). Required multiple iterations to discover correct approach of downloading matching driver and extracting libraries. General Limitations While conversation history exploration was comprehensive, took 3 parallel agents to identify the core issue of LLM calls not receiving history parameter - could have pinpointed faster with more targeted initial exploration Created 1674-line tutorial file directly without previewing structure for user confirmation first - should validate approach on large artifacts Modified test_render.py to print full traceback by replacing bare ’except:’ with ’except Exception as e:’, but this pattern (swallowing exceptions without logging) was in the original codebase, not AI-introduced. AI should have proactively identified this anti-pattern earlier. Multiple /init command runs performed similar exploration and analysis without remembering previous evaluation results - lacks session-to-session memory Spent time on systematic exploration (find commands, vulkaninfo checks) that could have been shortened if AI had more direct knowledge of common Docker+NVIDIA Vulkan setup patterns. Eventually succeeded but with more steps than an expert would need. Learnings Key Learnings Context loss requires tracing the complete call chain: data collection (conversation_history.json storage) → data passing (provider call signatures) → data usage (prompt construction). Missing any layer breaks context Before designing training plans, inventory existing resources (checkpoints, datasets, configs) and establish reuse strategy to avoid wasting compute resources. Ask ‘what exists?’ before ‘what to build?’ Docker containers running NVIDIA GPU workloads need two distinct library sets: CUDA runtime (compute) AND Vulkan/OpenGL (rendering). Many GPU-enabled containers ship with only CUDA. For simulation frameworks like SAPIEN that use graphics APIs, both stacks must be present with exact version matching to kernel driver. In spatial transcriptomics data processing, adata.X can be either normalized values (scanpy pipeline) or raw counts (STHD pipeline) - must check code rather than assume from data type Parallel multi-agent exploration accelerates understanding of complex codebases, but requires careful planning to avoid redundant work. Use agents for independent dimensions (history management, message flow, provider interface) not overlapping concerns Two-phase data collection (seed discovery + deterministic replay) is a robust pattern for robotics simulation: first phase filters for successful task completions and saves trajectory plans, second phase replays with saved plans to collect clean training data. This separates stochasticity from data quality. Symlink-based dependency sharing can dramatically reduce disk usage for large research projects (78GB -> 37MB) while maintaining independent project structure. Critical to symlink data directories rather than copy, and use relative paths for portability. Documentation optimization core principle: remove content discoverable through other means (like ‘make help’ for commands), preserve ‘big picture’ insights requiring cross-file understanding Vulkan ICD (Installable Client Driver) discovery requires both the nvidia_icd.json manifest AND the actual driver libraries to be present and version-matched. VK_ICD_FILENAMES environment variable overrides system search paths for containerized environments. Practical Learnings Python frozen dataclasses provide compile-time immutability guarantees but require explicit use of dataclasses.replace() for modifications. Direct assignment raises FrozenInstanceError. This pattern enforces functional programming style for config objects.
