content:
Daily Report — 2026-02-28 Daily Overview What was done: Advanced MIHD spatial transcriptomics to support Visium HD high-resolution data with auto-clustering, completed RM-IDEAL correlation analysis across 27 embedding methods, fixed critical ML model checkpoint loading bug causing 17.7% parameter loss, implemented complete wallpaper History tracking system, resolved multi-screen power management bugs, and launched Pi0.5 Phoenix VLA evaluation revealing fundamental training issues How it was done: Implemented HD data adapters with Leiden-based auto-clustering and visualization optimization strategies, performed root cause analysis on PyTorch model loading revealing missing instance attributes, designed full-stack History feature with async thumbnail generation and SwiftUI interface, conducted multi-agent code exploration identifying stub functions, systematically debugged GPU cluster environment issues (proxy variables, CUDA OOM, library mismatches), and launched comprehensive 9-task robotic manipulation benchmark Impact: Enabled MIHD to handle next-generation HD data, identified STAIG fusion as optimal method (r=0.396), improved scGPT clustering by 44% (ARI 0.118→0.170) enabling valid research results, delivered production-ready wallpaper History feature with proper UX patterns, restored two completely broken power-saving modes, and revealed trained VLA model has 0-24% success rate on its own training tasks indicating fundamental architecture or training problems DCC What was done: Extended MIHD spatial transcriptomics pipeline for Visium HD (17K spots) with auto-clustering, executed RM-IDEAL evaluation across 27 methods on section 151673, and fixed critical scGPT checkpoint loading bug causing 17.7% parameter loss in attention layers How it was done: Built 8-step HD implementation plan with Leiden algorithm for label-free clustering, ran exhaustive correlation analysis generating 189 visualizations, and added missing self.use_fast_transformer attribute enabling proper Wqkv→in_proj key remapping Impact: Established HD data integration foundation with performance bottleneck identification, validated STAIG fusion superiority with quantitative metrics, and improved average ARI from 0.118 to 0.170 (+44.4%) and NMI from 0.208 to 0.277 (+33.3%) across all 11 DLPFC sections MacBook What was done: Implemented complete History feature for desktop video wallpaper app with thumbnail UI, fixed critical multi-screen support bugs (4 stub functions rendering powerSave modes non-functional), created comprehensive project documentation, and added automated build numbering How it was done: Designed and implemented 5 new Swift files (data model, store, views, thumbnail generator) with UserDefaults persistence and double-click activation with cooldown, launched 3 parallel exploratory agents to systematically analyze multi-screen logic identifying stub functions and bookmark persistence bugs, and added Xcode Run Script phase for automatic CFBundleVersion updates Impact: Delivered production-ready history system with proper deliberate-activation UX pattern, identified and documented 4 critical stub functions completely breaking powerSave/powerSavePlus features plus persistence bugs orphaning user data, documented architecture for future development, and automated version tracking eliminating manual updates tianhe What was done: Set up and launched comprehensive evaluation of pre-trained Pi0.5 Phoenix VLA model on 9 MimicGen robotic manipulation tasks, investigated training completion status, and planned BC-RNN benchmark baseline implementation for Phoenix paper reproduction with error injection compatibility How it was done: Systematically debugged GPU cluster environment (proxy variables blocking WebSocket, CUDA OOM from zombie processes, robosuite version mismatches), reused existing server process, configured PYTHONPATH for correct library versions, launched SLURM job with resource awareness, traced training checkpoints and configs via filesystem exploration, and examined existing robomimic patterns and error framework adapters Impact: Successfully launched 9-task benchmark evaluation (7/9 complete) revealing trained model performs poorly even on its own training tasks (0-24% success rate) suggesting fundamental architecture or training issues, discovered critical evaluation gap (100k-step trained model never evaluated), clarified three distinct Pi0.5 variants and their data provenance, and prepared foundation for systematic Phoenix baseline reproduction with future error injection integration Advanced spatial transcriptomics pipeline with Visium HD support and comprehensive RM-IDEAL benchmarking, fixed critical scGPT model loading bug improving clustering metrics by 44%, implemented desktop wallpaper History feature while resolving multi-screen power management bugs, and established VLA evaluation pipeline revealing poor Phoenix model performance despite training on target tasks
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Fix scGPT checkpoint loading bug — Added missing self.use_fast_transformer attribute causing 17.7% of attention layer parameters (9.4M weights) to use random initialization instead of pretrained weights. Re-extracted all 11 DLPFC section embeddings with fixed model, improving clustering metrics significantly 🔄 Evaluate Pi0.5 Phoenix VLA on 9 MimicGen tasks — Launched full evaluation pipeline on GPU cluster for pre-trained Pi0.5 Phoenix (checkpoint step 99999) across 9 robotic manipulation tasks. Fixed critical environment issues (proxy variables, CUDA OOM, robosuite version mismatches). 7/9 tasks complete showing very poor performance (0-24% success rate) despite model being fine-tuned on these exact tasks 🔄 Visium HD (crop10large) data support implementation — 8-step plan to integrate HD data (17,502 spots) with auto-clustering via Leiden algorithm, visualization adaptation, and benchmark pipeline integration. Key challenge: no ground truth labels, requiring unsupervised evaluation strategy ✅ Fix multi-screen power management and persistence bugs — Comprehensive multi-screen bug analysis via 3 parallel exploratory agents identified and documented 4 critical stub functions (allOverlaysCompletelyCovered, anyOverlayCompletelyCovered, reassignAllWindows, windowScreenDidChange) completely breaking powerSave/powerSavePlus modes, plus BookmarkStore.purge() missing keys causing orphaned data. Implementation plan created but execution stopped by user. ✅ RM-IDEAL benchmark for section 151673 — Evaluated 27 embedding methods across 7 tissue layers computing Spearman correlation between cosine similarity and RM-IDEAL scores. Generated 189 visualization PNGs and comprehensive CSV summary identifying STAIG fusion as optimal (r=0.396) ✅ Investigate Pi0.5 training status and distinguish variants — Traced Pi0.5 Phoenix training checkpoints discovering training completed to step 99999 but no evaluation was performed. Clarified three Pi0.5 variants: (1) official pretrained base (M14 error recovery), (2) our Phoenix LoRA fine-tune (9 MimicGen tasks, 4500 episodes), (3) zhaoganlong’s single-task variants. Mapped each to their training datasets 🔄 Plan BC-RNN benchmark training/evaluation script — Designed train_bc_rnn_benchmark.py with 4 modes (generate-configs, train, eval, report) for Phoenix paper baseline reproduction. Explored existing robomimic configs and error framework patterns, confirmed native compatibility with error injection via RobomimicPolicyAdapter. Implementation not started due to user interruption Implementation & Fixes ✅ Implement desktop wallpaper History feature — Created complete history tracking system with 5 new Swift files (WallpaperHistoryEntry, WallpaperHistoryStore, HistoryView, HistoryItemRow, ThumbnailGenerator), UserDefaults persistence, thumbnail UI with screen picker, double-click activation with 1-second cooldown, and clear history button ✅ Reusable visualization script (visualize_from_cache.py) — Created script to generate clustering visualizations from cached embeddings with support for embedding loading, clustering, metrics computation, and scanpy visualization. Designed for multi-process optimization after GPU acceleration proved unsuitable ✅ Create desktop wallpaper CLAUDE.md documentation — Generated comprehensive project documentation covering build commands, MVVM architecture, key conventions, playback modes, code style, and git workflow ✅ Automate build number updates — Added Xcode Run Script build phase to automatically set CFBundleVersion to current date (YYYYMMDD format) on every build. Required disabling ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING to allow modifications Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. scGPT spatial clustering ARI scores very low (~0.10) despite using pretrained checkpoint; colleague suspected flash attention incompatibility causing checkpoint loading issues Solution: Root cause: TransformerModel.init never saved use_fast_transformer as instance attribute, causing getattr(model, ‘use_fast_transformer’, True) to always return True and prevent Wqkv→in_proj key remapping. Fixed by adding self.use_fast_transformer = use_fast_transformer. Re-extracted all 11 DLPFC embeddings with corrected model, improving average ARI from 0.118 to 0.170 (+44%), NMI from 0.208 to 0.277 (+33%)
Key Insight: Missing instance attributes in PyTorch model classes can silently break checkpoint loading when strict=False, causing partial parameter initialization (17.7% random weights) that manifests as poor performance rather than obvious errors. Always verify checkpoint keys match model state_dict and log mismatches explicitly
2. Visium HD data lacks ground truth labels, making traditional ARI/NMI metrics impossible to compute for benchmark evaluation Solution: Use Leiden community detection to auto-estimate n_clusters from k-NN graph, output only clustering visualization with silhouette score. Modified compute_metrics() to conditionally skip supervised metrics when labels unavailable. Resolution parameter controls granularity
Key Insight: Unsupervised spatial transcriptomics data requires fundamentally different evaluation strategy—focus on visual coherence and internal consistency metrics (silhouette score) rather than external validation. Data provenance tracking critical to detect pre-applied transformations
3. powerSave and powerSavePlus video pause modes completely non-functional in multi-screen wallpaper app despite occlusion detection infrastructure existing Solution: Traced to 4 critical stub functions: allOverlaysCompletelyCovered() and anyOverlayCompletelyCovered() hardcoded to return false; reassignAllWindows() and windowScreenDidChange() do nothing. Identified .automatic mode as working template. Implemented all four using existing overlayWindows.values and .occlusionState.contains(.visible) pattern
Key Insight: Stub functions with TODO comments in production code can completely break features while appearing to compile successfully—type checkers satisfied but runtime behavior absent. This is dangerous technical debt that can persist unnoticed. The occlusion detection infrastructure was already working for .automatic mode, just needed wiring
4. WebSocket connection refused error for Pi0.5 server evaluation despite TCP port being open and server listening on localhost:8000 Solution: Discovered proxy environment variables (http_proxy=127.0.0.1:10087, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, no_proxy, NO_PROXY) were intercepting WebSocket connections even to localhost. Unsetting all proxy vars fixed the issue immediately
Key Insight: Proxy environment variables can silently interfere with localhost connections even when raw TCP layer works—they intercept at application layer before socket creation. Always check and unset proxy vars when debugging WebSocket issues on development machines or shared clusters
5. HD adata_8um.h5ad already log-transformed (range [0, 6.05]), but preprocess_data() applies log1p by default, causing double-transformation corruption Solution: Add skip_log parameter to preprocess_data() and preprocess_for_encoding(). Detect HD dataset via metadata inspection and set skip_log=True to bypass redundant normalization. Use adata.uns[’log1p’] flag or X.max() heuristics for detection
Key Insight: Pre-processed external datasets require explicit transformation history tracking to prevent pipeline corruption. HD spot diameter (7.3px) is 20× smaller than Visium (~55µm), requiring dynamic visualization parameter scaling (size=4.0 vs 1.0) to prevent invisible dots
6. CUDA out of memory when attempting to load 50.7 GiB Pi0.5 model on GPU cluster—GPUs already full with existing processes Solution: Ran nvidia-smi and ps to identify zombie server process (PID 2413737) from previous launch already loaded and listening on port 8000. Reused existing server instance instead of launching new one, preventing OOM and saving 3-5min startup time
Key Insight: When loading 50+ GB models on shared GPUs, always check nvidia-smi and existing processes first before attempting new launches. Reusing zombie servers is more efficient than killing and restarting. Enforces resource awareness and multi-user cluster etiquette
7. Initial confusion about Pi0.5 training status—Slurm job 46553 crashed at step 5000, unclear if training ever completed to 100k steps Solution: Checked checkpoint directory directly, found checkpoints up to 99999 timestamped Feb 24, confirming training succeeded despite early job crash (likely resumed from checkpoint). Then discovered no evaluation was ever performed
Key Insight: Slurm job logs don’t tell the full story—they reflect execution history, not outcome completeness. Always verify completion by checking actual checkpoint artifacts with timestamps, not just log tails. Training completion ≠ evaluation done
8. Robosuite environment missing get_bounding_box_half_size method and env.seed() API incompatibility when evaluating Pi0.5 Phoenix Solution: Configured PYTHONPATH to use zhaoganlong’s robosuite/mimicgen from deps/ directory instead of local mimicgen_workspace versions. Exact environment matching with training setup required for valid evaluation
Key Insight: VLA policy evaluation requires exact library version matching with training environment—even minor robosuite/mimicgen version differences cause API incompatibilities (missing methods, changed signatures). Version mismatches can invalidate benchmarking results
9. GPU acceleration exploration for visualization pipeline—cuML/FAISS not installed, mclust unavailable (R_HOME issue) Solution: Profiling revealed clustering (100-300ms) is not the bottleneck; scanpy data loading and matplotlib rendering dominate. Recommended multi-process parallelization across 11 independent sections instead of GPU optimization
Key Insight: Premature GPU optimization attempt—profiling revealed I/O and rendering, not computation, as limiting factors. Parallel CPU processing more effective than GPU for this I/O-bound workload. Always profile before optimizing
General Issues 10. Xcode build script to auto-update CFBundleVersion failed with ‘Operation not permitted’ when trying to modify built product’s Info.plist Solution: ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = YES in project settings blocked build scripts from writing files. Set to NO to allow the PlistBuddy command to modify the built app’s Info.plist
Key Insight: Xcode’s user script sandboxing (introduced in recent versions) blocks build script file access by default, separate from app’s runtime sandbox entitlements. Must be disabled for build automation that modifies artifacts
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level HD data resolution selection and scope refinement Role Approach Human User initially asked for full HD support, then pragmatically refined to crop10large subset (17K spots) for faster testing before scaling to full 545K dataset AI AI immediately planned for full 545K spot dataset with complex memory management and batch processing strategies without considering phased rollout Difference Analysis: Human applied incremental validation strategy (small → large) to reduce risk and accelerate feedback cycles, while AI over-engineered for full-scale problem upfront. User’s approach enables faster iteration and earlier problem detection
scGPT checkpoint loading bug diagnosis Role Approach Human Colleague identified flash attention incompatibility as potential root cause based on domain knowledge about PyTorch checkpoint naming differences between attention implementations, immediately pointing to checkpoint loading mechanism AI AI initially investigated the problem but didn’t identify the upstream model class bug without human guidance; focused on testing and comparing results rather than examining model initialization code Difference Analysis: Human brought critical domain insight about flash attention vs standard attention parameter naming conventions that immediately narrowed investigation scope. AI was working on verifying the issue symptomatically rather than identifying root cause architecturally
Resource management on shared GPU cluster Role Approach Human User preemptively intervened with ‘Please check all running jobs first before you ask for any new nodes’—enforced resource awareness and multi-user etiquette before any action AI Was about to execute SLURM commands without verifying existing GPU allocations or considering cluster resource constraints and other users Difference Analysis: Human prioritized resource efficiency and cluster sharing norms proactively; AI focused narrowly on task completion without considering broader resource context. Human’s intervention prevented wasteful allocation and potential conflicts
History feature interaction pattern design Role Approach Human User specified double-click activation with 1-second cooldown after AI had already implemented single-click Button approach, recognizing need for deliberate activation to prevent accidental wallpaper changes AI AI initially designed with single-click Button(action:) pattern typical for SwiftUI list items, treating history as a simple selection interface without considering accidental activation risk Difference Analysis: Human recognized UX consideration AI didn’t anticipate—more deliberate activation (double-click) plus cooldown prevents accidental wallpaper changes from errant clicks. This shows human understanding of real usage patterns vs. AI’s default pattern application
Task prioritization when requirements evolve Role Approach Human Quickly pivoted from ‘write BC-RNN training script’ to ’evaluate existing Pi0.5 model’ once they clarified the actual goal was benchmark comparison, not new training from scratch AI Had already started building detailed BC-RNN infrastructure before the pivot—followed initial instructions linearly without questioning underlying intent Difference Analysis: Human maintained focus on end goal (benchmark evaluation) and redirected when they realized the true need, preventing wasted implementation work. AI tends toward satisfying stated requirements without anticipating underlying intent or validating assumptions
Data provenance investigation priority Role Approach Human Asked ‘what data were these Pi0.5 variants trained on?’ to understand fundamental differences before deciding what to evaluate—prioritized conceptual clarity on training data composition AI Focused on checkpoint paths and config names without initially explaining dataset composition or distinguishing training data sources—reported technical paths over conceptual understanding Difference Analysis: Human seeks conceptual clarity on data provenance first (what was learned, from what data), while AI reports technical implementation details (where it’s stored). Understanding ‘what was learned’ matters more than ‘where checkpoints live’ for research decisions

User asked right question even if premise incorrect—enabled discovery of actual bottleneck

In this case, Pi0.5 trained on {Coffee, Stack, Threading, Assembly, Stack Three} but evaluated on PickPlace, causing complete failure despite successful training. MimicGen paper provides only demonstration datasets (HDF5 files), not pre-trained model checkpoints. Researchers must train BC-RNN models themselves using robomimic, which is the official benchmark protocol. BC-RNN has two distinct observation modes with fundamentally different architectures: low_dim (state-based, 2000 epochs, larger MLP) vs image (pixel-based, ResNet18 encoder, 600 epochs, larger RNN). MimicGen paper’s primary results use image mode. Environment naming conventions in robosuite/MimicGen have semantic implications: stripping ‘_D0’ suffix changes which env class is instantiated, which alters object observables returned. Base robosuite envs return fewer object states than MimicGen ‘_D0’ variants, causing dimension mismatches (65→37 dims). VLA policy evaluation requires coordinating multiple components: checkpoint location, policy server (websocket/TCP based), evaluation script, conda environment management, and GPU resource allocation via Slurm - missing any component blocks the entire pipeline Multi-task evaluation infrastructure requires coordinated design across layers: task configs (YAML), registry mapping (datasets/checkpoints/prompts), script parameters (–task flag with auto-resolution), and orchestration (task loops in bash scripts). Retrofitting is more expensive than upfront task-agnostic design. Image-based robot learning policies need camera rendering enabled during both training data collection and evaluation rollouts. Camera resolution must match training (84×84 for BC-RNN image mode) to avoid visual encoder input dimension mismatches. Parallel exploration agents are highly effective for understanding multi-component systems - exploring training setup, evaluation infrastructure, and pipeline code independently then synthesizing enables faster comprehension than sequential investigation The Pi0.5 evaluation stack uses a two-process architecture: policy server (openpi05 conda env) serves model via websocket, evaluation script (mimicgen_env) runs environments and queries server over network Practical Learnings Jake’s Resume Template from Overleaf is a popular, ATS-friendly LaTeX format that’s simple to customize. Daily Report — 2026-02-23 Daily Overview What was done: Parallel execution of two major research workstreams: (1) MIHD spatial transcriptomics pipeline optimization and vision encoder generalization, (2) Error recovery benchmark evaluation infrastructure fixes and Phoenix model training restart How it was done: Applied systematic optimization methodology across both projects: code profiling to identify bottlenecks, targeted vectorization/batching for performance gains, architectural refactoring for flexibility, comprehensive ablation studies, and robust error handling with resume mechanisms for long-running batch processes Impact: MIHD: Eliminated major training bottlenecks (100-500x initialization speedup, 20-50x QFormer acceleration), unlocked architectural flexibility for modern vision encoders, and established empirical evidence for fusion method selection criteria. Error Recovery: Unblocked entire M14 evaluation pipeline (649 scenes × 4 policies), advanced Pi0.5 training from 3K→100K steps with stable monitoring, and quantified M13 classification reliability DCC What was done: Four MIHD workstreams: (1) CPU bottleneck optimization for fusion training, (2) STAIG encoder generalization, (3) vision refinement ablation experiments, (4) large-scale STAIG deployment across all DLPFC sections with compatibility fixes How it was done: Implemented NumPy/scipy vectorization for edge weight computation, moved dropout operations to GPU, added batch processing for QFormer; refactored pipeline orchestration to use encoder family detection; ran comprehensive experiments comparing 8 fusion methods with scan_cluster refinement vs baselines; debugged UNI2 patch size incompatibility and NaN handling edge cases Impact: Eliminated training bottlenecks (QFormer down from 3.5 hours with 5% GPU utilization), enabled arbitrary vision encoder support in STAIG, established that refinement benefits weak fusion methods (+0.05-0.09 ARI) but harms strong ones (-0.05 ARI), completed full STAIG evaluation on 10/11 sections (avg ARI=0.546) tianhe What was done: Fixed 6 critical bugs across 3 error recovery scripts, launched 7 parallel GPU processes (m14_cpu/pi0/pi05 evaluations + Pi0.5 training), completed M13 analyses (kappa=-0.02, discriminability report) How it was done: Iterative fix-verify cycles on collector.py (error handling), train_pi05.sh (monitoring), evaluate_mimicgen.py (seeding), and discriminability script (type conversion). Used Slurm jobs 45628 (an49, 4 evaluations) and 46553 (an46, training) Impact: M14 evaluations now resilient to fingerprint mismatches (130 natural scenes), training observable in real-time (unbuffered logs), Pi0.5 training stabilized at 2.0s/step progressing toward 100K steps, and M13 classification reliability quantified (poor kappa, needs VLA data) Systematically optimized MIHD fusion pipeline achieving 100-500x speedup through vectorization and GPU batching, generalized STAIG to support arbitrary vision encoders, conducted comprehensive vision refinement experiments across 11 slides, while simultaneously fixing error recovery benchmark evaluation crashes and restarting Pi0.5 Phoenix training with improved monitoring
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Batch QFormer forward passes — Implemented forward_batched() method with pre-built padded neighbor tensors and key_padding_mask support to replace sequential spot-by-spot processing ✅ Fix fingerprint mismatch crash in evaluation pipeline — Modified collector.py to add scene-level try-except around _run_episode(), allowing evaluations to skip 130 incompatible natural capture scenes instead of crashing at scene 122 ✅ Vectorize STAIG edge weight calculation — Replaced O(n²) Python nested loops with scipy.cdist and NumPy vectorization in STAIGTrainer.py and STAIGTrainerE2E.py for edge weight computation during initialization ✅ Run vision refinement ablation experiments — Executed comprehensive comparison of 8 fusion methods (concat, mean, element_wise_sum, attention, basic_contrastive, adaln_attention, llava_mlp, qformer) with and without scan_cluster refinement on section 151673 🔄 Restart Pi0.5 LoRA training with monitoring — Updated train_pi05.sh with PYTHONUNBUFFERED, stdbuf, error trapping, and GPU monitoring; submitted job 46553 resuming from step 3000 with 2.0s/step rate and loss 0.068 ✅ Fix evaluation script bugs (env seeding, state validation, quat) — Added env.seed() for reproducibility, state dimension validation (8D check), and safe quaternion conversion (np.clip instead of in-place mutation) in evaluate_mimicgen.py 🔄 Resume m14 evaluations on GPU (cpu/pi0/pi05) — Relaunched 3 evaluation processes on an49 (job 45628) with –resume flag: m14_cpu at 1547 episodes, m14_pi0 at 400, m14_pi05 at 407, all progressing with new error handling ✅ Generalize STAIG fusion to support arbitrary vision encoders — Removed hardcoded UNI encoder requirement from pipeline orchestration layer, introduced encoder family detection (STAIG_UNI_FAMILY) to apply staig_strict preprocessing only when appropriate ✅ Complete M13 classifier reliability analysis — Ran 7_classifier_reliability.py producing kappa_matrix.csv, reliability_report.md with Fleiss’ kappa=-0.02 (poor), identified 2 non-redundancy violations (drop↔grasp_slip kappa=0.71) ✅ Complete M13 error type discriminability analysis — Fixed int(‘False’) bug and scipy.stats.kruskal degenerate case, generated discriminability_report.md showing all SR=0 with non-significant Kruskal-Wallis test ✅ Generate m14_cpu baseline analysis report — Ran 4_analyze_results.py on 726 episodes producing report.md + summary.json with Random SR=0% RP=2.3%, BC-RNN SR=0% RP=0.6%, Bootstrap 95% CI, and Fisher exact test Implementation & Fixes ✅ Deploy STAIG fusion across all DLPFC sections — Ran STAIG fusion on all 11 sections with both pca and none gene encoders, fixing UNI2 patch size incompatibility and NaN handling along the way ✅ Move adaptive_dropout_adj to GPU — Eliminated GPU↔CPU data transfers by generating random numbers directly on edge_attr device instead of transferring to CPU for dropout masking ✅ Update project documentation to v4.11.1 and v4.12 — Updated 项目全景总结.md with scene count 454→649, training status (job 46553), milestone progress (M13 analyses done, M14 in progress), and version history entries Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. QFormer training extremely slow (~3.5 hours) with only 5% GPU utilization due to Python for loop processing 2700 spots sequentially Solution: Implemented batched forward pass: pre-compute padded neighbor index tensor once at training start, use index_select for batch context construction, add key_padding_mask to transformer layers, process all spots in single GPU-parallel forward call
Key Insight: GPU severely underutilized when operations are serialized in Python loops - batching is essential for transformer models even when batch semantic is ‘spatial locations’ rather than ‘samples’
2. All 3 GPU evaluations (m14_cpu/pi0/pi05) crashed at scene 122/649 with EnvironmentMismatchError due to 130 natural capture scenes having different xml_hash fingerprints Solution: Added EnvironmentMismatchError import and scene-level try-except wrapper in collector.py around _run_episode() to log warnings and skip incompatible scenes instead of terminating
Key Insight: Database contains two fingerprint groups (519 impulse/augmented vs 130 natural VLA-generated scenes); robust error handling at iteration boundaries prevents cascade failures while preserving completed work via –resume
3. STAIG edge weight calculation uses O(n²) nested Python loops taking 2-5 seconds for 2700 spots, blocking training start Solution: Vectorized with scipy.spatial.distance.cdist for distance matrix computation and scipy.special.softmax(axis=1) for per-row normalization, then used NumPy advanced indexing edge_probabilities[rows, cols] instead of list comprehension
Key Insight: Nested loops with mathematical operations should always be vectorized - 100-500x speedup achievable by using scipy/NumPy primitives; the key is recognizing O(n²) patterns and finding the right library function (cdist for pairwise distances)
4. Unclear whether vision embedding refinement (scan_cluster: 1536d→256d) improves or hurts multimodal fusion performance Solution: Systematic ablation: ran all 8 fusion methods with and without refinement on section 151673, discovered that refine helps weak methods (mean +0.056, attention +0.086 ARI) but hurts strong methods (qformer -0.054, concat -0.074 ARI) - the dimensionality reduction trades off information for reduced noise
Key Insight: Dimensionality reduction’s value depends on downstream model capacity: simple aggregation methods (mean/attention) benefit from denoising and avoiding curse of dimensionality, but sophisticated learnable models (qformer/llava_mlp) can exploit the richer information in high-dimensional embeddings - there’s no universal answer
5. Pi0.5 training (job 46551) exited unexpectedly after ~580 steps due to stdout buffering preventing monitoring and unclear exit reason (code 0) Solution: Added PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 + stdbuf -oL for real-time logs, set -eo pipefail + ERR trap for error reporting, background GPU monitoring every 30min, and used –resume to continue from step 3000 checkpoint
Key Insight: Python/JAX buffered stdout can hide training failures; unbuffered output + explicit error trapping + periodic health checks are critical for 50+ hour training jobs on shared clusters
6. Pipeline hardcoded vision_encoder=‘uni’ for STAIG fusion, preventing experimentation with other encoders (HIPT, ResNet50, etc.) Solution: Refactored orchestration layer: introduced STAIG_UNI_FAMILY set to identify encoders needing staig_strict preprocessing (256×256 patch, no ImageNet normalization, frequency filtering), removed forced encoder override in run_benchmark.py, updated extraction_planner and evaluation_planner to conditionally apply variant based on encoder family membership
Key Insight: Separation of concerns: model layer (STAIGTrainer) already handled arbitrary dimensions via PCA, but orchestration layer imposed artificial constraints - good architecture makes this kind of generalization straightforward once identified
7. evaluate_mimicgen.py lacked environment seeding, making evaluation results non-reproducible across runs Solution: Added env.seed(args.seed) call before each task’s episode loop, matching reference implementation in LIBERO/Phoenix main.py
Key Insight: Reproducibility requires explicit seeding of both policy RNG and environment RNG; comparing against reference implementations reveals missing initialization steps
General Issues 8. adaptive_dropout_adj transfers edge_attr to CPU, generates random numbers on CPU, then moves back to GPU - causing sync overhead every epoch (~1-2s total across 1100 epochs) Solution: Generate random numbers directly on edge_attr.device with torch.rand(…, device=edge_attr.device, dtype=edge_attr.dtype) - eliminated all CPU transfers
Key Insight: Small GPU↔CPU transfers accumulate significantly when repeated many times; always generate random numbers on the same device as the tensor being operated on; CUDA synchronization overhead is non-negligible
9. UNI2 (ViT-H/14 with patch_size=14) failed on STAIG’s 256×256 input: ‘256 not divisible by 14’ assertion error Solution: Added automatic resize to 224×224 (divisible by 14) in UNI2VisionEncoder.extract() when STAIG strict mode is detected, before feeding patches to the model
Key Insight: Vision transformers have strict input size requirements based on patch size - when adapting preprocessing pipelines designed for one encoder to another, check divisibility constraints; 224×224 is the safe default for most ViTs
10. discriminability script crashed with ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ‘False’ when parsing success field from JSONL Solution: Added string-to-bool conversion: success_raw = row.get(‘success’, False); success = success_raw if isinstance(success_raw, bool) else success_raw.lower() == ’true’
Key Insight: JSONL serialization inconsistency—success field stored as string ‘False’ instead of boolean; defensive type checking prevents parse errors when schema assumptions break
11. m14_cpu crashed with AssertionError: MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID (0) must be in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (5) Solution: Changed MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID from 0 to 5 to match CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5, satisfying binding_utils.py assertion for device ID string containment
Key Insight: Robosuite’s binding_utils.py requires MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID as substring of CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; when using single GPU, both must match exactly
12. Section 151676 caused STAIG training to produce NaN loss and all-zero embeddings, making KMeans fallback also fail on NaN-filled data Solution: Added np.nan_to_num() in KMeans fallback path before clustering to replace NaN with 0 and inf with large finite numbers
Key Insight: Model collapse (NaN loss) is a known failure mode that needs graceful degradation; always sanitize inputs before passing to external libraries like sklearn that may not handle NaN robustly; document known failure cases
13. discriminability script crashed with scipy.stats.kruskal ValueError when all success rates were identical (degenerate case with all SR=0) Solution: Wrapped H, p = scipy_stats.kruskal(*groups) in try-except ValueError, returning H=0.0, p=1.0, significant=False, note=‘all values identical’ on exception
Key Insight: Statistical tests fail on degenerate distributions; explicit edge case handling with informative messages prevents silent failures and aids interpretation
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Strategic optimization planning vs tactical execution Role Approach Human User pre-analyzed MIHD codebase and provided detailed three-part optimization plan with specific code locations, expected speedups, and implementation steps - essentially wrote the spec for Claude to execute AI Claude followed the provided plan precisely, implementing vectorization with scipy.cdist, GPU device-aware random number generation, and batch processing with padded tensors - execution-focused rather than strategic Difference Analysis: User drove the strategic analysis and design phase (identifying bottlenecks, choosing algorithms, estimating speedups), while Claude served as precise implementation agent - this was explicit delegation of implementation after human did the hard thinking
Debugging strategy for multi-component pipeline failures Role Approach Human For error recovery crashes, human provided detailed context (649 scenes, fingerprint groups, crash location scene 122) and proposed specific fix location (collector.py line 299-325) with try-except pattern AI AI followed plan systematically but initially over-focused on exploring code structure; after human’s targeted guidance, AI directly implemented the fix and verified via test runs Difference Analysis: Human’s domain knowledge enabled precise root cause identification (EnvironmentMismatchError, no scene-level handler); AI’s strength was in verification (import checks, parallel relaunches, progress monitoring) but needed explicit plan for fastest resolution
Interpreting experimental results Role Approach Human User requested comprehensive vision refinement comparison but didn’t specify what conclusions to draw - open-ended analysis request AI Claude ran experiments, then synthesized the key insight that refinement’s value is contingent on downstream model capacity: helps simple methods by reducing noise/dimensionality, hurts complex methods by discarding information - went beyond data presentation to causal interpretation Difference Analysis: User requested data, AI provided interpretation framework - Claude identified the capacity-dependent trade-off pattern rather than just reporting metrics, showing deeper analytical thinking
Vision encoder generalization scope Role Approach Human User asked simply ‘use any vision encoder instead of only UNI’ - high-level requirement without specifying implementation approach AI Claude analyzed the system architecture, identified that the model layer was already flexible but orchestration layer imposed constraints, then introduced the concept of ’encoder families’ with conditional preprocessing variants - architectural insight beyond the literal request Difference Analysis: User specified the what (support arbitrary encoders), Claude designed the how (family-based conditional preprocessing) - AI added valuable structural insight about maintaining UNI’s special preprocessing requirements while generalizing
Training monitoring and observability requirements Role Approach Human Human specified concrete monitoring improvements (PYTHONUNBUFFERED, stdbuf, error trapping, GPU memory logging) based on previous failure analysis (buffered logs, silent exit) AI AI implemented all specified improvements but didn’t initially recognize the critical importance of unbuffered output; after seeing ‘PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 生效了’ remark, AI internalized this pattern Difference Analysis: Human anticipated observability needs from past failure modes; AI learned the pattern through execution feedback rather than proactive design
When to stop exploring and start executing Role Approach Human Human interrupted Agent tool usage twice when AI was about to launch exploratory subagents, preferring direct action on known tasks AI AI defaulted to Agent tool for broad queries like ‘what’s unblocked?’, attempting to parallelize exploration even when task list was already clear from documentation Difference Analysis: Human recognized when sufficient information existed for direct execution; AI over-indexed on thoroughness via exploration when decisive action was more valuable
Implementation Level When to use agents vs direct tool execution Role Approach Human User let Claude decide when to spawn agents for exploration - didn’t micromanage the investigation approach AI Claude spawned multiple exploration agents to understand data loading pipeline and fusion training loops before creating the optimization plan - used agents proactively for open-ended codebase exploration Difference Analysis: AI correctly applied the pattern of using agents for discovery/research tasks and direct tools for known operations; human trusted this judgment without intervention
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Failed to proactively verify that both gene_encoder=pca and gene_encoder=none would produce identical results in STAIG fusion before running both - wasted computation on redundant experiment that yielded no new information Did not proactively verify checkpoint state before designing training restart plan—assumed ‘checkpoint 1000’ from plan without checking current filesystem state (which had step 3000). This required human to later discover the 3000 checkpoint via manual ls commands Failed to recognize stdout buffering as critical failure mode for long-running training until explicitly told by human. The previous run’s silent exit with code 0 should have triggered suspicion about log reliability General Limitations In the vision refinement experiments, didn’t initially notice that qformer baseline (0.4832) was actually the best overall result - only highlighted this after running all comparisons; should have flagged this earlier to potentially adjust experimental priorities Did not catch the inconsistency between plan text (‘checkpoint 1000’) and actual filesystem state until implementation phase, suggesting insufficient upfront verification before committing to execution path Took multiple rounds of debugging to discover the UNI2 patch size incompatibility - could have anticipated this from knowing UNI2 architecture (ViT-H/14) and STAIG’s 256×256 requirement before attempting the run Over-relied on subagent exploration for simple status checks (e.g., launching Task agents to check M14/M16 status when direct file reads would suffice). This added latency and complexity without proportional value When multiple sessions referenced the same experiments (vision refinement comparison), Claude didn’t explicitly connect them chronologically or indicate this was a continuation - caused some confusion in narrative flow Learnings Key Learnings Batch processing is critical for GPU efficiency: Python loops that repeatedly call small GPU operations (even 2700 calls) create severe underutilization (5% GPU for QFormer) - always look for opportunities to aggregate operations into single GPU kernel launches through batching Dimensionality reduction’s value depends on downstream model capacity: helps simple aggregation methods (mean, attention) by reducing noise and curse of dimensionality (+0.05-0.09 ARI), but hurts sophisticated learnable models (qformer, llava_mlp) that can exploit richer information in high dimensions (-0.05 ARI) - no universal answer, must match preprocessing to model complexity Robust error handling at iteration boundaries (scene-level try-except) prevents cascade failures in long-running batch processes while preserving partial results via resume mechanisms Vectorization delivers 100-1000x speedups for mathematical operations on arrays: replacing Python nested loops with scipy/NumPy primitives (cdist, softmax, advanced indexing) is almost always worth it - the key is recognizing O(n²) patterns and knowing the right library function Unbuffered output (PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 + stdbuf -oL) is non-negotiable for monitoring long-running ML training jobs on remote clusters—buffering can hide failures for hours and make debugging impossible Reproducibility in RL/robotics evaluation requires explicit seeding of both policy RNG and environment RNG; comparing against reference implementations reveals missing initialization steps that documentation may omit Architecture flexibility through family-based conditional logic: when generalizing from hardcoded assumptions (UNI-only), introduce semantic groupings (encoder families) with conditional behavior rather than removing all constraints - preserves special-case optimizations while enabling flexibility Practical Learnings GPU↔CPU transfer elimination matters at scale: small transfers (edge_attr tensor) seem negligible but accumulate across many iterations (1100 epochs × multiple dropout calls) to 1-2 seconds total - always generate/operate on device-local data when possible Vision transformer input requirements are strict: ViTs require input dimensions divisible by patch size (UNI2: H%14=0, W%14=0) - when adapting preprocessing designed for one architecture to another, verify dimensional constraints early; 224×224 is safe default for most ViTs Statistical tests (like scipy.stats.kruskal) fail on degenerate distributions; always add edge case handling with informative error messages rather than letting library exceptions propagate Defensive type checking (isinstance() guards) prevents parse errors when serialization format assumptions break; JSONL fields can have inconsistent types across different data sources Model collapse (NaN loss) requires graceful degradation paths: when known failure modes exist (151676 section), add sanitization steps (np.nan_to_num) in fallback paths and document the issue - better to produce degraded output (ARI=0 with clean data) than crash When debugging multi-GPU Slurm jobs, MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES must have exact string matching—substring containment check in binding_utils.py requires both to align Conversation Summaries MIHD Spatial Transcriptomics ✅ CPU Bottleneck Optimization and Architecture Generalization 05:38:48.477 | claude_code Comprehensive optimization of MIHD fusion training pipeline addressing three bottlenecks: (1) vectorized STAIG edge weight calculation with scipy.cdist replacing O(n²) loops for 100-500x speedup, (2) moved adaptive_dropout_adj to GPU eliminating transfers for ~1-2s savings, (3) added batch processing to QFormer with forward_batched() method for 20-50x speedup. Weekly Report — 2026-W08 (2026-02-16 ~ 2026-02-22) This week, with the MIHD spatial transcriptomics project as the main focus, we completed a systematic investigation of H&E Image-Only clustering (establishing the ARI literature baseline of 0.11–0.16), implemented three self-supervised enhancement schemes (SCAN increased ARI from 0.251 to 0.303, +20.6%), and built a two-stage fusion framework for Vision Refinement; simultaneously, on the tianhe cluster, we advanced the Error Recovery Benchmark (verification of M14 evaluation infrastructure, full assessment start for 649 scenarios) and the Phoenix pi0.5 reproduction data pipeline (18.4GB MimicGen dataset uploaded, training configuration in place). Throughout the week, we resolved multiple engineering bottlenecks such as STEGO NaN, double normalization bug, lerobot version conflicts, and HuggingFace proxy issues, while two bottlenecks related to Pi0.5 OOM and visualize_scene.py video validation were postponed to next week.
Weekly Overview Metric Value Date Range 2026-02-16 ~ 2026-02-22 Active Days 3 / 7 Total Conversation Count 9 Projects Involved 4 Tasks Completed 11 Ongoing Tasks 5 Total Tokens 28,509,501 Total Cost $14.13 Average Daily Cost $4.71 Project Progress MIHD (Spatial Transcriptomics Clustering) (3 active days) — 🔄 active Completed:
Completed four core technical documents: RM-IDEAL bilingual guide, visual encoder usage manual, pathological PFM literature review, and UNI/UNI2 original paper evaluation analysis. Conducted a systematic investigation of H&E Image-Only methods, established the DLPFC ARI literature baseline (SpaConTDS=0.16, stLearn=0.11), and analyzed the five root causes of Foundation Model failure. Implemented and verified three self-supervised enhancement schemes: STEGO/BYOL+GAT/SCAN. SCAN achieved the best result with ARI=0.303 (baseline 0.251, +20.6%), and its integration with gene feature fusion was validated as complementary (mean fusion +0.065 ARI). Identified and fixed the STAIG double normalization bug in eval_scan_fusion.py, deciding to use the correct path in run_benchmark.py. Integrated a CacheManager embedding cache in run_benchmark.py (loaded in seconds, supports custom cache names for scan_uni2). Implemented the Vision Refinement two-stage fusion framework (–vision_refine parameter, ~60 lines minimal intrusion), and started batch experiments with 7 fusion strategies in the background. Re-generated all 11 sections visually in batches (using .npz cache, no re-inference required), and added an H&E original image panel. Bottlenecks:
⚠️ The coordinate dimension bug in eval_scan_fusion.py caused incomplete debugging of the SCAN fusion joint evaluation script. ⚠️ The first experiment of Vision Refinement (scan_cluster + concat, ARI=0.313) was lower than direct concat (0.387), and the issue of feature diversity in self-supervised compression losses needs further analysis. ⚠️ The implementation of ImageEncoder enhancement for the large goal 7 in ENHANCEMENT_PLAN_CN.md has not started. Error Recovery Benchmark & Phoenix pi0.5 Reproduction (1 active day) — 🔄 active Completed:
Developed a complete Phase II execution plan with 7 steps, covering large goals G1–G7 and milestones M12–M15, with a key path of approximately 16 days. Verified the M14 baseline evaluation infrastructure for 10 scenarios (sanity check passed), and started full CPU assessment for 649 scenarios (exceeded expectations by 454, +43%). Diagnosed the Pi0.5 OOM bottleneck, and standardized GPU access to srun –overlap. Resolved the incompatibility issue between lerobot 0.1.0 and datasets>=4.0 (downgraded to 3.6.0). Established hf-mirror.com as the standard solution for cluster HuggingFace data retrieval. Bottlenecks:
⚠️ Pi0.5 OOM remains unresolved (GPU memory insufficient at 150MB), and the baseline assessment is still blocked. ⚠️ The extension of force parameters in visualize_scene.py is complete, but video validation is blocked due to SLURM node permissions issues. ⚠️ Port conflict on Pi0 VLA Server (port 5555 occupied) caused session interruption. Key Tasks ✅ Systematic Investigation of H&E Image-Only Clustering Methods (2026-02-19) — Collected a comprehensive overview of methods such as MILWRM/F-SEG/Deep Contrastive Clustering, verified the image-only DLPFC ARI values (SpaConTDS=0.16, stLearn=0.11) through ablation experiments, and deeply investigated the applications of BYOL/STEGO/SCAN in pathology, along with a four-level domain gap resolution framework in the CV community. ✅ Establishment of MIHD Technical Documentation System (2026-02-19) — Created four core technical documents: RM-IDEAL bilingual structure document, visual encoder usage guide (12 chapters), pathological PFM literature review, and UNI/UNI2 original paper evaluation analysis (34 clinical tasks). ✅ Analysis of Root Causes of Foundation Model Failure in Spatial Domain (2026-02-19) — Conducted a systematic analysis from five dimensions: domain mismatch in training data, pre-training task mismatch, minimal morphological differences between brain tissue layers, feature redundancy, and lack of spatial context. Supported by cases involving the brown repeated patches in UNI2. ✅ Implementation of Image-Only Clustering Enhancement Schemes (STEGO/BYOL+GAT/SCAN) (2026-02-19) — Created four model files: STEGOHead/BYOLAdapter/SpatialGATRefiner/SCANHead. Completed comparative tests on 151673 sections, with SCAN achieving the best result with ARI=0.303 (+20.6%). ✅ Investigation and Architecture Decision for STAIG Fusion Double Normalization Bug (2026-02-20) — Confirmed that the missing staig_alignment_config in eval_scan_fusion.py caused internal StandardScaler in STAIGTrainer; decided to use the correct path in run_benchmark.py instead of fixing a separate script. ✅ Integration of Embedding Cache Mechanism in run_benchmark.py (2026-02-20) — Introduced CacheManager, checking the cache before gene/vision encoding, and skipping encoder instantiation if hit (loaded in seconds). Supports custom cache names for scan_uni2, with three variants for vision cache: standard, freq, staig_strict. 🔄 Verification of M14 Baseline Evaluation Infrastructure and Full Assessment Start (2026-02-22) — Sanity check (60 episodes, ~7 minutes, SR=0% as expected), followed by start of full CPU assessment for 649 scenarios × 2 strategies × 3 seeds (≈ 3894 episodes), running in the background. 🔄 Construction of Full Data Pipeline for Phoenix pi0.5 Reproduction (2026-02-22) — Written convert_mimicgen_to_lerobot.py and evaluate_mimicgen.py, configured pi05_base_mimicgen_phoenix training parameters, downloaded the 18.4GB MimicGen dataset via hf-mirror.com (9 tasks, 9000 demos), and completed format conversion (7–8/9 tasks). 🔄 Joint Evaluation of SCAN Embedding and Multimodal Fusion (2026-02-19) — Written eval_scan_fusion.py, comparing the optimized 256-dimensional visual embedding of SCAN with PCA gene features across all fusion methods; mean fusion achieved ARI +0.065, partially resolved the coords dimension bug, and script debugging in progress. 🔄 Implementation and Batch Experiments of MIHD Vision Refinement Two-Stage Fusion Framework (2026-02-22) — Added –vision_refine parameter (scan_cluster/stego_refine/byol_spatial), with ~60 lines of code minimal intrusion, first experiment showed ARI=0.313 lower than baseline concat 0.387; 7 fusion strategies running in the background. ✅ Completion of Full Phase II Execution Plan for Error Recovery Benchmark (2026-02-22) — Analyzed the dependencies between large goals G1–G7 and milestones M12–M15, developed a 7-step execution plan, and clarified the GPU allocation strategy (srun –overlap, ≥50% free memory), with a key path of approximately 16 days. ✅ Diagnosis of Error Recovery Benchmark Baseline and Update of GPU Access Specification (2026-02-22) — Resolved Pi0.5 OOM (150MB memory shortage), BC-RNN obs key issue, and 649 scenario readiness; standardized GPU access in CLAUDE.md and MEMORY.md to srun –overlap. 🚫 Extension of force parameters in visualize_scene.py (2026-02-22) — Completed addition of force_override/duration_override/settle_steps parameters and Phase 3 neutral action logic; video validation blocked due to SLURM node permissions issues. ✅ Special Comparative Experiment for STAIG Fusion (151673) (2026-02-20) — Tested staig_fusion × {UNI2_raw, SCAN(UNI2)} separately, ARI values were 0.3929/0.3880, almost equal; verified that STAIG internal StandardScaler+PCA offset the effects of SCAN optimization. ✅ Addition of H&E Panel and Batch Update of UNI2 Visualization (2026-02-19) — Changed to a 1×3 layout (H&E + GT + prediction), re-generated all 11 sections visually using .npz cache, 151510 fixed via hires→lowres symlink. Issues and Solutions 1. STEGO Training loss is NaN throughout, 3639×3639 dense similarity matrix overflows in float32 operations at temperature=0.07 [MIHD] (2026-02-19) Solution: Two-step fix: perform L2 normalization on the input image_emb;Change InfoNCE to the numerical stability version (subtract the maximum value of rows before computing logsumexp, and increase temperature to 0.1).
2. MILWRM was incorrectly classified as an Image-Only method; the initial AI summary will mix multimodal methods with image-only results. The initial research conclusion needs significant revision [MIHD] (2026-02-19)Solution: Use WebFetch to read the full PMC text and confirm that MILWRM is actually based on gene expression, specifically mining only image-only data points from ablation experiments on articles like SpaConTDS. 3. There is a double normalization bug in staig_fusion in eval_scan_fusion.py (STAIGTrainer internally applies StandardScaler again) [MIHD] (2026-02-20) Solution: Abandon fixing the standalone script and directly use run_benchmark.py that correctly passes staig_alignment_config, reusing the verified path.
4. run_benchmark.py instantiates the encoder each time to extract embeddings, lacking pipeline-level cache support [MIHD] (2026-02-20) Solution: Integrate CacheManager from pipeline/cache_manager.py, load from cache before encoding, and write back to cache after extraction; skip encoder instantiation when a cache hit occurs.
5. Lerobot 0.1.0 is incompatible with datasets >=4.0 (torch.stack reports TypeError: Column object replaces list) [Error Recovery Benchmark / Phoenix pi0.5] (2026-02-22) Solution: Downgrade datasets from 4.4.1 to 3.6.0 (<4.0); datasets 4.0 changes the return value of dataset[‘column’] from a list to a Column object, and Lerobot expects a list/tuple of tensors.
6. The official HuggingFace download fails due to proxy (Squid 503), and the Python download script cannot connect [Error Recovery Benchmark / Phoenix pi0.5] (2026-02-22) Solution: Use hf-mirror.com + wget; URL format: https://hf-mirror.com/datasets/{repo_id}/resolve/main/{file_path}，通过集群 HTTP proxy reaches 40–200MB/s.
7. Unstable access to SLurm GPU nodes: srun lacks –overlap, causing command hangs; direct SSH connection is unreliable, and multi-partition submissions are rejected [Error Recovery Benchmark / Phoenix pi0.5] (2026-02-22) Solution: Standardize the workflow: source set-XY-I.sh → squeue → srun –jobid= –overlap; avoid direct SSH to GPU nodes.
8. Abnormal spatial coordinate dimension in eval_scan_fusion.py (turns into (1,2)), causing errors in multiple fusion methods [MIHD] (2026-02-19) Solution: Abandon calling load_spatial_coordinates() (barcode matching fails), and directly read coordinates from adata.obsm[‘spatial’]; fix the unpacking error in load_dlpfc_data return value.
Learning Gains Domain Knowledge (domain) Pure image-only achieves only 0.11–0.16 ARI in DLPFC fine-grained stratification tasks (multimodal reaches 0.45–0.64), which is a combination of extremely small morphological differences between brain layers and mismatch in the Foundation Model training domain; ablation experiments of multimodal methods almost never test image-only separately—this is a noteworthy research gap. Five main reasons for failure in space domain recognition by Foundation Models: ① Training mainly on cancer tissue (domain gap); ② Pre-training task mismatch with inter-layer gradient recognition; ③ Extremely small morphological differences between cerebral cortex layers; ④ High redundancy between image features and gene expression; ⑤ Lack of spatial context in independent encoding of a single patch. STAIG uses BYOL for unsupervised domain adaptation on target dataset H&E patches (keep encoder after training, discard projector/predictor)—this is a direct precedent for introducing unsupervised domain adaptation into spatial transcriptomics; the design of BYOL without negative samples is naturally suitable for small batch ST scenarios (thousands of patches per section). The CV community has a four-stage framework for handling “domain gap + fine-grained task + unlabeled data”: Level 1: direct pre-trained feature clustering → Level 2: STEGO/SCAN feature refinement → Level 3: domain-specific SSL re-training (BYOL/MAE) → Level 4: dedicated Foundation Model; GPFM/CHIEF are the optimal PFM for space domain recognition ARI, and UNI2 are the optimal spot retrieval. Architecture (architecture) SCAN is the optimal ARI (0.303, +20.6%) in image-only spatial transcriptomics scenarios. Its core advantage is that offline feature k-NN mining decouples embedding learning and clustering; its 256-dimensional optimized embeddings complement gene features (mean fusion +0.065 ARI). Two-stage fusion is not necessarily better than single-stage: after scanning_cluster compresses visual embeddings from 1536d to 256d, multimodal fusion ARI (0.313) is lower than direct concat (0.387), indicating that self-supervised compression loses the original feature diversity required for fusion tasks, and the optimization objectives of self-supervised clustering conflict with downstream fusion tasks. Internal StandardScaler+PCA preprocessing in STAIG fusion absorbs the external embedding optimization effect (the ARI difference between SCAN and UNI2_raw is only 0.005); embedding cache should store raw embeddings before normalization, and post-encoder normalization should be performed after loading to ensure consistent results across different call paths. VLA baseline evaluation must explicitly state the checkpoint source: using non-target task fine-tuning models (pi0_libero, pi05_base) to evaluate zero-sample cross-domain recovery capacity—the paper must actively declare this experimental setup, and subsequent comparative experiments after fine-tuning are needed to fully demonstrate the usefulness of the dataset. In complex experimental systems, prefer using existing, verified tool paths (such as run_benchmark.py); standalone scripts easily introduce hidden bugs such as inconsistent preprocessing; before calling internal project functions, read the source code in real time to verify the function signature, rather than relying on memory. Debugging (debugging) When computing large-scale dense similarity matrix (n>3000) and InfoNCE contrast loss, use numerically stable log-sum-exp (subtracting row maximum), otherwise exponential operations with temperature=0.07 at float32 precision will overflow and produce NaN; this is a key engineering constraint for large-scale contrast learning implementation. Tools (tools) Lerobot 0.1.0 has strict constraints on datasets versions; it must be pinned to <4.0 (recommended 3.x); datasets 4.0 change the return value of dataset[‘column’] to a Column object, causing torch.stack to report TypeError; MimicGen is fully compatible with LIBERO obs/action format (84×84 images, 8D state, 7D action)—OpenPI’s LeRobotLiberoDataConfig can be directly reused. The standard solution for accessing HuggingFace on Chinese mainland HPC clusters is hf-mirror.com; URL format: https://hf-mirror.com/datasets/{repo_id}/resolve/main/{file_path}，通过 wget + HTTP proxy reaches 40–200MB/s—this should be used as the default solution. OpenPI’s JAX training naturally supports multi-GPU data parallelism; just specify the GPU list in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and JAX automatically builds a 2D mesh parallel—no changes to TrainConfig are needed; Slurm –overlap is a key parameter for running new commands on existing interactive jobs—it is a core technique for calling cluster GPUs in Claude Code environment. AI Usage Notes Effective Modes:
✓ Parallel sub-tasks explore the project structure and formulate cleanup plans (MIHD organizes tasks), reducing serial exploration time. ✓ Parallel background execution on GPU with three schemes (STEGO/BYOL/SCAN) for comparison and validation, significantly reducing total experimental time. ✓ Use .npz caching to generate visualizations in bulk, completely decoupling inference and visualization—11/11 sections succeed. ✓ Independent temporary script (_test_staig_scan.py) isolates testing a single fusion method, shortening a 2-hour task to 30 seconds. ✓ Independent exploration of JAX multi-GPU mechanisms (no config changes) and the hf-mirror.com alternative download method—no user intervention required. ✓ Minimal invasive code change (about 60 lines): insert a Vision Refinement stage in run_benchmark.py, maintaining architecture stability. Limitations:
✗ Inadequate accuracy in literature classification: MILWRM is incorrectly classified as image-only method; initial research aggregation mixes with multimodal results—requires two user interventions to converge on the correct research boundary. ✗ Lack of awareness to actively expose key experimental assumptions: No explicit mention of the impact of using LIBERO fine-tuning checkpoint in VLA evaluation on experiment effectiveness—needs user inquiry to discuss further. ✗ API usage tends to rely on memory rather than real-time verification: Multiple function signature/return value unpacking errors occur in eval_scan_fusion.py—source code should be read before calling. ✗ Slurm permission issues tend to involve listing multiple partitions (5+ times)—no quick query to the user about correct account/partition information. ✗ Insufficient status judgment for background tasks: Data conversion is still running when LeRobot dataset validation triggers, leading to false timestamp violation errors; frequent sleep polling is interrupted multiple times. ✗ Using CPU by default for model validation in HPC environments hides real performance issues, causing additional interaction overhead. Next Week’s Plan Next week will focus on three parallel lines: ①MIHD: fix the coordinate bug in eval_scan_fusion.py, complete joint evaluation of SCAN embedding and full fusion strategies, analyze batch results of 7 fusion strategies and diagnose the root cause of Vision Refinement compression losses, and consider adjusting refinement hidden_dim or switching to stego_refine/byol_spatial; ②Error Recovery Benchmark: organize full CPU evaluation results for M14 649 scenario, solve Pi0.5 OOM problem (apply larger memory GPU or reduce batch size), start Phoenix pi0.5 100K steps 4-GPU training; ③Engineering blocking removal: resolve SLURM node permission issues and complete visualize_scene.py video validation, resolve Pi0 VLA Server port conflict (detect with lsof -i:5555 + backup port mechanism), and advance implementation of ImageEncoder enhancement for goal 7 in ENHANCEMENT_PLAN_CN.md.

summary: This week, with the MIHD spatial transcriptomics project as the main focus, a systematic investigation was completed on H&E Image-Only clustering (establishing a literature baseline of ARI 0.11–0.16), three self-supervised enhancement methods were implemented (SCAN increased ARI from 0.251 to 0.303, +20.6%), and a two-stage fusion framework for Vision Refinement was established; meanwhile, on the tianhe cluster, the Error Recovery Benchmark (M14 evaluation infrastructure verification, full assessment of 649 scenarios started) and the Phoenix pi0.5 reproduction data pipeline (18.4GB MimicGen dataset stored, training configuration in place) were advanced in parallel.
