title: Weekly Summary 2026-W08

content:
Daily Report — 2026-02-22 Daily Overview What was done: Advanced three major projects: implemented and tested MIHD’s Vision Refinement architecture while cleaning project structure; updated gadget documentation and generated 3 weeks of historical reports; transitioned Error Recovery Benchmark from Phase I infrastructure to Phase II experimentation through M14 baseline evaluation and Pi0.5 fine-tuning preparation How it was done: Used systematic multi-agent exploration for project organization, implemented Vision Refinement with 10 code modifications across 150 lines, ran parallel GPU evaluations across 7 fusion methods, executed M14 sanity check via Slurm cluster with EGL rendering, designed 7-step Phase II execution plan with dependency topology, and set up MimicGen dataset conversion pipeline for Pi0.5 fine-tuning Impact: MIHD gained new experimental dimension (two-stage fusion) with cleaner project structure; gadget achieved complete documentation coverage and comprehensive work history archive; Error Recovery Benchmark unblocked all Phase II work with proven evaluation workflow, established Slurm-based GPU access pattern, and initiated VLA fine-tuning pipeline for 9 Phoenix tasks DCC What was done: Completed MIHD Vision Refinement implementation, initial testing, and comprehensive file organization (deleted 3 redundant scripts, reorganized documentation, created unified plans.md) How it was done: Modified run_benchmark.py to add –vision_refine parameter with scan_cluster/stego_refine/byol_spatial options, tested on 151673 slice with PCA+UNI2+scan_cluster refine, launched 7-method fusion sweep in background; used Explore agents to generate cleanup plan, then executed file deletion, log migration, and documentation restructuring Impact: Enabled two-stage fusion experiments (refinement + multimodal fusion) though initial results showed refinement not universally superior (ARI 0.313 vs 0.387 direct concat); significantly improved project maintainability with root directory reduced to 2 core files and clear three-tier documentation structure MacBook What was done: Updated gadget documentation to add missing website tool coverage and generated batch historical daily reports for 21 dates spanning 2026-02-01 through 2026-02-21 How it was done: Used /init skill for systematic CLAUDE.md review, manually updated README.md with website tool details; iteratively called daily report generation tool for past dates, merging multiple device sessions per date into consolidated reports Impact: Completed documentation for all three gadget tools (summarize, test, website), established comprehensive 3-week work history archive covering Error Recovery Benchmark, MIHD, and cross-project activities tianhe What was done: Executed Error Recovery Benchmark Phase II baseline evaluation (M14 sanity check + full evaluation), created comprehensive execution plan with dependency topology, updated CLAUDE.md for Slurm workflow, and initiated Pi0.5 Phoenix fine-tuning pipeline with MimicGen dataset conversion How it was done: Created 3-level goal topology diagram, ran M14 sanity check (60 episodes, 7 minutes), launched full 649-scene evaluation in background via Slurm with EGL rendering; replaced SSH-based GPU access with squeue + srun workflow; set up MimicGen-to-LeRobot conversion pipeline for 9 Phoenix tasks (4500 demos, 18.4GB), completed 7/9 task conversions, configured pi05_base_mimicgen_phoenix training setup Impact: Validated end-to-end evaluation pipeline and unblocked Phase II experimentation; established stable GPU access pattern preventing SSH disconnections; diagnosed Pi0.5 OOM blocker (150MB allocation failure) preventing large-scale baseline runs; prepared infrastructure for fine-tuning Pi0.5 on 9 Phoenix manipulation tasks with 4-GPU training capability Completed MIHD Vision Refinement two-stage fusion implementation with initial testing and comprehensive file cleanup; generated gadget documentation updates and batch historical reports; executed Error Recovery Benchmark Phase II M14 baseline evaluation with GPU scheduling optimization and Pi0.5 fine-tuning pipeline setup
Tasks Architecture & Strategy 🔄 Error Recovery Benchmark full M14-cpu evaluation — Launched background evaluation of 649 scenes × 2 policies (Random + BC-RNN) × 3 seeds = 3,894 episodes on GPU 0 with EGL rendering. Estimated 6.5 hours based on sanity check timing ✅ Implement Vision Refinement two-stage fusion architecture — Added –vision_refine parameter to run_benchmark.py with three methods (scan_cluster/stego_refine/byol_spatial), inserted refinement stage between vision encoding and fusion with ~50 lines of logic, modified 10 functions including get_result_path, check_result_exists, load_existing_result, run_evaluation to support refinement parameter in caching and naming, updated experiment_logger.py CSV columns ✅ Error Recovery Benchmark M14 sanity check evaluation — Ran 10 scenes × 2 policies (Random + BC-RNN) × 3 seeds = 60 episodes via Slurm on GPU 0, validated collector resume capability, error detection (20 classifiers), and JSONL output format. Completed in 7 minutes with 0% success rate as expected ✅ Error Recovery Benchmark Phase II execution plan — Wrote comprehensive 7-step plan covering M12 (large dataset), M13 (classification justification), M14 (baseline evaluation), M15 (usefulness proof). Includes file checklist, GPU allocation strategy (50% memory threshold for 8 A800 GPUs), 16-day critical path timeline, and Slurm usage patterns ✅ Vision Refinement initial testing (151673 slice) — Tested PCA + UNI2 + scan_cluster refine + concat on 151673: vision embedding (3639,1536) refined to (3639,256), concatenated with PCA gene_emb (50d) to 306d. Results: ARI=0.313, NMI=0.433, Silhouette=0.146, higher than image-only scan_cluster (ARI 0.303) but lower than direct concat (ARI 0.387) ✅ Error Recovery Benchmark experiment status verification — Used parallel Task agents to search outputs, logs, and project summaries. Found: 649 error scenes generated (M1-M11 complete), MimicGen augmentation complete (+193 scenes), BC-RNN injection complete (+61 scenes), but M14 baseline evaluation NOT started due to Pi0.5 GPU OOM (150MB allocation failure on 2026-02-21 04:17) ✅ Create Error Recovery Benchmark goal dependency topology — Created comprehensive 3-level dependency visualization (G1-G7 goals, M12-M15 milestones, S-level sub-goals) identifying M14 as critical path blocker, inserted into 项目全景总结.md 🔄 Pi0.5 Phoenix fine-tuning pipeline setup — Downloaded all 9 MimicGen core datasets (4500 demos, 18.4GB), created convert_mimicgen_to_lerobot.py script supporting flat/nested HDF5 layouts, completed 7/9 task conversions (three_piece_assembly_d0/d1 remaining), configured pi05_base_mimicgen_phoenix training config (batch_size=64, 100K steps, cosine LR), created evaluate_mimicgen.py following Phoenix CVPR 2025 protocol, configured 4-GPU training capability, fixed datasets version compatibility (downgraded 4.4.1 → 3.6.0) 🔄 Vision Refinement full fusion method sweep — Launched 7 multimodal fusion methods (mean, element_wise_sum, attention, basic_contrastive, adaln_attention, llava_mlp, qformer) with scan_cluster refinement on 151673. Concat completed (ARI 0.313), others running in background. QFormer slow due to high memory (19.4GB) but low GPU utilization (4%, 55W) ✅ MIHD documentation reorganization — Created three-tier docs/ structure (research/, experiments/, archived/), moved GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md to archived/, moved BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md to docs/, moved research reports to research/, moved experiment summaries to experiments/, merged ENHANCEMENT_PLAN.md/ENHANCEMENT_PLAN_CN.md into docs/plans.md with project overview, Phase 1-2 progress, Batch 3-4 plans, architecture roadmap, and key metrics (current DLPFC ARI max 0.528) ❌ VLA baseline evaluation setup (Pi0 + Pi0.5) — Attempted to start Pi0 server (port 5555) and Pi0.5 server (port 5557) on GPU 1-2. Pi0 blocked by port conflict, Pi0.5 started successfully. Clarified checkpoint choice ambiguity: pi0_libero (LIBERO-finetuned) vs pi05_base (pretrained) both domain-mismatched for PickPlace task Implementation & Fixes ✅ gadget batch historical daily report generation — Generated structured daily reports for 21 past dates (2026-02-01 through 2026-02-21) covering Error Recovery Benchmark, MIHD, and other projects. Performed multiple export → analyze → merge iterations per date to consolidate multi-device conversation logs into unified reports ✅ Update Error Recovery Benchmark CLAUDE.md for Slurm workflow — Replaced unstable SSH-based GPU access with Slurm workflow: source set-XY-I.sh → squeue → srun –jobid=. Updated CLAUDE.md “Server Constraints” section and memory/MEMORY.md with 3-step pattern, documented SSH instability warning ✅ MIHD project file cleanup — Deleted 3 redundant scripts (run_benchmark_legacy_backup.py 77KB, run_benchmark_refactored.py 15KB, run_benchmark_from_config.py 19KB), cleaned all pycache directories, created outputs/logs/ and moved 5 pipeline_.log files (~5MB), deleted 16 summary_20260219* fragment files ✅ gadget CLAUDE.md and README.md documentation improvement — Used /init skill to discover missing website/ tool documentation, added Hugo blog architecture description, update.sh command reference, incremental media compression pipeline details, cross-reference to test/CLAUDE.md for benchmark flags, updated README.md tool table and Website section ✅ Update MIHD CLAUDE.md and Memory references — Removed non-existent docs/PCA_WORKFLOW.md reference, updated file paths to docs/BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md and docs/archived/GEMINI.md, added Vision Refinement usage example (–vision_refine scan_cluster), synchronized Memory file paths Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Pi0.5 VLA server hits GPU OOM when loading model (150MB allocation failure logged on 2026-02-21 04:17), blocking M14 baseline evaluation of 7,800 episodes (649 scenes × 4 policies × 3 seeds) Solution: Identified blocker but did not fix during session - requires either switching to GPU with larger memory or reducing batch size. Documented issue for follow-up; also initiated alternative path of fine-tuning pi05_base on MimicGen tasks to create domain-matched baseline
Key Insight: M14 baseline infrastructure complete and ready but cannot start until Pi0.5 memory issue resolved. Created parallel path (fine-tuning) to establish appropriate baseline while debugging OOM issue
2. VLA checkpoint selection ambiguity: pi0_libero (LIBERO-tuned) and pi05_base (generic pretrained) both domain-mismatched for PickPlace task, potentially weakening dataset usefulness claims Solution: User paused execution to question checkpoint relevance. Identified need for explicit decision: use existing checkpoints as-is for generic baseline or fine-tune on PickPlace/Phoenix data first. Initiated fine-tuning pipeline as solution path
Key Insight: Baseline evaluation requires careful model selection: domain-mismatched checkpoints may underperform due to distribution shift rather than dataset quality, making usefulness claims invalid. Need task-aligned baseline for fair evaluation
3. Vision Refinement scan_cluster method achieved ARI 0.313, lower than direct concat (0.387), indicating 256d compression loses information valuable for multimodal fusion despite improving single-modality clustering (0.303) Solution: Continue testing remaining 6 fusion methods (attention, adaln_attention, llava_mlp, qformer, etc.) to determine if certain strategies better utilize refined 256d embeddings; consider adjusting hidden_dim or testing alternative refinement methods (stego_refine, byol_spatial)
Key Insight: Self-supervised clustering methods optimize for cluster separability, which may not align with multimodal fusion’s information complementarity objectives. Dimensionality reduction can filter out features valuable for gene-vision complementarity even if less relevant for image-only clustering
4. GPU allocation strategy unclear: initially assumed only GPU 0 available despite 8 A800 GPUs existing on Slurm node Solution: Human clarified to check all GPUs via nvidia-smi and use any with 50%+ free memory. Updated plan to dynamically check memory usage and allocate CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES accordingly, enabling parallel task execution
Key Insight: In shared HPC environments, availability ≠ idle. Need memory-based criteria (50% threshold) rather than binary idle check. Multiple tasks can share node if memory allows, maximizing cluster utilization
5. SSH connections to GPU nodes (an49, an53, etc.) unstable and disconnect frequently, interrupting long-running experiments Solution: Switched to Slurm-based workflow documented in CLAUDE.md: use squeue to find active jobs, then srun –jobid= to attach to allocated node. Avoids direct SSH and leverages Slurm’s job management layer
Key Insight: Slurm job attachment (srun –jobid) more stable than direct SSH because designed for HPC workloads and respects cluster’s resource management layer. Job IDs persist across sessions enabling reattachment
General Issues 6. MIHD project accumulated redundant scripts (3 backup versions totaling 111KB), scattered logs (5 files, ~5MB), 16 temporary summary fragments, and dispersed documentation in root and docs/ directories Solution: Systematic cleanup using parallel Task agents for exploration: deleted redundant scripts (functionality replaced by run_benchmark.py/run_pipeline.py), created outputs/logs/ for centralized storage, deleted summary fragments (key data in experiment_comparison.csv), reorganized docs into three-tier structure (research/experiments/archived), merged ENHANCEMENT_PLAN files into unified plans.md, updated all references
Key Insight: Project iteration naturally accumulates redundancy; periodic ‘cleanup day’ needed: delete superseded backups, relocate temporary outputs, consolidate duplicate docs, update references. Root directory should contain only core entry documents
7. Port 5555 already in use when starting Pi0 VLA server, causing startup failure Solution: Detected via srun output. Options presented: kill existing process, use different port, or check if existing server reusable. Left for user to decide conflict resolution strategy
Key Insight: In long-running cluster jobs, resource conflicts (ports, GPUs, file locks) common. Need to check availability before allocation and have fallback strategies
8. gadget project CLAUDE.md and README.md both missing documentation for website/ tool (third tool in project), causing incomplete project overview Solution: Used /init skill to trigger systematic documentation audit, discovered gap, read update.sh and config.yml to understand functionality, added accurate documentation covering Hugo blog, incremental compression, and cross-references
Key Insight: /init command’s systematic review catches long-standing documentation gaps easily overlooked during incremental development, especially in multi-tool projects where each tool documented independently
9. QFormer training shows high memory usage (19.4GB) but extremely low GPU utilization (4%, 55W), causing slow training progress Solution: Identified this as QFormer architecture characteristic: model and data reside in VRAM but cross-attention computation is lightweight, with most time spent on CPU-intensive k-NN graph construction and loss calculation. This is expected behavior requiring patience
Key Insight: High memory occupancy ≠ high GPU load. Learnable query mechanisms result in training bottlenecked by CPU preprocessing while GPU cores remain mostly idle, with VRAM used for storage rather than computation
10. datasets library version 4.4.1 incompatible with conversion pipeline, causing import failures Solution: Downgraded from 4.4.1 to 3.6.0 to restore compatibility with MimicGen-to-LeRobot conversion scripts
Key Insight: Bleeding-edge package versions can break established workflows; pin to tested versions in production pipelines
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Vision Refinement two-stage fusion architecture design Role Approach Human User explicitly proposed ‘first use scan_cluster/etc self-supervised methods to refine vision embedding, then use multimodal fusion strategies to merge with gene embedding’ - a novel experimental design AI had not suggested AI AI previously implemented scan_cluster etc as independent fusion strategies (parallel with gene embedding), never considering them as vision embedding preprocessing steps Difference Analysis: Human’s two-stage thinking reflects deep understanding of method nature: image-only self-supervision is feature refinement, not fusion, and should be used at different pipeline stages. AI’s understanding more mechanical (fusion choices list), lacking insight into method composability

How to prove Error Recovery Benchmark is useful beyond ‘can generate scenes’ - need evidence that data actually improves models for thesis contribution Solution: Design G4 (dataset usefulness proof) as 4-step experiment: (1) convert 2000+ scenes to LeRobot format with state+image observations, (2) LoRA fine-tune π0.5 on error scenes for 2-4 hours on A800, (3) evaluate on held-out test split with stratified sampling, (4) measure improvement (expect 15-30% SR gain, 10-20% RP gain, statistical significance via bootstrap CI and Wilcoxon test)
Key Insight: Benchmark usefulness requires closed-loop proof: error data → model training → measurable performance improvement on unseen errors. This is the core thesis contribution beyond scene generation infrastructure - the ‘4-pillar validation’ that distinguishes publishable benchmarks from toy datasets.
2. UNI2 foundation model features achieve only ARI 0.11-0.16 on DLPFC spatial domain clustering (vs 0.5+ for gene+image multimodal), with brown repeated patches appearing uniformly across clustering results Solution: Identified 5 root causes: (1) training data domain gap (cancer-heavy, brain-rare), (2) pretraining task mismatch (coarse tissue classification vs fine-grained layer detection), (3) DLPFC layer differences are subtle (cell density/size, not color/texture), (4) feature redundancy with gene expression, (5) lack of spatial context. Analysis revealed UNI2 clusters by morphological similarity (blood vessels across all layers) rather than biological domains. Proposed 6 adaptation methods (STEGO, SCAN, BYOL, DINOv2-GAT, TTT-MAE, SFDA) following solution hierarchy: domain-specific pretraining > test-time adaptation > feature refinement > task-specific fine-tuning. Added H&E reference panel to visualization to confirm hypothesis.
Key Insight: Pure vision encoders cluster by morphological features not biological function - this is a classic fine-grained recognition problem seen across CV domains (bird subspecies, rock types, cell morphology). Low ARI reflects structural grouping (what looks similar) not functional grouping (what is biologically similar). General foundation models learn coarse semantics; domain-specific fine-tuning or feature refinement is necessary for fine-grained tasks.
3. Error Recovery Benchmark dataset phase imbalance - 90% scenes in pre_reach/reach, transport/place completely empty (0 scenes) Solution: Design strategy using BC-RNN (60-70% SR) as key to reaching later phases, lower detector min_step thresholds from 100→5-50 to capture lift/transport failures, use MimicGen to generate 200+ demo variants for increased trajectory diversity and later-phase trigger opportunities
Key Insight: Phase coverage requires policies with sufficient success rate to reach late phases (BC-RNN sweet spot) combined with adjusted detector timing - random policy fails too early (lift never reached), Pi0 has 0% SR (grasp never reached), only BC-RNN reaches transport/place with failures. This is a ‘reachability problem’ determined by success rate distribution.
4. How to rigorously validate that 24-type error taxonomy is principled, complete, and non-redundant for academic publication Solution: Three-pillar validation: (1) map 8 categories to FMEA failure modes from ISO 15066/10218/IEC 61508 industrial safety standards (provides theoretical grounding), (2) prove completeness via 6 phase × 3 family = 18-cell matrix showing no blind spots, (3) statistical validation using Cohen’s/Fleiss’ kappa (target: within-category κ>0.6, cross-category κ<0.3) to verify types are distinct
Key Insight: Academic taxonomy validation requires both theoretical grounding (industry standards provide FMEA-based rationale) and empirical evidence (statistical independence tests prove non-redundancy) - cannot rely on intuition alone for 24 types
5. M14 baseline evaluation (5448 episodes, 5-15h runtime) risks losing all progress if VLA server crashes mid-run Solution: Implemented resume support in collector.py: on startup, reads existing episodes.jsonl, builds a set of completed (scene_id, policy_name, seed) tuples, skips them in the triple loop, and rebuilds all_episodes dict to preserve summary correctness. Added –resume flag to 3_collect_data.py. Now crash-safe with automatic resume.
Key Insight: For long-running data collection (>1h), append-only JSONL logging + resume logic is essential. The key is idempotency: reading back the JSONL and rebuilding the summary dict ensures final results are identical whether run completes in one shot or across multiple resume attempts.
6. User didn’t understand ‘recovery training data’ concept in Phase II plan, blocking plan approval Solution: Provided concrete example comparing normal demo (reset→success) vs recovery trajectory (error_state→adjustment→success); explained it teaches model ‘how to fix mistakes’ not just ‘how to do it right from start’. User then chose human teleoperation for high-quality data despite time cost.
Key Insight: Technical jargon must be grounded in examples before implementation discussion; user prioritized data quality and real recovery demonstrations over automated proxies, willing to invest manual effort for authentic data

Commented out these 3 options in ~/.ssh/config and removed stale socket files from ~/.ssh/sockets/. Connection restored immediately.
Key Insight: SSH connection multiplexing (ControlMaster) is a Unix-only feature; Windows OpenSSH silently fails when these options are present, causing cryptic low-level errors that look like bugs rather than feature unavailability.

Key Insight: EGL device ID is relative to visible devices list, not absolute GPU hardware index - robosuite’s EGL assertion enforces this to prevent render target mismatches

HEST-1k shows pathology foundation models significantly outperform ImageNet baseline (UNI2 Pearson r=0.414 vs ResNet50 r=0.326), but comprehensive vision-only spatial domain clustering benchmarks largely don’t exist - most papers only evaluate multi-modal fusion, not isolated vision encoder performance. Need gene expression to distinguish functional regions with similar visual appearance. Error recovery benchmarks require proving usefulness through 4 dimensions (4-pillar validation): (1) large-scale diverse data (2000+ scenes), (2) theoretically-grounded taxonomy (FMEA/ISO standards), (3) baseline performance characterization (4+ policies), (4) demonstration of training improvement on foundation models (15-30% SR gain). This distinguishes publishable benchmarks from toy datasets - the core thesis contribution is closed-loop proof: error data → model training → measurable improvement. Cross-domain literature search is extremely valuable for identifying solution patterns. The image-only clustering problem in spatial transcriptomics is nearly identical to problems in: (1) fine-grained bird classification (subspecies differ only in beak shape/feather pattern), (2) remote sensing (ImageNet features fail on satellite images), (3) microscopy (material microstructures), (4) geology (rock thin sections). All domains converged on the same 4-tier solution hierarchy: domain-specific pretraining > test-time adaptation > feature refinement > task-specific fine-tuning. This suggests deep learning failure modes are universal across modalities. Phase imbalance in error scene generation stems from success rate distribution creating a ‘reachability problem’ - need policies with 60-70% SR (BC-RNN sweet spot) to reach late phases while still producing failures. Documentation-driven development for complex multi-milestone projects ensures shared understanding and alignment before execution, critical for research with advisor feedback loops. Evaluation paradigm fundamentally changes what is measured: same task (tissue type identification) evaluated as supervised classification (with labels, tests linear separability via KNN) vs unsupervised clustering (no labels, tests natural cluster structure via ARI) measures different aspects of embedding quality - high KNN accuracy doesn’t guarantee good clustering ARI. This explains why CRC-100K 9-class classification success doesn’t predict DLPFC spatial domain clustering performance. BYOL (Bootstrap Your Own Latent) solves SimCLR’s key weakness: need for large batches and negative samples. BYOL uses teacher-student framework with EMA updates + predictor head to prevent collapse, making it robust to small batches (256 vs 4096+), augmentation choices, and domain shift. This explains why STAIG chose BYOL over SimCLR for histology patches (where similar-looking patches from adjacent layers should NOT be pushed apart as negatives). The key architectural insight: predictor head asymmetry (online has it, target doesn’t) + EMA target prevents trivial solutions. FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) from industrial safety standards (ISO 15066 collaborative robots, ISO 10218 robot safety, IEC 61508 functional safety) provides rigorous theoretical grounding for robot error taxonomies - maps 8 categories to standardized failure modes like ’loss of grip’, ‘uncontrolled release’, ‘unexpected contact’. Academic taxonomy validation requires both theoretical grounding (industry standards) and empirical evidence (Cohen’s/Fleiss’ kappa: within-category κ>0.6, cross-category κ<0.3). VLA model landscape for error recovery: 8 models claim recovery capabilities but only 2 are open-source (RoboFAC, VLAC). FailSafe and VLA-SCT are most practical for integration (training-free, plug-in architecture, already validated on π0/OpenVLA). Recovery methods fall into 3 categories: dual-system (fast/slow), proactive (subtask backtracking), reactive (supervisor-guided correction). MimicGen can amplify 10 demos to 200+ variants for trajectory diversity, requires has_offscreen_renderer=True for VLA training. Resume logic for long-running data collection must rebuild summary state from JSONL, not just skip episodes. The naive approach (only skip completed episodes) breaks final summary statistics. The correct approach: (1) read JSONL on startup, (2) rebuild all_episodes dict, (3) add completed tuples to skip set, (4) continue collection. This ensures idempotency: running A→crash→resume→B produces identical results to running A+B in one shot. Practical Learnings Large file reading strategy: use limit parameter for initial exploration, then targeted offset ranges or Grep for specific content; avoid reading entire file unless necessary. For files >30k tokens, chunked reading with 400-line segments works well. Documentation refactoring with ‘complete preservation’ requirement needs verification: count all checklist items before and after to prove nothing lost. Windows OpenSSH does not support Unix domain sockets (ControlMaster/ControlPath), causing silent failures with cryptic error messages (‘Bad file descriptor’, ’nonexistent pipe’). The solution is not to switch SSH clients, but to disable connection multiplexing options. This is a reminder that cross-platform compatibility issues often manifest as low-level errors that look like bugs rather than feature unavailability. ARI improved from 0.065→0.121 for vision-only, concat fusion reached 0.275 ARI validating multimodal integration approach tianhe What was done: Built unified checkpoint management system with symlinks, created policy rollout visualization tool, and investigated VLA training data availability for PickPlace task How it was done: Created checkpoints/ directory structure linking BC-RNN/VLA/Robomimic models, wrote 200-line visualize_policy_rollout.py with MP4 rendering, updated configs and Makefile, searched zhaoganlong’s datasets Impact: Can now visualize policy behavior via MP4 rollouts and identified root cause of VLA failure (no task-specific finetuning); Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Fix MIHD coordinate swap bug — Corrected tissue_positions_list.csv column mapping where pxl_row_in_fullres (Y) and pxl_col_in_fullres (X) were swapped as pixel_x/pixel_y Implementation & Fixes 🔄 Re-run MIHD vision and fusion experiments — Regenerate embeddings and benchmark results for 33 vision-only and 88 multimodal fusion experiments after coordinate fix ✅ Create policy rollout visualization tool — Wrote visualize_policy_rollout.py script with offscreen rendering, HUD overlay, MP4 export, and support for random/BC-RNN/VLA policies ✅ Build unified checkpoint management system — Created checkpoints/ directory with symlinks to BC-RNN, VLA (Pi0/Pi0.5), and Robomimic models for consistent path references ✅ Investigate VLA training data availability — Searched for PickPlace-specific VLA checkpoints and training data; found only 10 source demos vs 500 demos for Coffee/Stack tasks Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Vision embeddings extracted from transposed image locations due to X/Y coordinate swap in tissue_positions_list.csv parsing Solution: Renamed columns to pxl_row/pxl_col (semantic names), swapped coordinate order to (X, Y) = (pxl_col, pxl_row), deleted vision cache, re-ran experiments
Key Insight: Spatial data requires explicit Y-as-row, X-as-column semantics; 10x scale factor validation (pixel coords × scalefactor = microns) catches coordinate system errors early
2. Pi0_libero checkpoint achieves 0% success on PickPlace despite 96-100% on Coffee/Stack Solution: Identified root cause: Pi0_libero is LIBERO-domain finetuned, lacks PickPlace-specific training data (only 10 source demos vs 500 for other tasks); proposed MimicGen→LeRobot→LoRA pipeline
Key Insight: VLA cross-task generalization fails when task domains differ (LIBERO vs PickPlace object/scene layout); finetuning requires 500+ demos expandable via MimicGen from 10 source demos
General Issues 3. No way to visually inspect VLA policy behavior on PickPlace task to diagnose 0% success rate Solution: Built visualize_policy_rollout.py with EGL offscreen rendering, frame-by-frame capture, HUD overlay (policy/step/reward/success), and MP4 export per rollout
Key Insight: Video rollouts reveal behavioral patterns (e.g., random flailing vs directed failures) that success rate alone cannot distinguish

Log export (data correction) completed successfully, but downstream report generation blocked by LLM API unavailability. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. MIHD vision encoder single-modal ARI extremely low (~0.065), inconsistent with historical UNI2 performance; embeddings showed suspicious patterns (many duplicate rows initially) Solution: Deep investigation of tissue_positions_list.csv revealed col4 is pxl_row_in_fullres (Y-axis) not pixel_x, col5 is pxl_col_in_fullres (X-axis) not pixel_y, but code naming was reversed. Confirmed by analyzing array_row/array_col step increments: col4 changes 119.8px/step (Y-axis), col5 changes 68.9px/step (X-axis). Fixed by correcting column names to (pxl_col, pxl_row) order
Key Insight: Data bugs are more insidious than model bugs: code runs normally, caches generate successfully, tests pass, but all results are based on wrong data. Requires tracing from macro-level anomalies (low ARI) back to raw data source (CSV column definitions). Spatial distance Euclidean invariance meant graph construction was unaffected, but vision patch content was completely misaligned
2. ccusage returns cost=0 for claude-opus-4-6, causing severe token cost tracking failure (Feb 17 actual ~$43 displayed as $0.90, 13x underestimation) Solution: Implemented fallback pricing mechanism in daily_summary.py’s fetch_ccusage() function via _fix_zero_cost_models() post-processing logic. Added _FALLBACK_PRICING dictionary (opus-4-6: input $5/M, output $25/M, cache_creation $6.25/M, cache_read $0.50/M) to calculate correct costs when ccusage returns cost=0. Fixed field name bug (mb.get(‘model’) → mb.get(‘modelName’) or mb.get(‘model’)) for compatibility. Re-exported logs for Feb 13-17, correcting displayed costs from $3-7/day to actual $18-48/day.
Key Insight: Third-party tool pricing defects cannot be directly fixed—implement local fallback mechanism as practical solution. LiteLLM uses versioned model names (anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1 with -v1 suffix) while Claude Code logs use simplified names (claude-opus-4-6), causing systematic mismatch. Fallback design must trigger only on anomalous values (cost=0) to maintain backward compatibility when upstream fixes issue. Cost tracking bugs can cause 90%+ underestimation (13x in this case), severely impacting resource planning decisions. Always verify third-party tool output schema by printing raw data, not assuming from documentation.
3. tianhe non-impulse injectors (friction/pose_perturb/gripper_bias) crashed with ‘AttributeError: no attribute mj_name2id’ when trying to resolve body/geom IDs in MuJoCo model Solution: Replaced direct mujoco.mj_name2id() calls with robosuite wrapper methods model.body_name2id() and model.geom_name2id(). Added _resolve_body_id() helper to try ’name’ first then ’name_main’ suffix (robosuite naming convention). Wrapped in try/except for graceful handling of missing bodies.
Key Insight: Robosuite wraps MuJoCo with its own API layer and adds _main suffix to object body names. Direct MuJoCo C API calls bypass the framework layer and break—must use framework-provided wrappers that handle name translation. Robot simulation frameworks layer abstractions over raw physics engines; direct API calls that bypass the framework break. Always examine working reference code (e.g., ImpulseInjector) in the same codebase before modifying.
4. tianhe BC-RNN policy crashes with KeyError ‘object’ because StateExtractor generates obs dict with ‘object-state’ key while robomimic training data used ‘object’ key (different robosuite tasks have inconsistent key names: PickPlace uses object-state, Lift uses object) Solution: Added key mapping in _to_robosuite_obs() Strategy 1 to alias object-state → object before returning raw obs. Updated Strategy 3 fallback to concatenate pos+quat from StateExtractor’s objects dict into object key. Validated with 79 unit tests and GPU integration test confirming KeyError eliminated.
Key Insight: Robosuite automatically appends -state suffix to grouped modalities (e.g. object → object-state), but training data uses original names. Adapter layers must bridge this naming convention gap. Different robosuite tasks have inconsistent observation key naming conventions. Manual obs reconstruction cannot guarantee key name consistency with training time. Safest approach is passing original env.step() return value directly with key aliasing. This highlights that cross-task compatibility requires either (a) unified obs format or (b) explicit key remapping layer
5. LLM responses for structured reports often return malformed JSON: unescaped quotes, incomplete objects, extra text, or truncation near token limits, causing parse failures and workflow interruptions Solution: Implemented 4-stage fallback parser: (1) direct json.loads(), (2) extract ```json blocks, (3) depth-based brace matching to find complete JSON object, (4) call LLM to repair malformed JSON. For APIs supporting it, use tool_use (Anthropic) or response_format=json_object (OpenAI) to enforce valid JSON
Key Insight: LLM-generated structured data requires defensive parsing with multiple fallback strategies. Native JSON mode (tool_use/json_object) significantly reduces but doesn’t eliminate failures. Including LLM-powered repair as final fallback creates robust pipeline. Each fallback layer handles specific failure mode: code blocks handle markdown formatting, brace matching handles truncation, repair handles syntax errors
6. BC-RNN model achieves 0% success rate despite KeyError being fixed—robot hovers over bin without approaching target can Solution: Generated 3 visualization videos (400 frames each) showing robot behavior. Root cause confirmed as undertrained checkpoint (epoch 600 with limited demo data), not framework bug. Videos reveal robot hovers but never attempts grasping. Need to train for more epochs or use better checkpoint.
Key Insight: GPU integration tests are critical even when unit tests pass. BC-RNN passed all 79 unit tests but required actual GPU rollout to discover 0% SR issue. Video visualization is essential for diagnosing behavior quality issues in robotic policies. Framework correctness vs model quality require different validation strategies: unit/integration tests confirm code logic; video visualization reveals behavior quality.
7. SSH connections to tianhe HPC cluster frequently disconnect, causing Claude Code session loss and inability to resume work; VS Code Remote SSH similarly affected Solution: Implemented layered defense-in-depth solution: (1) SSH keep-alive on both ends (15s heartbeat, 90s tolerance), (2) tmux session persistence so processes survive disconnects, (3) claude-tmux script for one-command session resume with auto proxy, (4) commented auto proxy in .bashrc to isolate user environment for shared accounts, (5) documented local client config for ControlMaster multiplexing and auto-ssh reconnection script.
Key Insight: Network instability requires redundant mitigation at multiple layers: protocol-level (TCP keep-alive), SSH-level (ControlMaster), application-level (tmux + auto-reconnect). No single layer suffices for production reliability. tmux decouples session state from connection state, enabling true resume capability. Session-scoped proxy configuration (not global bashrc) avoids affecting other shared-account users. When working on shared server accounts, every environment modification (PATH, proxy, aliases) must consider multi-user implications.
8. Multi-device daily report workflow needs synchronization mechanism—devices export independently but merge requires access to all devices’ exports, which may not be available on the merging device Solution: Adopted two-tier rclone sync: export uploads to /logs/, merge uploads final reports to /reports/. Added merge –sync flag downloading all devices’ logs/ before LLM aggregation. Implemented _merged_devices tracking to skip re-summarizing already-processed devices
Key Insight: Distributed workflows require explicit synchronization points. Separating raw exports (logs/) from aggregated outputs (reports/) prevents circular dependencies. Idempotent design (skip already-processed) enables safe re-runs without expensive redundant API calls
9. Original single-phase daily report design assumed single-device usage; when user wanted multi-device aggregation, existing architecture couldn’t handle it Solution: Complete redesign from single-phase (read conversations → call API → generate report) to two-phase (Phase 1: export conversations to JSON per device; Phase 2: merge all exports + call API for aggregated report). User explicitly requested this architecture change
Key Insight: User requirements evolve during development. Human (user) identified single-device limitation that AI didn’t anticipate in initial design. Two-phase architecture is more complex but necessary for actual use case. This shows Human systems thinking was superior in foreseeing distributed deployment constraints
10. Scene generation produced zero friction/gripper_bias scenes despite injectors being enabled (only pose_perturb worked initially) Solution: Discovered detectors only generated friction/gripper_bias ErrorSpecs for specific subtypes that didn’t trigger during runs. Implemented _augment_specs_with_alternatives() method to programmatically generate friction/stuck and gripper_bias/stuck specs when original detectors produce no results. Generated 100 additional friction scenes (55 stuck, 28 tip_over, 17 large_offset), expanding database to 454 scenes.
Key Insight: Error scene generation is a funnel: detector triggering → ErrorSpec generation → injector application → validation → scene acceptance. Enabling an injector doesn’t guarantee scenes—depends on detector triggering frequency. Different error types have vastly different acceptance rates based on task dynamics. Pose perturbation is more universally applicable than friction/gripper anomalies in pick-place tasks. Programmatic spec augmentation can overcome detector coverage gaps.
11. No MimicGen pretrained BC-RNN checkpoints available for PickPlace task Solution: Exhaustive search (official repo, HuggingFace, local filesystem) confirmed MimicGen only provides datasets, not pretrained model weights. Designed training-from-scratch plan using MimicGen-generated demo datasets with robomimic framework.
Key Insight: Official releases may provide data but not trained models. Always verify asset availability before planning dependent workflows. Training from demos became necessary fallback when pretrained checkpoints unavailable.
General Issues 12. Model checkpoints scattered across filesystem (BC-RNN under tangzijia/, VLA models under zhaoganlong/, 47GB total), hindering management and reproducibility Solution: Designed checkpoints/ directory with symlinks to avoid copies: bc_rnn/pick_place → original path, vla/{pi0_libero, pi05_base, pi0_base, pi0_fast_base} → zhaoganlong cache. Updated benchmark_v4.yaml to use new centralized paths.
Key Insight: Large model assets (47GB+ VLA checkpoints) require symlink-based organization to avoid duplication while maintaining centralized discoverability. Scattered checkpoints across filesystem hinder reproducibility and config management.
13. Hugo front matter generation used hardcoded summary ‘AI Daily Summary’ and wrong timezone (+08:00 instead of -05:00), inconsistent with existing bugJournal entries Solution: Modified generate_hugo_post() to extract actual summary from report’s blockquote (line 3, starts with ‘>’), changed timezone to -05:00, time to T00:00:00, removed ‘AI Daily Summary’ from keywords
Key Insight: Code generation should match existing content conventions, not impose new ones. Reading actual report structure (blockquote summary) is more maintainable than hardcoded strings
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level MIHD coordinate bug root cause diagnosis Role Approach Human User provided complete problem analysis and verification method: calculated array_row/array_col step increments’ pixel changes (Δcol4=119.8px, Δcol5=68.9px) to reverse-confirm column semantics—a data-feature-based verification method rather than relying on documentation or code comments. User demonstrated data scientist diagnostic thinking AI AI executed user-provided fix plan: modified column names, cleared caches, reran experiments, verified results (coordinate ranges, embedding uniqueness, ARI improvement). AI did not independently discover bug; implemented predefined solution Difference Analysis: User demonstrated data scientist diagnostic thinking (using data itself to validate hypotheses); AI served as execution tool. Bug’s insidiousness lay in code logic being correct and caches generating normally—only external indicators (abnormally low ARI) or data feature analysis could reveal it. User’s domain intuition (’this doesn’t look right’) was critical trigger
Two-phase export/merge architecture for multi-device aggregation Role Approach Human User recognized original single-phase design couldn’t handle multi-device scenario and explicitly requested redesign: ‘I want export to be local-only, then merge pulls from all devices and calls API.’ User provided conceptual architecture AI AI initially designed single-phase solution (read → process → generate) assuming single-device usage. Only after user intervention did AI implement two-phase design Difference Analysis: Human anticipated real-world deployment constraints (multiple devices, network-based sync) that AI missed in initial design. AI focused on immediate technical implementation without considering distributed usage patterns. Clear case where human systems thinking was superior
BC-RNN obs key mapping implementation approach Role Approach Human Provided complete implementation plan upfront with precise object-state → object mapping requirement, covering Strategy 1 (raw obs path) and Strategy 3 (StateExtractor fallback) with defensive programming. Anticipated the obs format mismatch from prior investigation and provided surgical fix. AI Executed implementation exactly as specified, validated with 79 unit tests, ran GPU integration test to confirm KeyError eliminated. Discovered 0% success rate requiring video analysis to distinguish framework bug vs model quality issue. Required visualization to diagnose root cause. Difference Analysis: Human’s prior investigation enabled precise specification of fix location and logic. AI validated correctness via testing but needed visualization to diagnose model quality issue. Collaboration pattern: human provides architectural direction from domain knowledge, AI executes and validates with systematic testing. User has domain knowledge (robosuite task differences); AI lacks predictive capability for framework details, requiring multiple trial-error + user correction iterations to approach solution. Typical AI limitation in complex system integration
Scope prioritization for M5/M6 milestone completion under deadline pressure Role Approach Human Explicitly constrained scope: ‘defer multi-task expansion, use only pretrained models, skip missing VLA models.’ Pragmatically focused on proving evaluation pipeline works with minimal risk rather than maximizing coverage. Applied ‘done is better than perfect’ principle. AI Initially proposed comprehensive 6-phase plan including downloading MimicGen datasets, training BC-RNN from scratch, running full 4-policy evaluation, and creating comparison reports. Designed for technical completeness but potentially over-scoped for deadline context. Difference Analysis: Human exhibited stronger project management instinct—recognizing that proving the system works with 2-3 policies is sufficient for paper writing milestone. AI leaned toward technical completeness without considering deadline pressure. Human’s pragmatic scoping prevented scope creep while maintaining milestone integrity.
ccusage pricing bug diagnosis strategy Role Approach Human Directly pointed to ‘ccusage cannot fetch LiteLLM’ as problem starting point, guiding AI to investigate LiteLLM pricing database and ccusage source code. Provided high-level problem localization from intuition. AI Launched multiple parallel Explore agents to systematically investigate ccusage integration architecture, log data structure, LiteLLM pricing JSON. Conducted broad evidence collection, verified hypothesis, and identified root cause (model name mismatch). Difference Analysis: User drives requirement but abandoned at implementation planning stage, possibly because: (1) plan insufficiently specific, (2) wrong timing (already did too much work that day), (3) insufficient evaluation of existing tool modifications. AI failed to capture user intent change. Human provided intuitive direction based on domain knowledge. AI’s systematic exploration validated hypothesis and ensured no missing details. Human’s intuition guided search space; AI’s breadth search confirmed root cause definitively.
Historical data correction strategy for cost tracking bug Role Approach Human Explicitly required ‘run on all days to fix this bug’ and ‘fix the numbers in all the jsons and report mds’, emphasizing batch correction necessity from business perspective. Stressed data consistency across 5-day history. AI Executed daily export commands for data correction, discovered report files need separate processing (merge command calling LLM). Encountered API failure blocking report regeneration but completed log data correction successfully. Difference Analysis: Human’s completeness requirement from business angle drove thorough fix vs just fixing current day. AI’s execution discovered technical dependencies (LLM API) causing partial blockage. Human emphasized data integrity; AI identified decoupling opportunity (separate export from merge).
SSH stability solution architecture for shared account environment Role Approach Human Specified two-part delivery: ‘On server, you handle it directly. For local PC, give me a document so local Claude can auto-execute.’ Separated concerns by control boundary and automation capability. Later specified conditional proxy: ‘only when I connect should settings activate, controllable via proxy_on/proxy_off.’ AI Initially created unified plan for both server and local, restructured after user clarified. Initially designed auto-proxy in claude-tmux only, not realizing .bashrc line 136 would affect all users. After feedback, commented global auto-proxy and documented manual proxy_on workflow. Difference Analysis: Human thought in terms of execution context (what I control vs. delegate) and shared resource implications (multi-user account). AI initially focused narrowly on ‘make it work’ without considering side effects on other users. Human’s infrastructure awareness prevented environmental pollution.
VLA config selection for robosuite environment compatibility Role Approach Human Immediately caught semantic mismatch: ‘Wait, don’t use droid config. This is robosuite environment, should use mimicgen version of pi0.5.’ Maintained context awareness about task-model compatibility constraints. AI Initially suggested testing with LIBERO and droid configs based on found checkpoint directories, without checking environment compatibility first. Exhibited premature optimization—found checkpoints and immediately proposed using them. Difference Analysis: Human maintained stronger environment-model semantic compatibility awareness. AI exhibited ‘found tool, use tool’ pattern without validating applicability. Human’s domain knowledge prevented wasted effort on incompatible configs.
Daily report automation deployment need Role Approach Human User manually created multiple bugJournal entries then said ‘write a Python code to do this’—extracting automation need from repetitive labor. Specified requirements: given template, auto-convert md, copy to configurable location, run update.sh AI AI entered Plan Mode designing deploy subcommand, identified existing generate_hugo_post() limitations (hardcoded summary, single-date only), designed batch processing + smart summary extraction. But user rejected at ExitPlanMode Difference Analysis: User drove requirement but abandoned at implementation planning stage, possibly because: (1) plan insufficiently specific, (2) wrong timing (already did too much work that day), (3) insufficient evaluation of existing tool modifications. AI failed to capture user intent change
JSON repair strategy selection Role Approach Human User accepted AI’s proposed 4-stage fallback but didn’t specify approach—trusted AI’s technical judgment on parsing strategies AI AI autonomously designed multi-stage fallback: direct parse → code block extraction → brace matching → LLM repair. AI also added tool_use/json_object mode suggestions for supporting APIs Difference Analysis: Here AI had superior technical knowledge of JSON parsing failure modes and fallback strategies. Human provided requirement (‘fix JSON parsing’), AI provided solution architecture. Collaborative: human sets requirements, AI provides technical solutions
conversation_summaries feature requirement Role Approach Human User explicitly requested section to ‘summarize the conversation with AI’ at session level, recognizing that task lists don’t capture what was actually discussed AI AI proposed technical schema (JSON structure, markdown rendering, prompt modifications) but didn’t anticipate user need for narrative summaries Difference Analysis: User drives product vision (what users need), AI provides implementation design (how to build it). Feature gap was user insight, not AI suggestion. Shows Human product sense superior to AI’s
AI Limitations Critical Limitations Did not independently diagnose MIHD coordinate bug root cause; completely relied on user-provided analysis and fix plan. Faced with ‘abnormally low ARI’ macro indicator, AI lacked capability for autonomous data source tracing (from results → embeddings → patch extraction → coordinates → CSV column definitions backward chain) tianhe BC-RNN integration went through three failed fix attempts across two sessions; AI didn’t foresee robosuite different tasks (PickPlace vs Lift) having inconsistent observation key naming, nor realize at first fix that StateExtractor-rebuilt obs cannot guarantee key name consistency. Required multiple user corrections to approach correct solution. Used deprecated MuJoCo C API (mujoco.mj_name2id) instead of checking robosuite wrapper API first, causing immediate crashes in three injectors. Should have examined existing working code (ImpulseInjector) to understand correct API pattern before modifying other injectors. Did not anticipate multi-device distributed usage pattern in initial daily report tool design—assumed single-device workflow and required user to request two-phase architecture redesign When generating JSON near token limits, AI may truncate output mid-structure, producing malformed JSON requiring defensive parsing and repair logic in production systems ccusage fix initial implementation incorrectly used mb.get(‘model’) field when actual JSON had modelName, without first verifying third-party tool output structure. Caused fix to be completely ineffective until human discovered numbers still wrong and re-investigated. Also launched excessive parallel exploration tasks with redundant information collection (reading same log files multiple times). Initially proposed testing VLA models with LIBERO/droid configs without verifying environment compatibility. Failed to maintain semantic context that target environment is robosuite/mimicgen, not LIBERO. Required human correction to redirect toward appropriate configs. Cross-session memory deficit: AI in 2026-02-16 tianhe session couldn’t autonomously recall VLA checkpoint downloads from previous session, requiring user prompt to search broader server paths Cannot proactively anticipate user needs for features like conversation summaries—these product insights come from user observation of gaps in generated reports Struggles with deeply nested meta-tasks: when conversations contain conversations about conversations, AI has difficulty determining which level to analyze without explicit guidance about task scope and expected output When generating 2026-02-17 daily report, AI as daily report analyst itself became observation object—‘observer is observed’ meta-level complexity exists. AI needed to analyze own behavior that day (behavior of generating daily reports), requiring certain self-awareness capability General Limitations Daily report automation deployment Plan Mode design was rejected by user; AI failed to capture user intent change or assess whether implementation plan specificity met user expectations, directly proceeding to ExitPlanMode rather than first asking for user feedback. Multiple failed ExitPlanMode attempts indicate difficulty judging when plan refinement is complete vs when user wants to continue iteration. User rejected plan exits 3 times across sessions, suggesting AI should ask ‘is this plan ready?’ rather than assuming completion. Cannot directly analyze video content to assess policy quality. BC-RNN rollout videos required manual keyframe extraction and human inspection to identify robot hovering behavior (ignoring grasp target). Could not infer 0% success rate indicated model quality issue without visual confirmation. When encountering API ConnectionRefused error during report regeneration, did not proactively propose fallback solution (complete data correction first, handle report generation separately later). Insufficient flexibility in workflow decoupling. Created long unified plan documents mixing server-side and local-client instructions without considering execution boundaries. Required user feedback to restructure into actionable separate deliverables. Weak project decomposition instinct. When user asked ‘Where are we now?’ (in Chinese), launched exploratory agents and read large documents instead of first checking for recent session context or TODO tracking systems. Over-relied on file reading when conversational context might have been sufficient. Learnings Key Learnings Data bugs are more insidious and destructive than model bugs: MIHD coordinate swap bug invalidated all vision experiment results, yet code logic was completely normal and all tests passed. Requires tracing from macro-level indicator anomalies (ARI) back to data source (CSV column definitions). This demands complete data scientist thinking chain; unit testing alone cannot discover such bugs Cross-framework integration naming convention differences are hidden traps: robosuite’s _main suffix, different tasks’ observation key name differences (object vs object-state), LiteLLM’s model name -v1 suffix—these details aren’t prominent in documentation but cause runtime errors. Robot simulation frameworks layer abstractions over raw physics engines (robosuite wraps MuJoCo). Direct API calls that bypass the framework layer break—must use framework-provided wrappers that handle naming conventions (e.g., _main suffix) and state management. Robosuite’s observation key naming convention: environment auto-appends -state suffix to grouped modalities (e.g. object → object-state), but training data often uses original names. Adapter layers must handle this mismatch. Safest strategies: (1) use framework-wrapped APIs not low-level APIs, (2) pass original data structures not manual reconstruction, (3) print actual output to verify field names not infer from docs. Always examine working reference code in the same codebase before modifying. Framework correctness vs model quality require different validation strategies. Unit/integration tests confirm code logic and eliminate errors like KeyError. Video visualization reveals behavior quality issues (robot hovering vs grasping). GPU integration tests are critical even when unit tests pass—BC-RNN passed 79 unit tests but required GPU rollout to discover 0% SR and visualization to diagnose undertrained checkpoint. Each validation layer serves different purpose. Multi-device collaboration daily report tool closed loop established: each device exports local logs → central hub merges remote logs → unified deployment to Hugo → GitHub Pages publishing. This workflow was intensively used on 2026-02-17 (processing 4 historical dates), proving two-phase architecture feasibility. Next step is automation (user already requested but not implemented). Meta-tooling (tools for analyzing tool usage) requires careful thought about workflow distribution—what happens on each device, how data synchronizes, how to handle partial information. Two-phase architectures (local export + centralized aggregation) are more robust than monolithic single-phase designs for distributed scenarios Error Recovery Benchmark scene library expansion from 251 to 454 is successful case of incremental extension: first implement impulse injectors (M4) → discover need for non-impulse types (M5) → fix MuJoCo API compatibility → generate multi-type scenes via detector candidate expansion mechanism. Demonstrates iteration path from minimum viable product (MVP) to feature-complete. Error scene generation is a funnel: detector triggering → ErrorSpec generation → injector application → validation → scene acceptance. Enabling an injector doesn’t guarantee scenes—depends on detector triggering frequency. Different error types have vastly different acceptance rates based on task dynamics. Pose perturbation is more universally applicable than friction/gripper anomalies in pick-place tasks. Programmatic spec augmentation (_augment_specs_with_alternatives()) can overcome detector coverage gaps. Third-party tool integration defensive programming: patch cost==0 (ccusage), field name compatibility (modelName or model), self-degradation for future fixes (when LiteLLM fixes, fallback becomes no-op). This ‘activate only when necessary’ patch strategy minimizes maintenance cost. Third-party tool pricing defects should be solved via local fallback mechanism rather than waiting for upstream fix. Design fallback to trigger only on anomalous values (cost=0) for backward compatibility. LiteLLM uses versioned model names (anthropic.{model}-v1 with optional :0 suffix) while Claude Code logs use simplified names, causing systematic mismatch. Cost tracking bugs can cause 90%+ underestimation (13x observed), severely impacting financial planning. Periodic audit of cost metrics critical. Human-AI collaboration works best when humans specify system architecture and strategic decisions while AI handles technical implementation and optimization. In this session, user’s architectural insights (two-phase design, multi-device sync) were critical; AI’s technical execution (parsing fallbacks, config optimization) filled gaps. Domain expert qualitative judgment is critical for discovering systemic problems. AI’s data-driven analysis and human experiential intuition form effective complementarity Remote development over unstable connections requires defense in depth across multiple layers: connection keep-alive (prevent), session persistence (survive), multiplexing (fast reconnect), and automation scripts (recover). Single-layer solutions fail under real-world network conditions. For shared server accounts, user-specific customizations belong in conditional blocks or separate launcher scripts, not universal .bashrc entries affecting everyone. tmux serves dual role as both state persistence and environment boundary. Session-scoped proxy configuration (not global bashrc) avoids affecting other shared-account users. LLM-generated structured data requires defensive parsing with multiple fallback strategies. Native JSON modes (tool_use for Anthropic, json_object for OpenAI) help but don’t eliminate failures—always implement repair as final fallback. Each fallback layer handles specific failure mode: code blocks handle markdown formatting, brace matching handles truncation, repair handles syntax errors Daily summary tools benefit from incremental schema evolution: start with basic task/problem lists, add session summaries for context, add prioritization metadata for filtering. Each layer serves different reader need. Batch documentation workflows benefit from two-phase architecture: (1) per-source extraction with local context, (2) cross-source consolidation with global deduplication. Pattern appears in summarize tool (export→merge), MIHD pipeline (Phase 1 cache embeddings→Phase 2 fuse), and error-recovery-benchmark (generate scenes→collect data) MimicGen release policy: only datasets provided, no pretrained model checkpoints. Official releases may provide data but not trained models—always verify asset availability before planning. BC-RNN (Behavioral Cloning with RNN) is straightforward supervised learning: collect human demo (state, action) pairs, train LSTM to predict actions, deploy as policy. Simple but effective baseline for manipulation tasks when sufficient demos exist. Training from demos became necessary fallback when pretrained checkpoints unavailable. Retroactive work log analysis (summarizing past week) is valuable practice turning raw conversation logs into structured knowledge artifacts, enabling pattern recognition and progress tracking across long timescales Idempotent design patterns (tracking what’s already processed, skipping redundant work) are essential for workflows that may be interrupted or re-run. The _merged_devices tracking prevented expensive redundant API calls when re-processing partially completed aggregations Large model asset management (47GB+ VLA checkpoints) requires symlink-based organization to avoid duplication while maintaining centralized discoverability. Scattered checkpoints across filesystem hinder reproducibility and config management. Centralized checkpoint directory improves discoverability. When fixing data quality bugs in historical data, decouple data correction (export) from downstream consumption (report generation). Avoid blocking entire pipeline due to downstream dependency failures (e.g., LLM API unavailability). Export phase depends on Node.js tools (ccusage), merge phase depends on LLM API—can proceed with export even if merge is blocked. Practical Learnings Complex research project documentation scope should cover not just main modules but also deps/ submodules (11 found in Motion framework), data conversion pipelines, and cross-repo integration points (LeRobot, OpenPI, MimicGen). Thorough exploration prevents incomplete documentation that hinders onboarding. Daily Report — 2026-02-16 Daily Overview What was done: Executed three major parallel workstreams: (1) diagnosed MIHD spatial embedding collapse and corrected error recovery documentation, (2) implemented and validated complete VLA integration infrastructure with natural error capture generating 150+ scenarios, (3) designed conversation summary feature for gadget summarization tool How it was done: Systematic engineering approach across devices: DCC performed root-cause analysis of 64-dim embedding bottleneck; Key Insight: The openpi library provides high-level create_trained_policy() function that encapsulates all model loading complexity. Using low-level APIs manually is error-prone and breaks when the library evolves.

This reveals VLA cross-task generalization remains challenging, but these failures provide valuable natural error data for benchmark purposes. Natural error capture (natural_capture mode) is more efficient than injection mode: 50 rollouts generated 150 scenes (~3 per rollout), while injection mode 10 rollouts generated only 3 scenes (~0.3 per rollout); natural failure modes are more diverse and realistic. Plugin-based architecture pattern in benchmark systems: detectors, classifiers, injectors all use base ABC + registry pattern for extensibility. Error classification system demonstrates this with 19 classifiers registered via CLASSIFIER_REGISTRY, enabling easy addition of new error types without modifying core logic. Documentation verification requires checking actual code registries and enums, not just reading docstrings or prior docs. DETECTOR_REGISTRY, CLASSIFIER_REGISTRY, and ErrorType enum are ground truth. Cross-conda-env communication architecture: VLA server uses TCP+pickle protocol to decouple model inference (openpi/openpi05 env) from benchmark framework (mimicgen_env). Length-prefix framing prevents message fragmentation, action chunking reduces inference calls. Environment isolation is critical for VLA/robotics projects due to conflicting dependencies. Observation preprocessing must handle multiple input formats gracefully: StateExtractor (framework-internal), raw env.step() (robosuite), and model-specific (VLA servers). Robust key lookup with fallbacks prevents silent failures. The observation dict format changes depending on source—need unified preprocessing layer. Spatial majority voting refinement (radius=15 nearest neighbors) can amplify rather than fix clustering errors when underlying embeddings are already collapsed. Refinement should be conditional on embedding quality metrics (e.g., disable if silhouette score < threshold). Dual VLM backend design (Gemini API + Claude Code CLI) provides flexibility: API suits batch automation, CLI suits interactive deep analysis and debugging; complementary coverage of different use cases. VLA integration for natural error generation requires architectural shifts: (1) policy server pattern for cross-conda-env execution, (2) camera observation support in environment wrapper, (3) observation preprocessing (quaternion→axis-angle, BGR→RGB, action chunking), (4) dual rollout modes (synthetic injection + natural capture). Fundamentally different from demo-replay synthetic perturbation approach. Systematic codebase exploration strategy (infrastructure check → model file location → config parameter confirmation → user decision confirmation) effectively supports complex multi-step project planning, avoiding missing critical dependencies. Backward compatibility is key consideration in data structure design: new conversation_summaries field through optionality and graceful degradation (missing field → no section rendering) ensures old reports continue working. This pattern applies broadly to evolving data formats. Error classification system’s 24 error types only triggered 5 types in actual VLA rollouts (joint_limit_approach, grasp_wrong_pose, misalignment_pre_grasp, overshoot, premature_release), indicating some error types require specific scenarios to manifest. Practical Learnings GPU batch processing for visualization (5 GPUs, 20 videos, zero failures) demonstrates value of parallel infrastructure. The subprocess.Popen + GPU assignment pattern scales well for embarrassingly parallel tasks. Falsy value handling subtlety in Python: 0 or default evaluates to default because 0 is falsy, causing bugs in 0-indexed counters. PrematureReleaseClassifier had step - (self._grasp_start_step or step) always returning 0 when grasp started at step 0. Solution: explicit is None checks for optional 0-indexed values.
